mechrevo-power set 55 --target-celsius 90 --polling-seconds 1 恢复原生温度阈值而保留 55 W 长期上限： sudo mechrevo-power set 55 set 不带温度参数会明确恢复原生温度策略，不会默默继承上一次的 90°C。 clear 则撤销整套工具配置。轮询、执行延迟和毫秒级突发仍可能造成温度尖峰。 本地打包 需要记录温度、PL1／PL2 和故障前样本时，可使用同包的 mechrevo-thermal。该命令只读，GPU 已失联时拒绝开始采样， 新增 Xid／不可纠正 PCIe 错误时会停止并标记结果无效。 配方在 packaging/arch/mechrevo-power-control/，只安装命令和说明，安装本身不会 启用功耗上限。它没有加入现有 DKMS 包，也没有作为新包发布到 AUR。 使用配方指定的源码提交构建；本地验证可以将来源切换为同一提交的本地 Git 仓库： cd packaging/arch/mechrevo-power-control MECHREVO_POWER_SOURCE=file:///absolute/path/to/mechrevo-drivers \ MECHREVO_POWER_COMMIT=<full-source-commit> makepkg --cleanbuild 不要把包含未提交更改的目录当作已经冻结的发布源码。 实现和边界 本机原来传给 thermald 的命令含 --adaptive，但没有可用的 INT3400 接口， 实际回退为 default engine。工具启用时明确选择 default engine 并指定独立 XML； 撤销时恢复原服务命令。没有替换 thermald 的二进制程序，也不开放其 D-Bus 控制权限。 XML 对 MSR 与 MMIO 两个 RAPL cooling device 同时设置范围：最高功耗为用户上限， 最低功耗按 thermald 2.5.13 自身的 50% 算法从该上限计算。 这里的 MinState 表示“最少降温、最高功耗”，MaxState 表示“最多降温、最低功耗”。 只修改前者可能弄反范围，使温控无法继续升级到其他降温设备，因此必须成对设置。 保留原步长后，控制状态的变化顺序会改变；这是一份带用户上限的原生温控配置， 不是原热控功率序列完全不变的承诺。 XML 本身只修改控制器缓存，不保证冷机时立即写入硬件。服务启动后的事件回调 检查两套长期约束，对高于上限的值各执行一次降限；已有更低值保持。 没有反复抢写功耗的后台循环。回调失败不会停止温控服务，但必须视为上限应用失败。 thermald 正常退出会恢复自身的启动快照。因此服务重启期间可能短暂回到原限值， 启动回调完成后再应用上限。服务停止期间、固件接管以及其他控制器写入不属于 持续保持保证。sysfs 没有原子比较后写入机制，初始化时也不能排除同时写入的竞争。 机器重启、睡眠恢复和 BIOS 更新需要另行验收。 这里只限制长期平均 CPU package 功耗。PL2 仍保留原策略，短时功耗可以高于 PL1； 平均窗口和能量采样也不能当成瞬时整机功耗。55 W 来自本机热设计参考值， 不是已验证的整机最大安全功耗。 需要临时验证 PL2 影响时，使用有独立恢复回执的 mechrevo-peak-trial，不能把 clear 当作 PL2 恢复命令。 源码和测试依据为 Intel 官方 thermal_daemon 的 v2.5.13， 冻结提交 5fdc5bbca7f8c3f5bb2ad6540e8211a159a88a3a。 实机结果单独记录在 GM6PX0X 验证记录，未验收项目不能由代码测试代替。

title: Arch / AUR 控制台包
body: 机械革命笔记本的 Linux 平台驱动与设备控制台，按机型提供功能。 Arch / AUR 控制台包 mechrevo-console 提供 Rust CLI、原生 GUI、OEM helper 和 mechrevo-control 桥接工具。控制台与 DKMS 包独立安装；内核驱动更新、已加载模块和控制台版本分别管理。 当前配方固定源码 97e66567bc779d37eb032f0e29a37fa9973658e6，版本为 0.1.0.r1553.g97e6656-1。固定提交保证每次构建使用同一份源码，工作区改动不进入包。 公开发布记录与本机安装验收分别记录。 构建与安装 Arch Linux 需要 Git、Rust、pkgconf、desktop-file-utils 和 libxml2；最低 Rust 版本以固定提交的 console/Cargo.toml 为准。运行依赖包含 Python、systemd、polkit 和图形库，具体包名由 PKGBUILD 声明。中文显示可安装 noto-fonts-cjk。 在此目录构建，再用包管理器安装： makepkg -s pacman -Qlp ./mechrevo-console-0.1.0.r1553.g97e6656-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst sudo pacman -U ./mechrevo-console-0.1.0.r1553.g97e6656-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst mechrevo-console --version mechrevo-console status --json mechrevo-control touchpad status 使用已有本地仓库时，设置 MECHREVO_CONSOLE_SOURCE=file:///absolute/path/to/mechrevo-drivers。 CARGO_TARGET_DIR 可指定绝对缓存路径，同一目录应由一个 Cargo 构建使用。 prepare() 执行 cargo fetch --locked 准备依赖；构建使用 --release --workspace --all-features --locked --offline。缓存完整时可设置 CARGO_NET_OFFLINE=true，锁文件不随构建更新。 触摸板 触摸板控制使用 Linux input 的 inhibited 属性。udev 负责识别触摸板，helper 写入后核对每个设备的实际状态。命令和热键共用这一入口，不依赖特定桌面的命令或 设备名称。系统需要提供 udev、logind、polkit 和该内核属性。 mechrevo-control touchpad off mechrevo-control touchpad on mechrevo-control touchpad toggle 查询直接读取内核，不提权。变更由 pkexec 调用 /usr/lib/mechrevo-control/touchpad-helper：活动本地用户可控制自身唯一活动 seat 上的触摸板；远程或非活动会话不获得该权限。该独立策略只授权固定 helper，OEM 设置继续使用原有管理员认证。 状态保存在 root 管理的 /var/lib/mechrevo-touchpad/。设备到达时，由 mechrevo-touchpad-restore@.service 的独立实例恢复状态；休眠恢复时由 /usr/lib/systemd/system-sleep/mechrevo-touchpad 调用同一 helper。 锁保护状态变更，失败会尝试恢复已修改的设备并报告回滚错误。卸载前会重新启用本工具 保存为禁用的触摸板。旧共享目录里的 I2C 状态不自动导入。 on 恢复内核输入事件。桌面自己的触摸板禁用设置独立生效；若使用过旧桌面脚本， 需先把桌面的触摸板设置恢复为启用。设备缺失、缺少内核属性或写入回读失败都会返回 错误。旧工具若已解绑设备，应先用旧工具恢复或重启，再使用新命令。 性能热键 选择一个性能键处理者，避免一次按键切换两次： # TCC profile 与性能灯同步；需要 tccd 才能切换性能档位 systemctl --user enable --now mechrevo-gaming-hotkey.service # 或使用 EC-only；只监听性能键，不处理触摸板键 systemctl --user disable --now mechrevo-gaming-hotkey.service sudo systemctl enable --now mechrevo-ec-hotkey.service 用户服务在 tccd 不可用时仍可处理触摸板热键。安装包不自动启用这两个常驻服务。 EC-only 控制仍限于受支持的设备接口，模式参数和硬件验证范围见 性能档位说明。 安装时仅迁移未修改的 TUXEDO 默认 profile，保留用户参数。五档 GUI 控制需要可信、 有效的 tccd 配置。OEM 应用由受限 helper 执行类型化计划；活动会话使用 auth_admin_keep，非活动会话使用 auth_admin，allow_any=no。授权拒绝或 helper 不可用会作为失败返回。GUI 本身以普通用户运行。 包内容与验证 主要入口为 /usr/bin/mechrevo-console、/usr/bin/mechrevo-console-gui、 /usr/bin/mechrevo-control。两个 helper 安装于各自固定的 /usr/lib/ 目录， 归 root 所有、模式为 0755、无 setuid；polkit 策略为 0644。desktop ID 与 Wayland app ID 均为 best.lmm.mechrevo-console。许可目录保留项目 GPL 和内嵌 Manrope 字体 OFL。 配方检查固定源码、文件类型、desktop 文件、策略的 action/路径/权限，并验证打包后 helper 和策略的字节、权限。安装后运行 pacman -Qkk mechrevo-console，再检查普通 用户 CLI、GUI 和实际硬件结果。以前的验证记录集中在 verification，其中每份记录只对应列出的提交和安装版本。 回滚可用保留的旧安装包执行 sudo pacman -U /path/to/old-package.pkg.tar.zst。 卸载使用 sudo pacman -R mechrevo-console，包管理器保留用户 GUI 偏好。 公开二进制发布 公开的 Arch x86_64 安装包应在干净的官方 Arch 环境构建。C/C++ 使用 -march=x86-64 -mtune=generic，Rust 使用 -C target-cpu=x86-64；检查三个 ELF 的最低 ISA 要求及链接环境。AUR 本机构建尊重用户的 makepkg 设置。 发布附件包含安装包、配方源包、SHA256SUMS、OpenPGP 分离签名和维护者公钥。 从可信渠道核对指纹后验签并检查摘要。源码标签、构建来源和二进制摘要随发布记录保存。

title: 界面设计
body: 机械革命笔记本的 Linux 平台驱动与设备控制台，按机型提供功能。 界面设计 机械革命控制中心使用 Rust / egui 原生界面，共用 Rust 核心处理设备状态与控制事务。布局在 desktop.rs，常用控制在 controls.rs，颜色与字体在 appearance.rs。功能范围见 PRODUCT.md。 信息与视觉层次 首页按使用顺序展示温度与风扇、性能档位、电池保养与屏幕亮度、常用设备控制、设备详情。实时读数和常用操作优先占用空间；数据来源、接口能力与回读说明按需展开。桌面布局的验收目标是在 1280×900 默认窗口中，同时看到五档性能选择、当前运行状态、预览入口、电池保养和屏幕亮度。 界面用石墨黑、暖白和少量暖沙色建立层次。面板通过背景明度、对齐与间距分组；侧栏使用浅层背景标出当前页面。常规面板、导航和档位按钮均无装饰描边，侧栏与正文之间用留白分隔。键盘焦点仍有明确轮廓，错误、忙碌和操作结果保留对应文字。 语义颜色 深色主题 浅色主题 页面背景 #0D0D10 #F7F7F5 面板背景 #17171B #FFFFFE 正文 #F1F1F4 #1E1E20 强调色 #EACFAB #744D26 CPU 读数与曲线采用正文色，GPU 采用琥珀色，并各自保留名称和单位。选中项使用暖色背景与文字共同表达状态。两套主题分别定义正文、次要文字、强调、警告和错误颜色；颜色回归将文字对比度 4.5:1 作为检查门槛。 Manrope 用于拉丁文字和品牌，中文由系统字体补全，运行时不下载字体。温度与风扇读数使用 egui 等宽字体，让相同位数的数值和单位保持位置稳定。背景保持纯色，面板没有纹理或阴影。 布局与响应式行为 布局按实际内容确定高度，保留读数和操作空间。常规面板圆角为 12，标准／紧凑模式内边距为 20／16；面板可用宽度不足 380 时分别降为 16／12。性能区使用开放布局，标题、当前运行档位和选择项直接排列，避免再嵌套一层面板。 性能按钮的列数由区内可用宽度决定：至少 720 时显示五列，480–719 显示三列，300–479 显示两列，更窄时显示一列。按钮最低高度为标准 68、紧凑 60，较长文字可以继续撑高。当前回读档位与待选择目标分别呈现，选项名称和用途保留为辅助技术可读的标签。 温度与风扇区域随真实内容自然增长。宽度达到 680 时，CPU／GPU 读数和对应风扇位于左侧，趋势位于右侧；窄窗改为上下排列。趋势绘图区高 104，区域整体还包含名称、当前值与采样时间。额外传感器、大字体和换行可以增加整体高度，不裁切内容来维持固定卡片尺寸。 默认窗口为 1280×900，最小为 360×280，均为逻辑单位。 可用宽度至少 1060 且高度至少 440 时显示 184 宽侧栏；其余尺寸使用可换行的顶部导航。 导航固定在正文滚动区之外。正文宽度不足 480 时，刷新、自动采样和显示设置移入滚动区，为内容保留可操作空间。 电池／电源与亮度在足够宽的正文中并列，在窄窗中上下排列；所有页面维持纵向滚动，长来源路径允许换行。 概览、控制、传感器、型号目录共用导航和设置。长设备名在标题区省略，悬停和设备详情保留全名；模拟数据始终有明确标识。 数据与控制 CPU／GPU 显示同类当前最高的有效温度，曲线显示对应实际来源的历史。历史按机器身份和传感器来源隔离，每个来源最多 120 点；缺失读数形成断点，重新绘制界面不会新增采样。至少三次有效采样才绘制曲线，横轴使用采样时间。明确标注 CPU 或 GPU 的风扇归入对应组，通用风扇编号独立显示。 自动采样默认开启。启动时只读刷新，此后距上次快照至少 3 秒且后台空闲时更新；待确认预览期间暂停。关闭后显示“手动更新”。界面重绘与硬件采样分别调度，动画设置只控制视觉过渡。 控制入口来自运行时枚举的接口。性能档位、电池、键盘和屏幕亮度都经过选择、预览、显式应用与回读。选择只修改请求目标，当前状态继续显示设备回读值；不可用项显示具体原因。型号目录展示产品资料，实际可控范围由后端能力结果决定，见 OEM 功能覆盖。 共享实现与 Project Z CLI 使用 Project Z 的 zclap = 0.1.4 解析命令。RGB 十六进制处理集中在核心的 color.rs，复用 zhex = 0.1.3。GUI 的 RGB 文本调用 mechrevo_console_core::color::format_rgb_hex，与其他前端共用格式规则。 GUI 的窗口、布局、绘制和输入继续由 egui / eframe 提供，设备能力与事务继续走共用核心。依赖版本见各 crate 的 Cargo.toml 与工作区 Cargo.lock；共享能力的接入位置与界面框架分别记录。 事务与偏好 启动和读取状态使用普通用户权限。需要授权的操作在显式应用后请求授权，后台重新核对接口、目标范围、绑定与原值。切换目标或手动刷新会作废旧计划，每份计划只使用一次。 写入、回读或必要恢复尚未结束时，窗口保持打开并显示进度。失败时保留原始错误和回读／恢复结果；状态未知时继续阻止后续写入与关闭，不自动重放操作。界面通过单个后台任务执行设备调用，重复刷新不堆积任务。 主题、80–160% 文字缩放、标准／紧凑显示、自动采样和动画偏好保存在 eframe 用户配置目录。操作计划与温度历史只保留在当前进程中。 验收依据 布局回归覆盖深浅主题、窄窗、大字体、DPI、长文本、键盘导航、底部可达性、未知读数及预览／应用隔离。完整桌面场景同时提供五档性能、充电、屏幕亮度、CPU／GPU 温度和双风扇数据，检查首屏入口与同排档位，并通过真实点击验证请求目标和当前值仍分别保存。 软件渲染图用于检查 egui 内容，原生窗口截图用于核对实际窗口、字体与交互。截图流程见 视觉验收。模拟数据只用于独立预览和测试；硬件写入、实体灯光、噪声以及各平台兼容性分别记录实机结果。本设计文档说明实现约定与检查范围，具体执行结果以对应验收记录为准。

title: 概览
body: 组合终端、shell、应用配置与内存管理，提供 Linux 工作环境。 oh-my-ztty 基于 Project Z 的 Linux 工作环境：ztty + zshard + zrc + zdot + zfetch + ssmcp + zmem。系统 zsh 负责执行命令，套件统一终端、编辑器和常用工具的配置。 官网 · English · 安装说明 · 配置与恢复 · 性能记录 · 0.2.1 实机报告 原生 Tab 补全覆盖套件组件、Codex／Claude／Gemini／OpenCode／pi／Amp、Go／Rust／Node 开发命令，以及 Project Z 等自研 CLI；Git、uv、Cargo 等复用已安装的系统补全。支持多级命令、参数取值与中文路径，个人补全规则优先。详见补全说明与覆盖清单。 安装 用户级发行包 先下载并查看安装脚本，再执行： curl -fLO https://github.com/LIghtJUNction/oh-my-ztty/releases/latest/download/install.sh sh install.sh ~/.local/bin/omztty shell 支持 Linux x86_64、ARM64。系统需提供 zsh 5.9+；图形终端使用 X11/XWayland，正式构建在 Ubuntu 24.04 验证。安装包包含七个 Project Z 组件的运行程序或原生配置，终端套件按用户安装，默认通过 sudo 将 zmem 安装为系统内存管理器。使用 --no-memory-manager 可跳过系统设置；重复安装会记住该选择，无需在安装时配置 Rust 或 Python。使用编辑器配置需要另行安装 Neovim 0.11+；日常运行和配置部署也不需要 Rust 或 Python。 Arch Linux（AUR） 通过 AUR 助手安装 oh-my-ztty-bin： yay -S oh-my-ztty-bin omztty doctor 系统软件包通过 AUR 助手更新，配置采用仍需执行下方命令。卸载软件包前，先运行 omztty config remove 恢复原配置，再通过包管理器移除软件包。未使用 AUR 助手时，可按安装说明使用 makepkg 安装。 七个独立项目 项目 作用 ztty 原生终端 zshard zsh 框架，提供补全、历史建议、命令高亮和延迟加载插件 zrc Neovim 与常用终端工具的原生配置，共用暖色 Ink 外观 zdot no_std 配置管理工具，预览、部署链接、备份和恢复，并显式执行 Git 同步 zfetch 零 crate 依赖的原生 no_std 系统概况工具，按需运行 ssmcp 按需把工作区接入 AI 的 MCP 工具 zmem 默认系统内存与 Swap 管理器，提供压力观测、后台任务约束和自适应交换空间 开发时同步各组件默认分支的最新源码，Git 子模块与 dependencies.lock.json 共同记录本次构建选用的提交。0.2.6 发布记录保留该已发布版本的组件组合与验收结果。zsh、Neovim 等系统应用需单独安装。进入 shell 后，可按需查看系统概况或启动 AI 连接。zfetch 的 Arch Linux 包名为 zfetch-project-z 与 zfetch-project-z-bin，发布状态见其仓库说明。 默认内存管理 安装器默认启用 zmem 系统服务，接管现有 Swap，把初始方案保存到 /etc/zmem/zmem.conf，后续升级保留本机配置。查看状态和策略，或把编译任务纳入后台管理： omztty memory status --json --processes omztty memory plan --json omztty memory run --class background -- cargo build omztty memory setup 可在跳过初次设置后启用 zmem；omztty memory rollback 恢复接管前记录的管理器与配置。系统服务运行 root 所有的 /usr/local/bin/zmem，独立于用户目录中的套件。卸载终端套件会保留系统内存服务；已卸载后仍可用 sudo /usr/local/bin/zmem rollback 恢复。默认参数和命令见内存管理说明。 Ink 默认外观 暖石墨背景、亚麻白文字、铜色重点、28 px 内边距与两行提示符，把路径、Git 分支和输入区分开。Neovim 与终端工具沿用同一套配色。提示符使用 zsh 内置能力；字体通过 Fontconfig 回退，不强制安装图标字体。自定义预设。 实机报告记录了 Ink 配置、桌面启动链、broker 复用、恢复步骤与验收范围。 设为默认工作环境 Shell、环境变量与 PATH omztty setup 引导初始化、接入现有 zsh rc，并按选择在本人 GitHub 账号下创建私有 dotfiles 仓库。也可以先只在本机使用： omztty setup --local --install-rc omztty env set EDITOR nvim --shared omztty env set PROJECT_ENDPOINT https://example.invalid omztty env list # 默认隐藏值 omztty path add ~/.local/bin omztty path add ~/tools/bin --append omztty path move ~/tools/bin first omztty path list --effective omztty rc add 10-aliases omztty rc edit 10-aliases omztty rc check omztty rc status # 打印位置和当前 zsh 的重载命令 共享配置集中在 ~/.config/oh-my-ztty/profile/shell/，机器专用变量默认保存在 ~/.config/oh-my-ztty/local/env.tsv。env file、path file、rc file NAME 显示准确路径；可以使用对应的 edit 命令或直接编辑文本文件。PATH 保存的是有序规则，~/ 在各台机器上按自己的 HOME 展开。 未启用 Git 时，修改前保存本地文件版本，可用 rc backups 和 rc restore ID 恢复。Profile 启用独立 Git 后停止生成这些快照，共享 shell 修改自动形成本地提交；用 sync history 和 sync restore REV [PATH] 查看、恢复，用 sync push 明确上传。机器专用变量留在 Git 外。同步会检查文本类型和允许路径，拒绝二进制文件。 omztty setup --repo dotfiles # 确认后创建本人的私有仓库 omztty sync status omztty sync push omztty update --config-only # 只拉取个人配置 omztty update --with-config # 拉取个人配置，再更新套件 GitHub 引导需要 gh auth login --hostname github.com，Git 提交需要已配置的 user.name、user.email。完整教程见 Shell 与环境变量和私有配置同步。 应用配置 先准备可编辑配置并查看部署计划，再备份已有文件、应用链接： omztty config init omztty config plan --json omztty config apply --backup omztty config status 统一配置覆盖 zsh、ztty、Neovim、Kitty、Foot、Ghostty、tmux、fzf、bat、ripgrep 和 Git 显示设置；应用程序本身单独安装。Git 配色通过配置说明中的显式 include 启用。采用配置后重新打开终端，账户的登录 shell 记录保持原值。 编辑源文件位于 ~/.config/oh-my-ztty/profile/，个人 shell 片段放在 profile/shell/rc.d/，个人补全放在 ~/.config/oh-my-ztty/completions/；已有的 local.zsh 仍会加载。对应 XDG 配置可改变这些位置；HOME 配置部署要求 XDG_CONFIG_HOME 位于 HOME 内。 升级后运行 omztty config refresh，即可更新尚未自行修改的默认文件；个人编辑、新增文件和主动删除的文件会保留。omztty config remove 恢复采用配置前保存的文件。用户级安装的 omztty uninstall 会先恢复这个受管理的 profile；恢复失败时保留运行程序供修复。通过 omztty dot 部署的其他仓库独立管理。完整位置与恢复步骤见配置说明。 常用命令 omztty terminal # 用 ztty 打开预设 shell omztty shell # 在当前终端体验 omztty info # 按需运行 zfetch，显示系统概况 omztty zfetch # 直接运行套件中的 zfetch omztty doctor # 检查组件、系统依赖和 zmem 服务 omztty memory # 查看内存压力和 Swap omztty config audit # 检查统一配置及已知旧 shell 框架位置 omztty ai context # 输出明确选择的 shell 上下文 omztty ai connect # 在当前工作区启动 ssmcp omztty update # 更新用户级安装 omztty uninstall # 先恢复配置，再卸载用户级安装 AI 建议的命令先进入输入行，由人确认执行。个人配置、补全与历史位于发行版目录之外，更新或卸载时保留。 当前源码构建还可通过 zfetch 查看启动链中的服务与配置路径： omztty info --boot # 查看启动服务和配置文件位置 omztty info --boot --json # 以 JSON 输出同一启动链 一起迭代 git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/LIghtJUNction/oh-my-ztty.git cd oh-my-ztty python3 scripts/workspace.py status python3 scripts/workspace.py sync python3 scripts/workspace.py check python3 scripts/build_bundle.py sync 默认获取七个组件的最新默认分支，并在 schema 2 源码锁中记录提交与观测时间。旧锁首次升级需要完整同步；此后可用 sync zshard 单独更新一个组件。打包时通过 Cargo --locked 从记录的源码编译五个原生程序，沿用已有的共享构建目录配置。 开发、测试和显式发布步骤见 CONTRIBUTING.md。性能数字与测量范围见性能记录。项目采用 MIT 许可证。

title: oh-my-ztty
body: 组合终端、shell、应用配置与内存管理，提供 Linux 工作环境。 oh-my-ztty A lean Linux terminal setup built on Project Z: ztty + zsh + zshard + zrc + zdot + zfetch + ssmcp + zmem. Website · 中文 · Install guide · Performance · 0.2.1 workstation report Install Per-user release Download and inspect the installer, then run it: curl -fLO https://github.com/LIghtJUNction/oh-my-ztty/releases/latest/download/install.sh sh install.sh ~/.local/bin/omztty shell Linux x86_64 and ARM64. Requires system zsh; the graphical terminal uses X11/fontconfig. The bundle includes the Project Z components and a native application configuration profile. The terminal suite installs per user. By default, the installer also uses sudo to set up zmem as the system memory manager; use --no-memory-manager for a per-user-only install. Installation is repeatable. Your login shell and existing tools remain available. Runtime and configuration commands need no Rust or Python. Arch Linux (AUR) Install the oh-my-ztty-bin package with an AUR helper: yay -S oh-my-ztty-bin omztty doctor Use your AUR helper to upgrade the system package. Configuration adoption remains explicit through the commands below. Before removing the package, run omztty config remove to restore adopted configurations, then remove it with your package manager. Installation guide includes the makepkg route. The suite Component Job ztty Native terminal zshard Original zsh framework: completion, suggestions, highlighting and lazy plugins zrc Native Neovim and terminal-tool configuration with one warm Ink palette zdot no_std dotfiles manager with plans, reversible links and explicit Git sync zfetch On-demand native system overview, zero crate dependencies ssmcp On-demand MCP workspace connection for AI zmem System memory pressure, managed background jobs and adaptive Swap Development follows each component's latest default branch. Git submodules and dependencies.lock.json record the exact sources selected for a build. The 0.2.6 release record describes the already published combination. Your Linux distribution supplies zsh. See the completion reference for command and version coverage. System memory zmem is the default memory and Swap manager. The installer adopts existing Swap, enables its system service and keeps local policy in /etc/zmem/zmem.conf. Subsequent installs preserve that configuration. omztty memory status --json --processes omztty memory plan --json omztty memory run --class background -- cargo build omztty memory rollback Use omztty memory setup to enable the bundled manager later. System setup copies zmem to root-owned /usr/local/bin/zmem; the service continues independently of the terminal suite. Memory policy and recovery explain defaults, workload classes and skipped setup. Ink preset A warm graphite, linen and copper palette, generous spacing and a two-line prompt with the path, cached Git branch and command status. The prompt uses zsh builtins; installed fonts fall back through Fontconfig. Customize the preset. The workstation report records the deployed Ink configuration, desktop launch chain, broker reuse, recovery steps and acceptance scope. Make it your default workspace Shell settings and private sync omztty setup guides local initialization, an optional zsh startup hook and a private dotfiles repository under your own GitHub account. Start locally with: omztty setup --local --install-rc omztty env set EDITOR nvim --shared omztty env set PROJECT_ENDPOINT https://example.invalid omztty env list omztty path add ~/.local/bin omztty path add ~/tools/bin --append omztty rc add 10-aliases omztty rc edit 10-aliases omztty rc check omztty rc status Shared data and zsh snippets live in ~/.config/oh-my-ztty/profile/shell/; machine-only environment values default to ~/.config/oh-my-ztty/local/env.tsv. Values are hidden in lists. The env file, path file and rc file NAME commands print their locations, and the corresponding edit commands validate manual changes. PATH rules keep their order and expand ~/ for each machine. Before Git is enabled, rc backups and rc restore ID manage local file versions. An independent profile Git repository switches shared shell changes to local commits and stops new snapshots. Use sync history, sync restore REV [PATH] and an explicit sync push; machine-only values stay outside Git. Synchronization accepts allowed text configuration and rejects binary files. omztty setup --repo dotfiles omztty sync status omztty sync push omztty update --config-only omztty update --with-config GitHub setup needs gh auth login --hostname github.com; commits need your Git user.name and user.email. Read the shell guide and private sync guide for command examples, file formats and recovery. Application configuration omztty config init omztty config plan --json omztty config apply --backup One editable profile manages zsh, ztty, Neovim, Kitty, Foot, Ghostty, tmux, fzf, bat, ripgrep and Git display settings. Existing configurations are backed up by zdot. After upgrading, run omztty config refresh to update defaults you have not changed; your edits and deliberately removed files are preserved. Configuration and recovery explains the native editor, application coverage and file locations. Everyday commands omztty terminal # Open ztty with the suite's zsh configuration omztty shell # Try the shell in your current terminal omztty info # Native system overview omztty doctor # Check binaries, system dependencies and zmem service omztty memory # Inspect memory pressure and Swap omztty ai context # Emit explicit shell context omztty ai connect # Start ssmcp in your workspace omztty dot plan --root ~/dotfiles --target "$HOME" # Preview dotfile changes omztty update # Update a per-user installation omztty uninstall # Restore configs and remove a per-user installation AI-generated commands are reviewed in the shell input line before execution. The suite does not start an AI model or resident agent at shell startup. Current source builds also expose startup inspection through zfetch: omztty info --boot # Inspect startup services and configuration paths omztty info --boot --json # Read the same startup chain as JSON Develop together git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/LIghtJUNction/oh-my-ztty.git cd oh-my-ztty python3 scripts/workspace.py status python3 scripts/workspace.py sync python3 scripts/workspace.py check python3 scripts/build_bundle.py sync fetches all seven default branches and records their commits and observation times in the schema 2 source lock. After the first full synchronization, sync zshard updates one component. The bundle compiles all five native programs from those sources with Cargo's --locked option and respects the configured shared target directory. Development and release guide covers local checks, source updates and explicit version publication. Architecture describes the runtime boundaries and extension interfaces. MIT license. Performance claims and their measurement conditions belong together; see the benchmark record.

title: Installation
body: 组合终端、shell、应用配置与内存管理，提供 Linux 工作环境。 Installation Choose a per-user release installation or the Arch Linux package. Both provide the same suite commands; use the matching update and removal instructions below. The bundle includes the terminal, shell framework and configuration tools. You need system zsh and the libraries listed below. Installing a release and managing its configuration require neither Rust nor Python. Requirements Requirement Supported configuration Operating system Linux x86_64 or ARM64 Shell System zsh 5.9 or newer Default memory manager Linux cgroup v2, systemd, util-linux and administrator access; Btrfs also uses btrfs-progs Optional editor profile Neovim 0.11 or newer, installed separately Private GitHub profile sync Git and the optional GitHub CLI (gh) Graphical terminal session X11 or XWayland Graphics libraries X11, Xrender, Xft, Fontconfig, Wayland, xkbcommon, FreeType, HarfBuzz, EGL and GLES Binary ABI glibc 2.34 or newer and libgcc for ztty and ssmcp The ztty 0.5.2 binary needs the listed graphics libraries even when you select the X11 backend. The release workflow targets Ubuntu 24.04 for both architectures. Other distributions also need compatible libraries. Install Neovim, other applications and language servers separately when you want to use their profiles. On Ubuntu 24.04, install the basic dependencies with: sudo apt-get install zsh git curl libx11-6 libxrender1 libxft2 libfontconfig1 \ libwayland-client0 libwayland-egl1 libwayland-cursor0 libxkbcommon0 \ libfreetype6 libharfbuzz0b libegl1 libgles2 libgcc-s1 Arch Linux (AUR) Install the oh-my-ztty-bin package with an AUR helper: yay -S oh-my-ztty-bin omztty doctor omztty shell With Git and Arch's base-devel tools installed, the package can also be built directly: git clone https://aur.archlinux.org/oh-my-ztty-bin.git cd oh-my-ztty-bin makepkg -si The package installs prebuilt release binaries under /usr/lib/oh-my-ztty and provides /usr/bin/omztty. Update it through your AUR helper: yay -Syu oh-my-ztty-bin If you adopted the application profile, run omztty config refresh after upgrading. This updates defaults you have not changed. Use the package manager to remove the runtime; omztty update and omztty uninstall are for per-user installations. If an older per-user installation is also on your PATH, use /usr/bin/omztty to select the package explicitly. Restore adopted configurations before removing the package: omztty config remove sudo pacman -R oh-my-ztty-bin Install a release Use the installer to keep the suite under your own account. Download it as a file, then run it: curl -fLO https://github.com/LIghtJUNction/oh-my-ztty/releases/latest/download/install.sh sh install.sh ~/.local/bin/omztty doctor The installer downloads the archive for your architecture, verifies its SHA-256 and file manifest, then installs under ${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/oh-my-ztty. Commands go into ~/.local/bin by default. You can use the absolute launcher path to initialize configuration and save its PATH entry: ~/.local/bin/omztty setup --local ~/.local/bin/omztty path add "$HOME/.local/bin" ~/.local/bin/omztty rc install Open a new zsh session to load it. For the current shell, add the directory once: export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH" An unrelated existing omztty executable stops installation. Existing tools with other names are preserved; the omztty launcher selects its bundled components explicitly. System memory manager The release installer enables zmem by default using sudo. zmem adopts existing Swap, installs a root-owned executable at /usr/local/bin/zmem, and keeps the system policy in /etc/zmem/zmem.conf. Existing configuration is preserved during upgrades. omztty memory status --json --processes omztty memory plan --json omztty memory run --class background -- cargo build For a per-user-only install or a machine without systemd, run sh install.sh --no-memory-manager. This skips system setup and remembers the choice on subsequent updates. It leaves an existing manager running. omztty memory setup enables the bundled zmem immediately; omztty update --memory-manager also records the choice for future updates. Use omztty memory rollback to restore the previous managers and configuration. The system service remains installed when the per-user terminal suite is removed; its independent recovery command is sudo /usr/local/bin/zmem rollback. See memory policy and recovery for defaults, workload classes and AI output. Start the environment Open a configured zsh session in your current terminal: omztty shell Type exit to return to your previous shell. To open the same setup in a new ztty window: omztty terminal Both commands use the suite's configuration for that session. Adopt the application profile below to link its settings into your home directory. Your account's login shell is unchanged. Set up your own shell settings Run the setup wizard after installation: omztty setup It prepares the standard profile, offers to connect your ordinary zsh startup file and can create a private GitHub dotfiles repository under your signed-in account. The remote step is optional; omztty setup --local prepares local configuration without it. Manage settings directly from the command line: omztty env set EDITOR nvim --shared omztty path add "$HOME/.local/bin" omztty rc add aliases omztty rc edit aliases omztty rc check The shell guide explains the values, file paths, manual editing and version history. The dotfiles guide covers private synchronization and restoring configuration on another machine. Once the profile has its own Git repository, shared shell changes made by these commands become local commits. Run omztty sync history to inspect them and omztty sync push when you want to upload them. Git mode stops new file snapshots; machine-specific values and the home rc startup block remain local. Adopt the default workspace The optional profile adds the suite's zsh, terminal and editor defaults to your home configuration. Create it, inspect the planned changes, then apply it: omztty config init omztty config plan --json omztty config apply --backup omztty config status --backup saves existing files before replacing them with managed links. omztty config remove restores those originals. The configuration guide explains each profile, personal settings and the optional Git display include. Open a new zsh session after adoption. Editable files live under ${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/oh-my-ztty/profile. The journal and backups live under ${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/zdot/oh-my-ztty. HOME adoption requires an absolute XDG_CONFIG_HOME within HOME; roots outside HOME are rejected. Suite upgrades preserve the editable profile. Run omztty config refresh after upgrading to update files that still match their shipped defaults. Custom edits, added files and deliberately removed files are preserved. Personal completion files belong in ${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/oh-my-ztty/completions/. The preset registers that directory for on-demand loading. It stays outside the runtime and survives updates and uninstallation. System overview Run omztty info to display system information through the bundled zfetch utility. omztty zfetch invokes the same tool directly. The shell does not run it automatically. Install options Choose another absolute command directory or omit the desktop entry: sh install.sh --bin-dir "$HOME/bin" --no-desktop A new installation creates a desktop entry by default. --no-desktop disables it; --desktop enables it again. When neither option is supplied, repeat installations and updates preserve the last successful choice. Disabling an existing installation removes only desktop links that still point to this suite. Replacement files and foreign links are preserved. Enabling the entry stops if an unrelated file or link already occupies its path. Personal shell configuration belongs outside the release directory. See configuration before adding aliases, themes or plugins. Offline installation Download an archive and its matching .sha256 file from the same published release. The x86_64 example below uses this release. sh install.sh --from ./oh-my-ztty-0.2.13-linux-x86_64.tar.gz Use the aarch64 archive on ARM64. If you have already obtained the digest from the release record, the installer's --sha256 option can supply it instead of a sidecar file. Update or reinstall For a per-user installation: omztty update To update the profile from your own configured Git repository, select a configuration update explicitly: omztty update --config-only omztty update --with-config --config-only pulls the profile without changing the runtime. --with-config updates a per-user suite and pulls its profile. The profile must have a clean Git working tree and a fast-forward update available. Use omztty sync status to inspect local edits first. If you adopted a home profile, run omztty config refresh after updating to receive changes to unmodified shipped defaults. Upgrade the AUR runtime through your AUR helper; its profile can still be updated with omztty update --config-only. To change the desktop entry choice during an update, select one option: omztty update --no-desktop omztty update --desktop Updates retain the desktop-entry choice saved by your last successful installation. Either option above changes that choice after the update succeeds. Each version has its own directory. A current link selects the active version, and completion caches are separated by release. Before activation, the installer prepares an audited completion cache. A failed preparation leaves the previous version active. Reinstalling the same archive verifies the existing files; it preserves and reports an installed version that has been modified. Uninstall For a per-user installation: omztty uninstall Uninstallation restores the adopted omztty config home profile before removing the runtime. Failed restoration or inconsistent deployment records preserve the installation for recovery. After restoration, suite-owned installation files and links are removed; personal profiles, additions, completion files and history are retained. Independent repositories deployed through omztty dot have a separate lifecycle. Use zdot remove first if you also want to restore those deployments.

title: Configuration
body: 组合终端、shell、应用配置与内存管理，提供 Linux 工作环境。 Configuration Keep your shell, editor and terminal-tool settings in one editable profile. omztty config copies the included defaults into your configuration directory and links them into place, with backups for existing files. The included Ink profile comes from zrc. zdot handles the file links and restoration; you edit the application files directly. Set up shell configuration Run omztty setup for the guided setup, or omztty setup --local to prepare local configuration. The wizard can connect your existing zsh startup file and create a private dotfiles repository under your own GitHub account. Use the command line for everyday settings: omztty env set EDITOR nvim --shared omztty path add "$HOME/.local/bin" omztty rc add aliases omztty rc edit aliases omztty rc check The shell, PATH and environment guide explains each command, the exact file locations, manual editing, version history and when changes take effect. Adopting the complete application profile below is a separate choice. Adopt the defaults omztty config init omztty config plan --json omztty config apply --backup omztty config status Open a new zsh session after adoption. Your account's login shell is unchanged. --backup saves existing application configurations so you can restore them with omztty config remove. The profile covers zsh, ztty, Neovim, Kitty, Foot, Ghostty, tmux, fzf, bat, ripgrep and Git display settings. Application installation is separate. Location Purpose ~/.config/oh-my-ztty/profile/ Shared profile repository, application files and profile.zdot ~/.config/oh-my-ztty/profile/shell/env.tsv Shared environment values ~/.config/oh-my-ztty/profile/shell/path.tsv Ordered, portable PATH rules ~/.config/oh-my-ztty/profile/shell/rc.d/ Shared zsh snippets ~/.config/oh-my-ztty/local/env.tsv Machine-specific environment values, outside profile sync ~/.config/oh-my-ztty/options.zsh Local options read before zshard initializes ~/.config/oh-my-ztty/local.zsh Existing local shell additions ~/.local/state/oh-my-ztty/backups/ File snapshots created before profile Git is enabled ~/.local/state/zdot/oh-my-ztty/ Application deployment journal and original files ~/.local/state/oh-my-ztty/history Interactive shell history ~/.config/oh-my-ztty/completions/ Personal completion files loaded on demand The corresponding XDG variables change these roots; XDG_CONFIG_HOME must be inside HOME for a home deployment. omztty config path prints the profile directory. Repeating init and updating the suite preserve the editable profile. Print the actual paths with omztty env file, omztty env file --shared, omztty path file and omztty rc file NAME. Open them through env edit, path edit or rc edit NAME, or use your editor directly. Keep the data-file format intact and run omztty rc check after manual edits. When the profile has its own Git repository, shared shell edits made through the CLI create local commits. They are pushed only on request. Use omztty sync history to review those commits and omztty sync restore COMMIT [PATH] to restore shared shell configuration or a selected profile file. Git identity must be configured before a managed shared edit; otherwise the edit stops before writing. Before Git is enabled, omztty rc backups and omztty rc restore BACKUP_ID manage local file snapshots. Enabling profile Git stops new snapshots, including for machine-specific variables and the ordinary home rc file; those local files stay outside Git. Existing snapshots are retained locally. In Git mode, the rc backup commands direct you to Git history and restore. Refresh defaults after an upgrade Update the suite with omztty update for a per-user installation, or yay -Syu oh-my-ztty-bin for the AUR package. Then refresh its defaults: omztty config refresh refresh updates a file only when it still matches the default from the profile's recorded suite version. It lists the paths it updates or preserves. Your edits, removed files, source symlinks, extra personal files and deployment mappings stay in place. Restart the affected application to load the new configuration. The profile keeps a verified reference copy of shipped defaults in .baseline/. That reference contains no personal edits and is replaced after a successful refresh. It lets refresh work after a system package replaces the runtime or an old release directory is removed. Older profiles without a baseline copy need their recorded installed release for the first refresh. Keep that release until refresh succeeds. A missing, modified or mismatched baseline stops the command before it changes the profile. Running it again at the same version does nothing. A change to the default file layout or mappings requires a profile review and is rejected without edits. Neovim Install Neovim 0.11 or newer separately, then run nvim for the Ink welcome page or open a file normally. The editor has a native status line, diagnostics, a project picker and a searchable shortcut panel. It needs no plugin bootstrap, download or patched icon font. Key Action Space ? Search the shortcut panel Space f f Find a project file Space f g Search project text Space f r Recent files Space b b Open buffers Space e File explorer Space w Save Space c a Language-server code actions Space c r Rename a symbol Space c f Format the current buffer Space d Diagnostics Space a c Inspect explicit local AI context Language servers start for relevant project files when their executables are already installed. Existing Mason executables are recognized. The welcome page starts no server. Large files disable costly features; project search runs on request with bounded output and a timeout. The zrc repository documents supported servers, local extensions, the palette and the module registry. Personal settings Edit linked application files normally or use the source under the profile directory. The suite reads local.zsh after common shell defaults. Git's module contains display settings only. Activate it once if desired: git config --global --add include.path "${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/zrc/git.inc" Identity, credentials and signing settings remain in the user's existing Git configuration. omztty setup can help create a private profile repository under your own GitHub account. Synchronization runs when you request it: omztty sync status omztty sync pull omztty sync push omztty config sync is an alias for these profile-sync commands. omztty update --config-only updates your configured profile repository; omztty update --with-config updates both a per-user suite installation and its profile repository. Plain omztty update updates the suite. Local variables, shell history and existing restoration records remain outside the profile repository. Shared shell edits use Git commits once profile Git is enabled; manual edits can be reviewed and committed by omztty sync push. Restore and maintain omztty config audit omztty config remove remove uses the saved manifest, checks link ownership and restores originals. A destination replaced outside zdot is preserved and reported. To change manifest mappings, remove the deployment, edit the manifest and apply it again. For a per-user installation, omztty uninstall restores this adopted home profile first. A restoration failure preserves the installed runtime for recovery. For the AUR package, run omztty config remove before sudo pacman -R oh-my-ztty-bin; package removal leaves home files in place. Other deployments made through omztty dot remain independently managed. Configuration files Create files below ${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/oh-my-ztty: File Load order Use options.zsh Before zshard initializes Keymap, completion and other startup options local.zsh After zshard and the default theme Aliases, plugins, custom themes and AI provider configuration Both files are optional. The installer and uninstaller preserve them. Startup options For example, put these settings in options.zsh: ZSHARD_KEYMAP=vi ZSHARD_COMPLETION=lazy ZSHARD_HISTORY_SCAN=200 Option Default in the suite Other choices ZSHARD_KEYMAP emacs vi ZSHARD_COMPLETION lazy eager, off ZSHARD_SUGGESTIONS 1 0 disables history suggestions ZSHARD_HISTORY_SCAN 200 Bound the number of inspected history events ZSHARD_HIGHLIGHT 1 0 disables first-command-token highlighting ZSHARD_SHELL_INTEGRATION 1 0 disables OSC 7 / OSC 133 integration Highlighting recognizes the first command token. It is not a full shell grammar checker. At the end of the input buffer, Right or Ctrl-F accepts a history suggestion; otherwise the keys move forward normally. Completion Press Tab after a command, an option or a partial value. The suite provides native zsh completion for its tools and their omztty entrypoints. Command Completion ssmcp Client 0.10.20 commands and options, including local, --account-compat and 007 upgrade ztty, omztty ztty ztty 0.5.2 launch options and control commands, including reload --binary omztty terminal Preset launch options, paths, and command completion after -e or -- zdot Deployment commands, synchronization actions and repository paths zfetch 0.1.1 output format and color options. The last format flag selects the output zshard Plugin actions, locally installed plugin names, hooks and completion directories zai AI actions and ssmcp arguments after connect omztty Suite commands and their nested component arguments For example, type ssmcp --theme n and press Tab to complete nord. Try ssmcp sessions lo, zshard plugin ver, or ztty -e git checko for nested commands. omztty ai connect, zai connect and zshard ai connect all share the ssmcp completion. Completion uses local command definitions and filesystem entries. It starts no component program and makes no relay request; enter remote client identifiers, session names and account values explicitly. The ssmcp definitions match the client's pinned release in dependencies.lock.json. Personal _command files in ${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/oh-my-ztty/completions/ take precedence over included definitions, in both lazy and eager modes. Open a new suite shell after adding one. Existing system completions, including Git, remain available. The per-user installer prepares an audited completion cache. The default lazy mode loads it on the first Tab; adding or changing completion inputs triggers normal revalidation. Use ZSHARD_COMPLETION=eager in options.zsh to initialize at startup, or off to disable completion. AI, development and author tools The suite also ships these native definitions. Completion definitions do not install the external applications. Family Commands AI clients codex, claude, gemini, opencode, pi, amp Developer tools go, npx, yarn, rustc, rustup, node, cmake Project Z services and input zcalld, ssmcpd, ztype, zuse Project Z desktop and game tools zmcl, onim, lmm, mechrevo-console Other author tools wgt, douyin, lightjunction, coolapk, binance-cli Try codex exec --sandbox work<Tab>, claude mcp add demo --transport ht<Tab>, go mod ti<Tab>, rustc -C panic=ab<Tab>, or zcalld library mcp apply --agent gem<Tab>. Prompt text and remote identifiers stay free text. Options that require directories exclude ordinary files, including when paths contain spaces or non-ASCII characters. Git, uv, Cargo, npm, pnpm, Bun, Python/pip, container tools and ordinary shell utilities retain their installed system completion definitions. Coverage depends on the corresponding completion package being installed. Rust uses the commands rustc, cargo and rustup; there is no generic rust command to register. Distribution definitions and commands delegated after -- may perform their own local discovery. The bundled definitions read local paths and static command grammar. They do not query AI accounts, relays, cloud APIs, game services or hardware for candidates. Personal definitions still take priority. Version targets and extension instructions are in the completion reference. Aliases and plugins Create a shared snippet with omztty rc add aliases, then open it with omztty rc edit aliases. For example: alias ll='ls -alF' if (( $+functions[zshard] )); then zshard load "$ZSHARD_HOME/examples/hello.plugin.zsh" fi Run omztty rc check after editing and open a new shell. The condition loads the plugin in sessions where zshard is initialized, including the preset suite shell. Existing aliases and plugin loading in local.zsh continue to work locally. The included hello plugin is a working example with a command, a hook and cleanup. See plugins for loading modes and pinned remote installations. Prompt selection The default Ink preset separates the path and cached Git branch from the input line. It also shows nonzero exit status and commands lasting at least two seconds. Its callback runs with zsh builtins. To use zshard's own minimal prompt, add this to options.zsh: OMZTTY_THEME=framework A custom zshard theme registration in local.zsh runs after Ink and replaces its callback. The callback receives the previous exit status and elapsed whole seconds, then assigns PROMPT and RPROMPT. For a custom theme with terminal integration, follow the zero-width OSC boundary handling in the actual Ink implementation. ZSHARD_PROMPT=off leaves prompt variables alone. State and cache The launcher sets these suite-specific locations, using XDG defaults when the environment variables are absent: Data Location History $XDG_STATE_HOME/oh-my-ztty/history Completion cache $XDG_CACHE_HOME/oh-my-ztty/zshard/<release-directory> Personal configuration $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/oh-my-ztty The usual XDG fallbacks are ~/.local/state, ~/.cache and ~/.config. The release-specific cache lets different installed versions retain their matching completion inputs. Terminal sessions The terminal launcher uses a suite-specific broker socket, @oh-my-ztty-<uid>-<suite-version>. Set OMZTTY_SOCKET when you explicitly want a different socket. The default terminal configuration requests a 13 pt font and 28 px padding. Fontconfig chooses among installed font families; personal Fontconfig rules can change the resolved font. The prompt does not require private-use icon glyphs. See the full zshard option reference and AI provider configuration.

title: Shell, PATH and environment
body: 组合终端、shell、应用配置与内存管理，提供 Linux 工作环境。 Shell, PATH and environment Use omztty to keep your zsh settings in a predictable directory and change them from the command line. Shared settings live in your profile. Once you enable Git for that profile, shared shell changes are recorded as local commits and you choose when to push them. Start with setup omztty setup The wizard prepares your profile, offers to connect it to your existing zsh startup file, and can help create a private dotfiles repository under your own GitHub account. It shows the configuration location and asks before the optional steps. GitHub synchronization uses the optional gh command and its existing login. For a local setup without a GitHub repository: omztty setup --local omztty shell omztty shell loads the settings in a new preset zsh session. To load the same settings when your ordinary zsh starts, preview and install its startup block: omztty rc install --dry-run omztty rc install The block goes into $ZDOTDIR/.zshrc when ZDOTDIR is set, otherwise ~/.zshrc. Existing startup code remains in place. Repeating installation keeps one block. This integration manages zsh; it does not change your account's login shell. Manage environment variables An environment variable is a named value that a shell passes to programs it starts. For example, tools use EDITOR to choose an editor. Setting a value in the profile makes it available to future shell sessions. omztty env set EDITOR nvim --shared omztty env set API_BASE_URL https://api.example.invalid omztty env list omztty env get EDITOR set saves a variable locally by default. Add --shared when the value belongs on your other machines and may be committed to your private profile repository. A local value overrides a shared value with the same name. list shows names and their sources; get NAME or list --show displays values explicitly. omztty env list --show omztty env unset API_BASE_URL omztty env unset EDITOR --shared unset removes the saved definition from the selected scope. A shared value or a value inherited from the parent session can still exist. Start a fresh shell to check the resulting environment. Shell quoting still applies when you enter a command. Quote spaces and use single quotes when dollar signs or command-looking text must remain literal: omztty env set PROJECT_LABEL 'work laptop' omztty env set EXAMPLE_TEXT 'literal $HOME, not an expansion' The stored value is data. The loader does not execute it as shell code. Use the dedicated PATH commands below to manage command-search directories. Manage PATH PATH is an ordered list of directories. When you type a command name, the shell looks through that list from left to right. A directory placed first takes priority over later directories containing the same command. omztty path add "$HOME/.local/bin" omztty path add "$HOME/dev tools/bin" --append omztty path list The default placement is at the front. --append places a directory after the inherited PATH. Only your chosen directory rules are saved: temporary virtual-environment and toolchain entries from the current process are not copied into the profile. Change a saved directory's priority or remove its rule: omztty path move "$HOME/dev tools/bin" first omztty path move "$HOME/.local/bin" last omztty path remove "$HOME/dev tools/bin" The same directory is not added repeatedly when a shell loads the settings again. Paths under your home directory are stored in portable form so another machine can expand them under its own home directory. Quote directories that contain spaces. A colon separates PATH entries and cannot be part of one saved directory. Compare the saved rules with the PATH inherited by the command: omztty path list omztty path list --effective Removing a rule stops oh-my-ztty from adding it. A directory supplied by the operating system, another startup file or a virtual environment can remain in PATH. Manage rc snippets An rc snippet is an ordinary zsh file containing commands to run during startup. Use snippets for aliases, functions and shell settings that need code rather than a named environment value. omztty rc add aliases omztty rc edit aliases omztty rc check omztty rc list omztty rc status For example, the aliases snippet can contain: alias ll='ls -alF' Import an existing file, inspect a snippet and switch it on or off from the command line: omztty rc add tools --from "$HOME/tools.zsh" omztty rc show tools omztty rc disable tools omztty rc enable tools omztty rc remove tools rc check validates environment and PATH records and checks snippet syntax without running the snippets. Enabled snippets are normal executable zsh code, and run when the settings load. rc add creates an enabled snippet, including when importing a file; review the source before importing it. With Git enabled, changing a shared snippet records a local commit. Before Git is enabled, the shell manager keeps local file snapshots. Enabled files end in .zsh and load in filename order. Disabling a snippet retains its contents in a .zsh.disabled file. Find and edit the files Every command group can print its actual location, including XDG overrides: omztty config path omztty env file omztty env file --shared omztty path file omztty rc file aliases With the default XDG locations, the layout is: File or directory Contents Included in profile sync ~/.config/oh-my-ztty/profile/ Profile repository and application files Yes ~/.config/oh-my-ztty/profile/shell/env.tsv Shared environment variables Yes ~/.config/oh-my-ztty/profile/shell/path.tsv Ordered PATH rules Yes ~/.config/oh-my-ztty/profile/shell/rc.d/ zsh snippets Yes ~/.config/oh-my-ztty/profile/.baseline/ Local copy of shipped defaults for refresh No ~/.config/oh-my-ztty/local/env.tsv Machine-specific environment values No ~/.local/state/oh-my-ztty/backups/ Local file snapshots made before Git is enabled No ~/.local/state/zdot/oh-my-ztty/ Application deployment journal and originals No XDG_CONFIG_HOME changes the configuration root, and XDG_STATE_HOME changes the state root. Home application deployment requires an absolute configuration root inside HOME. You can edit the files with any text editor. The CLI also opens them using your editor: omztty env edit omztty env edit --shared omztty path edit omztty rc edit aliases omztty rc check Use env set, path add and the other commands for routine changes; they choose the correct file and validate the input. Manual editing is useful when reviewing several settings together. The edit commands validate a temporary copy before saving it, so invalid edits leave the existing configuration in place. Each environment record has a variable name, one actual tab character, then the literal value. For example, an env.tsv file can contain: # Shared environment values EDITOR nvim PROJECT_LABEL development workstation Each PATH record has prepend or append, one actual tab, then an absolute directory or a home-relative directory: # Ordered PATH rules prepend ~/.local/bin append /opt/toolchain/bin Both formats accept empty lines and comments beginning with #. Use tabs between fields, not spaces. A value cannot contain a tab, carriage return or newline; a PATH directory also cannot contain a colon. Each variable name and directory appears once per file. Values are literal text: do not add shell quotes or an export prefix to a data record. An environment value containing $HOME stays exactly that text. PATH entries expand only a leading ~ or ~/ to the current machine's home directory. Rc snippets use ordinary zsh syntax. Run omztty rc check after editing files directly. Existing options.zsh and local.zsh files continue to work in the preset shell. options.zsh holds options needed before zshard initializes; local.zsh holds existing personal additions. They remain local unless you deliberately move the relevant settings into the shared profile. Load a change A new omztty shell session reads the updated settings. An ordinary new zsh session also reads them after rc install. To reload from an already running suite shell: source "$OMZTTY_ROOT/config/zsh/settings.zsh" Reloading also runs enabled rc snippets again. omztty rc status prints a reload command with the actual installation path, which is useful from an ordinary zsh session. A command cannot change the environment of the parent shell that launched it, so merely running env set or path add does not change that shell's current variables. A fresh session is the clearest way to check removals. Review and restore changes Git becomes the history for shared shell settings when the standard profile has its own Git repository. omztty setup --repo NAME and omztty sync init record the initial local configuration, using your configured Git name and email. The shell manager stops making new file snapshots. PATH changes, shared environment changes and snippet changes create local commits; they are uploaded only when you run omztty sync push. omztty sync history omztty sync restore COMMIT omztty sync restore COMMIT shell/path.tsv Choose COMMIT from the recent local history. With no file argument, restore selects the shared shell configuration. Supply a path relative to the profile to restore one allowed file, such as shell/path.tsv or shell/env.tsv. Restore requires a clean working tree, checks the selected configuration and records the result as a new local commit. It creates no file snapshot and uploads nothing. Use a new shell to load the restored settings, then omztty sync push when you want to synchronize that version. Git needs your commit name and email before recording a shared change. If they are missing, the command stops before writing the change. Set them for this profile if needed: git -C "$(omztty config path)" config user.name "Your Name" git -C "$(omztty config path)" config user.email "you@example.com" Machine-specific environment values and the ordinary home rc startup block stay outside Git. In Git mode, changes to those local files also create no snapshots. Existing snapshots from before Git was enabled stay on disk; new changes use Git history. rc backups and rc restore point you to the Git history commands in this mode. Before enabling Git For a profile without its own Git repository, the shell manager saves local file snapshots: omztty rc backups omztty rc restore BACKUP_ID Each ID describes one file's previous contents and permissions, or records that the file was previously absent. Restoring an absence record removes the newly created file. The current version is saved before restoring a record. Remove the startup block To stop an ordinary zsh from loading the managed settings while retaining the configuration: omztty rc uninstall --dry-run omztty rc uninstall Use omztty config remove separately when restoring an application profile that was deployed with config apply. Synchronize between machines The dotfiles guide explains private GitHub setup, explicit push and pull, and restoring a profile on another machine. The update commands have separate scopes: Command What it updates omztty update The installed per-user suite omztty update --config-only Your configured profile repository omztty update --with-config The per-user suite and your configured profile repository omztty config refresh Shipped application defaults that you have not changed Keep machine-specific values in the local scope. A private Git repository still has history: removing a value from the latest file does not remove it from earlier commits.

title: Memory and Swap
body: 组合终端、shell、应用配置与内存管理，提供 Linux 工作环境。 Memory and Swap zmem is the suite's default system memory manager. The release installer sets it up with administrator privileges, enables zmem.service, and hands management of existing Swap to zmem. The terminal, shell and AI tools use the same system policy. See what the system is doing omztty memory omztty memory status --json --processes omztty memory status --live --json omztty memory plan --json omztty memory doctor --json status uses the report of the active zmem daemon after checking its process identity. The report retains that daemon's policy history, measured paging rates, worker state and errors. --processes adds a current process list. The observation fields identify the report source, sampling age and stale data; process measurements have their own timestamp. omztty doctor also shows whether the system memory service is active. status --live and plan take an independent sample and show a proposed action without applying it. They begin with a new policy state, and paging rates are null until measurements are available. If the daemon report cannot be used, ordinary status labels its fallback as an independent snapshot and records the cache error. AI clients should check this provenance before interpreting a decision as a daemon report. Read pressure, controls and coverage Memory pressure and IO congestion are separate signals. zmem observes available RAM, memory stalls, file-page refaults and swap activity to decide whether to adjust memory budgets or Swap capacity. Busy IO alone does not establish the cost of disk Swap. Without confirmed disk Swap reads, file-refault evidence can favor retaining file cache; otherwise zmem uses a neutral paging preference with hysteresis. That neutral preference can lower an earlier elevated setting. Confirmed disk Swap read pressure follows a separate reduction path. From zmem 0.3.1, reclaim_latency_guard blocks automatic promotion when memory full stalls reach 1%, direct scans reach 64 MiB/s and anonymous refaults reach 4 MiB/s in the same warmed observation. It requests a ceiling of 60 and preserves an actual value already below that ceiling. The guard uses the ordinary adjustment rules: 10 seconds of supporting evidence, 30-second spacing between confirmed changes and steps of at most 20. These are conservative control thresholds, not measurements of input latency. If the current swappiness cannot be read, zmem reports readback_unavailable, leaves the requested value null and skips the sysctl write. The controls object reports requested and actual swappiness, its reason, the actual page-cluster value, the protection budget and the count of successfully protected scopes. protection_sampled_at_unix and protection_errors retain the most recent protection check's time and diagnostics between checks. managed reports background groups, populated groups, task counts, memory usage and eligible reclaim candidates. The protection_complete and coverage_complete flags expose incomplete control operations or observations. A plan's requested bytes describe an intended action; observed reclaim progress is reported separately. The background object reports requested_budget_bytes, actual_budget_bytes and per-group limits. The actual aggregate comes from reading back the limits of populated groups; plan_available, readback_complete and applied_complete identify available plans, complete observations and successful application. With complete information, a null budget means no temporary requested ceiling or an unlimited observed group; otherwise it is unavailable. plan.background_high_percent remains a pressure-severity hint. Use the byte fields to inspect requested and actual quotas. An empty background scope has no work to constrain or reclaim. zmem applies background budgets to jobs started in its managed class. Existing applications outside those groups keep their current placement. Interactive protection follows recognized desktop, terminal and remote-access processes into their nested cgroups and distributes a bounded budget through the hierarchy. Recursive kernel protection can pass an ancestor's budget to children even when a child's local memory.low is zero. Keep background jobs manageable The suite's source-bundle builder, direct Cargo commands in its component checker, and Project Z's build coordinator automatically start new Cargo builds, checks, tests, benchmarks, Clippy, documentation and compiler jobs in zmem's background class when an active, identity-verified zmem 0.2 or newer is available. This gives the daemon a separate group to budget before the job allocates memory. The existing outer Cargo build lock still coordinates shared build files. If the required Linux systemd manager or verified zmem daemon is unavailable, the build entry point reports the reason and runs the command normally. Set ZMEM_BUILD_BACKGROUND=0 for a build batch to keep the caller's current classification. This automatic routing applies to those source entry points' direct Cargo invocations; it does not add --dedup or register build memory for merging. Other background commands can use the explicit form below. Start a build or other background job through the managed scope: omztty memory run --class background -- cargo build Interactive work can use --class interactive. The disposable class is for work you explicitly allow to encounter a hard memory limit. Use the class before starting the process so the kernel accounts for its memory in the intended group. Wait before starting more heavy work With zmem 0.4, background and disposable commands check available RAM and memory PSI before execution. The default wait is 60 seconds. A timeout returns exit code 75 without starting the target; an interactive command bypasses admission. The suite's managed Cargo entry points inherit this behavior when the installed manager is upgraded. # Allow a batch job up to five minutes to find sufficient headroom. omztty memory run --class background --wait-timeout 300 -- cargo build --release --locked # Check once and leave the command unstarted if conditions are unsuitable. omztty memory run --class background --wait-timeout 0 -- YOUR_COMMAND A healthy first observation can pass immediately. After pressure or a missing observation, memory must satisfy stricter recovery conditions for three seconds. Launch reservations by the same user are spaced by at least three seconds to limit a simultaneous burst; scheduling can still change actual execution timing. Waiting emits JSON events on stderr, keeps stdout for the command, and can be cancelled with SIGINT or SIGTERM. This is not a persistent FIFO queue or a prediction of a program's peak memory. Admission does not install a permanent CPU quota or storage bandwidth cap. The zmem admission guide describes the launch reserve, thresholds and exit codes. Existing running programs outside the managed groups retain their placement; arbitrary terminal commands are not automatically intercepted. Reuse compilation work Keep the shared Cargo target directory when repeating local checks. Fresh temporary target directories cannot reuse that directory's earlier compiled artifacts. The source helpers retain the existing outer build lock and do not move Cargo metadata queries into admission. Official releases cache Cargo downloads, unpacked registry and Git dependency sources, final outputs and intermediate build artifacts. The cache is separated by architecture, runner and actual Rust toolchain identity, with source and lock identities in the key. Cargo still checks restored fingerprints, and installer, source-lock, smoke and graphical checks continue to run. The first run populates the cache; a warm-cache speedup has not yet been measured. See the Cargo build-cache documentation for the separate target and build directories. Background jobs inherit the managed aggregate's dynamic budget. Starting a background job adds no fixed half-RAM limit to its child scope. During pressure, the daemon calculates the aggregate from current managed usage, available RAM and the configured reserve plus a safety margin. Populated groups share the budget; empty groups receive no share. Existing external limits remain in force. Changes tighten groups before relaxing any limits. A failed tightening blocks that batch's relaxations, and a failed relaxation stops the remaining ones. Incomplete observations hold existing controls; only kernel readback confirms the resulting budget. Measured spare headroom allows gradual recovery even while the current memory.high limit produces PSI stalls, so work can regain capacity as room becomes available. Healthy policy removes the temporary restriction. Proactive reclaim selects populated managed groups with eligible clean file pages. Empty groups and groups without suitable pages are skipped; requests that produce no observed progress trigger a retry backoff. The current coverage and progress reports show which work this policy can affect. The default policy preserves processes. It does not discard application data, clear the entire page cache or provide application checkpoints. Applications remain responsible for saving their documents and progress. Enable IO controls for user jobs Setup with zmem 0.3.1 adds IO delegation and accounting to user@.service through /etc/systemd/system/user@.service.d/50-zmem-io.conf. The drop-in appends Delegate=io and enables IOAccounting=yes, preserving existing CPU, memory and PID delegation. An existing external file at the same path is kept, even if its contents match. A separate ownership journal lets rollback remove only an unchanged file that zmem created; changed or replaced files are preserved. Existing user managers may report user_io.state = needs_refresh. Installation does not restart user sessions or refresh every user's manager automatically. In the affected user's session, reload the manager's executable while keeping its processes: systemctl --user daemon-reexec omztty memory doctor --json Check user_io.io_available and io_enabled_for_children, then inspect the returned manager_cgroup: cgroup.controllers and cgroup.subtree_control should include io, and io.stat should exist. Managed child groups also need the relevant io.weight or io.max files. Unavailable observations remain null; the report checks the caller's manager, or the originating user when invoked through sudo. Delegation makes these controls available; a configured IOWeight does not establish its scheduling effect. Weight control also needs a supporting device backend, such as BFQ or enabled IO cost control, and kernel readback. io_weight_effective stays null because those configuration checks do not measure workload impact. The zmem 0.3.1 acceptance record separates host-specific observations from general policy. No fixed IO limit or desktop responsiveness gain is implied for another machine. Automatic Swap maintenance zmem 0.3 grows disk Swap in configured chunks and revisits retained owned files automatically. Maintenance attempts are at least 60 seconds apart, with one candidate per attempt, after growth or managed-background reclaim work. Cleanup uses an identity-checked, kernel-guarded unlink without migrating pages; a missing canonical pathname does not prove that a file is inactive. Active retirement waits for sustained healthy conditions, 600 seconds by default, and rechecks RAM and remaining Swap against the candidate's entire capacity. Known used files are skipped. Shared locking covers zmem's allocation and syscall-helper lifetimes, including a helper that outlives a timeout. Maintenance does not rewrite or apply filesystem deduplication to active Swap. See the zmem lifecycle guide for the separate cleanup and retirement gates. Register trusted jobs for memory deduplication With zmem 0.3 or newer, explicitly register a compatible background or disposable workload: omztty memory run --class background --dedup -- YOUR_TRUSTED_COMMAND omztty memory run --class disposable --max-memory 2048 --dedup -- YOUR_TRUSTED_BATCH_COMMAND The default dedup_enabled = true allows the daemon to manage scanning for registered tasks. It does not enroll other applications, and ordinary background commands keep their existing registration state. --dedup is unavailable for the interactive class. Unsupported or unverifiable process registration produces an error before the target command starts. KSM matching is system-wide: process, user and cgroup boundaries do not isolate its matching domain, and other software may already have registered eligible pages. Choose trusted workloads whose data may share that domain. zmem preserves external KSM controllers and advisors. For controls it owns, CPU, memory or IO pressure pauses scanning with run=0; 30 seconds of stable observations are required before scanning resumes. The 128-page batch and 100 ms sleep are scan settings, not a hard CPU quota. Pausing preserves merged pages; zmem does not force an unmerge with run=2 or PR_SET_MEMORY_MERGE=0. The dedup report exposes observed and target state, reason, ownership and bounded task discovery refreshed every 10 seconds. Check its observation age and coverage flags. The ksm report contains actual controls and a signed system-wide profit estimate; missing metrics remain null, and global profit is not attributable solely to zmem. Independent --live and plan previews do not have the daemon's registered-task history. The earlier 0.2.0 acceptance record does not measure these lifecycle or dedup additions. No fixed memory saving or responsiveness gain is implied by enabling them. Default policy The suite ships config/zmem/zmem.conf. On first setup, zmem copies this policy to /etc/zmem/zmem.conf. Later installs preserve the existing system configuration. Setting Default Observation interval 2 seconds Disk Swap growth step 2 GiB Maximum managed disk Swap 32 GiB Disk space kept available 8 GiB Target free Swap 4 GiB RAM reserve Scaled to installed RAM New zram capacity 50% of RAM Session protection Enabled Swappiness management Enabled KSM scanning control Enabled for explicitly registered tasks; registration remains opt-in Profile Balanced Edit /etc/zmem/zmem.conf with administrator privileges, then restart zmem.service. Existing occupied Swap stays active during adoption; the configured zram layout applies when zmem initializes a device at boot. The zmem documentation defines the configuration keys, policy limits and recovery behavior. Use dedup_enabled = false to disable zmem's scanning policy; this does not forcibly unmerge existing pages or take over an external controller. Use protect_sessions = false to disable automatic session protection. While protection is enabled, an already owned memory.low control reset to its original zero can be reapplied if the cgroup identity is unchanged; manually writing zero is not a persistent opt-out. Nonzero external settings remain protected. Setup, updates and recovery The normal release installation includes system memory setup. For a container, a non-systemd environment or a per-user-only installation, use: sh install.sh --no-memory-manager This skips system setup and records the choice for future updates. It does not stop an existing system manager. Enable zmem later with: omztty memory setup omztty update --memory-manager memory setup installs the bundled version immediately. update --memory-manager also records that system memory management should be included in future suite updates. The setup command copies the executable to root-owned /usr/local/bin/zmem; the system service runs that copy, independently of the user-writable suite directory. To restore the memory managers and configuration recorded before zmem took over: omztty memory rollback The system memory service has its own lifetime. Removing the per-user terminal suite keeps it available, along with /etc/zmem/zmem.conf. If the suite has already been removed, its recovery command is: sudo /usr/local/bin/zmem rollback Package-managed installations can use omztty memory setup when their bundle includes zmem. Their ordinary runtime updates continue through the distribution's package manager.

title: Plugins
body: 组合终端、shell、应用配置与内存管理，提供 Linux 工作环境。 Plugins Add shell commands, completions and prompt behavior by loading ordinary zsh files. Start with the included example, then add the plugins you want to local.zsh so they load in future sessions. Load a local plugin Inside the preset shell, try the included example: zshard load "$ZSHARD_HOME/examples/hello.plugin.zsh" hello world To load it in future shells, put the first line in local.zsh. A canonical file path is loaded once in a shell. Choose a loading mode Interface When the file is sourced zshard load FILE Immediately zshard defer FILE At the next ZLE editing line zshard lazy COMMAND FILE When that command is first used Each deferred batch attempts every queued plugin once. A failure does not discard the later plugins; the batch returns its first nonzero status. Plugins queued during a batch wait for the next editing line. Failed plugins are not retried automatically. A lazy plugin must define its command or make the external executable available. The wrapper preserves the original argument boundaries. Installing a plugin does not make startup load every installed plugin. Loading remains a separate configuration choice. Pin a remote plugin A remote plugin needs a full 40-character Git commit and an entry file inside that checkout. This example installs the published zshard hello sample: zshard plugin add hello \ https://github.com/LIghtJUNction/zshard.git \ a55c2d08b4299b25ec007b45641df87e8c0d0bbb \ examples/hello.plugin.zsh zshard plugin verify hello zshard use hello Add zshard use hello to local.zsh if you want it in each shell. The checkout and its lock file record the pin. Installation does not source the downloaded file. Loading it runs that code inside your shell. verify explicitly checks Git HEAD and uncommitted changes; ordinary shell loading is separate from that integrity check. Git file transports and repository hooks are disabled during plugin installation. The entry must resolve inside the checkout. Export and restore pins Keep an exported lock file with your chosen configuration: zshard plugin export > plugins.lock zshard plugin restore plugins.lock Restore verifies matching installed checkouts, installs missing pins and refuses a different existing pin. It does not load code. A failed batch retains successfully installed entries so a retry can continue. Use zshard plugin remove hello to remove that installed checkout. Changing a pin means explicitly removing it and installing the reviewed replacement. Hooks and cleanup Plugins register hooks through zshard hook EVENT FUNCTION and remove them through zshard unhook EVENT FUNCTION. Supported events include chpwd, precmd, preexec, periodic, zshaddhistory, zshexit and zsh_directory_name. A plugin owns its functions, variables, hooks and widgets. The hello example exposes cleanup as zshard_plugin_hello_unload, which is called by: zshard unload hello Removing an installed checkout does not undo code already loaded in the current shell. Use cleanup or open a new shell. Unload refuses to claim success when the plugin supplies no cleanup function. Completions and themes Register a directory of standard zsh _command completion files with zshard completions DIRECTORY before completion initializes. With the default lazy setting, that means before the first Tab. With eager loading, initialization has already happened by the time local.zsh runs. Registration after initialization returns an error. Register a prompt callback with zshard theme FUNCTION. It receives the last exit status and elapsed whole seconds and assigns PROMPT and RPROMPT. Keep external commands out of the callback to retain the default prompt's process behavior. See the complete extension reference and the working hello plugin.

title: AI integration
body: 组合终端、shell、应用配置与内存管理，提供 Linux 工作环境。 AI integration Use the AI commands to inspect local shell context, connect a client to your workspace or place a proposed command in the editing buffer. Start by inspecting the context below, then choose an ssmcp connection or a provider CLI for requests. Inspect context From any shell: omztty ai context Inside the preset shell: zai context The result is one zshard.context.v1 JSON object: Field Meaning cwd Current working directory shell, shell_version The active zsh runtime last_exit Recorded prior status in the interactive shell capabilities Available context, command staging and ssmcp interfaces history_included false environment_included false It does not read file contents or emit the previous command. A fresh standalone process starts with last_exit set to 0. The directory path is included when you send a request to a provider. Connect a workspace omztty ai connect This starts the bundled ssmcp in the current directory. Inside the preset shell, zai connect provides the same handoff and forwards supplied arguments to ssmcp. Use the ssmcp 0.10.20 connection instructions when connecting an AI client. Model selection and account setup stay with that client. Use a provider Set ZSHARD_AI_COMMAND to a zsh argv array in local.zsh. Each array element becomes one argument. The provider receives the context and request on standard input. You can inspect that transport locally with the standard cat command: ZSHARD_AI_COMMAND=(cat) zai ask 'Show the request envelope' This diagnostic echoes the request; it does not call a model. For regular use, replace the array with your installed provider CLI and its documented stdin arguments. After configuring a provider, use zai ask inside the preset or omztty ai ask from another shell: omztty ai ask 'Explain this directory context' The launcher reads the persistent provider configuration. Returned text is displayed without automatic shell evaluation. A provider's authentication, pricing and own context behavior remain part of that provider. Stage a command In an interactive preset shell: zai propose 'git status --short' The command is put into the editing buffer. Review, edit or cancel it; pressing Enter executes it. Staging requires an interactive TTY and a single printable command line. Runtime boundaries Opening a shell performs no provider request or MCP connection. The included ssmcp has its existing Rust standard-library and networking dependencies and runs when requested. A live AI session has a different memory footprint from the idle terminal measurements. The AI contract defines argument handling and context fields. The cat example above checks the local request format; a real provider requires its own setup.

title: Dotfiles
body: 组合终端、shell、应用配置与内存管理，提供 Linux 工作环境。 Dotfiles Keep your shared shell and application settings in a private GitHub repository through omztty setup and omztty sync. The standard profile path stays the same across installations, and the CLI prints its actual location with omztty config path. The shell guide covers PATH, environment variables and rc snippets. The configuration guide covers the application profile. You can also manage an independent repository with omztty dot, as described below. Synchronize the suite profile Start the interactive setup: omztty setup The wizard prepares the local profile, offers to install the zsh startup block and asks whether to configure GitHub synchronization. The remote step is optional. It uses the GitHub CLI's current account and accepts a private repository owned by that account. Install gh through your package manager and sign in when you want GitHub synchronization: gh auth login omztty setup --repo dotfiles This creates a private dotfiles repository under your signed-in GitHub account and uploads the selected profile files. The command shows the account and repository before the confirmed remote operation. Your existing Git identity is used for commits. Local-only setup works without the GitHub CLI: omztty setup --local --local initializes configuration without connecting an ordinary shell startup file. Add --install-rc to install that block explicitly. A script can use --yes together with an explicit --local, --repo NAME or --from OWNER/NAME choice; --yes alone does not choose a remote operation. If you already created an empty private GitHub repository under your own account, connect it explicitly: omztty setup --local omztty sync init git -C "$(omztty config path)" remote add origin git@github.com:YOUR_LOGIN/dotfiles.git sync init creates the local Git repository and records the initial configuration. It uses your configured Git name and email, and does not create a remote or push. Replace YOUR_LOGIN with the signed-in account name. Use setup --from below when that repository already contains a profile you want to restore.
