Unknown protocols require an implemented adapter in zconv and an explicit zcall integration with conformance tests. zcall::api also exposes zconv's borrowed Embeddings, Images, Batch and Files codecs, endpoint paths and multipart writers. Use zcall::api::json for their caller-owned token workspace. These resource APIs remain separate from the six conversation protocols and do not send HTTP requests, upload files or execute batches. Structured tool results expose typed child blocks through BlockView::result_contents. Author arrays with Request::append_tool_result_contents; their record spans belong to the current document and cannot be copied to another request. Request::stream_options preserves usage preferences, including preferences returned in EncodeReport::transport_stream_options for targets without that JSON field. Set EventEncoderConfig::usage_emission to UsageEmission::Continuous when intermediate observed counters are required. Missing counters stay absent. BlockType::Reasoning carries raw reasoning and ReasoningSummary carries a summary. Anthropic source-owned blocks, citation deltas and usage metadata have explicit provider events. They can be replayed to the same format; server tool blocks never become local ToolReady work. Strict conversion is the default. Provider context references, file IDs, opaque signatures and extension values retain their source namespace. When a target requires absent facts, the caller supplies them through an explicit context. Loss permissions are narrow and accompanied by inspectable field-level reports. Build and verify cargo test --all-targets --locked cargo +1.99.1 test --all-targets --locked cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings python3 scripts/check_package.py python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py' See examples/request.rs for backend switching, examples/stream.rs for the shared event consumer, examples/endpoint.rs for URL construction and examples/discover.rs for a runnable discovery client. The semantic contract, support matrix, resource recovery, dependency audit, measurements, validation evidence and release procedure describe the implemented boundaries. License: MIT OR Apache-2.0.

title: v1 semantic contract
body: 协议无关的模型调用内核，由宿主提供传输与缓冲区。 v1 semantic contract Responsibility and stability zcall::v1 describes one model invocation and its result. It never performs network I/O, authenticates, retries, chooses a model, executes a tool, persists a conversation, reads a clock or decides whether an agent has finished its task. Those decisions stay with the harness. A response that requests tools ends the model turn in WaitingTools and leaves the agent's task open. The contract covers field meanings, presence, event ordering, terminal behavior, error classes, usage accounting, capability evidence and explicit degradation. The implementation can change private zconv storage without changing these meanings. Rust source compatibility is governed by crate SemVer. No promise is made about Rust type layout, a C ABI, dynamic linking or cross-compiler ABI. Requests and provenance RequestBuilder writes directly into caller-owned RecordStorage. Importing a wire request uses zconv's JSON parser and protocol decoder. Both paths produce the same editable request representation. Views borrow the request, so mutable edits cannot occur while a view is live. There is one arena of message, block, tool and extension records, plus a fixed-size header. A builder's explicit authoring format governs defaults whose meaning differs between protocols, such as function strictness. It is not a model capability declaration. The format can be selected once at the integration boundary; the ordered messages, tools and business logic remain unchanged when the target backend changes. Imported requests always retain the actual source identity. Presence::Missing means the source did not specify a field. Null means an explicit JSON null. Value includes empty strings, empty containers, false and zero. Setters preserve that distinction and encoders reject unrepresentable target semantics. No unknown count or capacity is silently replaced by zero. Text borrows either UTF-8 or a validated JSON string. An unescaped string is available through as_str; an escaped one can be compared without allocation or decoded into a caller buffer. Json preserves exact validated bytes. Integer usage values remain integers or borrowed decimal JSON; no floating-point cast is used. A value outside u64 can remain inspectable in a complete response. Messages and their blocks preserve order. Roles, media reference kinds, function names, arguments, results, refusal and reasoning are explicit types. Thought text, public summaries and opaque signatures have different meanings. Tool argument JSON and ordinary text are separate Data variants. Identities and context An overall response ID, an output item ID and a tool call ID have distinct namespaces. They are exposed separately. zcall never substitutes a call ID for an output item ID or fabricates a response ID, timestamp or token count. EncodeContext carries facts missing from a source: transport model, required maximum output tokens, response timestamps and tool-name/ID mappings. Gemini model and streaming selection can belong in the transport URL; the encode report returns them for the harness instead of hiding a network operation. Stored server context, provider file IDs and opaque extension values retain their source format/version/profile. Changing providers does not rename these references into target references. The harness must materialize history or explicitly permit dropping a reference, receiving the resulting loss report. Capabilities and preparation Request::prepare is the sending boundary. It derives requirements from the actual IR, checks the selected adapter operation, the protocol's expressible subset, caller-provided model evidence and deployment restrictions, then runs the target encoder against the current input. Its output is uncommitted until the entire operation succeeds. Supported, Unsupported and Unknown remain distinct. An image field in a protocol supplies no evidence that a particular model supports images. Model and deployment declarations contain their source and optional revision. Context windows, output limits and named reasoning levels remain unknown when the caller has not supplied evidence. Token counts must come from the caller's tokenizer or another explicit measurement; byte counts are not token counts. Strict policy rejects required unknown capabilities, incompatible features and unverified conditions. Narrow options permit specified uncertainty, with a diagnostic for each affected requirement and layer. A condition validated by the actual encoder is marked separately from a condition merely accepted by policy. Report capacity is caller-owned and recoverable from zero. Request::encode is a lower-level semantic conversion operation. It checks representability, context and losses but does not promise a model/deployment capability check. This distinction lets offline converters use the crate without inventing model evidence. Stream submission and lifetimes Construct a Session, mark its outgoing request prepared, then call step with bytes and a synchronous consumer. SessionStep reports consumed input, accepted events and progress. The consumer returns Continue to accept an event or Pause to reject it. Pause leaves that exact event pending. Consumer side effects belong only to the Continue branch. An event's strings and JSON borrow the session only for the consumer call. The higher-ranked callback lifetime prevents storing those borrowed views in a longer-lived queue. A harness that needs an asynchronous work item must copy the necessary data into its own bounded storage. Calling step again cannot leave an exposed borrowed pointer dangling because the earlier callback borrow ended. SSE framing, CR/LF handling, UTF-8 replacement and protocol JSON parsing belong to zconv. Fragments can split an escape, a UTF-8 sequence, a CRLF pair or any other byte boundary. One call can contain many events and a single event can span many calls. Committed events and consumed bytes are never replayed to recover a capacity failure. Repeated wire begin metadata is checked against the current identity and normalized into one logical Started event. Usage can arrive before Started; consumers must not assume the first event contains the response ID. Text delta events need not have an explicit preceding block-start event in a source that does not provide one. Keys expose choice, item and part indices. When real identity fields arrive later, IdentityUpdated exposes the newly known identity and Session::identity returns the current view. Previously known fields must remain consistent. An event encoder checks these updates against explicit caller context before writing target identity fields. Event::reasoning_kind distinguishes Thought, Summary and Unspecified. An unspecified compatible-protocol field is not evidence of either meaning. An encoder rejects translation between these meanings unless an exact allowed loss applies; it does not present a public summary as private thought text. SnapshotVerified is validation of a completed snapshot, not content to append. Tools always retain complete argument bytes for exact validation. Responses text snapshots are checked byte for byte by default. Explicitly disabling text snapshot retention selects a documented length-only check, reducing aggregation storage without changing delta-authoritative output. Tool and call lifecycle The session distinguishes idle, prepared, receiving, tool formation, waiting for results, resolved tools, completed, incomplete, upstream failure, local cancel intent, confirmed cancellation, truncation and local failure. Tool argument fragments may be incomplete JSON. Before ToolReady, the aggregate must be a complete JSON object under the configured parser limits. This is a JSON-object validity contract; it does not claim full JSON Schema validation of a tool's parameters. The harness may apply its domain/schema validator before executing a tool. Interleaved tool calls have separate identities and ordered argument aggregates. ToolReady is submitted once per completed tool. submit_tool_result records the association with a known ready call; an unknown ID, duplicate result or illegal state yields a lifecycle error. Append the actual result to a caller-managed follow-up Request; the kernel does not retain an unbounded transcript. Session::tool(call_id) borrows the retained name and complete arguments after ToolReady, allowing the harness to inspect or copy them outside the callback. pending_tool_count reports ready calls whose results have not been submitted. The borrowed tool view prevents mutable session reuse while it is still live. request_cancel records local intent. The transport can still deliver a racing normal completion. confirm_cancel records a transport-confirmed cancellation. transport_failed is a caller-reported transport failure, distinct from an upstream error event and a parser/converter failure. A single terminal event is accepted locally. Repeating terminal input or sending new bytes after terminal state is a lifecycle error; terminal events are not emitted twice. Explicit EOF must follow the source's termination rule. Missing protocol termination produces Truncated. GenerateContent SSE ends after valid candidate finish reasons and caller EOF. A terminal model turn that needs tool results does not claim completion of the outer agent task. These local rules do not promise distributed exactly-once execution or delivery. StepStatus::Done means the turn's bytes and events have ended. The terminal outcome and CallState distinguish success, waiting for tools, incomplete output, upstream failure and confirmed cancellation; Done alone is not a success flag. Usage, losses and recovery Stream usage is cumulative. A present update replaces that source field, while an absent update preserves the previous known field. zconv's shared accumulator normalizes Anthropic cache reads/writes and Gemini thought counts, using checked arithmetic. It retains underlying source bases so partial cumulative updates cannot add the same usage twice. Overflow is a semantic error. Nonstream loss policies separately permit extensions, reasoning, stored context and metadata. losses enumerates actual affected fields with source identity and semantic location. Stream loss permissions list exact field classes; loss events identify the source and affected field. A permission does not justify discarding other unlisted data. Errors have stable classes for JSON, protocol input, unsupported adapter/version/ profile/feature, unknown or mismatched capability, missing context, forbidden loss, capacity, configured limits, truncation, lifecycle, upstream failure and transport failure. Capacity failures additionally name the region, needed capacity, exactness and retry ownership. See RESOURCES.md.

title: Endpoints and protocol discovery
body: 协议无关的模型调用内核，由宿主提供传输与缓冲区。 Endpoints and protocol discovery HttpEndpoint binds a base URL to a wire format. Discovery finds a usable format by producing small generation requests and checking the HTTP responses supplied by the application. Both APIs borrow their configuration and use caller-owned buffers. HTTP, credentials, TLS, deadlines and retries belong to the transport. Configure a known protocol use zcall::v1::*; let endpoint = HttpEndpoint::new( "https://gateway.example/proxy/v1", Protocol::OpenAiChat.into(), )?; let mut output = [0; 512]; let url = endpoint.url_into(Some("my-model"), false, &mut output)?; assert_eq!(url, "https://gateway.example/proxy/v1/chat/completions"); # Ok::<(), EndpointError>(()) Use endpoint.format() as the target format for Request::prepare or Request::encode. The resulting request bytes go to the URL returned by url_into. For GenerateContent, the request encoder reports the model and stream setting through EncodeReport::transport_model and EncodeReport::transport_stream; supply the same values to URL construction. Protocol URL from https://gateway.example Model in URL OpenAI Completions /v1/completions No OpenAI Chat /v1/chat/completions No OpenAI Responses /v1/responses No Anthropic Messages /v1/messages No Gemini GenerateContent /v1beta/models/{model}:generateContent Yes Gemini Interactions /v1beta/interactions No An origin-only URL receives the default prefix above. An explicit path prefix is retained verbatim: https://gateway.example/api with Chat becomes https://gateway.example/api/chat/completions. Include /api/v1 when your gateway requires that version segment. Trailing slashes are normalized. A complete recognized endpoint is retained without appending it twice; selecting a conflicting protocol returns EndpointError::ProtocolMismatch. The HTTP route and adapter schema version are separate settings. For example, Gemini Interactions uses the current Format schema identifier v1, while an origin-only URL defaults to the /v1beta/interactions HTTP route. Pass an explicit /v1 base URL for a deployment exposing that route. Anthropic's Format.version supplies the anthropic-version probe header. GenerateContent URL construction takes a model name, accepts a leading models/, and encodes the model as a path segment. When the base URL already contains a complete GenerateContent endpoint, None keeps its model and Some(model) replaces it. stream=true selects :streamGenerateContent and sets alt=sse; stream=false selects :generateContent and removes the SSE query selector. Other query parameters, including routing parameters such as api-version, are preserved. Base URLs use ASCII URI syntax; supply punycode hosts and percent-encoded non-ASCII path/query text. URL validation rejects unsupported schemes, missing hosts, URL userinfo, fragments, control characters, malformed escapes and dot path segments. The application decides which hosts it may contact. url_into reports the exact required output capacity before changing an undersized buffer, so the caller can enlarge the buffer and retry. Discover an unknown protocol Create one discovery session for the base URL and a caller-selected model. next_probe produces a POST URL, JSON body, content type, accept header and optional protocol-version header. Add the deployment's authentication, send the request, and supply the response to observe. A successful selection is an HttpEndpoint that can be cached and reused for subsequent calls. use zcall::v1::*; let mut discovery = Discovery::new("https://gateway.example/v1", "my-model")?; let mut url = [0; 512]; let mut body = [0; 512]; let probe = discovery.next_probe(&mut url, &mut body)?.unwrap(); assert_eq!(probe.format.protocol, Protocol::OpenAiChat); assert_eq!(probe.method, "POST"); assert_eq!(probe.url, "https://gateway.example/v1/chat/completions"); // Your transport sends probe.body with probe's headers and authentication. let response = br#"{"id":"r","object":"chat.completion","model":"my-model","choices":[{"index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"OK"},"finish_reason":"stop"}]}"#; let mut tokens = TokenStorage::<128>::new(); assert_eq!( discovery.observe(200, Some("application/json"), response, &mut tokens, Limits::default())?, ProbeOutcome::Supported, ); assert_eq!(discovery.selected().unwrap().format().protocol, Protocol::OpenAiChat); # Ok::<(), DiscoveryError>(()) The default candidate order is Chat, Responses, Anthropic Messages, Gemini GenerateContent, Gemini Interactions and Completions. Discovery stops at the first verified candidate. A service may support several protocols; customize the order when the harness prefers one. A complete endpoint URL narrows the candidates to that endpoint's protocol, while its response must still pass verification. Provider hostnames and model names are never used as proof of protocol support. use zcall::v1::*; let formats = [Protocol::OpenAiResponses.into(), Protocol::OpenAiChat.into()]; let mut config = DiscoveryConfig::new("my-model"); config.formats = &formats; config.max_output_tokens = 32; config.chat_token_limit = ChatTokenLimit::MaxCompletionTokens; let discovery = Discovery::with_config("https://gateway.example/v1", config)?; assert!(discovery.selected().is_none()); # Ok::<(), DiscoveryError>(()) Each candidate gets a separate, nonstreaming Reply OK. generation probe with a configurable output-token limit, defaulting to 16. The probe contains no tools or conversation history. Responses and Interactions include store:false. Providers can bill these requests. Supply a model and credential that are valid for the deployment; an unknown model or rejected generation setting remains an unsuccessful attempt. Chat uses max_tokens by default; select ChatTokenLimit::MaxCompletionTokens for models requiring that field. Interpret outcomes and retry ownership Protocol selection requires a successful HTTP response, a recognizable JSON response shape and validation by the corresponding zconv adapter. An HTML success page, a generic models list, ambiguous response data or an error envelope does not produce a selection. A selected endpoint establishes that the probe's request/response path worked; tool, modality, context and streaming capabilities still use the existing capability checks and session APIs. Observed result Discovery outcome Recognized and valid successful response Supported HTTP 401 AuthenticationRequired HTTP 403 Forbidden HTTP 429 RateLimited HTTP 5xx ServerError(status) HTTP redirect Redirect(status) HTTP 404 / 405 / 410, including model-routing failures NotFound Other request rejection Rejected(status) Unrecognized successful response UnrecognizedResponse Transport reports connection/timeout failure TransportFailed attempts() retains each completed candidate's format and outcome. Failed candidates can be followed by next_probe; success or exhaustion makes it return None. selected() is None after exhaustion. Never relabel an authentication error, quota error or server failure as evidence that a protocol is unsupported. Call observe or transport_failed for the outstanding probe before requesting the next one. Buffer and resource errors preserve the pending operation for retry; no candidate is silently skipped. Read DiscoveryError before deciding whether to enlarge a buffer, adjust a limit or stop. The caller must bound HTTP response size before buffering it, and may stop probing on authentication, rate-limit or server errors according to its own policy. The library performs no hidden network retry, redirect or timeout. Cache a selected HttpEndpoint under the base URL, deployment and credential scope used for discovery. Reuse it with Request::prepare for normal calls. Run a new discovery when that routing or credential context changes, or when the application's expiry policy requires it. There is no process-wide cache or cross-tenant mutable state in the library. Run the external transport example The discover example uses std and an installed curl executable. It adds no Cargo dependencies and is separate from the no_std library. Set API_KEY through your environment, then run: cargo run --example discover -- https://gateway.example/v1 my-model auto cargo run --example discover -- https://gateway.example/v1 my-model responses The second command constructs an explicit endpoint without network access. Auto mode supplies Authorization: Bearer for OpenAI-style protocols, x-api-key for Anthropic and x-goog-api-key for Gemini. Gateways with different authentication rules should adapt the send function to their existing transport. Set CHAT_TOKEN_LIMIT=max_completion_tokens when required by the model. API keys are passed to curl through stdin; the example omits URL query values from its diagnostic output. The example disables curl's user configuration and automatic redirects, uses a 5-second connection timeout and a 20-second overall timeout, and caps response bodies at 64 KiB. TLS verification and the environment's proxy settings remain enabled. Tests use local HTTP fixtures, so running the test suite does not contact a model provider or spend credits. Protocol references OpenAI Chat Completions OpenAI Responses Anthropic Messages Gemini GenerateContent Gemini Interactions The URL and response contracts above are checked against these references and the zconv 0.2.2 adapters. The repository's endpoint, discovery and local-HTTP tests cover the implemented behavior; live availability depends on the selected deployment, model and credential.

title: Performance and memory measurements
body: 协议无关的模型调用内核，由宿主提供传输与缓冲区。 Performance and memory measurements Endpoint and discovery run (2026-11-11) The endpoint/discovery source at commit 413ca14 was measured with Rust 1.99.1, zconv 0.2.2 and an AMD EPYC 9V74 host exposing nine logical CPUs. Each workload warms up for 200 iterations and reports the median of seven samples of 20,000 iterations. The optimized profile uses thin LTO and one codegen unit. Network access and model execution are outside these measurements; host contention and CPU frequency are uncontrolled. Workload Median µs Sample mean range µs Validate a base URL and build a Gemini streaming URL 0.480 0.452–0.505 Initialize discovery and build the first probe URL/body 1.952 1.927–2.015 Initialize, build a probe, parse and confirm a 229-byte Chat response 6.833 5.705–10.855 The last row includes the whole local discovery setup and confirmation path. It does not measure a response parser alone or end-to-end network latency. The allocation-counting integration test observes zero heap allocations for all six URL/probe paths and successful response confirmation. HttpEndpoint occupies 56 bytes and Discovery 480 bytes on this target, excluding borrowed strings, caller buffers, token storage and temporary stack frames. The CSV includes the new workloads and the existing kernel measurements from the same run. The environment record identifies the source, compiler and method. These absolute measurements make no speedup claim against another library or a different host. Rust 1.99.1 / Edition 2024 run (2026-11-11) The Edition 2024 migration was benchmarked on production-source commit 8288cb9, using Rust 1.99.1 and the published zconv 0.2.0 dependency. This run used an AMD EPYC 9V74 host with nine logical CPUs exposed. The older run below used an Intel Xeon Platinum 8573C host. Consequently, the differences between dates cannot be attributed to a Rust edition change or a code optimization. Both paired request workloads inspect their actual parsed IR before encoding. The zconv baseline checks the same message count and produces byte-identical output. Each row reports the median of seven per-sample means, with 20,000 iterations per document sample and 5,001 per stream sample, after warmup. The input throughput figures include parsing, encoding, and the stated harness work; they are not model inference throughput. Workload Input bytes Median µs Sample mean range µs Input MiB/s zcall: small request, inspect IR, encode 111 3.07 2.46–3.93 34.47 zconv: same small IR conversion 111 2.90 2.42–4.79 36.48 zcall: Unicode request, inspect IR, encode 1,783 3.87 3.74–5.16 439.79 zconv: same Unicode IR conversion 1,783 3.88 3.79–3.97 438.60 zcall: tool request, object validation, encode 513 4.85 4.70–5.26 100.81 zcall: complete response decode and content view 229 2.17 2.08–2.24 100.61 zcall: stream supplied in one 309-byte fragment 309 5.35 5.16–6.37 55.03 zcall: same stream in 16-byte fragments 309 5.45 5.29–5.65 54.10 zcall: same stream in one-byte fragments 309 8.04 7.79–11.25 36.66 The small-request median is approximately 5.8% higher than its direct zconv baseline in this run; the sample ranges overlap substantially. The Unicode medians are within 0.3% of each other. Neither observation establishes a statistically reliable relative speed difference. In particular, zcall does not omit an IR inspection for the comparison. The 2026-11-11 CSV records the full precision of all nine measurements. Its environment record captures the compiler, edition, commit, CPU, flags, dependency checksum, source hashes and caller-owned type sizes. The measured memory sizes match the older table below on this x86_64 target; sizes remain architecture and compiler dependent. Historical Rust 2021 baseline (2026-11-10) This is the 2026-11-10 baseline, measured from source commit be9c04f with Rust 1.99.1 and Edition 2021. On 2026-11-11, the crate adopted Edition 2024 with Rust 1.99.1 as its declared minimum; that migration must be evaluated on its own commit. The archived numbers below retain their original source hashes and are not silently relabeled as post-migration results. The recorded workloads complete in single-digit microseconds for small document operations and in 7.92–12.26 microseconds for the same 309-byte streamed model turn, depending on fragmentation. These are local kernel measurements, not network latency, model token throughput or a claim about all protocol payloads. The CSV contains the full run. The environment record includes compiler, CPU, flags, dependency checksum, source hashes and measured type sizes. The implementation and workload are in benches/kernel.rs. Method The run used stable Rust 1.99.1 on x86_64 Linux, with the published zconv 0.2.0 registry dependency. The managed environment exposed an Intel Xeon Platinum 8573C and nine logical CPUs. CPU frequency, host contention and scheduling were not controlled; no CPU affinity or target-cpu=native setting was used. Task-local Miri, fuzz and other compilation work had finished before the timed run. cargo bench uses optimization level 3, thin LTO and one codegen unit. Each workload warms up for 200 iterations, then runs seven samples of 20,000 iterations; streaming samples use 5,001 iterations. Instant measures elapsed time, divided by iterations. Inputs and outputs pass through black_box. The median, minimum and maximum are per-sample means. The min/max range is not a confidence interval. --quick and debug-mode runs are smoke checks and are not the measurements reported here. The paired text-request baseline parses into zconv IR, inspects the message count and encodes Chat to Responses. Both implementations use the same input, target, token/record capacities and semantically equivalent work. Output byte equality is asserted before timing. zcall does not bypass IR inspection for this comparison. Tool validation, complete responses and stateful streams are reported as absolute costs because a codec-only baseline would omit their contract work. Results Workload Input bytes Median µs Sample mean range µs Input MiB/s zcall: small request, inspect IR, encode 111 4.44 4.04–4.81 23.84 zconv: same small IR conversion 111 4.31 3.86–4.58 24.53 zcall: Unicode request, inspect IR, encode 1,783 6.09 5.87–6.21 279.08 zconv: same Unicode IR conversion 1,783 6.16 5.70–6.43 276.17 zcall: tool request, object validation, encode 513 7.85 7.71–8.42 62.34 zcall: complete response decode and content view 229 3.76 3.59–3.81 58.14 zcall: stream supplied in one 309-byte fragment 309 7.92 7.73–9.35 37.21 zcall: same stream in 16-byte fragments 309 8.97 8.18–9.26 32.87 zcall: same stream in one-byte fragments 309 12.26 11.61–12.86 24.04 The small paired workload's medians differ by about 2.9%; the Unicode paired workload's medians differ by about 1.0% in the opposite direction. The overlapping sample ranges do not establish a performance advantage for either library. They show the cost of the stable wrapper at these tested sizes, under this environment's noise. A broader claim needs larger corpora and controlled runs. Fragmentation increases the number of calls, framing checks and resumptions. The one-byte case is a useful recovery stress case; the same text and one terminal event are checked in every case. Each streaming iteration includes session construction, preparation, parsing, lifecycle handling and callback submission. Buffers are reused between iterations without hidden allocation. Explicit memory ownership These are size_of / memory_bytes() measurements on the recorded target. They are not a layout ABI and may differ on another compiler or architecture. Caller-owned type or header Bytes TokenStorage<128> 2,560 RecordStorage<32> 6,912 Request header, excluding records and input 664 Response header, excluding records and input 448 StreamWorkspace<64, 8, 4>, including rollback checkpoints 4,352 Session state, excluding caller buffers/workspace 640 EncoderWorkspace<64, 4>, including rollback checkpoints 1,984 EventEncoder state, excluding caller buffers/workspace 1,200 The stream benchmark supplies three 256-byte buffers for framing, payload and aggregation. Its persistent session state plus workspace and these buffers total 5,760 bytes. This excludes the input slice, consumer-owned storage and temporary call-stack frames; it is not a measured peak stack usage claim. The library does not impose these example capacities. Zero-capacity tests grow each required region explicitly and resume without replaying committed work. Requests write into the actual zconv record storage. Stable views add no second message tree. Session events borrow their replay record during the callback instead of copying the complete raw event on every submission. Text that does not need a final exact snapshot remains incremental. Tool arguments and exact Responses snapshots need retained bytes; their growth is separately visible in Session::memory().aggregate_used and aggregate_peak. The resource contract specifies each retry and growth rule. Both production crates are no_std, forbid unsafe code, have no alloc access and have no other dependencies. The resolved-graph/source audit and successful bare-metal build check that property. A counting-allocator integration test also observes zero allocations during request decode/edit/encode and session input. The test harness and benchmark may allocate their fixtures before kernel work; those allocations are not library behavior. Reproduce cargo bench --bench kernel --locked cargo test --test allocation --locked python3 scripts/check_package.py Run on an otherwise idle machine when comparing changes. Keep the workload, compiler, flags, dependency version, fragmentation and semantic checks identical. The current measurements do not cover long histories, huge tool schemas, many simultaneously active items, all media forms, cancellation-heavy workloads or exhaustive capacity-growth patterns. Their correctness tests are separate from these timing measurements. No vendor HTTP endpoint was called.

title: Resource ownership and recovery
body: 协议无关的模型调用内核，由宿主提供传输与缓冲区。 Resource ownership and recovery The harness owns every growing region. TokenStorage<N>, RecordStorage<N>, StreamWorkspace<T,E,I> and EncoderWorkspace expose capacity and byte costs. The arrays have private, correctly typed elements; an arbitrary unaligned byte buffer is never reinterpreted as Rust objects. There is no hidden heap, cache or global mutable state. Complete documents borrow their input. Request and response headers are fixed size; record storage contains the actual zconv IR. An input can outlive the token tape, because retained JSON/text values borrow only the original bytes. Reusing records requires dropping their live views first. For a live edited document, replace_storage grows its record store in place. If the consuming relocate alternative fails, RelocationError::original returns the original document together with its capacity error; prior edits and the usable handle are retained. A failed growth attempt does not discard work. Region Meaning Needed value Retry rule Tokens JSON token tape Lower bound at the failing token Retry the document, or replace stream workspace and keep the unconsumed suffix Ir Complete request/response records Decoder lower bound; builder operations exact Retry decode or grow existing typed storage; failed builders keep prior content Output Complete encoded bytes Exact Discard partial output, enlarge, repeat the encode; no input consumed Scratch Decoding a JSON string containing tool argument JSON Exact Enlarge scratch and repeat; request/response unchanged Framing Current SSE wire event Lower bound Replace session buffer; consumed input remains retained Payload Decoded/joined SSE data Exact Replace payload; original complete source event remains buffered Events Current frame's event IR Lower bound Replace workspace; committed earlier events remain committed Items Active choice/content/tool state Lower bound Replace workspace, keeping retained state Aggregate IDs, complete arguments and required snapshots Lower bound unless explicitly marked exact Replace aggregate; earlier accepted data is preserved Reports Capability diagnostics Exact Enlarge diagnostics and repeat preparation before sending Context Caller tool identity/name bindings Exact Enlarge typed binding storage before encoding Error.capacity is the authoritative value for a particular failure. A configured parser/depth/input limit is a Limit error, not a request to silently allocate more storage. Errors mark retry ownership as Unconsumed or Retained. Stream loop Advance the transport cursor by step.consumed for every result, including NeedBuffer, NeedEvents and Failed. Never resend that prefix. When a buffer needs growth, replace the named buffer or workspace and retry using only the remaining suffix. A callback returning Pause has not accepted the current event; resume with a consumer that can accept it. emitted counts accepted events. An exhausted output buffer in EventEncoder is drained independently of staging the next event. Its pending bytes retain a cursor, so one-byte and zero-byte outputs do not duplicate previously written bytes. An event rejected before staging can be retried after capacity recovery. Aggregation cost Ordinary text deltas do not create an unbounded conversation transcript. Tool arguments must be retained through completion for validation. Default Responses text snapshot checking also retains text for byte-for-byte comparison. These costs scale with the retained content and appear in aggregate capacity/peak statistics. Choosing a larger caller buffer is visible in the memory report. Session item tables and checkpoints are separate caller-sized tapes. Checkpoints allow a failed state transition to roll back without corrupting committed items. They are included in workspace byte totals. Completed model turns may retain tool identities until result association or explicit reset; the caller chooses when to recycle the session. See PERFORMANCE.md for measured type sizes and benchmark configuration. These are target/compiler measurements, not a Rust layout ABI.

title: Optional HTTP and Unix gateway
body: 协议无关的模型调用内核，由宿主提供传输与缓冲区。 Optional HTTP and Unix gateway The default build remains the allocation-free, safe Rust, no_std call kernel. The server feature enables std and adds a bounded HTTP server, Unix socket ownership, caller-key management and a gateway for the six registered conversation protocols. Both feature graphs contain only zcall and zconv. Responsibilities Component Library responsibility Host responsibility Server Fixed workers, bounded admission, cancellation and shutdown reports Process/service lifecycle and optional native accept loop transport::Listener TCP accept; private, owned Unix socket binding and cleanup Verified UID and optional native stale-socket probe Handler Extension point for any HTTP path or additional format Route semantics and application policy gateway::Gateway Authentication, model-route callback, registered JSON/SSE conversion Upstream transport, TLS and provider credentials server::auth Private key schema, metadata, insertion, rotation and revocation Secure randomness, atomic persistence and synchronization Connection / PeerInspector Timeout, cancellation, half-close and peer-hook contracts Native peer credentials and trusted locality Enable features = ["server"] on the versioned dependency. The feature adds heap buffers and threads; the default kernel does not. It adds no HTTP/TLS or serialization crate. OS networking and filesystem calls come from Rust's standard library. This is not a claim that a native binary has no OS libraries. Run a real local example cargo run --features server --example server -- --check cargo run --release --features server --example server The first command opens an ephemeral loopback listener, sends real HTTP requests in all six registered formats and verifies the fake upstream's replies. The second serves at 127.0.0.1:9416 until Enter is pressed. Its upstream is an in-process fixture: it never contacts a provider or reads an account. For an application, construct Gateway::new(router, transport), pass it to Server::new(config, handler), then call listen(Listener::bind_tcp(...)). Router chooses the upstream protocol/model and explicit provider headers. Transport::execute returns an owned response reader and must honor the given cancellation/deadline. UpstreamBody::cancel is called when the response is dropped, including a downstream error; it must be nonblocking and idempotent. A host can retain its existing TLS client or use Unix upstream transport. A custom Handler can own additional paths or new protocols. The server does not install health, management, model-list, plugin or CORS routes. Gateway rejects unknown conversation endpoints instead of pretending to convert them. Protocol and HTTP boundaries The registered conversation formats are OpenAI Completions, Chat Completions and Responses, Anthropic Messages, Gemini GenerateContent and Gemini Interactions. The gateway tests exercise all 36 source/target combinations for common text and usage semantics over real local TCP. This does not mean every provider-specific field has an equivalent in every target. A response message identity with no target representation, for example, produces ForbiddenLoss; it is not silently discarded. JSON and fragmented SSE use the same strict zconv-backed conversion as the standalone kernel. Inbound caller credentials, Cookie and arbitrary request headers are never forwarded upstream. Provider credentials must be supplied explicitly in the selected Target. Successful finite responses require JSON; streaming requests require an SSE media type. Body and response limits apply during reads/writes, and owned upstream bodies are cancelled on error. http::read_request defaults to JSON API clients and rejects browser Origin headers and encoded bodies. read_request_with_policy lets the host explicitly permit Origin, opaque encoded bytes or another request media type. Duplicate fields, ambiguous length/transfer framing, size limits and deadlines remain strict. Expect negotiation and request trailers are unsupported. A well-formed HTTP/1.1 GET WebSocket handshake receives 426 Upgrade Required with a message to use HTTP/SSE. This is a transport fallback signal, not a WebSocket connection: no 101 response or WebSocket framing is implemented. Malformed or other Upgrade requests remain 400; Origin, Expect and duplicate header checks retain their earlier priority. The decision does not depend on an application path. Response headers are validated before output. Early rejection writes the response, closes the write half, then discards at most 64 KiB of input for at most 200 ms. HEAD replies omit the body. A streaming callback that panics after writing cannot append a second HTTP response to the partial stream. read_request_with_decoder accepts an optional host BodyDecoder; a complete Server accepts the same hook through Server::with_hooks. Without that hook, encoded bodies are rejected with 415 unless the host explicitly requests opaque encoded bytes. The decoder receives the normalized encoding name, bounded wire bytes, decoded-byte limit and the original absolute read deadline. The library checks cancellation and that deadline before and after decoding, validates the returned size, removes transfer/content encoding and replaces Content-Length with the decoded length. Both wire and decoded bodies have independent bounds. A host decoder must also bound its codec window and temporary allocations, and cooperate with cancellation and the supplied deadline. These checks cannot preempt an arbitrary callback. zcall contains no native decompressor or unsafe codec binding; a host can supply its existing implementation. Unix sockets and peer identity Listener::bind_unix(path, verified_uid) requires an absolute path with real directory ancestors and an existing private parent owned by that UID. It does not trust an environment variable for identity or create parent directories. The socket and stable lock use mode 0600. Non-socket nodes, symlinks, an untrusted owner or an unsafe lock are rejected without replacement. The default bind operation refuses an existing socket. A host may use bind_unix_with_probe with its bounded native liveness probe to confirm a stale owned socket. Rust's standard library has no Unix connect timeout, so the library does not hide an unbounded connection probe in the default path. The ownership guard is shared by the listener and accepted stream clones. Cleanup waits for the last guard and checks the socket's device/inode before unlinking it. A replacement node is preserved. The stable lock file remains for later binds, preventing old and new waiters from locking different inodes. A local socket location is not an OS UID/PID assertion. PeerInspector can read native peer credentials through a borrowed SocketRef. Hosts using their own accept loop submit an already verified Peer; request headers never supply it. Admission and shutdown ServerConfig fixes worker count, queue size, request/response limits and read/write/request deadlines. The built-in acceptors block in the OS and idle workers wait on a condition variable. There is no listener polling timer. Queue saturation produces a bounded 503 response. A native host can omit listen and use submit(connection, peer) or submit_boxed with any Connection + Send implementation. shutdown(budget) stops admission, cancels active work, discards queued work on tracked workers and uses one shared deadline. It returns the counts of remaining workers, acceptors and wake helpers. A user handler, upstream reader or connection destructor that does not cooperate is reported rather than forcibly killed. A later call can reap it after it finishes. The tests include both an uncooperative handler and a blocked queued connection destructor. The built-in Handler is shared and requires Send + Sync. It is not a worker-local factory for application types that are !Send. zcalld therefore retains its thread-local plugin/curl orchestration while sharing the HTTP, protocol, auth and connection primitives. Caller keys CallerKeys::from_json and auth::load retain the existing private JSON array: id, name, secret, lan and workspace, including anonymous legacy items. The parser rejects ambiguous identities/secrets, unknown fields, invalid types, excessive entries and oversized files. On Unix, load requires a regular file without group or other permission bits. entries() exposes metadata only. ApiKey, CallerKeys, provider Target and outbound request types do not implement secret-printing Debug output. Authentication checks valid keys before loopback trust so a verified key keeps its server-owned workspace. Remote peers require a key with lan permission. Insertion and rotation validate before mutation. Revocation applies to later authentication; it does not cancel accepted requests. to_json returns a secret-bearing buffer for the host's private atomic writer. The library does not generate weak random keys or force a file-format migration. KeyAuthenticator can share Arc<RwLock<CallerKeys>> for in-process updates. Host integration and evidence The HTTP/protocol extraction starts from MIT-licensed zcalld source 226764bd980419bfd123bf297b891e09ccdc94c1, retaining its protocol and staged-close regressions. zcalld can re-export server::http and server::protocol, delegate caller-key parsing to server::auth, and implement Connection on its existing stream. Its cancellation flag and JSON error name remain host choices. Signals, systemd, provider/plugin policy, privacy, migration and account storage remain application responsibilities. Local tests use only buffers, private temporary paths, loopback TCP and Unix sockets. The formal workflow runs the server feature on five native targets and separately checks the default no_std kernel on WebAssembly, ARM Linux and Cortex-M.

title: Supported operations and boundaries
body: 协议无关的模型调用内核，由宿主提供传输与缓冲区。 Supported operations and boundaries Support means the operation is connected to a real zconv adapter and exercised through zcall. It does not imply every vendor option or every model is supported. Adapter Complete requests/responses SSE source SSE target Version/profile boundary OpenAI Completions Yes, text prompt/choices Yes Yes v1; no tools or flattening arbitrary chat history OpenAI Chat Yes, text/tools/media subset Yes Yes v1; explicit compatible profile for declared reasoning extensions OpenAI Responses Yes, ordered output/input items Yes Yes v1; context and distinct output item identities remain explicit Anthropic Messages Yes Yes Yes Complete: 2023-06-01 and 2026-10-21; streaming: 2023-06-01 Gemini GenerateContent Yes Yes Yes Complete: v1/v1beta; streaming: v1beta with SSE framing Gemini Interactions Yes Yes Yes Independent v1 interactions/steps adapter The complete-document test matrix includes all 36 source/target text directions. Tool and media operations are tested against their actual representable subsets. The streaming tests use the same consumer for all six sources and encode unified events to all six targets. Different targets can require caller IDs, timestamps, usage, output budgets or explicit loss permissions. These are conversion conditions, not implicit defaults. Semantics Semantic category zcall interface Condition / limit Text and ordering Borrowed Text, messages/blocks/choices Source order retained; escaping decoded on demand Missing/null/empty/zero Presence Target must have an equivalent supported meaning Image/audio/file/video references Typed media kind and source Cross-provider file IDs remain source-bound; unsupported target forms fail Function tools and results Typed definitions, calls, results, ToolReady Arguments complete to a valid JSON object; tool execution/schema checking are caller-owned Strict function defaults Authoring/source contract and explicit strict field Responses unresolved strict defaults require explicit resolution for incompatible targets Structured output OutputConstraint / validated schema JSON Verified dialect mappings only, including Chat/Responses portable forms Reasoning and signatures Thought/summary and opaque signature Namespace and target semantics must match or be explicitly dropped Refusal and safety Refusal content and completion reasons An unsupported target fails instead of turning refusal into a successful answer Usage Exact integer complete counts, cumulative StreamUsage Cache/thought normalization is inherited from the shared tested accumulator Context references/extensions Source format/version/profile No implicit provider reference substitution Item IDs versus call IDs Separate view/event fields Cross-target stream item identity changes require explicit policy and a report Complete output snapshots SnapshotVerified Validated; never appended a second time as delta content Structured tool results Data::Content and BlockView::result_contents Typed nested text/media; authored arrays use request-owned record storage Usage preferences and emission StreamOptions, transport report, UsageEmission Continuous mode emits only observed counters; unsupported intermediate-usage targets reject it Anthropic provider content ProviderBlock, ProviderDelta, ProviderUsage Same-format replay only; server tools never produce ToolReady Resource APIs use the separate zcall::api namespace. Embeddings, Images, Batch JSONL/objects and Files metadata/multipart are borrowed wire codecs with caller-owned token and output storage. HTTP, polling, upload transport and batch execution remain application responsibilities. Explicitly outside the implemented adapter subset Unknown protocols, unknown schema versions and unsupported profiles. Raw Gemini streamed JSON arrays, NDJSON, WebSockets and network transports. Streaming media and provider event families without a verified mapping. Image resource SSE contracts, Gemini image/grounding metadata and Anthropic server-tool/citation payloads have explicit codec support; unsupported cross-provider semantic mappings still fail. A vendor's entire JSON surface or undocumented compatibility fields. Full JSON Schema validation, tool execution, tokenizer/model discovery and automatic context-window negotiation. Network/tool exactly-once semantics, retries, clocks, randomness and transcript persistence. These operations produce explicit errors when their bytes enter an implemented adapter. A string identifying a new protocol is not an adapter registration. Adding an adapter Add parsing, conversion and exact protocol semantics to zconv first. Keep the codec independent of network I/O and supply malformed/capacity tests. Register a distinct typed Protocol mapping in zcall's private adaptation layer; validate its version and profile at construction. Extend operation-specific adapter capability evidence without declaring model support. A format's ability to contain a field remains separate from model and deployment evidence. Run the existing stable request/response/session conformance flow with the new source and target. Include all byte splits, backpressure, zero capacity, terminal-once behavior, IDs, usage and forbidden-loss tests. Publish the dependency version, pin it, and pass the registry packaging gate. The release workflow never publishes a Git-only dependency. This is a statically compiled adapter mechanism: no runtime plugin loader, dynamic ABI or unchecked JSON passthrough is used.

title: 概览
body: 用于管理 zcalld 本地模型网关的原生控制面板。 zcall-gui zcall-gui is an optional native control panel for zcalld. It manages providers, AI tool settings, plugins, privacy rules, usage, service state and updates by calling the installed zcalld --json interface. Closing the window leaves the gateway service running. The application uses zgpui 0.1.5, with its public Git source pinned in Cargo.lock and the same revision recorded by the vendor/zgpui submodule. Cargo resolves only these two first-party packages; the GUI enables the toolkit's native feature and imports zgpui::native. Window creation, input, fonts and OpenGL use platform libraries; there is no embedded browser or third-party Rust crate. Build and run git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/LIghtJUNction/zcall-gui.git cd zcall-gui cargo fetch --locked cargo build --release --locked --offline ./target/release/zcall-gui Rust 1.100 and a native C compiler are required. On Arch Linux, install base-devel rust pkgconf libx11 libgl freetype2 fontconfig. On Ubuntu/Debian, install build-essential pkg-config libx11-dev libgl1-mesa-dev libfreetype6-dev libfontconfig1-dev. Linux Wayland sessions use XWayland. Management commands require zcalld 0.2.0 or newer. Use zcall-gui --zcalld /absolute/path/to/zcalld --config /path/to/config.conf to select a custom CLI or configuration. A missing CLI presents Install background service. Installation requires an explicit review and confirmation; opening the GUI never downloads or starts a gateway. Install the gateway The GUI obtains a complete native gateway from an official stable core release. It first verifies the small zcalld-installer helper against that release's SHA-256 list and checks its version and supported installer protocol. The same helper implements the core CLI's zcalld install commands. It validates and stages the full archive, including the gateway, native plugins and platform helpers, before changing an owned installation. The confirmation page shows the version, installation location and administrator requirement. New installations use a private location and do not request administrator privileges: Platform Default location Linux $XDG_DATA_HOME/zcalld/runtime, or ~/.local/share/zcalld/runtime macOS ~/Library/Application Support/zcalld/runtime Windows %LOCALAPPDATA%/zcalld/runtime After a committed transaction, the GUI remembers the actual executable path. It also discovers the default private installation on later launches, so editing PATH is not required. An explicit --zcalld or ZCALLD_BIN still takes precedence. Unknown shared or legacy directories are not adopted; an unmanaged legacy executable can be left in place while a new private installation is prepared. Installation leaves service control and user configuration separate. For a committed private installation whose selected configuration is explicitly reported missing, the next action is Initialize configuration. It invokes the core's existing init command after a fresh state check; an existing or unreadable file is never treated as missing. The confirmation identifies the configuration location. No service is started by initialization. On Linux, Install user service then verifies or creates the user unit for that exact executable and configuration. A pre-existing unrelated unit is an error, even if the service manager reports a unit with the same name. Only after this explicit check does the bootstrap flow offer Start gateway. On macOS and Windows, the core's existing service-start registration remains a separate explicit action. Opening the GUI, preparing a bundle and completing its installation do not start or stop a service, refresh an account, install a model or rewrite an AI tool's configuration. Controls Overview: see the gateway state and one next step: add a provider or connect your AI tools. Click either count to open its list; service controls stay in Service settings. Providers: search by name, model, protocol or endpoint; add or update an endpoint, select a protocol, set a default model, test it, or remove it. API keys are masked and sent to the CLI through stdin. AI tools: detect supported tools, apply a gateway route, or revert an earlier configuration change. Plugins: inspect enabled state, install a local library or pinned remote source, enable/disable, update or remove a plugin. Newly installed native code requires a separate enable action. Privacy: select off, secret sanitization, or secret plus personal information sanitization. Usage: inspect recorded upstream attempts, including retries, successful and failed attempts, input/output tokens, cache and reasoning details, and attempt success rate. The page reads local accounting on first open or when you select Refresh; other pages do not scan usage history. Enable or disable local recording from this page, then explicitly restart the service to apply the saved setting. Disabling recording preserves existing history. Older gateways without detail counters still show their supported totals; a missing recording-status field is shown as unknown. Updates: install a missing gateway, update a complete unmanaged gateway, inspect or recover an installation, or use the package manager for a managed installation. GUI updates remain separate. Tab / Shift+Tab move focus, Enter activates buttons, Ctrl+A selects an input, and standard copy/paste shortcuts work. Ctrl+Q closes the GUI. Provider rows open details on demand. Adding an endpoint uses two short steps; removal stays in the detail panel. Appearance and language The window uses neutral light or graphite surfaces, restrained blue accents and the platform's native interface font with glyph fallback. Controls, input focus and status colors share the application-local palette. It does not install fonts or change desktop fonts or other applications. The AI tools list gives each of the 16 supported tools its own vector mark and display name. Connection state and the current or saved route appear separately. Detection-only tools have no inactive connect button. Narrow windows move route actions below the tool details, and paging controls complement wheel scrolling. The route picker repeats the selected tool's mark and name. All icon geometry is bundled; displaying this page requires no network request. Asset sources and licenses record the original SVGs and native conversion. Open Settings at the lower left to select System, Light or Dark, and System, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, English or Japanese. Choices are stored locally and restored on the next launch. System preferences are read at launch and when opening Settings; there is no background desktop-preference polling. Language strings live in four complete catalogs under resources/locales. Tests check matching keys and locale fallback. An explicit session override is also available: zcall-gui --theme dark --language ja The previews use synthetic local configuration in a private native window. Overview in light mode Providers in dark mode Updates Gateway and native plugins The gateway update button prepares a fixed official release and displays its confirmation. Its saved plan is bound to the release commit, platform, archive checksum and installation location. The GUI rechecks the downloaded helper and approved plan before invoking them. Verification and recovery paths are available in Details. If an owned gateway is still running, the installation stays at Waiting for service exit. Stop it through the existing service controls, then use Complete update or Check status. A launched helper or pending transaction is never reported as an installed update. Closing the window does not cancel a helper already performing a transaction; reopening reads its local result. The prior installation and recovery journal are retained for Restore previous. The same GUI entry point is available without opening a window: zcall-gui --core-install prepare zcall-gui --core-install apply zcall-gui --core-install status zcall-gui --core-install resume zcall-gui --core-install rollback These commands return JSON. prepare obtains the official metadata and verified helper; apply is the explicit installation action. status only reads local installation state. Native bootstrap needs system curl and tar; Windows uses native file-handle security APIs to set and verify private cache permissions. The GUI and installer add no third-party Rust dependency or Python runtime requirement. A core release without the complete archive and installer protocol is rejected before installation. Managed paths remain on their package-manager update route. For AUR packages, the existing native terminal preserves package review, authorization, source-versus-binary package identity, and actual exit status. GUI executable zcall-gui --update check zcall-gui --update apply The GUI self-updater downloads only its official stable GitHub release for the current platform, checks SHA-256 and the staged executable's version, retains one previous GUI binary, then replaces that executable. A user-writable GUI can update in place. Managed GUI packages use their package manager. Linux and macOS keep the current process alive until you close it and open the new version. Windows uses a small deferred helper after the current process exits. The current first implementation is unsigned; Windows/macOS may require their normal downloaded-application approval. Releases and packages Published binaries and archives are available through GitHub Releases. Arch recipes are zcall-gui (source) and zcall-gui-bin (binary), both requiring zcalld 0.2.0 or newer. Release and installation instructions cover AUR, portable archives, staged installs and the patch-bump workflow. Development and evidence Daily checks run locally: cargo fmt --check cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings cargo test cargo build --release --offline xvfb-run -a -s '-screen 0 1100x740x24 -nolisten tcp' python3 scripts/ui_smoke.py xvfb-run -a -s '-screen 0 1100x740x24 -nolisten tcp' python3 scripts/usage_recording_smoke.py xvfb-run -a -s '-screen 0 1440x1000x24 -nolisten tcp' python3 scripts/agent_identity_smoke.py The Linux GUI has been opened on an Intel UHD GPU. The real-window test uses an isolated Xvfb display. It exercises provider stdin credentials, agent route changes, plugin activation, privacy selection and update checks against a local fixture. A separate run uses the actual developing zcalld CLI and an isolated home to verify saved providers, agent apply/restore, privacy changes and appearance persistence. Neither run calls a remote model. Screenshots contain isolated test configuration. Validation evidence records the scope and current limits. The 0.1.4 release record identifies the exact source, native jobs and published archives. The recording smoke uses a stateful synthetic CLI and a 45-second native window. It checks that enabling recording only saves configuration, restarting requires confirmation, successful restart clears the pending state, and disabling preserves the displayed history before and after another confirmed restart. It saves seven screenshots and a JSON result under _validation/usage-recording; it does not operate a real service. The native backend currently uses X11/GLX on Linux, Win32/WGL on Windows and Cocoa/OpenGL on macOS. Apple has deprecated OpenGL; there is no Metal or native Wayland backend in this version. Native screen-reader accessibility and complex-script shaping are also not implemented. License: MIT. Dependency propagation records the frozen shared-library snapshot and downstream ownership.

title: Dependency propagation
body: 用于管理 zcalld 本地模型网关的原生控制面板。 Dependency propagation Unified native library The active GUI dependency is zgpui =0.1.5, stored as the vendor/zgpui Git submodule. The application enables native and imports zgpui::native. The package name, Rust dependency key and source directory use the same name; there is no legacy package alias. The outer zcalld repository distributes this application through apps/zcall-gui. Its source pin must follow the accepted GUI commit. Project Z coordinates the library release and aggregate pins. The 0.1.2 consumer checkpoint updated the manifest, lock and vendor gitlink in e6ed24b, with local unit, Clippy and isolated native CLI-flow checks. The 0.1.3 integration introduced window-local palette and font selection for Ink. The previous GUI snapshot fixed the 0.1.4 rendering correction at 7838c3c94cf018c02bb36e17c941ca651c5c0e24. The toolkit uses power-of-two alpha textures where required by older OpenGL implementations. Its official Windows GDI Generic/OpenGL 1.1 and macOS image gates verify glyph interiors and rounded corners. These are functional image checks, not a physical-GPU performance measurement. The official toolkit release gate records that platform coverage. The default toolkit appearance remains unchanged for other applications. The unified-library acceptance record documents the local validation scope. The current manifest, lockfile and vendor gitlink select the canonical 0.1.5 source. That source shares the Linux font implementation with a source-only headless raster companion and validates packed grayscale and negative-pitch glyphs before copying coverage. This GUI continues to use zgpui::native; it does not depend on the companion or change its window, theme or CLI contract. The exact accepted source remains recorded by the gitlink. The earlier cross-platform release evidence above describes its original source; current dependency propagation has its own local validation record. The existing v0.1.3 tag remains fixed at 651aee3dc1eb43b561baafa77ce0ed12d9f3b2ff, which uses zgpui 0.1.4. The 0.1.5 dependency change belongs to development source after that tag. The native release workflow checks out the requested tag for both build and publication, and verifies that checkout against the tag before packaging. Advancing main does not change this frozen release source or its artifacts. Historical native-library correction The record below describes the earlier zui snapshot and its original acceptance. It is retained as provenance; the active dependency is defined above and in the committed manifest, lockfile and gitlink. The GUI freezes zui at 5e37fcfb791eec9ac523fc19373e95d0a513112f. Its runtime correction is 9eac4c9a2232b6cdb82a29bf6adf94f96e9412bb; the final commit adds maintenance instructions and does not change runtime sources. Cargo resolves zui-native 0.1.0 through vendor/zui and imports it as zui. The package version and Cargo.lock entry remain unchanged in this pre-release source correction. The Git submodule records the exact implementation. Historical impact and ownership The observed Project Z impact command returned zcall-gui, ztype and zui. The aggregation checkout was at 32e5e82685e107b5b1f85a32d054922a0b8cbfa6 with working-tree changes at observation time. The outer zcalld repository also distributes this GUI as a source submodule, so that relationship must be registered even though the core executable does not link the GUI. Consumer Required propagation Receiving owner zcall-gui Pin vendor/zui to the frozen commit; preserve the exact path package and lock entry; native tests and package validation GUI maintainer ztype Pin the same zui source; check manifest/lock; verify its compact window and native/source-package checks; push its result Existing ztype maintainer through Project Z coordination zcalld Pin apps/zcall-gui to this final GUI snapshot; verify its source distribution and management integration; push its result Existing zcalld maintainer Project Z aggregation Register the outer source-submodule edge; update repository pins and lock/manifest; verify impact and consistency; push acceptance records Existing Project Z maintainer The GUI side has verified real CLI actions in an isolated home, native update command wiring, the rebuilt 1080 by 740 window, and actual X11 class/size/UTF-8 properties. The shared probe also verifies ztype's 660 by 264 dimensions. Native release gates test Linux x86_64/aarch64, Windows x86_64 and macOS arm64/x86_64 before public artifacts are published. Native C objects inherit CFLAGS. The GUI's Arch source recipe disables makepkg C LTO while retaining Rust thin LTO; the real source-package build and check succeeded with that setting. Downstream source-package owners must check their own compiler/linker combination. This file records the frozen snapshot and handoff boundaries. Final downstream commit IDs, test results, and any concrete blocker with its receiving owner belong in the coordinating Project Z acceptance record and delivery report. They must be collected; publication or notification alone is not completion. Keeping acceptance records outside this source-pin chain avoids repeatedly changing the library or GUI merely to record a consumer's acceptance. Project Z is the sole crates.io publisher for zui-native 0.1.0.

title: 概览
body: 面向 Omarchy 的 zcalld 桌面入口与命令集成。 zcall for Omarchy A native bar panel for the zcalld local AI gateway. Click the bar icon to see agents, saved account limits, usage and routes. Select an agent and a model or group, then apply the change directly in the panel. The panel uses the warm graphite, linen and copper Ink palette from oh-my-ztty, with Omarchy's native keyboard focus and popup positioning. It reads local data when opened or refreshed; it has no polling loop or separate background service. Closing it leaves the gateway running. The independent desktop GUI is optional. Four views View What it shows and does Agents Installed clients, their saved gateway route, an explicit Apply action and recovery of owned changes. Detection-only adapters remain read-only. Limits Saved quota readings and an explicit Update button for accounts that support quota queries. Missing or expired readings remain unavailable. Opening the view does not contact providers. Usage Today, 7 days, 30 days or all history; provider filtering; token, request, cost and cache summaries; a native bar chart and provider rows. Routing Existing route groups and their strategies. Choose a model or group and apply it to a particular agent. There is no invented global-default setting. Refresh local data rereads the local snapshot. It does not ask providers for a new quota reading. Usage is calculated from the existing history file with bounded working memory. A partial scan is labelled. Costs use recorded amounts or saved model prices and show how many requests could be priced. A partial known amount is labelled as such; an estimate is not a provider bill. Unknown prices, cache splits and unsupported billing tiers remain unpriced. “Today” uses the local calendar day; 7 and 30 days include today. The top-right Open button focuses the optional desktop GUI if it is already running, or launches it with a bounded startup lock. When the GUI is absent, it opens the full controls. The More menu opens the existing terminal controls for service management, providers, accounts, library, privacy, plugins, logs and updates. Right-clicking the bar icon opens those full controls directly. Install the native panel Requirements are Omarchy 4.5, Python 3.11+, and zcalld 0.2+. Python uses only its standard library. Omarchy supplies Quickshell, the UI components, the configured terminal and gum. The optional zcalld-compat package provides the backend's community, OAuth, privacy and advanced-routing capabilities. Explicit quota updates require its quota capability (available from 0.1.6); older helpers retain saved readings and show how to enable updates. Register the frontend through Omarchy's Git plugin manager: omarchy plugin add https://github.com/LIghtJUNction/zcall-omarchy --yes omarchy plugin enable lightjunction.zcall --section right Enabling the plugin adds a widget through Omarchy's own bar configuration. It retains other widget entries and keybindings. The Ink palette follows the shell's light or dark preference; light mode uses darker copper for readable text. Labels use a preferred monospace family with native font fallback. These choices apply only to this panel and do not change the desktop theme or font configuration. The panel follows the display language, with English, Simplified Chinese and Traditional Chinese strings. Its optional language setting overrides only this plugin (en, zh-CN or zh-TW). The native popup handles outside-click dismissal, other open panels and the available screen edges. Arch package and terminal menu The AUR package adds the command and application launcher. The optional menu installer adds a separate Zcall section to Omarchy's normal menu: yay -S zcall-omarchy zcall-omarchy install --plan zcall-omarchy install --apply Package installation owns /usr/share/zcall-omarchy, the command at /usr/bin/zcall-omarchy, the desktop launcher and the MIT license. It does not edit a home directory from a package hook. The native bar plugin and the menu extension are independently removable; installing the package alone does not silently enable a widget. zcall-omarchy show # Native panel; terminal fallback if it is unavailable zcall-omarchy open # Full terminal/menu controls zcall-omarchy open providers zcall-omarchy open library For exact registration, preview, backup and removal steps, see installation. Use the panel Left click opens or closes the panel. Right click opens full controls. Tab / Shift+Tab move focus between controls; Enter / Space activate a focused button. Ctrl+Tab / Ctrl+Shift+Tab switch the four views. Ctrl+R refreshes local data. Escape dismisses the current menu or closes the panel. In Agents, choose Change, select a route and press Apply. The saved agent configuration changes through zcalld's existing adapter. Reload or restart that agent when prompted; the panel does not restart it or the gateway. Revert requires a second explicit confirmation and delegates to the backend's ownership checks. It does not force an overwrite of user edits. In Limits, Update queries only the selected supported account. It never falls back to another account. A timeout preserves the saved reading and offers a clear retry action. Closing the panel lets the submitted update finish; it does not restart or repeat it. The usage and quota views are snapshots. They are not a live monitor, a billing statement or proof that every configured provider is currently reachable. Provider filtering includes identities present in historical usage or cached quotas, so its options are not a count of currently configured providers. Full controls The existing terminal forms remain available for detailed work: Area Operations Service Health, start, stop, restart, enable and disable the user service Providers and models Endpoints, protocols, private API keys, model catalog, aliases and group configuration Library MCP servers, instructions and skills; agent bindings; preview, apply and revert Privacy and plugins Privacy settings; pinned community extensions; MCP endpoint settings Accounts Import, select, enable, disable and remove accounts through the backend's account store Logs and updates Local service journal and explicit update checks or installation API keys are entered without terminal echo and passed through standard input. They do not become command arguments or new environment variables. Detailed library changes first show the backend's dry-run result. Unsupported adapters and ownership conflicts remain visible errors. The frontend does not implement provider transport, OAuth refresh, masking or agent-file rewriting. Those remain in zcalld and its optional plugins. Scripts and custom configurations The panel's local JSON boundary is also available for inspection: zcall-omarchy panel snapshot --period 7d --provider all zcall-omarchy panel action agent.route --payload '{"agent":"codex","route":"daily"}' zcall-omarchy panel action agent.revert --payload '{"agent":"codex"}' # Use an opaque account ID returned by the local snapshot: zcall-omarchy panel action quota.refresh --payload '{"account":"ACCOUNT_ID"}' zcall-omarchy action status zcall-omarchy --config /path/to/config.conf action models Actions are explicit mutations. Snapshot reads do not send generation requests or refresh real provider accounts. ZCALLD_CONFIG, ZCALLD_BIN, or --config select the backend configuration and executable. A custom --config passed to show opens the terminal controller rather than reusing a panel bound to another configuration. The bar plugin also accepts an optional config setting. Remove or recover zcall-omarchy uninstall --plan zcall-omarchy uninstall --apply omarchy plugin remove lightjunction.zcall --yes sudo pacman -R zcall-omarchy Remove the menu integration before deleting its package or checkout. If that menu has not changed since installation, uninstall restores the original bytes and permissions. If unrelated entries were added later, it removes only its unchanged marked block. An edited Zcall block is preserved for review. The private ownership record lives under $XDG_STATE_HOME/zcall-omarchy, normally ~/.local/state/zcall-omarchy. Keep it until uninstall or recovery completes. Removing either frontend entry leaves gateway accounts, agent settings and service state independent. Development and releases python3 scripts/check.py ZCALLD_TEST_BINARY=/absolute/path/to/zcalld python3 scripts/check.py python3 scripts/validate-qml.py python3 scripts/validate-panel-state.py python3 scripts/preview-panel.py --output /tmp/zcall-panel-preview --theme dark python3 scripts/bump.py patch The native checks use installed Omarchy modules. The preview renders synthetic data in a separate, short-lived Wayland window and does not execute the controller. The lifecycle check uses a fake subprocess to verify lazy loading, rapid filter changes, action completion after closing and error handling. See validation and integration contracts. Routine CI is manual. The Bump version workflow supports patch, minor and major versions, then explicitly dispatches the release workflow. Formal releases check the portable tests and publish a source archive, checksums and the standard AUR recipe. Existing tags are not overwritten. See releasing. License MIT. Omarchy and zcalld are separate projects with their own licenses.

title: Installing the two Omarchy entry points
body: 面向 Omarchy 的 zcalld 桌面入口与命令集成。 Installing the two Omarchy entry points The menu extension and the bar widget are separate integrations. Installing the menu does not silently change the bar. The bar opens a native panel; detailed management uses the same on-demand CLI controller. 1. Package, application launcher and menu Install zcalld 0.2 or newer, then install the zcall-omarchy Arch package. Its desktop entry makes Zcall visible in the ordinary application launcher. yay -S zcall-omarchy zcall-omarchy install --plan zcall-omarchy install --apply The reviewed menu plan adds 18 entries in the zcall namespace to ~/.config/omarchy/extensions/omarchy-menu.jsonc. They cover status, five service actions, providers, models, agents, library, privacy, community plugins, accounts, usage, logs and updates. The plan displays the exact generated JSONC block. Installed actions use the stable package entry /usr/share/zcall-omarchy/bin/zcall-omarchy. The private ownership record is $XDG_STATE_HOME/zcall-omarchy/install.json, normally ~/.local/state/zcall-omarchy/install.json, with mode 0600. The existing menu namespace is checked before writing. No keybinding, bar layout, gateway service or agent setting is changed by this installer. Open Zcall in the normal Omarchy menu. The same submenu can be opened with omarchy-menu summon zcall. To reverse only the menu integration: zcall-omarchy uninstall --plan zcall-omarchy uninstall --apply Keep the package until this step is complete.
