Uninstalling restores an untouched original menu byte for byte, or removes the unchanged managed block while retaining later unrelated entries. It refuses to discard edits inside the managed block. 2. Official Git plugin and bar button Use Omarchy's installed plugin manager: omarchy plugin add https://github.com/LIghtJUNction/zcall-omarchy --yes omarchy plugin enable lightjunction.zcall --section right The first command installs the Git checkout under ~/.config/omarchy/plugins/lightjunction.zcall and registers its manifest.json. The manifest declares a single bar-widget entry point, BarWidget.qml. It does not replace Omarchy's bar. The enable command adds the widget to the right-hand section through Omarchy's shell IPC. This step does change bar configuration: the installed Omarchy 4.5 implementation persists it in ~/.config/omarchy/shell.json, under bar.layout.right. Its configuration writer serializes JSON, so formatting may change. Existing widget entries and the selected bar remain semantically in place. Back up that file before a coordinated desktop installation if an exact pre-install copy is needed. Left-click toggles the native Agent / Limits / Usage / Routing panel. Right-click opens full terminal controls. The panel uses Omarchy’s popup positioning and reads a local snapshot when opened or manually refreshed. Closing it does not stop zcalld. It works without the separate menu extension. The optional widget settings are config (an absolute zcalld configuration path) and language (en, zh-CN or zh-TW). With no language override, labels follow Omarchy. Changing this plugin setting does not change the desktop language. Inspect the installed plugin with Omarchy's normal plugin catalog. If the running shell has not completed a rescan, allow it to finish before enabling the new ID; do not modify the shell JSON by hand to bypass registration. To disable the button while keeping the checkout: omarchy plugin disable lightjunction.zcall To remove its registration and checkout through the official manager: omarchy plugin remove lightjunction.zcall --yes These operations change the bar through Omarchy's own configuration handling. They do not remove the separate menu extension or application-launcher entry. Final removal Remove the menu block and the optional Git plugin first, then remove the frontend package: sudo pacman -R zcall-omarchy The zcalld backend, its accounts, library and agent configuration remain independent. Source of the integration contract This implementation follows the Omarchy shell plugin documentation and the actual installed Omarchy 4.5 scripts omarchy-plugin-add, omarchy-plugin-enable, omarchy-plugin-disable, omarchy-plugin-remove and PluginRegistry.qml. The initial validation record distinguishes isolated checks from a live desktop installation.

title: Omarchy integration contract
body: 面向 Omarchy 的 zcalld 桌面入口与命令集成。 Omarchy integration contract zcall-omarchy is a second front end for zcalld. It owns panel and menu presentation and delegates gateway state to the zcalld CLI. It does not open a network listener, create a service, poll provider accounts or implement provider transport. Verified platform The initial integration was inspected against the installed Arch package omarchy 4.5.0-3. The package version comes from pacman -Q omarchy; its legacy source version file is not used as the compatibility check. The inspected official interfaces are: Interface Use Root manifest.json, schemaVersion 1 Discover a third-party Git plugin qs.Ui.BarWidget and BarIconButton Reuse the desktop's widget layout, theme and interaction qs.Ui.Panel and KeyboardPanel Native popup ownership, keyboard focus, dismissal and screen bounds qs.Commons.Translations, Color and Style Theme and translated labels, with a plugin-only language override omarchy-shell shell summon ID {} Open on the focused screen and require its ok acknowledgement; otherwise use terminal controls omarchy-hyprland-focus-app Focus an existing optional GUI before starting one omarchy plugin add/enable/disable/remove Let Omarchy manage the optional bar entry omarchy-menu summon ROUTE Open the built-in menu at the Zcall route ~/.config/omarchy/extensions/omarchy-menu.jsonc Add isolated zcall.* menu rows omarchy-launch-terminal COMMAND... Open interactive forms and detailed output in the configured terminal gum Choose entries, confirm a concrete change and collect nonsecret fields zcalld ... --json Read and modify gateway configuration through its existing controller The plugin ID is lightjunction.zcall. It declares a bar widget, with no service entry point and no polling timer. Left-click opens the native panel; right-click opens the existing full controls. It does not replace omarchy.menu, change default key bindings, or install an autostart process. Installation boundaries The official Git installation remains available: omarchy plugin add https://github.com/LIghtJUNction/zcall-omarchy.git omarchy plugin enable lightjunction.zcall --section right The independent menu installer adds only its marked zcall.* rows. It must preserve unrelated JSONC entries and comments, reject an existing conflicting namespace, preview its exact managed addition, and remove only that owned block during uninstall. User changes made after installation must survive removal. The bar plugin and menu extension can be removed independently. Normal package installation places the controller under standard system paths; it never edits another user's home directory from a package hook. Controller boundaries Every child process is invoked with an argument list, not a constructed shell command. API keys are collected without echo and passed only through the zcalld --api-key-stdin pipe. They are never placed in argv, environment variables, menu actions, installer state, or logs. Read-only screens use existing JSON commands. Provider edits, route edits, privacy settings and community plugin operations use their existing CLI commands. Agent configuration is changed only after the user selects the agent and route and confirms the concrete action. An unsupported/detect-only agent remains viewable without inventing a provider adapter. The panel runs finite, asynchronous local subprocesses when opened, refreshed or explicitly applied. Rapid filter changes coalesce to the newest choice; older output cannot replace it. Closing the panel does not cancel a submitted agent change or quota update, or start another read. An already-running finite read can finish. The terminal controller exits when closed. The bar gives a bounded, actionable error message; fuller diagnostics remain in the terminal. It does not retain raw credentials or request content. Sources Official shell and plugin reference Official menu extension sample Official plugin validator Official menu launcher zcalld controller source Implementation and validation results are recorded separately; this document describes the verified integration surface and ownership boundaries. Local panel boundary The panel snapshot command returns schema version 1. It contains whitelisted status, provider filter choices, agents, routes, groups, usage aggregates and cached quota readings. Raw account files, request messages, API keys and provider URLs are not forwarded to QML. The agent.route and agent.revert actions validate current capabilities before delegating to the existing controller. They do not restart an agent or gateway. No automatic retry follows a failed mutation. The quota.refresh action takes one opaque account ID from the snapshot, checks its current capability and delegates to the compatibility helper. Legacy cache rows without an account binding are never guessed into an account. Disabled, unsupported and externally managed credentials remain explicit errors. The action Process belongs to the bar widget, outside the popup content Loader. Hiding the panel or changing tabs does not kill it. The backend's 75-second quota action budget covers the provider request and credential checkpoint drain; QML imposes no shorter timeout. A failed update retains the previous saved quota. Usage cost_usd represents complete coverage only. The panel may show known_cost_usd for a partially priced period, alongside priced_requests / requests and the recorded or saved-price basis. The saved model catalog supplies estimates; missing billing details stay unpriced. Every dynamic Text uses PlainText. Labels passed into shared shell controls are also neutralized before presentation. The panel keeps a bounded number of local rows and chart buckets; the backend streams usage history rather than loading the complete log into memory. The optional GUI activation uses Omarchy's focus helper with the exact zcall window identity, followed by a private runtime flock during bounded startup. This prevents repeated clicks from creating simultaneous launches. It adds no persistent lock holder; a missing GUI falls back to the full controls.

title: 概览
body: 本地模型网关，集中管理提供方、路由规则与模型调用。 zcalld A native local AI gateway for Linux, macOS and Windows, built on zcall, zconv, zplugin and zsys. The CLI daemon owns transport, bounded queues, credentials and protocol conversion. Privacy, community providers, model-group decisions and desktop notifications are optional plugins. zcall-gui is a separate native application built with zgpui; closing it leaves the gateway running. There is no embedded browser in either application. The optional compatibility package supplies the Go privacy and advanced-rule workers and one lazy Bun host for existing JavaScript community plugins. zcall-omarchy is a second, independent frontend that uses Omarchy's native plugin and menu interfaces without another background gateway. The daemon reuses zcall's optional server module for HTTP framing, protocol conversion and caller-key parsing. zcalld owns worker queues, native plugin instances, upstream transport and bounded gzip/zstd decoding; each worker retains its own plugin state. Install On Arch Linux, choose one core package and add the capabilities you use: paru -S zcalld-bin # Source build alternative: paru -S zcalld paru -S zcalld-compat # Privacy model, community plugins and subscription accounts paru -S zcall-gui # Optional native desktop application paru -S zcall-omarchy # Optional Omarchy bar and terminal menu frontend Releases provide Linux x86_64/aarch64, Windows x86_64 and macOS Apple Silicon/Intel archives with platform-native plugin libraries. Linux and macOS use the system libcurl; the Windows archive includes its TLS transport DLLs. Incoming gzip/zstd requests use native codecs: distribution libraries on Linux, static zstd plus system zlib on macOS, and static codecs on Windows. These are real operating-system dependencies, not an embedded browser runtime. zcalld init # Edit the generated provider and route to match an available upstream. zcalld check --json zcalld serve The default configuration uses an Ollama-compatible upstream. zcalld does not download or execute an LLM. Configuration follows --config, ZCALLD_CONFIG, then the platform user configuration directory. Run zcalld --help for the exact local path and command list. Preserve an existing Magpie setup Migration first creates a private copy; it does not stop Magpie or change agent settings: zcalld migrate magpie --json zcalld migrate magpie --apply --json zcalld migrate verify --json zcalld check --json The importer preserves public model IDs and catalog metadata, routes, accounts, enabled community packages, the reversible privacy key, custom rules and history. It reports unresolved routes or unsupported rules explicitly. The old TCP address can remain unchanged while zcalld's own CLI and GUI prefer a private Unix socket on Linux and macOS. See MIGRATION.md for the service transaction and rollback. Credential refresh ownership matters: an active native Codex login remains externally managed and is reread for each request. The gateway does not race another process to rotate that account's refresh token. Explicit handoff requires the recorded original owners to have exited. Configure and use [server] listen = 127.0.0.1:9415 unix_socket = auto workers = 4 queue = 16 token_env = ZCALLD_GATEWAY_TOKEN [provider cloud] base_url = https://api.example.com/v1 protocol = chat api_key_env = CLOUD_API_KEY [route coding] provider = cloud model = upstream-model Put secrets in the private credentials file beside the configuration, as NAME="value" assignments. Environment values take precedence. Provider credentials and caller credentials are separate; incoming authorization, cookies and query keys are not forwarded upstream. A non-loopback listener requires a LAN-capable credential. Protocol names are chat, responses, anthropic, gemini, completions and interactions. Native per-protocol endpoint overrides accept a base URL or a complete endpoint URL. Same-protocol forwarding retains provider extensions. Cross-protocol conversion uses strict zcall semantics and rejects unsupported information loss. Endpoint Purpose /v1/chat/completions, /v1/responses OpenAI-style generation /backend-api/codex/responses Codex ChatGPT Responses ingress; shared authentication, privacy and routing /v1/messages Anthropic Messages /v1beta/models/{model}:generateContent Gemini generation /v1beta/models/{model}:streamGenerateContent Gemini streaming /v1/completions, /v1beta/interactions Additional protocol ingress GET /v1/models Public routes with preserved catalog metadata GET /backend-api/codex/models and bound account metadata paths Optional native Codex metadata; disabled until explicitly configured GET /healthz Readiness POST /mcp/zcalld/tools, POST /mcp/magpie/tools Optional community-tool MCP; the legacy address remains valid Management zcalld status --json zcalld providers list --json zcalld keys list --json zcalld providers add work --base-url https://api.example.com/v1 --api-key-stdin zcalld routes list --json zcalld groups set group/work --members work/model-a,work/model-b --mode rotate zcalld agents detect --json zcalld agents apply claude --route group/work --json zcalld agents revert claude --json zcalld plugins list --json zcalld plugins mcp show --json zcalld accounts list --json zcalld plugins quota list --json zcalld privacy show --json zcalld desktop show --json zcalld profiles save work --json zcalld library list --json zcalld library targets --json zcalld usage enable --json zcalld usage summary --model group/work --json zcalld usage export --file usage-export.jsonl --json zcalld update check --json Provider --api-key-stdin updates an exclusive credential reference in place. If another provider, header or gateway token shares that reference, the edited provider receives a separate credential slot and the other references keep their saved value. New slots avoid existing saved credentials, configuration references and environment variables. Use --api-key-env NAME to select an existing credential instead; it cannot be combined with --api-key-stdin. Environment values still take precedence over saved credentials. Invalid or oversized credential files are rejected before either file is changed. Model edits through providers add/edit --model or routes set --model use the configuration reader's INI value rules: the parsed model must be nonempty, contain no control characters and fit in 512 UTF-8 bytes. Provider model and route errors are rejected before reading --api-key-stdin, creating backups or writing files. Group routes preserve the selected model's literal quotes and surrounding spaces. Provider add/edit validates the effective base URL and protocol together before reading credentials or writing files. Route and group edits preserve the selected provider's literal name, including quotes or spaces. Configuration updates and removals recognize section headers with surrounding whitespace, while keeping whitespace inside names distinct. Managed model groups own their public route names. Direct route edits and provider model options cannot overwrite or remove a group route. Removing a member route, or a provider that still supplies a group route or member, is rejected before credential input, backups or file writes. First update the group's members with groups set, or remove the group with groups remove. These route-changing commands also reject malformed routing.json instead of treating it as an empty group list. Group definition files preserve member weight and off settings and literal route names, including commas. Explicit settings replace the selected member's values; omitted settings keep them. Invalid new weights or disabled-state values fail before files or backups change. See the group configuration examples. Agent edits preserve unrelated fields and keep exact-byte backups. Revert refuses to overwrite later user edits unless explicitly forced. Account controls operate on the actual private compatibility-host store. Community packages must be deliberately enabled; trusted native libraries run inside the daemon process. The agent library manages MCP definitions, instruction sets and skill files separately from gateway providers. Preview/apply/revert keeps exact owned bytes and refuses conflicting user edits. Skills can be fetched from an HTTPS or local Git repository, restricted to one subdirectory, and updated from a remembered branch, tag or commit. Fetching never checks out or runs repository code; later local edits require an explicit force before replacement. Community MCP uses the optional HTTP plugin interface and the same shared Bun process as community providers; initialize and ping do not start that process. Caller-key permissions remain separate from upstream credentials. Privacy runs before model-group classification. JSON and fragmented SSE responses restore masked values. If a required privacy worker is unavailable, requests fail closed before upstream generation. With compatibility 0.1.3 or later, private daily audit files continue recording detection metadata and per-agent counters; request bodies and restoration maps are not stored. Audit writes have size and retention bounds. A disk-write failure is reported without discarding a valid redacted request. Group modes include order, smart, rotate, usage, pace, weight and drain; turn affinity is bounded. Explicit upstream 429/503 responses may select another member before downstream headers are committed, with at most four total attempts. An already-started stream or an ambiguous network failure is never replayed. Advanced rules support IANA time zones, RE2 message conditions and trusted workspace conditions through a lazy optional worker; ordinary groups do not start it. Caller-key management provides keys add, rotate and revoke; new key material is accepted only through --api-key-stdin. Saved key changes require a gateway restart and never restart the service automatically. plugins quota list reads local saved results. With the optional compatibility helper 0.1.6 or newer, plugins quota refresh --account ACCOUNT_ID explicitly updates one supported account; ordinary status and quota-list commands do not refresh credentials or contact providers. Usage recording counts upstream attempts, including retries, and exposes input, output, cache and reasoning token details. usage enable validates the native observer and destination before saving; usage disable retains history. Both report whether an explicit gateway restart is required. The GUI provides recording controls, retained totals, refresh and a separate restart action. Summaries support model and time filters, scan native or migrated history with bounded record buffering, and skip records over 1 MiB, excluding LF or CRLF. usage export --file PATH preserves original bytes and refuses existing destinations. See the usage boundary validation and Magpie alignment matrix for tested scope and remaining gaps. Desktop integration is a separate native plugin, disabled by default. It can keep the device awake while an agent is working and deliver usage, balance, renewal, expiring reset-credit, first-mask and completed-turn notices. Only existing fresh observations are used; notifications add no provider polling. A completed turn requires a terminal success that was fully delivered to the client; tools, cancelled requests and truncated streams do not count as completed answers. Use zcalld desktop configure --file SETTINGS.json for explicit settings, or desktop plan --source /absolute/path/to/magpie followed by desktop sync --source PATH --expect-plan HASH to preserve existing preferences. Inspection and configuration validation do not send notifications or acquire an inhibitor. Saved changes take effect after the gateway is restarted. Windows and macOS notification identities require the native platform's explicit registration or permission step; their packaged helper never requests that permission implicitly. Services Linux user service, after configuration: systemctl --user daemon-reload systemctl --user enable --now zcalld.service journalctl --user -u zcalld.service The Linux system service runs as the dedicated zcalld user and reads /var/lib/zcalld/config.conf. Initialize that private state directory before starting it; /etc/zcalld/config.conf is a template. Both units use readiness notification, private socket permissions and a 60-second stop budget so an in-progress credential rotation can finish writing. On macOS, zcalld service start manages a per-user launchd agent. On Windows it manages a per-user scheduled task. service status queries the actual platform manager and checks gateway health. Unix sockets are used where supported; Windows clients use loopback TCP. Build, submodules and release git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/LIghtJUNction/zcalld.git cd zcalld make check make package make bump BUMP=patch make release # Or: gh workflow run bump.yml -f bump=patch Use Rust 1.100.0, Python 3.11+, a native compiler, and libcurl, zstd and zlib development libraries. On macOS, add the Homebrew zstd library directory to RUSTFLAGS so the static archive can be found. The native release workflow provides the exact Windows static-codec build recipe. Project Z library dependencies use their public Git repositories, with exact revisions pinned in Cargo.lock. Git submodules retain the matching source snapshots for coordinated development. The optional GUI, Omarchy frontend and compatibility repositories are also submodules; they keep independent releases. Day-to-day checks run locally. Formal release workflows validate five native targets, including real privacy, routing and community MCP worker calls, publish versioned archives plus SHA256SUMS, and update source/binary AUR recipes. Linux also runs the migration transaction and rollback fixtures before publication. Source archives recursively include the exact tracked submodule commits; private and untracked development files are excluded. The bump command updates workspace versions, internal dependency version constraints, the lockfile and changelog as one recoverable operation. Upgrading a shared library is a separate, deliberate change to its lockfile revision and matching submodule pin. Before tagging a Windows-specific correction, dispatch the Release workflow on the candidate branch with candidate=true, tag=<full commit SHA> and platform=windows. This runs the complete Windows build, recovery, control, runtime, compatibility and archive checks without publishing. Platform selection only narrows candidates; formal releases always validate all five native targets. RELEASING.md describes publishing and recovery. PLUGINS.md describes the SDK. PERFORMANCE.md contains measured daemon baselines, with versions and workload limitations. GUI renderer and native-platform evidence live in its own repository. No client pricing table, subscription tier or paid feature gate is built into these projects. Deployment acceptance, 2026-11-20 records the installed 0.2.4 gateway with 0.1.5-2 compatibility workers: migration preservation, real JSON/SSE generation, package provenance and full-process-tree memory including swap. Its scope differs from the historical minimal-daemon benchmark. MIT licensed. Magpie compatibility code retains upstream notices in the optional compatibility repository. Codex transport compatibility Responses clients that negotiate WebSocket transport can fall back to HTTP/SSE through the gateway. See the negotiation contract and local validation for the supported boundary.

title: Native usage records
body: 本地模型网关，集中管理提供方、路由规则与模型调用。 Native usage records The routing plugin records each completed upstream attempt when its configuration contains usage_file. This includes ordinary model routes while the plugin is enabled; a routing group is not required. The observer preserves response bytes. Enable and disable recording zcalld usage enable --json zcalld usage disable --json Both commands save settings only. A changed setting returns {"ok":true,"recording_configured":true,"restart_required":true} when enabling, or recording_configured:false when disabling. Restart the gateway separately to apply the saved configuration consistently. The commands never restart it. Repeating the same setting returns restart_required:false; that means this invocation made no change, not that the running service has been inspected. Enabling first validates the main configuration and loads the installed native routing plugin against staged settings. If validation fails, the existing configuration stays unchanged. A successful update atomically replaces routing.json, preserves its existing permissions and routing groups, and saves a private backup. A newly created configuration uses private permissions. New installations use usage.jsonl beside config.conf. Existing absolute usage_file paths are retained. Disabling moves the path to usage_history_file so summary and export can still read it; enabling reuses that file. Neither command deletes or rewrites history. Managed recording works with an empty groups array. An explicit routing plugin using the same native library and configuration file is reused, preventing duplicate usage rows. Each row contains time (Unix seconds), the requested model, selected public route in upstream, HTTP status, elapsed_ms, byte counts and these token fields: Field Source input_tokens Provider-reported input, prompt or promptTokenCount output_tokens Provider-reported output, completion or candidatesTokenCount cache_read_tokens Cached input details, Anthropic cache reads or Gemini cached content cache_write_tokens Anthropic cache creation, including separate 5-minute and 1-hour fields reasoning_tokens OpenAI reasoning details or Gemini thoughts Input and output retain their existing provider-reported meaning. Providers differ in whether those totals include cached input or reasoning. Cache and reasoning fields therefore describe separate reported counters; adding all five columns does not produce a portable total. No price or cost is inferred. Bounded collection Usage is collected from top-level usage / usageMetadata, Responses response.usage, and Anthropic message.usage. The scanner skips text and tool arguments without retaining them, so a large response does not hide its usage. It stores at most 64 KiB for a usage object, 128 bytes for a JSON member name, and 128 levels of nesting. Oversized usage objects are ignored. SSE data: fields support optional spaces, CRLF and multiple data lines; cumulative totals are merged by maximum within an upstream attempt. Each new attempt resets them. Summary and export zcalld usage summary --json zcalld usage summary --model group/work --since 1767312000 --until 1767398400 --json zcalld usage export --file ./usage.jsonl The time range includes --since and excludes --until; both accept Unix seconds. --model matches the requested route, including migrated Magpie req. Native Unix timestamps and migrated Magpie RFC 3339 t timestamps are supported. Records without a readable timestamp are excluded only when filtering by time. The summary retains requests, failed, input_tokens, output_tokens and source, and adds cache_read_tokens, cache_write_tokens, reasoning_tokens and recording_configured. The last field describes the saved recording setting only; it does not report whether a running service has loaded it. Old rows using in, out, cache_read, cache_write and reasoning are read alongside native rows. A missing token field contributes zero; historical rows are never rewritten to invent missing measurements. Requests count recorded upstream attempts, so a refusal followed by a retry contributes two rows. Summary reading is bounded to one 1 MiB record at a time. Export preserves the original bytes and creates a new private destination; it will not overwrite an existing file. Verification cargo test -p zcalld-plugin-routing covers protocol fields, chunk boundaries, large text and SSE events, bounded usage objects and attempt resets. scripts/test-usage.py --binary PATH --routing-plugin PATH exercises the native gateway against loopback fixtures and checks its persisted rows and summary. It also enables recording without groups or an explicit plugin, verifies one row per attempt with explicit and automatic bindings, then disables recording and checks that the retained history no longer grows after a restart. The usage cases in scripts/test-control.py cover mixed native/Magpie history, time and model filters, large-record bounds, private export, idempotent settings, configuration preflight failures and preservation of groups, history and modes.

title: Native plugins
body: 本地模型网关，集中管理提供方、路由规则与模型调用。 Native plugins zcalld loads optional native plugins through the pinned zplugin ABI. The gateway uses zcall for protocol handling; plugins add explicit routing and request policy without a second runtime for those native hooks. Optional compatibility plugins start their own helper processes only when that capability is used. Enable the included plugins Build the workspace or install the packaged shared libraries: cargo build --release --workspace --locked Add the following sections to the gateway configuration. Their order matters: the aliases plugin selects a route before the policy plugin checks that route. [plugin aliases] path=/usr/lib/zcalld/plugins/libzcalld_aliases.so config_file=aliases.conf [plugin policy] path=/usr/lib/zcalld/plugins/libzcalld_policy.so config_file=policy.conf The paths above are the system-package installation paths. For a source checkout, use absolute paths to target/release/libzcalld_aliases.so and target/release/libzcalld_policy.so. Configuration files resolve relative to the gateway configuration directory. aliases.conf: # Public model name = configured gateway route fast=local think=reasoning policy.conf: allow=local,reasoning max_bytes=262144 An alias performs one exact mapping. It does not recursively resolve other entries. Unknown model names pass through to later hooks and normal routing. Duplicate aliases, empty names and control characters are configuration errors. The policy plugin checks exact, case-sensitive route names and an optional request-body size limit. Omitting allow permits all route names; omitting max_bytes leaves the gateway's body limit in charge. Unknown settings, duplicate settings, duplicate allowed models and a zero size limit are errors. The included configuration contains no provider credentials. Interface and ordering The shared crate is zcalld-plugin-api. Its interface ID is dev.zcalld.gateway, version 1. Hook Input Successful result configure Explicit UTF-8 configuration Initializes one worker's instance route Selected model/route name Zero keeps the input; a byte count selects a UTF-8 replacement request Protocol ID and JSON request bytes Zero keeps the input; a byte count replaces the body observe HTTP status, elapsed milliseconds, input/output body bytes Records a completed call without receiving its content Request hooks run before routing, once per plugin in configuration order. A request hook runs before the gateway's normal protocol conversion. The gateway validates rewritten requests and keeps its own authentication and resource limits. Plugins cannot replace these core checks through this interface. Protocol numbers are frozen independently of Rust enum layout: Value SDK constant Protocol 1 protocol::OPENAI_CHAT OpenAI Chat Completions 2 protocol::OPENAI_RESPONSES OpenAI Responses 3 protocol::ANTHROPIC_MESSAGES Anthropic Messages 4 protocol::GEMINI_GENERATE_CONTENT Gemini GenerateContent 5 protocol::OPENAI_COMPLETIONS OpenAI Completions 6 protocol::GEMINI_INTERACTIONS Gemini Interactions Plugin methods return zplugin::Result<T>. Positive application status 1 means a policy denied the model; 2 means a plugin's request-size limit was exceeded. The SDK exports these as status::MODEL_DENIED and status::REQUEST_TOO_LARGE. Other failures retain their zplugin diagnostic. A load, ABI, configuration, routing or request error stops the affected operation. Every observer is called even when an earlier observer fails; the first observer failure is returned to the host for logging. Observation happens after the request, so it cannot replace response bytes already delivered. Memory and lifetimes Each worker loads and creates its own plugin instances on that worker thread. The host stores owning proxies backed by an Rc<Plugin> library lease. Proxies are neither Send nor Sync; zcalld adds no unsafe thread-sharing implementation. Each instance keeps its own counters and configuration. Aggregating state across workers belongs to a plugin designed to do so. Inputs and outputs are borrowed for one method call. A plugin must not retain their pointers. Public route names are limited to 512 UTF-8 bytes. The host accepts at most 32 configured plugins and 65,536 configuration bytes per plugin. Unchanged request hooks use an empty output slice, so aliases and policy do not allocate a request-output buffer in the host. A transforming plugin returns Error::BufferTooSmall until the output slice fits. The host grows that slice up to the configured request-body limit. On BufferTooSmall, plugin state must remain unchanged because the host retries the hook. A successful positive byte count must describe initialized output and fit inside the supplied slice. Native code runs inside the daemon with its privileges. Only explicitly configured, trusted absolute library paths are loaded. ABI checks catch interface incompatibility; they do not sandbox native machine code. Libraries use zplugin's pinned policy and remain resident until the process exits. Restart the service after upgrading an installed plugin. Write a plugin Use a separate cdylib crate and the shared SDK: [lib] crate-type = ["cdylib"] [dependencies] zcalld-plugin-api = { path = "../zcalld/crates/zcalld-plugin-api" } zplugin = { version = "=0.3.1", default-features = false, features = ["std", "macros"] } Implement all four GatewayPlugin methods, then export the generated adapter: zplugin::export!( GatewayPluginExport<MyPlugin>, constructor = create, version = (1, 0, 0), unload = pinned ); The aliases implementation and policy implementation are complete examples. The SDK also exposes GatewayPluginApi::write_c_header for C/C++ declarations usable from Zig. No Rust String, Vec, trait object or future layout crosses the interface. Changing method order, arguments or semantics requires a new interface version. A plugin package version is separate from the ABI version. The included plugins derive their package descriptors from Cargo version variables, so the release bump command updates their reported version automatically. Verification Run the plugin unit tests and exercise the actual shared-library ABI: cargo test --locked -p zcalld-plugin-api -p zcalld-plugin-aliases -p zcalld-plugin-policy cargo build --release --locked -p zcalld-plugin-aliases -p zcalld-plugin-policy cargo run --locked -p zcalld-plugin-api --example check_plugins -- \ target/release/libzcalld_aliases.so target/release/libzcalld_policy.so The unit tests cover explicit alias selection, UTF-8 names, duplicate and malformed configuration, replay-safe buffer growth, policy denial, exact body-size limits, atomic reconfiguration and saturating observation counters. The executable example loads both real libraries, applies alias selection followed by policy, rejects a blocked model and an oversized request, and invokes the observation hook. The gateway integration tests exercise plugins through its HTTP ingress. Memory and request timings belong to measured gateway workloads, not the interface's type definitions. Optional privacy and community interfaces The gateway keeps dev.zcalld.gateway version 1 unchanged. Additional capabilities use separate version 1 interfaces. A library can export several interfaces with zplugin::export_interfaces!; each interface binding constructs an instance. Plugins that share request state between bindings must arrange that sharing explicitly on the worker thread. The included adapters use worker-local shared state and never make native proxies Send or Sync. Interface ID Purpose and contract dev.zcalld.context Receives bounded request metadata. phase=request precedes request hooks; phase=route carries bounded routing metadata. Request text is supplied to transformation hooks, not copied into the metadata envelope. HTTP credentials and cookies are excluded. dev.zcalld.response Begins after final upstream headers, then transforms chunks after protocol conversion. A zero result holds output; it does not mean passthrough. The final flush is delivered once. dev.zcalld.provider Returns an owned provider-stream resource for explicitly selected community providers. The resource retains its native library and cancels unfinished work when dropped. dev.zcalld.retry Offers a next public route and an optional patch to an already filtered body. The server independently limits retry eligibility; zero declines. Request hooks run in configuration order before route selection. Managed community hooks are followed by privacy and then group routing. The gateway validates the modified request before choosing the upstream model. Context consumers choose the phase they need: community middleware starts one transaction during request; routing reads its already filtered request-hook input. Request text must not be persisted by a routing classifier. Response transforms run in reverse plugin order. Privacy restores placeholders before community middleware receives the reply, including JSON and placeholders split across SSE events. The community adapter reconstructs supported reply objects and usage for the upstream onResponse contract. It bounds capture at 16 MiB and opens the Bun process only when enabled provider or middleware code needs it. The provider-stream resource is dev.zcalld.provider-stream, version 1. Its operations are head (1), body (2), and cancel (3). Head metadata is bounded at 16 KiB; status 3 means pending. Both head and body polling return promptly so the gateway can enforce request deadlines and shutdown. Raw body bytes use a 512 KiB credit window in the Bun host; cancellation does not replay a POST. The native bridge translates the core's UTF-8 JSON body string to the host's base64 wire representation. Plugin-specific wire formats stay outside the core. Application status Meaning 3 Provider head or body is pending 4 Privacy policy blocked the request 5 Required privacy filtering is unavailable 6 Community plugin operation is unavailable 7 All members of the requested routing group are unavailable 8 Routing control or observation failed Response buffer retries must preserve exactly one logical write. A plugin may cache the pending transformed bytes and copy them on retry; it must not advance its stream twice. The host rejects lengths larger than the supplied buffer. The native trust boundary still applies: bounds checks do not make untrusted machine code safe. Install community packages The optional zcalld-compat component contains the private privacy worker and pinned Magpie-compatible Bun host. It opens no separate gateway listener. Neither runtime is started by an unconfigured core. The native adapters are supplied with zcalld; the helper package and Bun are needed only for the capabilities that use them. zcalld plugins install /absolute/plugin.mjs --name sample --json zcalld plugins install npm:package-name@1.2.3 --json zcalld plugins install github:owner/repository --revision FULL_COMMIT_HASH --json zcalld plugins inspect sample --json zcalld plugins config sample --file /absolute/private-options.json --json zcalld plugins enable sample --json zcalld plugins disable sample --json zcalld plugins update sample --revision NEW_FULL_COMMIT_HASH --json zcalld plugins remove sample --json New packages start disabled. Git revisions are immutable full hashes, npm versions are exact, and copied local packages have recorded SHA-256 digests. An optional supplied digest must match. Native packages are verified before activation and loading. Package lifecycle scripts are disabled. These controls identify what is installed; they do not sandbox code or establish its publisher's trustworthiness. The registry, options and copied authentication live beside the selected configuration, inside its private extensions directory. Public list and inspect results omit credentials and options. Importing an existing Magpie setup preserves its enabled package choices, custom privacy rules, keyed placeholders, installed model cache and historical masking records in a separate candidate. Import never refreshes live credentials. See the compatibility component's README for model availability, migration boundaries, public plugin RPC and the persistent authorization session helper. The local AstrLink Guard path is tested with actual pinned model files; other explicit model selections fail closed until their adapters are installed. Bounded member retry The independent RetryPlugin v1 interface leaves GatewayPlugin v1 unchanged. Its retry method proposes a next public route; zero declines. Its request method optionally patches the already filtered request. BufferTooSmall must not advance group counters, choose a second member or duplicate an observation. The core permits only complete 429/503 refusals before downstream headers. It limits the refusal buffer to 64 KiB, the entire request to four attempts and one deadline, and rejects repeated provider/protocol/model targets. Selection does not rerun request middleware, privacy filtering or the classifier. A started SSE stream, HTTP 500 or interrupted transport is never replayed. Sources zplugin native ABI and lifetime contract zcall semantic and transport boundary Community tool exports can be served over the optional MCP endpoint. Privacy audit history (compatibility 0.1.3+) The optional privacy binding accepts an absolute history_dir. Newly managed bindings set it to privacy/history; older bindings derive it from the settings file's parent directory. The active redact.key preserves HMAC identity. History is an audit archive, not a source of original values for restoration. The native privacy plugin uses the existing context interface to send only three bounded labels: agent (512 bytes), session (1024 bytes), and the request path as what (2048 bytes). Labels describe the caller's request and are not authenticated identities. Raw headers, credentials, prompts, peer information and workspace paths are excluded. Detection events precede provider execution, so the audit does not invent a final provider, upstream model, generation outcome or duration. Each request with detections appends one private daily JSONL record. Values contain placeholders, categories, detection methods, optional shape hints, lengths and counts, without complete original values or request/response bodies. A record keeps at most 4096 distinct values and encodes at most 1 MiB. omitted_hits makes truncation explicit while the total count remains available. Existing record bytes and ordering are preserved. No-hit requests update counters only; disabled privacy and empty configuration probes write neither events nor counters. Daily checked counters retain looked, masked and whole fields. At most 1024 distinct agent labels plus other are kept, with excess identities merged into other. Counters flush periodically, explicitly when native plugin instances drop their worker references, and again on worker stdin EOF. The flush RPC returns true only after successful persistence. The 30-day and 100 MiB JSONL retention policy removes complete days during periodic cleanup. Audit persistence is best effort and separate from mandatory redaction. A mask result can carry a fixed audit_error message with a valid redacted body. The native adapter emits a static journal diagnostic on a failure transition; shutdown obtains a flush acknowledgement because worker stderr is isolated. Required masking or restoration failures still reject the request. Writers and Linux cutover coordinate on a private lock outside the history directory: history_dir.parent / ("." + history_dir.name + ".zcalld-audit.lock"). This lock stays in place when the history directory is atomically exchanged. The transaction treats JSONL and checked snapshots separately and rejects conflicting independent changes instead of concatenating every file.

title: Native Codex metadata
body: 本地模型网关，集中管理提供方、路由规则与模型调用。 Native Codex metadata The optional community extension can serve the read-only metadata requests used by Codex 0.170 alongside the existing Responses gateway. Model instructions, account information and quota windows come from the explicitly bound Codex account. The extension does not manufacture a catalog, select the first available account or refresh native Codex credentials. This feature requires zcalld 0.4.0 and zcalld-compat 0.2.0 or newer. It is disabled by default. It reuses the community extension's lazy Bun host, with no additional listener, polling task or daemon. Supported requests All entries accept GET with an empty body and retain the gateway's normal authentication and Origin checks. Gateway path Fixed upstream path on https://chatgpt.com Query /backend-api/codex/models /backend-api/codex/models Exactly one client_version /backend-api/wham/usage, /api/codex/usage /backend-api/wham/usage None /backend-api/wham/accounts/check, /api/codex/accounts/check /backend-api/wham/accounts/check None /backend-api/wham/config/bundle, /api/codex/config/bundle, /codex/config/bundle /backend-api/wham/config/bundle None client_version is limited to 64 ASCII letters, digits, dots, plus signs, hyphens or underscores. Missing, duplicate, escaped or extra query parameters are rejected. Requests cannot supply an upstream URL. Redirects are rejected. These contracts follow the official Codex 0.170 model endpoint, model schema and backend client. Other account, task and mutation endpoints are not claimed by this extension. Changing where a client sends requests remains a separate, explicit client configuration decision. Bind an existing provider and its routes The account must already be configured for an enabled builtin:codex provider. For example: [provider codex-local] base_url = https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex protocol = responses plugin = builtin:codex plugin_account = builtin:codex#work plugin_npm = @ai-sdk/openai [route my-codex-model] provider = codex-local model = upstream-model-slug These identifiers are examples. Use the actual local provider, account key and upstream model slug. A missing plugin_account is accepted only when the registry has an explicit account_defaults["builtin:codex"]. Another enabled account is never an implicit substitute. Create a binding file containing the routes that this account may describe: { "enabled": true, "loopback": { "provider": "codex-local", "routes": ["my-codex-model"] }, "callers": { "office-client-key-id": { "provider": "codex-local", "routes": ["my-codex-model"] } } } Omit callers when remote access is unnecessary. Each entry names a caller-key ID, not its secret. A remote caller must authenticate with that key and have its own binding. The global gateway token alone does not choose an account for remote metadata. The loopback entry applies only to an actual loopback or Unix peer. Apply the binding and materialize the installed helper's embedded runtime: zcalld plugins codex configure --file /absolute/codex-binding.json zcalld plugins runtime configure zcalld plugins codex show zcalld check For a nondefault configuration, add --config /absolute/config.conf to each command. Configuration commands do not start a host, contact providers, refresh credentials or restart the gateway. Review the result, then restart through the normal service manager. For a Linux user service, use systemctl --user restart zcalld.service. Upgrading the helper alone does not replace script paths held by an existing private registry or running host. runtime configure materializes the new embedded runtime while preserving accounts, selections, options and enabled state. A normal restart loads it. Install compatible core and helper packages before enabling this feature. zcalld plugins codex disable disables these metadata routes while retaining their bindings. Ordinary Responses generation and community MCP remain independently configured. Identity and model boundaries The core supplies actual peer classification, the verified caller-key ID and loaded provider/route relationships. Host, X-Loopback and X-Caller-Key-Id headers cannot create those relationships. The optional HTTP interface requests this context with flags 3; existing flags 1 handlers, including MCP, retain their previous context. Configured provider credentials, base URLs and headers are excluded. An incoming ChatGPT-Account-Id is an untrusted consistency hint. If present, it must match the account selected by the explicit binding. Duplicate, empty, malformed or mismatched values are rejected. The hint never selects an account or grants access. Incoming Authorization is never used as upstream authentication. A model is returned only when a configured static route maps to a slug in that account's official response. The exposed slug becomes the public route ID; the upstream entry's instructions and capabilities are retained. An upgrade target uses its advertised canonical slug or its unique local alias. The upgrade is omitted when the target is absent from the filtered catalog or has multiple aliases without a canonical route. Missing instructions are rejected, and unbound upstream models are omitted. Dynamic groups and routes belonging to another provider cannot borrow a member's metadata. The filtered catalog gets its own content-derived ETag. Usage, account-bootstrap and config-bundle responses preserve validated upstream JSON bytes. No quota percentage, account or instruction text is synthesized. These are request-time upstream reads; the local quota-cache CLI is a separate interface. Externally owned native credentials are reread from their bound source without writing them. Expiry or an account change fails explicitly. The native owner remains responsible for refresh; metadata does not call loaders, refresh hooks or generation APIs. Bounds and failures Each metadata request uses the smaller of the gateway's overall timeout and 30 seconds, including waiting for cold shared-host initialization. Response data is limited to the smaller of the configured response limit and 4 MiB. Streaming retains the existing byte-credit and cancellation protocol. Timeout, a TCP reset or a full Unix-socket disconnection releases the request's own calls and cancels its pending stream. The worker and shared host remain available for later requests, and another request's initialization wait is preserved. A client that closes only its write direction can continue reading its response. Ordinary TCP FIN alone is treated as a possible write half-close; its request retains the normal response and deadline. An enabled community plugin that fails initialization makes that native host fail closed for subsequent calls. The management CLI retains partial-load diagnostics. Redirects, invalid JSON, incompatible content types, missing model instructions and oversized bodies fail explicitly. Returned errors use static categories; arbitrary upstream error text, credentials and response headers are not reflected. Successful metadata responses expose only JSON content type, cache policy and an applicable ETag. Compaction uses the Responses pipeline Codex 0.170 requests remote compaction through an ordinary Responses stream containing a compaction_trigger input item. Existing decompression, authentication, privacy, group routing and protocol handling apply. This feature does not alias an old /responses/compact path to generation. The builtin adapter preserves opaque IDs and encrypted_content in compaction, compaction_summary and context_compaction items. Ordinary message normalization remains unchanged, and plaintext still passes through privacy masking and restoration. See the official remote compaction implementation and wire item types. Subscription-credit policy The optional Codex adapter can refuse generation when a subscription window is exhausted. The policy belongs to the selected account, independently of access tokens, refresh ownership, and migration rollback fingerprints. For a previously imported Magpie account, inspect the current source policy: zcalld plugins codex policy plan --source /absolute/path/to/magpie --json The result contains aggregate counts and a plan_hash. After reviewing them, synchronize exactly that plan: zcalld plugins codex policy sync --source /absolute/path/to/magpie \ --expect-plan PLAN_HASH --json The source account must match the existing private migration map by login ID and its recorded user fingerprint. The policy's user comparison follows Magpie's lowercase, trimmed identity rule. An unknown or changed identity blocks the synchronization. This command does not import, open, replace, or refresh target credentials; a native client's intervening token rotation does not make the policy operation overwrite its credentials. Source settings can change after a migration, so policy synchronization is explicit. The stored shape is account_policies[OPAQUE_ACCOUNT_KEY] = {"codex_no_credits": true} in the private extension registry. Absence means unrestricted; a malformed present value is an error. A running compatible host reads policy for its final account selection on every request. It rechecks the policy, account enablement, and identity immediately before generation, including when it reuses a cached loader. Requests and client headers cannot supply policy. After the upgrade has materialized and started this runtime, ordinary policy changes need no further host restart. For restricted accounts, the adapter reads the fixed official usage endpoint with existing credentials before generation, using an eight-second ceiling, a 64 KiB response bound, the request's cancellation, and no redirects. It checks the account-wide primary and secondary subscription windows from that response. A known exhausted window returns HTTP 429 before generation; missing, malformed, or expired availability returns HTTP 503. Existing group fallback may then select another member. Neither outcome starts a paid retry on the blocked account. Unlimited credits or a positive credit balance do not establish subscription availability. A one-second cache and shared concurrent lookup reduce duplicate usage reads. Cancelling one caller does not cancel another caller's shared lookup; cancelling the last waiter aborts that lookup. The cache is bounded to 64 credential identities. Its in-process key is a digest of the selected workspace and the resolved access token, so different members of one workspace cannot share quota state. Cache entries, pending lookups and observed response holds use that same key. Usage checking and generation use one resolved credential snapshot. Immediately before generation, the adapter rereads the current authentication and verifies that its workspace and token still match. A change during the check stops the request before generation; the next request checks the new credentials. Token renewal therefore invalidates the short quota cache without changing the stored account policy. No automatic retry or background token refresh is added. Fixed account-wide full-window response headers can tighten a cached hold; named header families do not establish a model mapping. Unrestricted accounts add no usage request. Metadata reads remain available independently of the generation guard. See the credential-isolation validation for the shared-workspace and credential-switch regressions. This is a client-side spending rule, not a server billing guarantee. Another client, or a single request that crosses the remaining window, can change availability after the check. No official server switch preventing all credit charges is claimed. The behavior follows the account-window hold in Magpie's pinned credit policy. The local acceptance suite uses generated embedded modules, a native gateway, fake credentials and a network guard. It covers live policy changes on a cached loader, malformed policies, final account selection, concurrent changes, cancellation, metadata reads while generation is held, and a group fallback that retains request redaction. It makes no real provider request. Verification and limits Evidence Coverage Native metadata fixture Generated bundle and native HTTP plugin; explicit binding; actual peer classification; forged headers; query/method rejection; bounds; cold-init cancellation; shared failures; no host when disabled Installed Codex client fixture Codex 0.170.0 app-server parses account windows and bound model aliases; malformed usage produces a client error; no model turn is started HTTP cancellation fixture TCP reset and full Unix disconnect release pending calls; the same worker and shared host remain usable; TCP and Unix write half-closes retain responses Native compaction fixture Plain, gzip and zstd through the actual privacy worker and routing plugin; opaque IDs and ciphertext in JSON/SSE; plaintext masked upstream and restored downstream Native policy fixture Per-account policy updates, final-account selection, fail-closed quota checks, cancellation and privacy-preserving group fallback MCP fixture Existing tools, sessions and cancellation Builtin hook tests Fixed origin, redirects, malformed metadata, external ownership, bounded reads and compaction preparation These fixtures use synthetic credentials and local network substitutes. They do not exercise a real subscription, spend credits, refresh an account or change a user's Codex configuration. Passing these contracts does not establish that every Codex feature or every provider account has been tested. Installed-client acceptance With Codex 0.170.0 installed and the native build artifacts available, run on Linux: python3 scripts/test-codex-client-metadata.py \ --binary target/release/zcalld \ --community-plugin target/release/libzcalld_community.so \ --pluginctl _release/native-compat/zcalld-pluginctl \ --redact-plugin target/release/libzcalld_redact.so \ --privacy-worker _release/native-compat/zcalld-privacy \ --routing-plugin target/release/libzcalld_plugin_routing.so This separate acceptance target requires the installed client. It sends only initialization, account-rate-limit and model-list RPCs through an isolated gateway. The fixture uses disposable credentials and local metadata, verifies the parsed client values, and rejects attempted external HTTP connections through a local proxy. The portable native suite includes HTTP cancellation checks without requiring Codex.

title: Codex transport negotiation
body: 本地模型网关，集中管理提供方、路由规则与模型调用。 Codex transport negotiation Codex 0.170.0 can start a Responses request by negotiating WebSocket transport. A gateway that serves Responses over ordinary HTTP must return the client's supported negotiation result. Returning HTTP 400 ends the request before Codex can use the otherwise working HTTP/SSE endpoint. zcalld returns 426 Upgrade Required for a complete, body-free HTTP/1.1 WebSocket handshake. Codex then submits its Responses request over HTTP and reads the streamed SSE response. This follows the explicit fallback branch in Codex 0.170.0's client. Scope The gateway does not return 101 or establish a WebSocket session. This is transport negotiation for clients that implement HTTP fallback. A client that requires a persistent WebSocket session still needs a WebSocket-capable adapter. The check belongs to HTTP transport and does not hard-code an AI endpoint. It requires GET, HTTP/1.1, Host, the WebSocket upgrade and connection tokens, version 13, a valid 16-byte nonce, and no request body or transfer encoding. Malformed upgrades remain rejected. Browser Origin restrictions, duplicate-header rejection and Expect handling retain their existing precedence. The subsequent HTTP request uses the same authentication, route selection, privacy plugins, provider handling and response conversion as other requests. No provider or Agent configuration needs to be rewritten to negotiate this fallback. Validation The transport regressions exercise TCP negotiation followed by a real local HTTP/SSE generation fixture, the private Unix socket, and malformed upgrades that must not become successful negotiations. An additional installed-Codex fixture uses a temporary home and a local synthetic provider; it does not use real accounts or contact a paid model. Its result is recorded separately from ordinary HTTP integration checks. ChatGPT endpoint path The built-in OpenAI provider chooses different default URL paths according to its authentication mode. In Codex 0.170.0 provider selection, API-key requests use /v1, while ChatGPT requests use /backend-api/codex. The Responses client appends /responses to that base. zcalld accepts the exact /backend-api/codex/responses path as a Responses ingress alias. It uses the same authentication, body limits, decoding, privacy, routing and upstream protocol path as /v1/responses. Account, model-catalog and quota requests use the separately configured account-bound metadata extension. Arbitrary /backend-api paths remain unavailable. The installed-client fixture preserves each built-in provider's default path and replaces only its scheme and authority with a server inside the isolated network namespace. It asserts that both the ChatGPT WebSocket handshake and its subsequent zstd POST use /backend-api/codex/responses. Its recording proxy forwards that path unchanged; the actual gateway must map it to the configured upstream Responses endpoint. The API-key case separately verifies /v1/responses. The earlier transport fixture explicitly overrode every built-in provider to /v1. It proved negotiation and decoding but missed the ChatGPT default-path failure. The updated regression demonstrates the installed pre-alias gateway returning 404 before testing the fixed gateway with the same client and fake credentials. No real default external URL is contacted. Quota response metadata Codex can report both its default allowance and separate model allowances in the same upstream response. zcalld preserves the default x-codex family and named families such as x-codex-bengalfox and x-codex-other-v2. The Codex 0.170.0 header parser discovers a named family from its primary-used-percent header and normalizes its ID by replacing hyphens with underscores. Field Forwarding rule Primary and secondary used-percent, window-minutes, reset-at Default family and named Codex families Limit name Default family and named Codex families Credits has-credits, unlimited, balance The three shared x-codex-credits-* fields Rate-limit-reached type The fixed x-codex-rate-limit-reached-type field A named family consists of nonempty ASCII letter/digit segments separated by single hyphens. Matching ignores header-name case and preserves the upstream values. Unrecognized suffixes, empty family segments, private headers and non-Codex families remain excluded. The filter does not allocate a lowercase copy of each name; the existing 16 KiB upstream-header bound applies to all accepted and rejected fields together. The same response path preserves these fields for JSON, SSE and upstream 429/503 responses. The HTTP regression checks two named families, mixed-case names, exact numeric strings, shared credits and rejected private fields. The installed-client fixture uses separate default and named-family cases under both API-key and ChatGPT authentication. Codex records the last rate-limit update in each completed TokenCount rollout event, so each family is asserted independently against exact synthetic values. These fixtures use disposable private homes and local synthetic providers. They do not read the user's Codex settings or contact a real account. Codex account-rate-limit requests use the separate account-usage API. The optional metadata extension serves that endpoint, and its installed-client fixture checks parsed quota windows and bound model names independently of response-header forwarding. Compressed HTTP requests The handshake and the request body are separate compatibility requirements. Codex with ChatGPT authentication sends zstd after falling back to HTTP. The gateway accepts identity, gzip and zstd, decodes before routing and privacy, and normalizes the downstream request metadata to the decoded body. It removes the old content-encoding and transfer-encoding fields and sets the decoded content length. Both the received bytes and decoded bytes must fit max_body_bytes. The zstd history window is capped at 8 MiB; gzip uses a 32 KiB window. Native decoding produces at most 16 KiB per output step, checks the original receive deadline and shutdown flag between steps, rejects incomplete or corrupt frames, and frees the decoder on every exit. These are cooperative checks between native calls, not hard real-time preemption. Linux links distribution zstd and zlib packages. macOS links zstd statically and uses system zlib; Windows links both codecs statically with the same dynamic CRT as the Rust program. No Rust crate dependency is added, and standalone updates on macOS/Windows do not gain a new codec DLL or dylib requirement. Distributed notices accompany the binaries. The installed-client fixture record covers the actual Codex 0.170.0 binary with temporary credentials and no external network. Its ChatGPT case requires zstd at ingress, ordinary JSON at the fake provider, no forwarded caller Authorization, and one completed HTTP/SSE response. Separate native privacy acceptance checks masking and restoration for both encodings.

title: Optional desktop events
body: 本地模型网关，集中管理提供方、路由规则与模型调用。 Optional desktop events The desktop plugin connects existing gateway activity, quota observations and privacy events to the operating system. It adds five notification categories—usage, balance, reset, turn completion and newly masked values—and optional activity-based sleep inhibition. It is disabled unless explicitly configured. Loading the library, checking a configuration or showing settings does not start a notification worker or an operating-system action. It is an optional native library, not a GUI or a separate daemon. It makes no provider requests, opens no browser and does not refresh accounts. Quota notifications consume successful observations produced by operations that already took place. Configure and inspect Use the same --config path as the intended gateway: zcalld desktop show --config /absolute/path/config.conf --json zcalld desktop configure --file /absolute/path/desktop-settings.json --config /absolute/path/config.conf --json zcalld desktop disable --config /absolute/path/config.conf --json show describes saved configuration and static capabilities. Its scope explicitly says that these are not live daemon counters. Changes return restart_required: true; these commands do not restart the gateway or register a desktop notification identity. To preserve existing Magpie preferences, first inspect a plan and then apply its exact hash: zcalld desktop plan --source /absolute/path/magpie-config --config /absolute/path/config.conf --json zcalld desktop sync --source /absolute/path/magpie-config --expect-plan PLAN_HASH --config /absolute/path/config.conf --json plan is read-only. sync rejects a changed plan. Neither command starts the worker, asks for notification permission or performs a quota request. The native plugin accepts this JSON configuration. Paths must be absolute; state_dir and inbox must differ. The CLI supplies its managed paths when omitted from a CLI configuration file. { "enabled": true, "keep_awake": true, "keep_display": false, "usage_alert": 90, "balance_alert": 0, "reset_reminder_hours": 24, "turn_done_seconds": 30, "mask_alert": true, "language": "en", "state_dir": "/absolute/private/desktop-state", "inbox": "/absolute/private/desktop-inbox", "backend": "native" } A zero numeric threshold disables that category. usage_alert is a percentage from 0 to 100; balance_alert is a nonnegative amount in the explicitly observed unit. reset_reminder_hours is bounded to 8,784 hours, and turn_done_seconds to 86,400 seconds. keep_display applies only where the backend supports it. An optional absolute notification_helper selects the Windows or macOS helper described below. Unknown configuration fields are rejected. Notification wording is deliberately limited to category, approved type labels, counts, percentages, balance/unit and elapsed time. It does not contain account names, provider credentials, prompts, restored values or arbitrary upstream errors. English wording is the fallback; Chinese title labels are provided. This component does not claim complete localization of every notification body. What triggers each action Action Required evidence Suppression and rearming Keep awake An active gateway request lease, or a counted request that ended within the previous ten minutes The last lease releases its activity even after an early rejection, cancellation or failed retry. Disabling or stopping the plugin releases its OS inhibitor. Metadata, health and unrelated HTTP routes do not create generation leases. Usage warning A fresh, successful observation with a real used_percent at or above the configured threshold Once per source/window/reset period. A fresh reading below the threshold rearms it. Failed, stale or cached observations do not rearm it. Balance warning A fresh, successful observation with an explicit finite amount and unit, at or below the threshold Once until a fresh balance rises above the threshold. Unknown units are omitted rather than inferred from a credits field. Reset reminder Either an observed window of at least 24 hours, below 85% used and resetting within the configured lead; or verified available reset credits expiring within that lead The two branches use separate durable marks. Five-hour windows do not trigger renewal reminders. Missing window span is treated as unknown, not inferred from time remaining. Non-account auxiliary windows are excluded except an explicitly identified weekly pool. Turn complete A recognized agent and private conversation identity; a successful final response delivered to the client; no client tool continuation, truncation or incomplete/error outcome; all requests in that conversation finished Wait four quiet seconds, then require the configured minimum turn duration. A later request cancels the pending completion. Unknown protocols, oversized observations and unproven completion suppress the notification. Conversation state expires after 30 minutes of inactivity. Newly masked values A privacy producer confirms distinct new placeholders after its durable audit operation, and publishes only approved kinds/counts Repeated event IDs are suppressed. Counts are gathered for three seconds and notifications are limited to one per minute. Regex occurrence count, warning-only matches and restored response text are not treated as new values. The reset behavior follows both branches of the pinned Magpie implementation: dueReminders at 1e174f8. That source defines the 24-hour minimum, 85% ceiling, fresh-observation rule and separate renews / expires cases. It also defines the ten-minute tolerance for comparing reset times and the forty-day retention for notification marks. The plugin preserves those semantics without adopting Magpie's background quota polling. Sleep-inhibition and turn behavior are based on the same pinned awake and turndone.go sources. The implementation counts requests observed by this gateway; it does not invent activity for work that occurs entirely outside it. Platform capabilities Platform Inhibition Notifications and setup Linux A held logind Inhibit("idle:sleep", ..., "block") Unix file descriptor Dynamically loads libsystemd.so.0 and sends org.freedesktop.Notifications.Notify to the user's local session bus. No helper executable is needed. A notification service and logind authorization must exist. Windows SetThreadExecutionState on the dedicated plugin worker; optional display flag The native zcalld-desktop-notify.exe uses Windows toast APIs and an explicitly registered dev.zcalld.desktop Start Menu identity. Missing identity is reported, not registered automatically. macOS IOKit assertions for system idle sleep and, when requested, display idle sleep The native zcalld-desktop-notify.app bundle uses UserNotifications with bundle identity dev.zcalld.desktop. Normal delivery requires existing authorization. Linux's block inhibitor may prevent more than idle suspend, depending on logind and the desktop. It does not guarantee that the screen stays lit; display_inhibition remains false there. Windows and macOS display inhibition is a separate native capability. Administrative overrides, OS policy and user decisions can still prevent inhibition or notification delivery. Linux accepts only single local Unix D-Bus addresses. DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS, or the user runtime bus, supplies the notification bus. DBUS_SYSTEM_BUS_ADDRESS may select a local system bus; its default is /run/dbus/system_bus_socket. TCP and multi-address fallback strings are rejected. This also permits private-bus testing without contacting the user's desktop. Each D-Bus method call has a 500 ms timeout. The Windows helper exposes explicit --register; the macOS helper exposes explicit --request-permission. These are operator actions, not startup/configuration side effects. The plugin only invokes --notify-stdin, passes at most 2 KiB of structured text, and gives the owned child a 750 ms deadline before killing and waiting for that child. It does not pass provider/API environment variables. Toasts have no launch URL or action handler. On macOS, running a raw executable outside its correctly identified application bundle does not substitute for an installed identity. Build and validate the platform helper without registering or sending a notification: python3 plugins/desktop/native/build.py --out-dir /absolute/build-output --self-test Linux reports that no helper is required. Windows needs MSVC and the Windows SDK C++/WinRT headers; macOS needs the platform clang, Foundation and UserNotifications frameworks. No helper downloads a runtime package. --self-test checks JSON/XML handling only. Event boundary and bounded work dev.zcalld.events is a separate optional ABI v1. It leaves the existing observer ABI unchanged. configure and status are passive. The host activates the shared controller after all gateway workers initialize, or an actual request/event activates it lazily. Instances with the same settings share one controller; conflicting settings for the same state directory are rejected. A worker never owns the final strong reference to its controller. A request receives one owned dev.zcalld.request-events lease. Its three operations are response head, delivered body and finish. Early returns and retry failures still drop that lease. Held retry responses do not enter its body stream. Body observations occur after protocol conversion and privacy restoration, so a successful notification corresponds to what the client received. The observer never changes response bytes. A failed optional observer is released while generation continues. The parser uses the shared zconv stream representation for the six supported wire protocols. Each SSE frame is bounded to 256 KiB; a non-streaming JSON observation to 1 MiB; parser storage to 8,192 JSON tokens and 1,024 decoded events. Large, unknown or malformed input disables completion observation for that request. Transient parsing buffers are not written to disk. The shared worker has a queue of 128 events. A queue collision or overflow drops the optional notification, not the gateway request. Conversation tracking is bounded to 1,024 entries. The durable ledger has at most 2,048 notification marks, 2,048 seen event IDs and 512 source timestamps, with a 2 MiB serialized limit. These are application storage bounds, not a claim about total process memory. Cross-process events Privacy and maintenance helpers can atomically publish to the configured private inbox: { "kind": 2, "event": { "version": 1, "event_id": "opaque-stable-event-id", "agent": "codex", "counts": [{"kind": "TOKEN", "new_values": 2}] } } Kind 1 is a fresh quota observation. It uses an opaque source ID and observation ID, an observation timestamp, fresh / success, a bounded list of windows, and optional explicitly known balance and reset_credits. A window may omit span_seconds; it can then support a usage threshold but cannot support a renewal reminder. Reset-credit expiry is accepted only from a producer with the documented provider evidence; the consumer does not fetch or infer that evidence. Kind 2 contains only new-value counts. record_key is not required. Kind 0 is reserved for host activation and is rejected in inbox files. The publisher uses a random 32-hex-digit .json name and atomically renames a private .pending-* file after writing. Each envelope is at most 16 KiB; queued, claimed and pending files together are bounded to 128 entries and 2 MiB. The consumer claims at most 32 files per pass, scans at most 256 directory entries, and checks the inbox every two seconds while enabled. Both publisher and consumer use the same nonblocking .publish.lock for publication and claim renames. A rename therefore cannot disappear from a concurrent capacity calculation. Removing a durably consumed file only reduces the count. The consumer commits its ledger before deleting a claim. A leftover claim after restart is replayed against durable deduplication. Delivery is a best-effort, at-most-once attempt after that commit: it is not a guarantee that an OS notification was displayed. In particular, a crash between committing a mark and asking the OS may lose a notification; it must not repeat a sensitive operation or a model request. Created directories use private permissions and created files are private. Unix files are checked for ownership, links and broad permissions. Windows writes apply the existing shared private-DACL implementation before writing; this is not a claim that arbitrary preexisting file ACLs have been audited. State and payload reads are bounded, and symlinks/reparse paths are rejected. The ledger stores opaque identifiers and thresholds, not prompts, credentials or restored values. Diagnostics and verification The plugin status ABI reports activation, current activity, notification/inhibition capabilities, accepted notification count and dropped/invalid/suppressed counts.
