Static capability strings are unknown, available, unavailable, denied, identity_required, failed and record_only. notifications_accepted means the native API or record backend accepted the request; it does not mean the user saw it. A saved CLI setting is not proof that an already-running gateway loaded it. backend: "record" is for isolated fixtures. It never invokes native notification/inhibition APIs. It records bounded JSONL category/text entries, inhibition transitions and changed activity snapshots. It rotates at approximately 1 MiB into one previous log. State snapshots include active_requests, completed and suppressed; completion is the conservative semantic proof used by eligible turn observations, not an accounting substitute for gateway usage logs. The focused test commands are: cargo test --locked -p zcalld-plugin-desktop --lib cargo clippy --locked -p zcalld-plugin-desktop --all-targets -- -D warnings python3 scripts/test-desktop.py --binary /absolute/zcalld --desktop-plugin /absolute/libzcalld_desktop.so The Python suite contains five portable cases and two Linux-specific native API cases. Linux requires a C compiler, pkg-config, libsystemd development headers and dbus-daemon. One case validates dynamic symbol signatures with an isolated mock library; the other uses the actual libsystemd library and a private D-Bus peer, including Unix-FD transfer and release. Neither contacts the real notification service or logind. The portable cases cover passive configuration, all five notification categories, stale/fresh deduplication, cross-process publication locking and graceful shutdown. Host integration is additionally covered by scripts/test-desktop-host.py, including privacy-restored output, early rejection, internal retry, cancellation and semantic completion. These tests use synthetic local providers and private state. Native helper compilation and self-tests belong in each platform's release gate; Linux execution and Windows cross-compilation alone do not establish macOS or Windows runtime behavior.

title: Caller API keys
body: 本地模型网关，集中管理提供方、路由规则与模型调用。 Caller API keys Caller keys authenticate clients to zcalld. They are separate from provider credentials. These commands use the same zcall caller-key parser and mutation API as the gateway. Commands Command Effect zcalld keys list --json Return IDs, names, LAN permission and workspace metadata; never secrets. zcalld keys add ID --api-key-stdin Add a caller-supplied secret with a new explicit ID. zcalld keys rotate ID --api-key-stdin Replace that ID's secret; retain its name, LAN and workspace metadata. zcalld keys revoke ID Remove one explicit ID from the saved key file. All commands accept --config PATH. Management output is JSON, with or without --json. Unknown arguments, repeated options and missing values are errors. add and rotate require --api-key-stdin; there is no secret argument, generated-key output or implicit random replacement. The key arrives as one UTF-8 line, optionally followed by LF or CRLF, up to 16 KiB without surrounding whitespace. Supply it from an existing private credential source: zcalld keys add workstation --api-key-stdin \ --name "Workstation client" \ --workspace /absolute/project/path \ < /secure/path/new-caller-key.txt add also accepts --lan. Without it, a key authorizes loopback clients only. The workspace is an absolute, server-owned scope, not a client request header. Use a separate explicit ID for each independently revocable client. Saved state and running requests A successful mutation reports saved: true, applied: false and restart_required: true. It does not restart the gateway. Apply the saved change with an explicit restart after reviewing the result: zcalld keys list --json zcalld service restart A running daemon retains the keys it loaded at startup. Rotation and revocation take effect for subsequent authentication after that restart; they do not retroactively cancel an accepted request. list describes saved metadata and reports runtime_state: "unknown", rather than claiming the daemon has reloaded. On the first add, an existing gateway configuration without caller_keys_file is bound to caller-keys.json beside that configuration. An existing file at that default path is parsed and preserved before insertion. Create a valid gateway configuration with zcalld init first. When local trust is disabled, adding the first configured caller key changes previously unrestricted clients to key authentication after restart. Explicit trust_loopback = true retains the existing local-trust policy. A supplied valid key still carries its verified ID and workspace. A non-loopback listener must retain a LAN-capable caller key or a valid configured token_env. Revoking the last LAN key without that alternative is rejected before saved files are changed. Startup validation also checks the rest of the configuration; it does not start a plugin host or contact a provider. Files, locking and recovery The existing JSON array format is retained: id, name, secret, lan and workspace. Optional legacy metadata remains optional. Anonymous legacy entries are listed with id: null and manageable: false; changing named keys preserves them. There is no ambiguous positional deletion of an anonymous key. Key files and stable lock files must be regular files without symlinks. On Unix, secret files and locks require private permissions and current-user ownership; hard links and directories writable by other users are rejected. Writes use mode 0600. Windows writes restrict the file to the current Windows account and SYSTEM before writing its contents. Windows listing does not certify the DACL of an arbitrary existing file; a mutation creates a newly protected replacement. A configuration-directory lock serializes caller-key management operations. A second lock beside the key file also protects a file shared by multiple configurations. Locks are nonblocking: a competing operation fails clearly and can be retried after the first operation finishes. Stable lock files are not removed on exit. Changes use private backups under the configuration's backups directory and same-directory atomic replacement. Validation failures preserve existing files. A reported write failure restores previous bytes, including the case where rename completed before a durability error. If restoration itself fails, the command reports the private backup needed for recovery. These are atomic file replacements with checked rollback, not a claim of a crash-atomic transaction across two files. Backups contain previous secrets and retain private permissions. Normal output and error messages do not include submitted or stored secrets. Verification The isolated fixture suite accepts an explicit binary: python3 scripts/test-keys.py --binary /absolute/path/to/zcalld It checks stdin-only handling, metadata-only output, default binding, rotation/revocation, anonymous entries, preserved data on rejection, competing file locks and private backup permissions. On Windows the same suite reads the actual DACL of key, backup and lock files. Rust unit tests additionally inject a failure after rename to verify rollback of both the changed file and a newly created key file. No fixture uses real accounts, starts a service or sends a provider request.

title: Agent library
body: 本地模型网关，集中管理提供方、路由规则与模型调用。 Agent library zcalld library keeps shared instructions, skill files, and MCP definitions in the zcalld configuration directory. Editing the library does not change an agent's files. Apply the selected content explicitly, inspect the result, and start a new agent session when that agent reads instructions or skills only at startup. The gateway does not read this state, watch these files, run MCP servers, or keep a library worker alive. These commands run only when invoked. Start with a preview zcalld library list --json zcalld library targets --json zcalld library apply --agent claude --dry-run --json zcalld library apply --agent claude --json apply selects entries assigned to the requested agent. --kind mcp, --kind instructions, or --kind skills restricts the operation. The default is all. The result lists changed paths and counts, never MCP environment or header values. --dry-run validates the complete operation without writing agent files or an ownership record. targets reports the supported categories and instruction overrides; it does not claim an application is installed or its service reachable. All management commands accept the existing --config PATH and --json options. The previously supported library list, import, export, add-mcp, and apply commands remain available. Instructions Instructions consist of a selected named set, an agent assignment list, and optional extra text for each agent. The default set always exists conceptually and may be empty. zcalld library instructions set default --file ./shared.md --agents claude,codex zcalld library instructions create research --name Research --file ./research.md zcalld library instructions rename research --name 'Research work' zcalld library instructions use research zcalld library instructions extra --agent claude --file ./claude-extra.md zcalld library instructions show research --json zcalld library instructions show --agent claude --json zcalld library instructions list --json zcalld library instructions apply --agent claude --dry-run zcalld library instructions apply --agent claude assign --agents claude,codex replaces the assignment list. enable --agent NAME adds one agent and disable --agent NAME removes it. Apply afterwards to update that agent. An empty file passed to extra clears its extra text. link ID --file PATH reads a user-maintained source file on each apply. It does not copy the file or grant permission to modify it. A later set ID --file PATH copies text into the library and detaches the link. Removing a linked set never deletes its external source. remove ID deletes a nondefault set; removing the active set selects default. To clear the default set, set it from an empty file. Applied text is placed between zcalld:library:begin and zcalld:library:end comments. Text outside those comments remains byte-for-byte unchanged. The next apply checks that the prior managed block has not been edited. A conflicting edit, malformed marker, higher-priority AGENTS.override.md, missing linked source, or source that is also the destination stops the operation. Existing Magpie instruction blocks require explicit review before another writer is added. Skills A skill is a directory containing SKILL.md and its supporting files. Installation copies the entire directory, including binary resources and executable scripts; no script is run. Only Git's .git metadata is excluded. Internal symbolic links are materialized as ordinary files. Links outside the source, cycles, special files, and excessive trees are rejected. The files array returned by skills show --json contains relative resource names separated by / on every platform; pass those names unchanged to skills read/write --file. Absolute source and destination paths use the native filesystem format. zcalld library skills install review --dir ./skills/review --agents claude,codex zcalld library skills fetch review-remote --git https://github.com/owner/skills.git \ --path skills/review --ref main --agents claude,codex zcalld library skills create notes --file ./SKILL.md --agents claude zcalld library skills list --json zcalld library skills show review --json zcalld library skills read review --file SKILL.md --json zcalld library skills write review --file references/style.md --input ./style.md zcalld library skills update review zcalld library skills assign review --agents claude,opencode zcalld library skills apply --agent claude --dry-run zcalld library skills apply --agent claude install --dir copies a local folder. install --git and fetch --git read a skill from an HTTPS Git repository or an existing local repository. --path selects the directory containing SKILL.md and defaults to the repository root; --ref selects a branch, tag or commit and defaults to the remote's HEAD. The saved source includes the exact resolved commit, which show and list expose for review. Credentials belong in Git's credential helper, not in the URL. update NAME uses the remembered folder or Git source. A branch follows its new head; a commit remains pinned until an explicit --ref selects another revision. --git, --dir, --ref and --path can replace the remembered source. Updating a Git skill with locally edited stored files stops without changing anything; --force explicitly replaces edits present when the update starts. Files added, removed, edited or whose executable bit changes during source loading stop the update, including when --force is set. Fetching and updating save the library copy only. Review it, then apply it to the intended agents with skills apply. An update that changes an existing path between a file and a directory is rejected; the stored files and source metadata keep their previous versions. Fetch that revision under a new skill name and review it, then disable the old name and apply the replacement to each selected agent. For example, to replace review in Claude: zcalld library skills fetch review-next --git https://github.com/owner/skills.git \ --path skills/review --ref main --agents claude zcalld library skills show review-next --json zcalld library skills disable review zcalld library skills apply --agent claude --dry-run zcalld library skills apply --agent claude Git objects are read directly into the bounded file transaction. Fetching does not check out the repository, invoke its filters or hooks, initialize submodules, install dependencies, or execute scripts. Binary resources and executable bits are preserved; symlinks and submodules are rejected. Temporary Git objects are removed when the operation ends. Git is required only for these on-demand commands and each subprocess has a 120-second deadline. disable NAME preserves the stored files and assignments while excluding that skill from subsequent applies. enable NAME restores its eligibility. remove NAME removes the library's entry and its stored files; applying to an agent then removes only the previously managed copy. An unrelated agent skill is left alone. An extra file, edit, executable-bit change, or replacement link in a managed agent copy is a conflict, so apply and revert stop before changing any targets. Each tree is bounded to 32 MiB, 2,048 files and 32 directory levels; an individual file is limited to 8 MiB. One operation is bounded to 64 MiB and 4,096 output files. Exceeding a bound is an error, never a partial skill import. MCP definitions MCP entries use the imported Magpie metadata shape: { "name": "example", "transport": "stdio", "command": "example-mcp", "args": ["--read-only"], "env": {"TOKEN": "${EXAMPLE_TOKEN}"}, "agents": ["claude", "codex"] } For a remote server use transport: "http" or "sse", url, and optional headers. The library preserves unknown metadata, selected header accounts, assignments and disabled state. Selected account headers replace matching base header names case-insensitively. Header accounts and the definitions themselves are private files; listing or showing an MCP entry prints metadata only. zcalld library mcp add --file ./server.json zcalld library mcp set example --file ./replacement.json zcalld library mcp update example --file ./replacement.json zcalld library mcp show example --json zcalld library mcp show example --file ./private-copy.json zcalld library mcp assign example --agents claude,codex zcalld library mcp disable example zcalld library mcp enable example zcalld library mcp remove example zcalld library mcp apply --agent codex --dry-run zcalld library mcp apply --agent codex set is an upsert of a complete definition, add requires a new name, and update requires an existing name. add-mcp --file PATH remains an alias for mcp set. An explicit empty agents array selects no agents. For compatibility with the earlier zcalld CLI, an entry with no agents member is eligible for an explicitly requested agent. Imported Magpie entries already have assignment arrays. Transport conversion is explicit: Gemini uses httpUrl for streamable HTTP and url for SSE; Antigravity uses serverUrl; OpenCode uses local/remote and an array command; Zed uses context_servers. Codex uses [mcp_servers."NAME"] tables, http_headers, env_http_headers, bearer_token_env_var, and env_vars. Environment references stay references: the CLI does not resolve secrets into new agent files. Unsupported interpolation or transport combinations fail before any files are written. Codex startup timeouts and disabled-tool lists are supported; other agents' disabled-tool permission formats are reported as unsupported rather than silently discarded. Application matrix These are file-format adapters. No agent is installed or started by the library. Paths below are the normal user locations; supported native directory overrides are honored. library targets is the machine-readable capability report. Agent Instructions Skills MCP destination / format Claude Code .claude/CLAUDE.md .claude/skills .claude.json, mcpServers Codex .codex/AGENTS.md .codex/skills .codex/config.toml, TOML tables Gemini CLI .gemini/GEMINI.md .gemini/skills .gemini/settings.json, mcpServers Qwen Code .qwen/QWEN.md .qwen/skills .qwen/settings.json, Gemini format Antigravity / agy .gemini/config/GEMINI.md .gemini/config/skills .gemini/config/mcp_config.json OpenCode config directory AGENTS.md config directory skills opencode.jsonc or opencode.json, v1/v2 MCP layout Copilot CLI .copilot/copilot-instructions.md .copilot/skills .copilot/mcp-config.json Cursor No user-wide file adapter .cursor/skills .cursor/mcp.json Crush config directory CRUSH.md config directory skills crush.json, mcp Grok Build .grok/AGENTS.md .grok/skills .grok/config.toml, TOML tables Pi agent directory context file agent directory skills Native mcp.json; detected MCP adapter/extension settings OmO .omo/agent context file .omo/agent/skills .omo/agent/mcp.json, native Pi format omp .omp/agent/AGENTS.md .omp/agent/skills .omp/agent/mcp.json Zed No adapter No adapter native settings directory settings.json, context_servers VS Code No adapter No adapter native user directory mcp.json, servers Claude Desktop No adapter No adapter native config directory claude_desktop_config.json, stdio only Kiro CLI .kiro/steering/AGENTS.md .kiro/skills .kiro/settings/mcp.json DeepSeek Harness .dsh/AGENTS.md .dsh/skills No native YAML profile-patch adapter Shared agent directory .agents/AGENTS.md .agents/skills No adapter Windows and macOS use their native application-data locations for Zed, VS Code, and Claude Desktop. Crush uses its local application-data directory on Windows for MCP/skills and its XDG configuration directory for instructions. omp honors OMP_PROFILE/PI_PROFILE, PI_CONFIG_DIR, and PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR; OmO honors OMO_CODING_AGENT_DIR and SENPI_CODING_AGENT_DIR. Codex/Pi/OmO instruction overrides are checked. Gemini/Qwen custom context filenames are read from their settings. Pi native MCP requires a version that implements it (0.99 or newer); the CLI does not infer an installed binary's version from a directory. A detected pi-mcp-adapter uses mcp-adapter.json; pi-mcp-extension uses its documented default-home file. Conflicting extension registrations or disabled native MCP without an adapter are reported explicitly. Ownership, conflicts, and rollback library-managed.json records only what zcalld applied. JSON/JSONC MCP updates preserve surrounding keys and comments. TOML servers occupy marked blocks; unrelated tables remain unchanged. Skill copies record each file's SHA-256 and executable bit. Instruction blocks retain the exact last written text. An existing entry with a different definition is a conflict. An identical existing JSON MCP entry is left unowned and reported in unowned_equal_servers. To explicitly transfer responsibility for an identical entry, apply with --adopt-existing. That permits future zcalld updates/removal of that entry. Existing unowned TOML tables are not adopted by guessing their syntax or ownership. zcalld library revert --agent claude --dry-run zcalld library revert --agent claude zcalld library mcp revert --agent codex Revert withdraws managed content without deleting the stored library. It preserves unrelated manual content and refuses externally changed managed content. Apply and revert prepare every change before writing, take a private backup, and restore earlier files if a write fails. A per-library process lock rejects concurrent CLI writers; a changed target detected during preparation also stops the operation. Other applications do not necessarily honor that lock, so close their settings editors before applying a reviewed change. Migration and portable copies The metadata remains library.json. Body files use the source layout: library/instructions.md library/instruction-sets/ID.md library/instructions/AGENT.md library/skills/NAME/** The Magpie migration copies this body directory as well as metadata, safely materializes internal links, and privately archives mcp-signins.json. It does not apply the imported library to live agents or claim ownership of their files. Linked external instruction sources retain their explicit paths. zcalld library export --file ./private-library.json --assets ./library-assets zcalld library import --file ./private-library.json --assets ./library-assets Without --assets, import/export transfers metadata only. A full export can contain MCP header/environment credentials; it is written privately and is not printed. The imported Magpie applied record is preserved as source metadata. It is not accepted as proof that zcalld owns a live agent file. Boundaries retained from the source audit Magpie also provides market discovery, WSL target mapping, profile-specific DSH YAML patches, MCP OAuth sign-in, an MCP hub, skill routing, cloud/peer synchronization, hooks, commands, subagents and rule automation. Those execution paths are not implemented by this native library module. Imported metadata and archived credentials are retained. Unsupported application is an explicit error; enabled metadata-only automation flags appear in apply warnings. This implementation is not a claim of complete Magpie library parity. The audit of the development machine found six MCP entries (two stdio, four HTTP), no skills or shared instruction assignments, no MCP OAuth/header accounts, and no enabled library hub/router/shared-skill/automatic-update settings. No live files were modified to run the tests. Validation and source references cargo test -p zcalld maintenance::agent_library::tests --locked cargo build -p zcalld --locked python3 scripts/test-library.py python3 scripts/test-control.py Set ZCALLD_TEST_BINARY to test a specific built executable. The integration suite uses temporary homes and synthetic MCP definitions; it does not connect to MCP servers, start agents, run skill scripts, or make model requests. It covers CRUD, assignment, transport shapes, native-file preservation, dry runs, removal, conflicts, private exports, executable resources, link containment and locking. Behavior was checked against the pinned upstream source yetone/magpie at 1e174f8f9f613a920203a4658d259456fcab5d0d: library schema, instructions, skills, target paths, MCP encoding, environment references, and Pi MCP selection.

title: Magpie alignment and remaining acceptance
body: 本地模型网关，集中管理提供方、路由规则与模型调用。 Magpie alignment and remaining acceptance Reviewed: 2026-11-22 (Asia/Taipei). This matrix describes the current implementation candidate. It is a review map, not a declaration of complete Magpie parity or a release gate result. Reference and evidence boundaries Product reference: the official Magpie README and reference manual. Frozen source reference: 1e174f8f9f613a920203a4658d259456fcab5d0d. Existing integration contracts link specific files at that revision. The moving manual can describe newer behavior; it is not evidence that every feature existed at the frozen revision. The measured installation for this iteration is Magpie 0.1.2512. Its version and the frozen source reference are separate identifiers; no identical-build claim is made. Source paths establish implemented behavior. Named scripts establish relevant test coverage; their presence does not mean every platform, live provider, or configuration passed this iteration. Actual commands, revisions and outcomes are recorded in the iteration validation report. Native means implemented in this repository. Bridge means an optional compatibility component is required. Partial and remaining identify a specific boundary, not a count of missing product features. Rows differ in scope and must not be summed into a feature score or a claim of more/fewer total features. Configuration, agents and access Capability family zcalld implementation and evidence Remaining acceptance / GUI boundary Agent discovery and model configuration Native registry, atomic apply/revert and custom adapters in adapters.rs; test-control.py. The built-in model registry has 16 entries, 10 writable and 6 detect-only. Detection is not model configuration support. Verify each writable adapter against current native applications and add supported writers for the six detect-only entries. GUI Agents consumes these capabilities. Providers and model catalog Native provider CRUD/test/discovery and retained model metadata: config.rs, control.rs, test-control.py. GUI has provider management and search. One native key or key-environment binding per provider; no native per-provider multi-key pool is demonstrated. Separate provider entries are not equivalent to key rotation, cooldown and quota aggregation. Routes, groups and rules Native aliases and seven group modes: smart, order, rotate, usage, pace, weight and drain. Advanced RE2/time-zone conditions use a bridge: routing, advanced.rs, test-routing.py, test-routing-advanced.py. Group editing rejects nested group members. Nested selection, cycle detection and recursive fallback remain a gap. No dedicated GUI route/group editor is present. Profiles CLI snapshots gateway configuration, credentials and privacy settings: control.rs, test-control.py. This is not Magpie's complete per-agent model/profile snapshot behavior. Agent-specific visible-model lists and complete group/library profile semantics need separate work; no dedicated GUI profile page. Caller API keys Native list/add/rotate/revoke, LAN permission and trusted workspace metadata: keys.rs, caller_keys.rs, test-keys.py. Generation-specific model scopes, token/currency budgets and issuer policy enforcement are not established by these key-management tests. MCP tool permissions are a separate path. No dedicated GUI key editor. Management interface JSON CLI and service control: main.rs, control.rs, test-control.py, test-service-install.py. The GUI invokes the CLI. A complete authenticated HTTP management API, Web management surface and interactive TUI are not supplied by the native CLI contract. The ten writable model adapters are Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Pi, Qwen Code, Aider, Goose, Zed and VS Code. Cursor, Amp, Continue, Cline, Roo and Kilo are detect-only in this registry. The Library has a separate target matrix; support for writing an agent's MCP file does not imply support for changing its model. Generation transport and usage Capability family zcalld implementation and evidence Remaining acceptance / GUI boundary Protocol translation and streaming zcall-backed Chat, Responses, Anthropic Messages, Gemini GenerateContent, Completions and Interactions; strict conversion through protocol.rs and server.rs. Fixtures: integration.py, test-transport.py, test-native-runtime.py. Six protocol names are not proof of every source/target feature combination. Keep tool calls, reasoning and unsupported-loss behavior tied to exact fixtures. See ARCHITECTURE.md. WebSocket generation Documented HTTP/SSE fallback behavior and native compressed ingress: CODEX_TRANSPORT.md, test-codex-transport.py. Accepting a client's fallback does not implement native Responses WebSocket sessions. Session reuse, cancellation and event semantics need their own implementation and acceptance. Audio, token counting and Ollama API Generic provider configuration can address an OpenAI-compatible upstream; see config.rs and example configuration. No dedicated native audio/transcription, Anthropic count_tokens, or Ollama /api/* ingress contract was found in the reviewed routes. Ollama's /v1 compatibility is not native Ollama API parity. Retry, cancellation and recovery Bounded explicit-refusal retry and recovery hooks: server.rs, recovery.rs, test-recovery.py, test-generation-cancellation.py. Preserve the no-replay boundary for started streams and uncertain network failures. Expand acceptance only for newly introduced retry/account selection behavior. Request and token records Bounded JSON/SSE collector, five token counters, legacy history, model/time filters and export: usage.rs, maintenance.rs, test-usage.py, test-control.py. Native enable/disable works without groups and avoids duplicate explicit/automatic bindings. The endpoint records upstream attempts, including retries. Detailed end-to-end usage fixtures cover same-protocol paths; preservation of all details through cross-protocol conversion remains unverified. Cost and usage attribution Counts retain provider-reported input/output/cache/reasoning semantics; see USAGE.md. GUI displays aggregate request/token history and recording settings. No native price catalog, currency ledger, invoice reconciliation or complete provider/account/session cost attribution is established. Mixed providers' five counters must not simply be summed. GUI time/model filtering and cost drill-down are not implemented by the aggregate page. The Usage observer sees the response-plugin stream, which can follow protocol conversion. A parser that recognizes an upstream usage shape cannot recover a field already removed by a converter. Cross-protocol accounting therefore needs fixtures that compare the original upstream counters, the delivered response and the persisted record, including cache creation and reasoning. Accounts, plugins and reusable agent configuration Capability family zcalld implementation and evidence Remaining acceptance / GUI boundary Subscription accounts and provider authentication Account import/selection and optional provider runtime: maintenance.rs, community plugin, test-account-runtime.py, test-native-compat.py. These bridge paths are not a universal native OAuth implementation or complete GUI sign-in flow. Live login/refresh/revocation requires provider-specific acceptance; fixtures do not demonstrate every subscription provider. Codex quota and policy Account-bound quota/credit policy and explicit maintenance/recovery bridge: CODEX.md, test-codex-policy.py, test-weekly-maintenance.py. A specific Codex policy must not be generalized to all providers, all account quotas or general-purpose automation. Plugin lifecycle and middleware Native ABI plus optional managed/community host: extensions.rs, plugins.rs, PLUGINS.md, test-native-compat.py. Community behavior requires the helper/runtime. Native ABI support does not establish arbitrary Magpie plugin UI, marketplace, hot reload or every middleware hook's compatibility. Privacy masking/restoration Optional native redaction adapter with worker preflight: redact plugin, extensions.rs, test-privacy-init.py, test-builtin-fetch.py. GUI exposes privacy settings. Local model availability, detection quality and complete masking-history UI require their own acceptance. A settings toggle alone is not evidence of redaction quality. Library MCP/instructions/skills Native CRUD, assignment, owned-file apply/revert, backups and conflict handling: library.rs, LIBRARY.md, test-library.py. File-format support follows library targets, not the model-adapter list. There is no dedicated GUI Library editor; WSL mappings and unsupported target formats remain explicit boundaries. Git Skills This iteration adds fetch/update from HTTPS or a local Git repository, selected subdirectory/ref, resolved commit provenance and local-edit conflict checks: library_git.rs, library.rs, test-library.py. Repository files are read as objects; skill code is not executed by fetching. Marketplace discovery, scheduled updates, shared skill routing and GUI source management remain separate capabilities. MCP tools and hub Optional community-tool endpoint with permission filtering: community MCP adapter, plugin_http.rs, MCP.md, test-mcp.py. This endpoint is not an arbitrary Library MCP-server hub. Aggregating stdio/remote servers, per-server lifecycle and remote MCP OAuth sign-in are not implemented by Library metadata import or tool exposure. Library market and automation Metadata is retained and unsupported execution paths are identified in LIBRARY.md and library.rs. Market discovery, hooks, commands, subagents, rule automation, automatic skill updates and skill routing are not completed merely by importing their flags. No executable parity claim is made. Synchronization Explicit migration, import/export and selected policy/desktop sync exist: migration.rs, library.rs, desktop.rs. These operations do not supply general cloud/peer synchronization, conflict reconciliation or a remote-device management UI. MCP OAuth and provider OAuth are distinct acceptance targets. Archived credentials are data preservation, not proof that a sign-in/refresh flow executes. Similarly, MCP-specific caller permissions do not prove generation model scopes or token/currency budget enforcement. Desktop and operations Capability family zcalld implementation and evidence Remaining acceptance / GUI boundary Desktop activity and notifications Optional native desktop plugin, activity leases and completion/quota events: desktop.rs, desktop plugin, test-desktop-host.py, test-desktop.py. Native OS notification/inhibitor behavior needs platform-specific evidence. This is not a general automation scheduler or a replacement for all Magpie tray interactions. Migration and recovery Private staging, verification and explicit cutover: migration.rs, cutover.py, test-cutover.py. A successful import preserves supported state; it does not prove execution of every imported Magpie feature or authorize a live service switch. Installation and updates Native installer, package-aware updates and service installation: installer.rs, test-installer.py, test-service-install.py. Release/package/platform results must name exact artifacts. Dependency updates alone do not demonstrate faster execution or less memory. GUI workflow and appearance The companion zcall-gui repository contains src/main.rs, src/pages.rs and src/usage.rs; Usage adds explicit loading/error/empty states, refresh and enable/disable with a separate restart action. Current navigation is Overview, Providers, Agents, Plugins, Privacy, Usage and Updates. Routing, Library, caller keys and profiles remain CLI workflows. GUI unit tests and scripts/ui_state_smoke.py/scripts/ui_smoke.py cover their stated scenarios, not every native desktop. This iteration's concrete progress Git Skills: native source fetch/update, recorded revision, resource handling and conflict refusal; the focused Git cases in scripts/test-library.py cover pinned revisions, failed fetches and links. Usage correctness: bounded scanning survives long JSON, compact SSE data: fields and Anthropic message_start; cache reads, cache writes and reasoning are persisted without retaining response text. Usage lifecycle: native enable/disable preflights the plugin and saved configuration, preserves groups/history/permissions, and deduplicates an explicit binding with managed loading. GUI: Usage presents saved recording state and keeps service restart an explicit action; older CLI output without that field is treated as unknown. Provider search and refreshed layouts belong to the companion GUI changes, with native visual evidence recorded separately. Hook buffers: request-hook buffer ownership and reuse are implemented in src/plugins.rs, with focused unit cases and scripts/benchmark_rewrites.py. Performance conclusions require the run report. recording_configured reports saved settings, not an inspected running daemon. An idempotent command returning restart_required:false only says that invocation changed no settings. No performance figures or overall feature-completeness percentage are inferred from this matrix. Next priorities and completion criteria Close the everyday management loop: route/group, Library and caller-key GUI workflows; acceptance must perform real CLI-backed mutations, reload their state and exercise failure recovery. Add provider multi-key pools and generation access/budget policies with identity-specific fixtures; define cost attribution and provider token semantics before adding currency totals. Verify detailed cross-protocol usage, then prioritize native WebSocket and additional endpoints from real client requirements; require streaming, tools, cancellation and accounting evidence together. Extend Library execution deliberately: MCP hub/OAuth, market, synchronization and automation each need their own contract, lifecycle and conflict tests. Retained metadata is not completion evidence. Reconcile the remaining agent writers, nested groups and profile semantics against the frozen source and installed version. Use requirement-specific acceptance instead of counting table rows.

title: Community plugin tools over MCP
body: 本地模型网关，集中管理提供方、路由规则与模型调用。 Community plugin tools over MCP zcalld can expose the tools of explicitly enabled community plugins through its existing HTTP listener. The optional zcalld-community native plugin implements this endpoint. It shares the same Bun host as community providers and middleware; there is no second gateway or MCP daemon. The canonical endpoint is /mcp/zcalld/tools. /mcp/magpie/tools remains an alias so existing agent configurations can keep working after an authorized migration. An individual plugin is available at either endpoint followed by /<prefix>. This preserves the behavior of the pinned Magpie plugin-tools endpoint. Install and configure Install the optional zcalld-compat package and Bun, then install a plugin from an explicit local source or a pinned Git/npm source: zcalld plugins install /absolute/path/tools-weather.mjs --name weather zcalld plugins enable weather zcalld plugins runtime configure zcalld plugins mcp enable zcalld check zcalld service restart For a Git source, provide its full immutable commit with --revision. For an npm source, use npm:package@exact-version. The plugin manager records the installed content digest. Installation alone leaves a new plugin disabled. Community plugins are trusted local code with the user's filesystem and network access; their tool definitions are not a sandbox. runtime configure materializes the helper's embedded host bundle and updates the private extensions/host.json binding. It does not start Bun, load a plugin, or refresh an account. Run it after a compatibility-package upgrade so an existing binding does not continue pointing at an older cached host script. Restart the gateway after changing the loaded native library or host bundle. zcalld plugins mcp show --json zcalld plugins mcp disable The tool switch is separate from plugin provider/auth functionality. A disabled tool switch returns an empty tool list and refuses execution while leaving those other capabilities available. The running adapter reads the switch for each request. initialize, ping, notifications, and the empty-list/disabled cases do not start Bun. Tool discovery and execution start the shared host on demand. Protocol and naming The adapter supports MCP initialize, ping, tools/list, and tools/call over HTTP POST. It negotiates 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26, or 2024-11-05, following the pinned upstream transport contract. GET and DELETE return 405 with Allow: POST; there is no server-originated SSE stream. Notifications return 202 with an empty body and never execute tools. An initialization response can assign an opaque Mcp-Session-Id; this label is not an authentication credential or a stateful server session. Aggregate tool names use <plugin-prefix>_<tool>. The prefix removes the common middleware-, opencode-, tools-, page-, or agent- prefix and -auth suffix, normalizes unsupported characters, and is capped at 24 ASCII characters. Aggregate names are capped at 64 characters, with _2, _3, and subsequent suffixes resolving collisions in plugin order. An individual-plugin endpoint uses the original tool name. Disabled or failed plugins contribute no tools. Tools follow the existing OpenCode hook shape: export default async () => ({ tool: { echo: { description: "Repeat a supplied string", args: {type: "object", properties: {text: {type: "string"}}}, async execute(args, context) { context.abort.throwIfAborted() return args.text }, }, }, }) Tool arguments, descriptions, and results are not written into gateway access logs. A tool's result is returned to the calling agent without applying the AI request privacy transform, matching upstream. If the agent subsequently includes that result in a model request, the ordinary gateway privacy pipeline applies. Authorization and limits The core validates Host, Origin, and caller authentication before invoking the native HTTP capability. It forwards only selected MCP headers, the verified caller identifier, peer-loopback status, and configured bounds. Authorization, Cookie, query parameters, and gateway credentials are not sent to the tool host. The migrated private registry stores mcp_permissions by caller identifier, without gateway secrets. An empty permission list allows every tool; - denies all; magpie-tools allows this server; magpie-tools/<name> allows a specific tool. The legacy server permission name is retained for both URL aliases. Issued keys inherit the intersection of their own and their issuer's permissions. Read-only, browser-only, disabled, expired, or unmapped verified keys are refused. These rules follow upstream's MCP access implementation. A loopback request without a verified key can use the endpoint only after the core's configured local-access policy has accepted it. A verified restricted key remains restricted even on loopback. Remote requests need an accepted key with matching private MCP permission metadata. Creating or changing caller keys must also update this derived permission state; an unknown identifier does not become an unrestricted caller. The request body is capped at 4 MiB and a batch at 128 messages. The response is bounded by the gateway's configured response limit, at most 16 MiB. HTTP body delivery uses the existing 64 KiB frames and 512 KiB credit window. Tool calls have a maximum execution timeout of 55 seconds, bounded further by the gateway deadline. Caller and issuer concurrency limits use a cancellable FIFO queue. Cancelled or oversized tool operations are not replayed. Token and currency budgets are not implemented for MCP tools. Migration and plugin configuration reject those nonempty restrictions with an explicit error. They are never silently converted into unlimited tool access. This limitation does not prevent importing unrestricted keys or tool/concurrency restrictions. Migration and upgrade import-magpie now carries over the effective built-in tool switch and permission metadata. It reads plugins.yml, the persisted plugin-tools.json note, and caller-keys.json without starting community code. In upstream, an enabled plugin known to supply tools keeps the built-in tool capability in use; this effective state is retained. YAML input, nesting, alias expansion, and issuer chains have explicit bounds. To update an already staged private configuration after installing the new helper, use its actual extension directory: zcalld-pluginctl --root /absolute/staged/extensions import-mcp \ --source /absolute/original/magpie-config zcalld-pluginctl --root /absolute/staged/extensions runtime configure Both commands are filesystem operations. They do not run a live account host or switch a service. The original configuration is read only. Keep the original MCP URL until the normal migration transaction takes over its listening address; copying a URL alone does not preserve a service supplied by the old process. Verification The portable integration suite installs and enables an isolated local .mjs fixture and exercises the real native HTTP gateway: python3 scripts/test-mcp.py \ --binary /absolute/zcalld \ --community-plugin /absolute/libzcalld_community.so \ --pluginctl /absolute/zcalld-pluginctl \ --bun /absolute/bun Use the platform's .dylib or .dll and executable names on macOS or Windows. The suite covers initialization without a host, real tool results, tool errors, notifications, batches, aliases, permission filtering, disabled plugins, multiframe output, response bounds without replay, a single shared host across workers, and cancellation/drain at gateway shutdown. Owned Bun exit is checked with process identities on POSIX and an opened process handle plus WaitForSingleObject on Windows; an unrelated reused PID is not a shutdown signal. No real provider, credential, model call, or paid service is used.

title: Migrate from Magpie
body: 本地模型网关，集中管理提供方、路由规则与模型调用。 Migrate from Magpie The migration keeps the original Magpie installation available while zcalld takes over its local gateway address. It preserves public model IDs, full catalog metadata, configured routes, community packages, caller keys, privacy state and history. The service transaction is separate from copying the configuration: a prepared copy does not own the live port or refresh the original accounts. The Linux handover uses scripts/cutover.py. It requires a user systemd session, Python 3.9 or newer with Linux pidfd support, a libc/filesystem providing renameat2, the packaged zcalld user unit, and the compatibility helper. The configuration importer and gateway support other platforms; this transaction script is specifically for Linux and systemd. Advanced time, text, agent and folder conditions are preserved and validated during planning. See Routing rules and trusted workspaces for the condition syntax, compatibility helper requirement and verified workspace bindings. A rejected condition remains a compatibility gap until corrected; migration does not silently drop it. 1. Install the candidate and create a private copy Install the core and compatibility packages before preparing the transaction. Their installed paths are: Component Installed path Gateway /usr/bin/zcalld Compatibility helper /usr/lib/zcalld-compat/zcalld-pluginctl Privacy worker /usr/lib/zcalld-compat/zcalld-privacy User service zcalld.service Keep the original Magpie package and executable installed. Do not start the new user service yet, and do not rewrite existing agent configurations to perform this handover. Existing callers can continue using TCP port 3425; zcalld's own local clients prefer its private Unix socket. First inspect the importer report: zcalld migrate magpie --json For a complete copy of the currently visible catalog, save Magpie's local metadata response in a private directory. This is a GET request and does not ask a provider to generate a response: umask 077 zcalld_migration_files="$HOME/.local/state/zcalld/migration-input" mkdir -p "$zcalld_migration_files" curl --fail --silent --show-error \ http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1/models \ > "$zcalld_migration_files/live-models.json" zcalld migrate magpie \ --source "$HOME/.config/magpie" \ --catalog "$zcalld_migration_files/live-models.json" \ --config "$HOME/.config/zcalld/config.conf" \ --apply --json The destination must be new. The importer refuses to replace an existing configuration; keep an existing staged migration and review it rather than running another import over it. If the original providers, plugins, caller keys or relevant privacy settings have changed since the copy, create a fresh candidate before preparing the service transaction. Import planning rejects mapped upstream model IDs that are empty, contain control characters or exceed 512 UTF-8 bytes. Catalog and plugin model values remain literal strings when written to INI: quotes, backslashes and surrounding spaces are preserved, so reloading the imported configuration selects the same upstream model. Inspect the report and check the actual configuration: zcalld migrate verify --config "$HOME/.config/zcalld/config.conf" --json zcalld check --config "$HOME/.config/zcalld/config.conf" --json The service transaction requires zero unresolved models and zero reported compatibility limitations. A successful configuration check validates configuration and native plugin loading. It does not establish that every remote account can currently generate a response. The copied privacy configuration must refer to the installed worker, and its key must remain the same as the original key. The community host configuration must reference existing Bun, host and Pi files. The importer materializes its runtime modules under the new configuration's extensions directory. A candidate created with a development helper may still point its privacy worker at a source checkout; update that path to the installed worker before preparation. Google installed-application OAuth credentials, when required by an existing login, belong in the private migration input. They are not embedded in the public repository. An account without its matching OAuth client configuration needs that configuration before it can refresh. The importer also copies library metadata and the complete instruction-set, instruction and skill bodies under the original library directory. Internal file and directory links are materialized as ordinary private files; links outside the library and directory cycles stop the import. Helper scripts keep owner-only execution permission, but migration never runs them. The copied data therefore remains available after the original application is removed. Original MCP OAuth sign-in state is preserved in the private snapshot and in migration-archive/mcp-signins.json when present. Retaining that state does not activate an MCP authorization flow or claim that a new MCP host is already connected. On Arch Linux, compatibility executables and their bundled resources live in /usr/lib/zcalld-compat. The older libexec layout is still recognized. A saved privacy or routing worker path is redirected only when it exactly names the old default, that path is absent, and the new installed helper is executable. This lookup does not rewrite private configuration or completed recovery journals; custom paths and existing filesystem nodes remain authoritative. 2. Prepare the recovery journal Run the script as the desktop user who owns Magpie, without sudo. Choose the actual Magpie main PID that owns port 3425. The script checks the executable, UID, process start identity and open listening socket; it does not select a process merely by its name. magpie_main_pid=REPLACE_WITH_VERIFIED_MAIN_PID zcalld_cutover_state="$HOME/.local/state/zcalld/cutover-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)" python3 scripts/cutover.py prepare \ --source "$HOME/.config/magpie" \ --config "$HOME/.config/zcalld/config.conf" \ --binary /usr/bin/zcalld \ --pluginctl /usr/lib/zcalld-compat/zcalld-pluginctl \ --magpie-pid "$magpie_main_pid" \ --state "$zcalld_cutover_state" The state directory must not exist yet. Preparation creates it with mode 0700 and writes journal files with mode 0600. It also saves a complete executable recovery.py copy with mode 0700 and records its SHA256 in the journal; moving or removing the source checkout does not remove the recovery program. It records the original launch, process identity, binary hashes, service state, catalog and credential fingerprints. When an enabled, assigned library entry uses Magpie's exact local /mcp/magpie/tools endpoint on port 3425, it also saves the negotiated MCP protocol and complete tool definitions in private expected-mcp.json. An empty tool directory is a valid baseline. The original launch environment can contain secrets: keep the whole journal private and do not commit it or attach it to a public issue. If Magpie is already managed by a user service, add its exact unit with --old-unit. If a private native Codex owner manifest has been recorded, add --external-owners with its absolute path. That manifest identifies independent processes by boot ID, PID and start time. They are excluded from the old gateway subtree and are not stopped by the transaction. Preparation checks all of the following: The source and destination are separate, and the candidate records the expected source and migration snapshot. The new user service is installed and inactive. The candidate preserves TCP port 3425, explicitly trusts local callers and enables a Unix socket. The live Magpie catalog and candidate catalog contain identical complete model objects, including metadata fields. Source topology, including the MCP library, and relevant privacy settings still match the copied snapshot. An assigned Magpie MCP entry completes initialization, ping and tool listing against the still-running original service. Other URLs, ports and paths are not probed or rebound. Candidate community credentials have not been used or changed since import. The candidate privacy history still matches its snapshot, its effective history path is private and expected, and active privacy key identities match. Runtime files and installed binaries exist, and the configuration check succeeds. Preparation writes the private journal and performs local checks. It leaves Magpie running and does not start a candidate daemon or compatibility worker. If preparation fails, correct the reported condition and use a new state directory; a failed preparation has not switched the service. Review the state before proceeding: python3 "$zcalld_cutover_state/recovery.py" status --state "$zcalld_cutover_state" The phase must be prepared. A binary or configuration update after this point requires a fresh preparation, because apply verifies the recorded hashes again. 3. Apply the handover The apply command performs the authorized service switch: python3 "$zcalld_cutover_state/recovery.py" apply --state "$zcalld_cutover_state" It records each transition before making the corresponding change: Phase Action pausing_old Back up the original autostart entry, install a reversible Hidden=true override, and disable an explicitly supplied old unit. Send SIGTERM only to the verified Magpie main process. old_stopped Wait for the recorded gateway subtree, including its credential worker, to exit. Confirm that TCP 3425 is free. synchronized Copy the final privacy audit history, community authentication state and usage tail; run a fresh, local import-builtin using the installed helper. starting_new Add a reversible user-service drop-in for the chosen binary and configuration, then start zcalld. active Verify TCP and Unix health, socket ownership and mode 0600, every model object's full metadata and, when retained, the MCP protocol and complete tool definitions over both transports; then enable the user service and mark the migration complete. The wait is bounded, with a default of 90 seconds and an optional preparation --timeout from 60 through 600 seconds. The script does not send a forced kill to the recorded gateway or credential workers. Its service drop-in uses KillMode=mixed, a 60-second stop timeout and SendSIGKILL=no so an incomplete drain remains visible. There is a short interruption between releasing and rebinding port 3425. Requests already in progress depend on the old application's shutdown behavior. The transaction does not replay them or send a test generation request. Its verification requests are limited to local health, model metadata and the retained MCP endpoint's initialization, initialized notification, ping and tools/list. They never execute tools/call. The MCP check follows session headers and catalog pagination, accepts empty catalogs and compares every tool definition independently of list order. It currently requires finite JSON metadata responses; an incompatible response, rejection, protocol change or tool metadata mismatch fails activation and enters rollback. A failed apply attempts rollback automatically. An interrupted apply is recovered with the explicit rollback command below; do not start a second transaction against the same partially switched state. Privacy history during handover Privacy history is an audit record, not the dictionary that restores placeholders. Magpie stores placeholder metadata in daily files; original values and surrounding request text remain in process memory. The active redact.key makes placeholder labels stable. Copying history cannot reconstruct values that an exited process held only in memory. These distinctions follow the upstream record format and writer. The compatibility worker's optional history_dir must resolve to the candidate's privacy/history. When the setting is absent or empty, it is derived from the directory containing its settings file. Preparation checks that effective path and records the worker binding's fingerprint. Continuing audit collection requires a compatibility worker with audit support; the older 0.1.2 worker preserved the imported archive but did not produce new records. Entry Transaction handling YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl Preserve complete JSON-object lines and their original byte order. Record keys can be out of order when concurrent requests finish in a different order. checked-YYYY-MM-DD.json Preserve the whole counter object. These files are replaced atomically, rather than appended. A historical redact.key inside the history directory Preserve and fingerprint it as an immutable, opaque file. It is separate from the candidate's active privacy/redact.key. A stable sibling lock, such as privacy/.history.zcalld-audit.lock Validate it and acquire it without blocking. It stays outside the exchanged directory and is never part of the copied history. The original application can append a completed request, create a new day, prune an old day or clear and recreate a day. Its checked counters use a timer and whole-file replacement. The transaction therefore compares complete file manifests; it does not concatenate every file or rewrite records into a guessed common schema. Preparation requires the candidate history to match the migration snapshot, and the source, snapshot and active candidate key to match. The original application may continue updating its own history while it runs. After its recorded processes have drained, apply captures the final complete history and publishes it to the candidate. It rejects a candidate that changed under another writer. Rollback uses that final handover history as its base. After the new worker drains, it captures the candidate's complete final history. The original directory must still equal the recorded base, or already equal the result of this same interrupted rollback. If both applications' copies changed independently, the script stops for review instead of overwriting one side or guessing a merge. Accepted single-owner changes include appended records, new days, whole-day pruning or clearing, and checked-counter replacement. After drain, synchronization creates a private sibling lock when needed and holds both source and destination locks through staging, exchange, post-checks and the durable journal update. A writer that opened the lock before an exchange and a writer opening it afterwards therefore contend on the same inode. Preparation only checks existing locks and creates no source state. Publication uses Linux renameat2: a complete private staging directory is exchanged atomically with an existing history directory, or published without replacement when no directory existed. The journal is saved before the exchange. The displaced directory remains a private recovery copy, so an interruption does not leave a half-copied live history. A retry recognizes the before/after fingerprints and does not append the same records again. Recovery copies normally stay inside the transaction directory; if that directory is on a different filesystem, an adjacent private directory is recorded in the journal to keep the exchange atomic. Retain those recorded recovery directories together with the journal. Unknown entries, symlinks, hard links, non-private files, incomplete JSONL, an active writer lock or a changed key stop the operation. The parser is bounded to 4,096 files, 512 MiB in total, 16 MiB per JSONL record and 8 MiB per checked-counter file. No history contents or key bytes are printed. The transaction can preserve only state that the original application wrote to disk. Magpie's in-flight records and timer-held counters may not be persisted when it exits; waiting for process termination does not reconstruct those in-memory values. Credential refresh ownership A refresh token may change when it is used. Two independently refreshing copies can leave one application with an invalid token, so account ownership is part of the handover. Community and gateway-owned builtin accounts are copied again only after the original gateway and its recorded worker have exited. The final builtin import uses the installed helper, so its embedded adapters match the compatibility package. An existing native Codex login remains externally managed. Its adapter reads the current native auth file for each request and does not refresh that account independently. Existing native Codex sessions keep running, and their default provider and model settings are unchanged. They do not block installation or the gateway switch. Externally managed ownership is an explicit delivered state. If its current access token expires, the original native owner must refresh it, or ownership must be handed over deliberately after those owners exit. The gateway does not automatically claim ownership in the background. The separate handoff command requires the account selector and its private owner manifest: /usr/lib/zcalld-compat/zcalld-pluginctl \ --root "$HOME/.config/zcalld/extensions" \ handoff --account 'builtin:codex#ACCOUNT_SLOT' \ --owners /absolute/private/codex-owner-manifest.json \ --json Replace the selector with the actual imported key. Handoff checks the source account, reads the latest native authentication state and verifies that the recorded processes have exited using their full process identities. The transaction itself does not invoke handoff. Automatic rollback also skips externally managed Codex accounts. 4. Roll back while preserving new state Keep the journal for as long as rollback may be needed: python3 "$zcalld_cutover_state/recovery.py" rollback --state "$zcalld_cutover_state" Rollback first stops zcalld and waits for the service's recorded processes and credential worker to drain. Only then does it synchronize credentials and history, restore the original launch files and service enablement, and restart Magpie. The rollback data handling is deliberate: Data Rollback behavior Gateway-owned builtin authentication The helper validates source fingerprints and writes back the current compatible tokens. Externally managed native Codex authentication Skipped; the native auth file and owner remain unchanged. Community authentication Copy current account values back only if the source fingerprint is still the one recorded at handover, or already equals the desired value from an interrupted rollback. Privacy keys Keep their recorded identities; a changed active or archived fallback key requires review. No key is regenerated or overwritten. Privacy audit history Publish the new worker's final complete history only while the original still matches the handover base or this rollback's already-applied result. Preserve the displaced tree as a private recovery copy. Existing usage Preserve the original imported JSONL prefix byte for byte. Usage recorded by zcalld Append converted Magpie rows using t, in, out and ms, retaining the complete original row under zcalld_record and a transaction/offset marker. Unknown cache accounting stays explicit. Autostart and unit overrides Restore the saved files only if their current content still matches the transaction's own replacement. Original executable Verify that its contents still match the recorded binary before launching it. Restoring an old directory snapshot alone is insufficient after token rotation: that snapshot may contain an expired refresh token. Rollback therefore synchronizes current credentials before restarting the original application. Keep original packages installed until the migration has been accepted. For an original desktop launch, the script restores the recorded executable, arguments, working directory and environment through a temporary user systemd unit. It also restores the autostart file for future logins. For an explicitly supplied old unit, it restores that unit's enablement and starts it again. Rollback is resumable. If a credential or privacy-history source changed under another owner, a key changed, a process did not drain, a usage ledger no longer has the expected prefix, or a launch file was edited independently, the script records recovery_required and stops before the conflicting overwrite or restart. Inspect the private journal and commands.log, resolve that specific conflict, and rerun rollback with the same state directory. Do not replace current account files with their stale snapshots. A completed rollback reports rolled_back. Repeating it is a no-op. Verification and scope Run the isolated transaction tests with: python3 scripts/test-cutover.py These tests use temporary files, a fake service controller and temporary loopback/Unix HTTP servers. They cover final source-state synchronization, a failed activation with automatic rollback, credential changes completed during drain, external Codex preservation, concurrent source changes, interrupted rollback recovery, credential changes while acquiring the handover lock, a private recovery copy, launch-file conflict detection and complete catalog comparisons. MCP fixtures cover preparation without starting the candidate, TCP/Unix parity with an empty catalog, full tool metadata and protocol mismatches, HTTP/JSON-RPC rejection with rollback, private baseline drift, session propagation, pagination, reply IDs and duplicate tool names. Privacy fixtures additionally cover the observed 947-byte JSONL tail, final writes during drain, checked counters, whole-day clearing and pruning, active and fallback keys, unsafe nodes, held writer locks, a writer racing an atomic exchange, failed activation with new audit rows, and process interruption both during private copying and immediately after exchange. Repeated rollback must preserve each row exactly once. These tests do not stop a real service, access a real account or execute a tool. The migration implementation is in src/migration.rs; the packaged service definition is in packaging/systemd/user/zcalld.service. The service transaction can validate local startup, permissions and catalog equivalence without exercising a remote provider. Record real provider availability separately when it has actually been checked.

title: Performance evidence
body: 本地模型网关，集中管理提供方、路由规则与模型调用。 Performance evidence The 2026-11-22 iteration report compares the native gateway with Magpie on matched local JSON/SSE routing and measures large-request rewrites against the previous core. It records exact artifacts, accounting checks, process-tree memory and workload limits. Historical reference: zcalld 0.1.0 These are historical 0.1.0 minimal-daemon measurements. For the installed 0.2.4 gateway with 0.1.5-2 compatibility workers, see the 2026-11-20 deployment acceptance, which reports the complete gateway process tree, the separate GUI and swap accounting. The approximately 10 MiB baseline below does not describe that compatibility deployment. Six runs completed 30,000 of 30,000 measured gateway requests successfully. Across three runs per configuration, throughput medians were 2,210.08 requests/s with no plugins and 2,379.19 requests/s with aliases and policy enabled. The observed throughput ranges overlap; these measurements describe this workload on a shared development machine and do not establish a plugin speedup or penalty. The tested core is 797ac0e. All six runs used the same 1,174,304-byte release executable, approximately 1.12 MiB. Measurements were recorded on 2026-11-20, 03:09–03:13 Asia/Taipei (19:09–19:13 UTC on November 19). Results Each cell gives the median across three runs, followed by the observed minimum–maximum in parentheses. Latency rows summarize each run's percentile; they are not percentiles of a pooled 15,000-request sample. Metric No plugins Aliases + policy Throughput, requests/s 2,210.08 (1,996.48–2,334.87) 2,379.19 (1,689.42–2,500.78) p50 latency, ms 1.6021 (1.5666–1.6479) 1.5522 (1.5371–2.0546) p95 latency, ms 3.6091 (2.4729–4.1393) 2.8218 (2.3041–4.2286) p99 latency, ms 5.2506 (2.9850–5.4215) 4.0207 (2.8702–9.2050) Idle RSS, KiB 9,920 (9,784–10,004) 10,584 (10,548–10,660) Sampled peak RSS, KiB 13,064 (13,024–13,188) 13,704 (13,652–13,752) Process creation to healthy response, ms 11.371 (10.920–12.147) 15.416 (10.944–26.747) Successful measured requests 15,000 / 15,000 15,000 / 15,000 Observed daemon threads 5 5 Observed child processes 0 0 Median idle memory was 9.69 MiB without plugins and 10.34 MiB with both plugins. Median sampled peak memory was 12.76 MiB and 13.38 MiB respectively. RSS comes from the daemon's Linux /proc status and includes its mapped shared libraries. Thread and child counts were observed at idle, after warm-up, and after the measured workload. Sampling occurs every 10 ms; short memory spikes may fall between samples. Every run and its raw evidence Run Configuration Requests/s p50, ms Idle RSS, KiB Sampled peak RSS, KiB Raw result 1 No plugins 2,334.87 1.6479 10,004 13,188 baseline-1.json 1 Aliases + policy 1,689.42 2.0546 10,660 13,704 plugins-1.json 2 No plugins 2,210.08 1.5666 9,784 13,024 baseline-2.json 2 Aliases + policy 2,500.78 1.5371 10,584 13,752 plugins-2.json 3 No plugins 1,996.48 1.6021 9,920 13,064 baseline-3.json 3 Aliases + policy 2,379.19 1.5522 10,548 13,652 plugins-3.json The initial pair showed lower throughput with plugins. In both later pairs, the plugin run had higher throughput than the corresponding baseline. The direct mock reference also varied substantially: 1,045.71–1,724.30 requests/s across the baseline runs and 1,082.96–1,494.55 requests/s across the plugin runs. These observations support reporting run variation alongside the medians. They do not isolate its causes or the execution cost of individual hooks. Workload and measurement All runs used Linux x86_64, kernel 7.3.4-arch1-1, Python 3.14.10, and 24 available logical CPUs. The machine was shared and the benchmark was not pinned to CPUs. Follow-up runs executed sequentially in the order baseline 2, plugins 2, baseline 3, plugins 3, without concurrent builds by this task. Every run used 4 gateway workers, 4 concurrent clients, queue capacity 16, 11 configured routes, 100 warm-up requests, and 5,000 measured requests. Warm-up requests are excluded from the success totals above. The plugin configuration loads the native aliases and policy libraries on each worker. Its public model fast maps to local; both configurations select the same mock upstream model. Payloads are 79 bytes for the baseline and 78 bytes for the alias configuration. The benchmark client creates a new downstream HTTP connection for each request. The gateway reuses upstream connections per worker. The mock returns a deterministic small JSON response over loopback HTTP, with TCP_NODELAY enabled. There is no TLS handshake, network provider call, or model generation in this workload. Latency includes local HTTP processing, mock work, and client scheduling; it begins when an executor worker starts the request and excludes time waiting in the executor queue. Startup measurements include process creation and a health poll at 10 ms intervals. Each run also sends 5,000 requests directly to the same mock. All 30,000 direct reference requests succeeded. That path creates a fresh mock connection for every request, while the gateway path pools its upstream connections. The threaded Python mock creates a handler thread per connection. These different connection topologies explain why the pooled gateway path can outperform the fresh-connection reference. Ratios between them do not isolate gateway overhead. The figures cover this small, non-streaming request workload. They do not measure maximum capacity, TLS/provider latency, long SSE sessions, large conversation bodies, or cross-protocol conversion cost. The HTTP integration suite exercises streaming and conversion correctness separately. Reproduce Build the workspace, then alternate the two configurations: cargo build --release --workspace --locked python3 scripts/benchmark.py --requests 5000 --warmup 100 \ --workers 4 --concurrency 4 --output docs/benchmarks/baseline-new.json python3 scripts/benchmark.py --requests 5000 --warmup 100 \ --workers 4 --concurrency 4 --with-plugins \ --output docs/benchmarks/plugins-new.json The script owns its temporary configuration, mock, daemon, and local test credentials; it stops the daemon and removes the temporary files after the run. Keep raw JSON results with any published summary so the workload and observed variation remain inspectable.

title: 概览
body: 为 zcalld 提供独立的兼容与扩展适配。 zcalld compatibility component This optional component preserves the interfaces used by Magpie community plugins and the local privacy engine. It starts no Magpie gateway, opens no network listener of its own, and contains no GUI. The native zcalld core does not link the Go runtime or Bun. The imported code is fixed at Magpie commit 1e174f8f9f613a920203a4658d259456fcab5d0d. UPSTREAM.json, NOTICE, and LICENSE record its provenance and modifications. Components Component Process and purpose zcalld-privacy Private stdio worker for masking, local AstrLink Guard inference, and reversible JSON/SSE restoration. One worker is shared by the enabled native privacy plugin. zcalld-pluginctl Short-lived CLI helper for installation, registry changes, private migration, provider metadata, and public plugin RPC. community/vendor/host.js Pinned upstream OpenCode v1 and pi host. The native community plugin starts one Bun process lazily and uses its byte-credit and cancellation protocol. internal/redact Original rule engine, stable keyed placeholders, JSON field selection, known-value masking, and split-event restoration. internal/pii/guard Original AstrLink Guard tokenizer and CPU implementation. Model weights are not included. Native libraries and JavaScript packages are trusted code with the user's privileges. A revision or checksum identifies code; it does not sandbox it. New installations start disabled. Import explicitly preserves the enabled state of the user's existing plugins. Build The compatibility worker is built separately from the Rust gateway. go build -o bin/zcalld-privacy ./cmd/zcalld-privacy go build -o bin/zcalld-pluginctl ./cmd/zcalld-pluginctl go test ./privacy ./community ./internal/redact ./internal/lazyre ./internal/pii/guard The parent zcalld workspace builds the native redact and community adapters through zplugin. Arch packages place helpers in /usr/lib/zcalld-compat with CLI links in /usr/bin; portable archives use /usr/libexec/zcalld. Native plugins are supplied by the core in /usr/lib/zcalld/plugins. Bun is needed only for JavaScript plugins; Git is needed only for Git installation sources. Manage packages Every command takes --root /absolute/config-directory/extensions. The parent CLI supplies that argument. zcalld-pluginctl --root "$PWD/example/extensions" list --json zcalld-pluginctl --root "$PWD/example/extensions" install /absolute/plugin.mjs --name sample --json zcalld-pluginctl --root "$PWD/example/extensions" install npm:package-name@1.2.3 --json zcalld-pluginctl --root "$PWD/example/extensions" install github:owner/repo --revision FULL_COMMIT_HASH --json zcalld-pluginctl --root "$PWD/example/extensions" enable sample --json zcalld-pluginctl --root "$PWD/example/extensions" config sample --file /absolute/options.json --json zcalld-pluginctl --root "$PWD/example/extensions" disable sample --json zcalld-pluginctl --root "$PWD/example/extensions" remove sample --json Git sources require a full immutable commit. npm sources require an exact version. Local sources are copied and hashed. A supplied --sha256 must match; native libraries are checked again before activation and loading. Bun package lifecycle scripts are disabled. Local source trees reject symlinks and special files. Installed generations remain separate so an update does not overwrite code serving an existing stream. Public results include names, paths, kinds, versions, revisions, checksums, and enabled state. They omit options, authentication, and private settings. Configuration files and copied authentication use private permissions and atomic replacement. Preserve a Magpie setup Import into a fresh candidate directory before changing a running service: zcalld-pluginctl --root /absolute/candidate/extensions import-magpie \ --source /absolute/magpie-config \ --privacy-root /absolute/candidate/privacy \ --model-root /absolute/magpie-cache --json The importer copies installed npm packages and dependencies, package options, plugin authentication, the provider cache, privacy settings, the existing redact.key, masking history, and installed model files. It never starts plugins or refreshes a token during import. It reports counts and generated configuration paths. Existing destination state is rejected. Local/Git plugin specifications that cannot be resolved from the installed npm tree require explicit installation; failure is reported. The built-in account adapters are separate from the imported community authentication. The import result states builtin_oauth_imported: false; the parent migration command handles those accounts. The generated paths are absolute. Moving a candidate requires rewriting them. Keep the original application active until the parent migration checks and cutover complete; copied rotating credentials should not be refreshed by two gateways concurrently. Privacy behavior The worker reads the settings file for every request. It preserves the Magpie redact* flags, custom words and rules, kind actions, allowlist, threshold map, and model selection. zcalldEnabled: false disables masking without deleting those settings. Absence of that override honors the imported flags. The importer retains existing masking history. The worker does not write original values or request bodies to disk; its reversible value map lives in memory. A durable private key keeps placeholders stable. Replies are restored after the gateway converts protocols, including placeholder fragments split between SSE events and tool arguments. Block actions stop egress. An explicitly selected but unavailable model holds requests back; automatic model selection may use rules while model files are absent, matching the upstream request-time fallback. This adapter does not download missing model weights automatically. The local model adapter currently runs AstrLink Guard. It was tested against the installed pinned 7216b6a3b897 model, including tokenizer and classifier fixtures. Privacy Filter selections are reported as unavailable and fail closed; this component never silently substitutes a different model for an explicit selection.
