title: zclick 0.1.1a2 交付记录
body: 基于 zclap 的 Click 参数语义与 Python 预览绑定。 zclick 0.1.1a2 交付记录 本轮结论与发布状态 本轮完成了可复用的 Rust 解析结构、参数输入借用、受条件约束的原生排序，以及 Python 类型选择、帮助和终端格式化路径的优化。两台主机上，1,000 个选项的重复解析相对已发布 0.1.1a1 分别为 2.535× / 2.354×，完整调用相对 Click 8.5.1 分别为 1.771× / 2.017×。完整调用对旧版的改善只有 1.042× / 1.050×，不能称为这一版本的大幅新增收益。下文的两个数依次表示本地与发布 CI 测量。完整性能记录 纯解析对 Click 的优势没有跨主机复现。 1,000 个选项在本地测得 1.236×，CI 则为 0.975×；CI 中 a2 的中位耗时略高。两组数据均保留，不能只选本地较好的结果。 0.1.1a2 已发布到 GitHub Releases 和 PyPI。 Release 43052475382 的 61 个任务全部成功，标签 v0.1.1a2 指向源码 7e3d597873b737bbfc8c2df090773aad56d9bd73。公开 PyPI 的 12 个 wheel 与一个源码包，SHA-256 均与实际下载核对的 GitHub 制品一致；也已在仓库外的隔离环境从 PyPI 安装并运行示例。发布核验 0.1.1a2 仍是预发布，完整 Click 兼容目标尚未达成。 CPython 子解释器兼容继续记为 UNFINISHED。小规模重复解析、单选项完整调用和嵌套命令在两台主机上仍慢于 Click，因此没有“所有 Click 应用都大幅提速”的结论。兼容性清单、未完成项 固定目标与依赖 本轮继续使用同一个 Click 行为目标；源码、API、文档和官方测试都来自固定版本。 项目 固定值与边界 项目版本 Python 0.1.1a2；Cargo 0.1.1-alpha.2 Click 目标 8.5.1；源码 cf19179e8e2fd54c601378cec9e0d21bb12b6fb1 zclap registry 精确版本 0.1.4；正式依赖不使用 Git 分支或开发机路径 原生绑定 PyO3 0.30.1，包含其必要的传递与构建依赖 Rust / MSRV 1.99.1，Edition 2024 Python 最低 3.10；普通 CPython wheel 使用稳定 ABI，PyPy 和 free-threaded CPython 使用各自构建 Python 运行时第三方依赖 空；Click、pytest、Maturin 等属于开发、构建或对照环境 版本与来源见 target.json、zclap.json、Cargo.toml 和 pyproject.toml。Rust 语义核心使用 no_std + alloc，直接第三方依赖只有 zclap；Python 扩展使用 std 和 PyO3，仍会分配 Python 与 Rust 对象。 应用迁移方式保持为 import zclick as click，子模块导入对应改为 from zclick.xxx import ...。发行包不安装顶层 click，不修改原版 Click，也不通过全局 sys.modules 重定向其他库。已有示例、类型声明和 py.typed 的入口见 README。 优化实际减少了什么工作 复用结构，保留每次调用的状态 解析 schema 是选项名字和参数消费规则的结构表。一个命令或解析器最多保留最近一份由 Rust 拥有的不可变 schema；每次调用先读取当前定义并核验，匹配时复用，变化时建立新表。这样，未变化的名字和查找表不必反复构造。核验本身仍在计时范围内。实现、结构变更测试 默认值函数的结果、环境变量、提示输入、Context 和回调结果不进入这个缓存。修改参数、别名、参数个数、callback 或类型方法后，后续调用仍读取当前 Python 对象。重入拥有独立解析状态，已经执行过的命令也有 pickle 和 deepcopy 回归。动态语义、复用命令测试 减少输入复制和解释层的重复操作 普通参数字符串在一次原生调用期间借用解释器提供的 UTF-8 缓冲区，并保留原 Python 对象的所有权。参数来源通过索引记录，避免把相同内容或空缓冲区误当成同一个对象。含 surrogate 的字符串走可逆表示；这条路径和结果对象的创建仍可能分配内存。边界测试 Python 适配层减少了临时类型映射表、重复导入和部分格式化辅助对象。内置类型选择每次读取当前公开类型对象；字符串子类、自定义转换器和被替换的方法仍可被观察到。单行帮助的常见情况避免提前加载 inspect，特殊空白继续使用当前解释器的标准库语义，包括 Python 3.12 与 3.13 的差异。表面接口回归 大参数表预建位置索引，再稳定排序 普通 CPython 对象、实际的 list 容器和至少 512 项声明参数满足守卫条件时，原生排序先建立首次出现位置的查找表，再做稳定排序。它减少了重复 list.index 线性查找，排序本身最坏仍需 O(n log n) 时间。小列表、自定义相等比较、属性或真值协议，以及 PyPy，继续执行 Python 的实际 sorted 和 index 规则。排序实现、排序回归 以上工作仍使用 zclap 做实际选项识别和最终验证。类型转换、参数回调等 Python 扩展点保留当前方法调用。完整执行时间还包括启动、导入、命令构造、上下文、转换、用户回调和输出，因此重复解析的加速比不能直接当作整个应用的加速比。架构说明 双主机三方性能一览 两次测量都将固定 Click、已发布 a1 wheel 和冻结的 a2 wheel 放在同一个 Python 解释器下比较；没有用历史报告的 a1 数字替代当轮对照。每轮的工作树开始和结束时均干净，各主机的全部测量 worker 都绑定 CPU 0。两次运行的处理器、解释器和构建环境不同，因此分别报告，不合并为一个“平均提速”。 记录 本地测量 发布 CI 测量 源码 c949d301 7e3d5978 Python / CPU CPython 3.12.14 / AMD EPYC 9V74 CPython 3.14.10 / AMD EPYC 7763 a2 wheel 目标 本机构建 manylinux_2_34 发行构建 manylinux_2_17 完整样本 本地 JSON CI JSON 下表保留全部 18 项重复调用场景。比值为各自主机上参考中位耗时 / a2 中位耗时，大于 1 表示 a2 耗时更低。Click 对照与旧版 a1 对照分列，不能将项目已有的性能优势全部归为本轮新增收益。 场景 本地 Click/a2 CI Click/a2 本地 a1/a2 CI 分别安装到独立环境。每轮使用新的隔离进程，每台主机各 12 轮；每六轮包含三方的全部六种先后顺序一次，冷启动各场景另有独立顺序。输出、解析结果和对象身份先检查再计时，原始报告保留 wheel、源码、Cargo.lock、主机和每轮观测。正常 GC 保持启用。测量协议 大规模重复解析相对旧版的改进在两台主机的每轮配对中都出现，但完整调用只有小幅新增改善。本地 1,000 选项完整调用的 a1/a2 分配峰值，本地从 a1 的 163,850 字节降到 a2 的 54,281 字节，CI 从 175,010 字节降到 54,355 字节。Python 分配指标不覆盖所有 Rust 分配，不能替代整个进程的内存测量。 验证方法与兼容边界 发布门禁仍要求固定的 33,459 个官方用例 ID，其中 31,000 个为压力用例，以及 196 项公开 API及成员契约、12 个官方 typing 空白，以及排序中的相等比较和首次位置规则。大命令的部分动态边界在独立解释器中验证，避免前一个测试改变优化适用条件、掩盖后一个测试。本次发布的 12 个普通兼容测试任务与 28 个压力测试任务均已成功完成，原版 skip/xfail 仍单独记录；逐环境计数见发布验证记录。 本轮实际平台结果 以下计数来自本次公开的 compatibility-evidence.zip，对应同一个发布源码提交。每个环境都收集了 321 个项目测试与 2,459 个官方普通用例；表内是每个所列运行时各自的结果。官方列中，原版 Click 与 zclick 的计数一致，缺失用例、额外用例和意外新增 skip 均为 0。所有任务没有失败或错误。逐环境证据 实际测试环境 项目测试：通过 / 跳过 官方普通：通过 / 跳过 / 预期失败 title: zclick 0.1.1a3 交付记录
body: 基于 zclap 的 Click 参数语义与 Python 预览绑定。 zclick 0.1.1a3 交付记录 发布与安装 0.1.1a3 已发布到 PyPI 和 GitHub Releases。 发布流程 43377480224 的 61 个任务全部成功，标签 v0.1.1a3 指向源码 9afcc7537212563f66a5d99c9f08f99bfa692731。13 个发行文件由已配置的可信发布者上传，包括 12 个 wheel 和一个源码包。 python -m pip install --upgrade zclick==0.1.1a3 已实际下载全部 16 个 GitHub 公开资产并核对大小和 SHA-256；其中 13 个发行文件与 PyPI 的记录一致。全部 13 份公开发布证明的发布者身份及文件摘要也已核对。首次普通索引安装遇到 PyPI 索引同步延迟，失败记录保留；2026-11-13 06:30:38 UTC，第二个仓库外全新环境通过相同的普通 PyPI 索引安装成功，没有使用直接 wheel URL。环境未安装原版 Click，提示输入的问候示例退出码为 0。完整发布核验 CI 性能测量与正式 GNU wheel 的 18 个 Python／原生运行时文件内容完全相同。基准 wheel 的归档 SHA-256 为 3a8b394925e2ac56830e75dda74b84182480c0449bfac199dc044d0cb8921bc2，公开 GNU wheel 为 9316d37ec25f53c18985b0e85e064c5468e36f693acd3d53201c930b89fa9773；归档本身不同，运行时文件逐项相同。制品对比证明 本轮结果 本轮将动态解析计划的准备与执行合并为一次原生调用，减少固定协议名称、列表遍历和上下文调度的重复工作，同时修复帮助缓存、参数容器和警告顺序的兼容差异。完整数据来自两次独立记录的 Linux 运行，每次都重新比较固定 Click 8.5.1、已发布的 zclick 0.1.1a2 wheel 和 a3。英文完整性能报告 相对 a2，单参数重复解析的耗时比为 1.615×／1.674×，嵌套命令为 push 减少一次线程局部读取，命令组调度复用固定协议名称，错误分支的辅助模块在需要时导入。上下文资源释放、自定义类型转换和 Python 方法覆盖继续执行。测量不支持把总收益分配成各项技巧的精确占比。调度实现 兼容性修复与性能一起保留 帮助选项首次创建后的对象身份、参数列表的真值与容器身份、名称去重的哈希顺序，以及调试模式的重复参数警告，均按固定 Click 行为回归。没有为优化跳过警告或冻结用户方法。配对回归 跨平台测试抓到了新入口在 PyPy 上读取不存在的函数 __builtins__ 属性的问题。修复在模块初始化时捕获对应 builtins 字典，并覆盖字典和模块两种加载器输入；已经用真实 PyPy 验证。修复前的 6cdbcd7 原始测量仍保留，正式报告采用修复后的完整运行，两个运行没有混合或挑选较快样本。 测量来源与可复现范围 记录 本地 API 审计及 12 个类型示例；Rust 的 23 项测试、格式与 Clippy 检查、核心 wasm32 no_std 构建和依赖许可审计；Bash、Zsh、Fish、PowerShell 的 9 项真实 Shell 集成测试。12 个发行 wheel 均在相应运行环境实际安装并执行；源码包也重新构建成 wheel 后执行，不能仅凭文件标签推断平台通过。 wheel 覆盖 Linux 2024、registry zclap 0.1.4 和 PyO3 0.30.1 未改变。核心仍为 no_std + alloc，Python 运行时没有第三方依赖，也不依赖原版 Click。依赖审计 子解释器兼容仍未完成，因此 a3 仍为 alpha。 原生模块在子解释器中明确拒绝初始化，稳定发布门禁继续阻止带有未完成兼容项的稳定版。CliRunner --candidate-wheel dist/benchmark-candidate/*.whl \ --iterations 1000 --repeats 12 --seed 20261111 --affinity auto \ --output reports/benchmarks-0.1.1a3.json 候选目录只放本次构建的一份 wheel。默认基线锁定实际发布的 a2 和固定 Click；历史 a1 锁仍可显式选择用于复现旧报告。正式计时期间停止并行构建和本地测试，不将短诊断输出当作正式结果。

title: zclick 0.1.1a1 交付记录
body: 基于 zclap 的 Click 参数语义与 Python 预览绑定。 zclick 0.1.1a1 交付记录 结论与当前边界 本轮在 LIghtJUNction/zclick 中实现了可构建、可安装的 Python/Rust 命令行库，提供 zclick 公开命名空间及对应子模块，原生解析使用发布到 registry 的 zclap。代码、测试、示例、类型声明、性能测量、跨平台构建和自动发布流程已分阶段提交。 当前版本为预发布 0.1.1a1，完整兼容验收尚未达成。 已确认的兼容缺口是 CPython 子解释器：原版 Click 可以在已验证的主解释器先初始化场景中使用，当前 zclick 会明确拒绝子解释器导入。固定官方测试集通过不能消除这一差异；仓库保持 UNFINISHED 记录，并阻止带有未解决兼容项的稳定版本发布。兼容性清单和机器可读缺口记录给出了范围与复现入口。 本轮的运行时代码冻结于 86bab2a8de3092155a912a4028382aba8188e6db。本地基准记录该提交，首轮独立 CI 记录 a8bc735a3df168b62b2e11d99b34e7ab40530ba7，最终发布 CI 记录 3281e18f215dec976c3ce0c4b5dd933ad4d62616。这三次测量之间没有更改运行时代码；后续提交只更新发布说明、测试证据规范化和构建编排。三份原始数据均保留，实际发布结果列在本记录末尾。 固定目标和依赖 项目 本轮固定值 证据 Click 兼容目标 8.5.1，2026-11-06 发布，2026-11-11 核验 target.json Click 源码 cf19179e8e2fd54c601378cec9e0d21bb12b6fb1 同一提交的文档、公开 API 与官方测试，不混用移动中的文档版本 zclap registry 精确版本 0.1.4 zclap.json、Cargo.lock 校验和 zclap 对应源码 4d87f3ae3743e81509d5ac5500909955667c860f 已对照发布包的 VCS 信息与当前源码、测试 原生绑定 PyO3 0.30.1 Cargo.lock，包含必要的传递与构建依赖 Rust / MSRV 实际验证的 1.99.1，Edition 2024 rust-toolchain.toml、CI 编译与 no_std 检查 Python 声明最低 3.10 pyproject.toml 与各解释器 CI Python 默认运行时依赖 空 wheel 元数据检查；原版 Click 仅属于开发、对照测试环境 发行包只安装 zclick，不覆盖原版 click，不通过 sys.modules 改写其他库的导入。Maturin、pytest、Hypothesis、mypy 和 Click 对照环境与默认运行时依赖分开管理。依赖审计脚本与发行包检查脚本分别检查源码依赖边界和实际包内容。 使用和实现 应用迁移的基本改动是： import zclick as click from zclick.testing import CliRunner from zclick.types import ParamType from zclick.core import Command, Group, Context 原有 from click.xxx 导入应对应改为 from zclick.xxx。公开类型声明和 py.typed 随包提供。三个可执行示例分别覆盖问候与提示、链式命令与结果回调、以及自定义类型、上下文资源和超过 64 位的整数；README 中的三个执行命令已实际运行，输出分别为两行 Hello, Ada!、HELLO Rust 和 demo: 18446744073709551616。示例入口 代码分层 层 当前实现职责 Python 公开层 类与装饰器、Context 生命周期、可覆盖的参数钩子、默认值与环境读取、Python 类型转换、帮助组装、终端工具、补全和 testing Rust/PyO3 绑定层 解析动作编排、组命令分发、Python 对象所有权和安全回调 Rust 语义核心 token 与 arity 处理、位置参数分配、参数执行顺序、值来源选择、ANSI 与文本换行 zclap 通过真实事件解析识别选项，执行 finish() 最终检查，参与消费后参数值的字节解析 这是具有较多 Python 职责的混合实现，不能称为整个库都由 Rust 执行。公开对象和任意用户方法仍然遵守 Python 的动态规则；Rust 负责上述集中计算和编排路径。核心 crate 使用 no_std + alloc，直接第三方依赖只有 zclap；Python 扩展使用 std、PyO3，并会创建和分配 Python 对象。架构与源码说明 调用开始时会从当前参数对象重新建立解析计划。这样，修改 command.params、选项属性、类型转换方法或 callback 后，下一次调用能观察到变化。默认值函数、环境变量、提示输入和 Context 状态不会作为执行结果缓存。代价是每次调用都有结构转换和分配成本，性能表包含这些成本。 zclap 只借用当前调用拥有的字符串和参数表，没有 Box::leak、永久字符串驻留或伪造 'static。回调期间不持有会阻止重入的原生可变借用；原生分发对象参与 GC，并在整个 Python scope 返回或抛出后释放捕获引用。Python 整数转换保留任意精度，带 surrogate 的字符串采用可逆表示，库内部不调用 Rust process::exit 杀死宿主。动态语义测试、原生分发测试 测试方法与已取得证据 兼容清单来自固定版本的官方 API 和源码，包含 196 项公开 API及其成员、签名、默认值、属性和弃用行为。官方测试库存包含 33,459 个唯一用例 ID，其中 31,000 个为压力用例；清单和排序后哈希固定在 test-manifest.json。 迁移测试只修改包名、模块引用、monkeypatch 路径、子进程导入、发行元数据查找及必要的模块限定 repr。没有修改行为断言、输入参数、预期结果或原版 skip/xfail 条件。每轮保存迁移日志、逐例结果、实现提交和源码哈希，发布门禁验证精确的 ID 集合。 冻结快照 86bab2a8 的 CI 43028777836 已全部成功：Linux CPython 3.10–3.15、3.14t/3.15t、PyPy 3.11/3.12，macOS 与 Windows CPython 3.14，以及 Rust、四 Shell 和子解释器安全诊断。各平台保留不同的原版平台跳过条件，不能把它们写成实际执行通过的用例。 在本地冻结快照的最后一次压力对照中，Click 与 zclick 各 31,000 passed，双方 0 failed、0 skipped、0 xfailed，缺失和额外用例均为 0。31,000 个唯一 ID 的 SHA-256 为 41721cdd2cdc8245395eb046937570a7d9ce8c8e5945c306ef6e98d7ce8a048a；该次原生模块 SHA-256 为 87f1d9d65e88eb08bea9b31afaf35fe9ae45cd3a3976f28919e5e01f1c958bea。原始结果保留在 reports/final-stress-fixed，未将后来的 Git 提交号覆盖到旧报告中。 首轮 Release 43029689108 的各平台普通、压力、API、typing、Shell 和安全测试均成功，证据汇总发现了 Python 3.10 的五个枚举参数 ID 显示差异。修复只规范这五个完整 ID，并新增同份报告内的碰撞拒绝；重放真实报告后，33,459 项及原清单 SHA-256 均完全一致，未修改行为断言。最终发布仍要求新提交重新通过完整验收与实际安装包执行检查，结果和平台计数列在本记录末尾。 性能结果 比值统一定义为 Click 耗时 / zclick 耗时；大于 1 表示该场景下 zclick 更快，小于 1 表示性能回退。两个环境均使用 release 构建、9 轮样本，并保存原始 wall/CPU 时间与源码哈希。以下不是对任意 CLI 应用的统一加速承诺。完整方法、每项时间和内存表 场景 本地 CPython 3.12 最终发布 CI CPython 3.14 热调用，1 个选项 0.694× 1.058× 热调用，10 个选项 0.822× 1.151× 热调用，100 个选项 1.148× 1.169× 热调用，1,000 个选项 1.706× 1.997× 复用底层 parser，1 个选项 0.403× 0.520× 复用底层 parser，1,000 个选项 0.660× 0.435× 嵌套命令 0.970× 0.889× Unicode/ANSI 文本换行 7.344× 8.724× 全新进程，1,000 选项命令 1.183× 1.148× 全新进程，1,000 选项 --help 1.288× 1.017× 1,000 选项热调用在本地从 11.176 ms 降到 6.553 ms，在最终发布 CI 从 11.149 ms 降到 5.582 ms。该边界复用已经定义的 Command，但包含新 Context、解析计划、参数处理、转换和回调。全新进程测量另行包含 Python 启动、导入、Option/Command 构造、执行、输出捕获和进程退出。 冷启动帮助收益没有稳定复现：1,000 选项命令在最终 CI 从 63.205 ms 到 55.066 ms，比值为 1.148×；同规模帮助仅从 63.471 ms 到 62.415 ms，比值为 1.017×。保留的首轮 CI 对照还记录到帮助从 73.347 ms 到 76.995 ms，比值为 0.953×。因此不能把本地 1.288× 的冷启动帮助结果当成普遍结论，也不能宣传小命令必然提速。 从执行成本看，Rust 省下的是解释循环、参数编排和文本处理中的一部分工作；跨 Python/Rust 边界、读取可变对象、建立当前调用的数据结构和返回 Python 对象仍要耗时。小任务里，这些固定成本可能超过计算本身；较大的命令和文本处理才在两台主机上都表现出明确收益。测量没有把每一种成本单独隔离，因此这是一种结合代码路径的解释，不是独立的分项性能归因实验。 两个环境都按 Click 再 zclick 的固定顺序运行，没有绑定 CPU 或锁定频率，主机、解释器和缓存状态也不同。小幅差异不能解释为统计显著结果。Python tracemalloc 不包含所有 Rust 分配；本地进程峰值 RSS 分别约为 22.78 MiB 与 23.82 MiB。本项目没有零分配或内存全面减少的结论。 尚未完成和需要单独处理的场景 CPython 子解释器兼容仍未完成。 PyO3 0.30.1 中部分 Python 对象缓存不按解释器隔离，直接放行可能让一个解释器调用另一个解释器保存的对象。因此当前模块在初始化最早阶段检查解释器身份，对子解释器抛出 ImportError，同时验证主解释器随后仍可调用。这个保护解决的是错误共享对象的风险，没有实现 Click 的子解释器行为。 诊断分别记录安全拒绝和兼容是否通过，也保留原版的环境问题：本地 CPython 3.12 在部分 child-first 导入/销毁顺序下，原版 Click 和独立的 datetime 对照均出现 teardown 崩溃，报告保留返回码而没有预热导入来隐藏它。能够稳定工作的 main-first 原版场景仍足以表明 zclick 存在差异。解释器边界说明 第三方扩展的内部导入需要单独迁移。 实测的 click-didyoumean==0.3.1、click-plugins==1.1.1.2 和 click-repl==0.4.1 仍然导入原版 Click，分别涉及原版类继承、isinstance 检查或上下文栈差异。应用里的别名只改变该模块的名字绑定，不会改写扩展文件自己的导入。这些诊断测试通过不代表扩展已经兼容。完整扩展报告 CliRunner 仍有解释器和进程状态边界。 它会替换流、环境和工作目录，不应作为同一进程中多个线程并发隔离的工具。free-threaded 构建成功与其线程安全是两件不同的事；本轮没有借此宣称并行加速。 平台结论仅覆盖列出的解释器、操作系统和实际执行路径。Windows 宽字符缓冲区回归包含系统 API 边界模拟，四 Shell 补全则实际执行生成的 shell source；不把两者统称为每一种终端设备都已验证。 构建和发布机制 发布前固定不可变提交，完整兼容性与安全验证和 wheel/sdist 构建并行执行；只有两方面全部成功才进入发布。wheel 在源码目录之外安装并执行，musllinux 包在固定摘要的 Alpine 镜像中验证；sdist 会重新构建 wheel 后再执行。类型声明、项目许可证、Click API 声明许可和 Rust 依赖通知随发行包提供，并核对 notice 原始字节的哈希。构建与发布指南 版本脚本同时更新 Python、Cargo 工作区和 lockfile，支持 prerelease、patch、minor、major 和显式版本。标签必须与项目版本一致；本次使用 release: 0.1.1a1 提交触发同一套完整门禁。GitHub Release 和 PyPI 上传是两个独立任务，前者成功并不自动代表后者已认证并发布。发布工作流 主要文件 内容 文件 入门、导入迁移与示例 README.md 公开 API、行为、平台与测试映射 COMPATIBILITY.md 固定目标、完整测试 ID、未完成项 compatibility/ 实现与依赖边界 architecture.md 两台主机的性能与内存原始结果 performance.md、benchmarks/results/ 开发、完整验证、版本和发布 development.md 扩展与补全 extensions.md、shell-completion.md 本次版本变化 CHANGELOG.md 最终发布结果 GitHub 预发布和 PyPI 发布均已成功。 Release v0.1.1a1 的实际 Git 标签指向 3281e18f215dec976c3ce0c4b5dd933ad4d62616。GitHub 发布页包含 12 个 wheel、1 个 sdist、原始基准 JSON、完整兼容性证据 ZIP 和发布说明，共 16 个文件；这些公开下载文件均已逐个验证与 GitHub 资产元数据的 SHA-256 一致。PyPI 的同版本页面提供同一批 13 个发行包，其 SHA-256 与 GitHub 已验证文件逐个一致。 公开下载的 Linux x86_64 wheel 还在未安装原版 Click 的全新虚拟环境中再次安装执行，原生解析、组命令、Unicode 输出、大整数和帮助均通过，未出现 click 模块注入。这项检查使用公开 Release 的实际文件，与 CI 原生模块烟测分开记录。 发布任务 实际结果 固定源码完整验收与证据门禁 成功，33,459 个原始 ID 与固定哈希一致 12 个 wheel 全部构建、检查并实际安装执行成功 sdist 从源码包重新构建 wheel，安装执行成功 GitHub Release 成功，明确标记 prerelease PyPI 上传 第二次尝试成功，2026-11-11 14:28:58 UTC 完成；13 个发行包已公开 首次 Release workflow 为 60 个任务成功、1 个任务失败，唯一失败任务是 PyPI 上传返回 invalid-publisher。配置发布者后，仅重跑失败的上传任务，第二次尝试于 2026-11-11 14:28:58 UTC 成功，workflow 当前结论为 success。本次重试使用已验证的相同发行文件，没有重写旧报告或替换软件版本；PyPI 元数据与制品哈希核验保留独立确认结果。 正式发布证据中的测试计数 以下是每个实现各自的结果；Click 与 zclick 对应计数相同。完整机器可读摘要位于 compatibility/releases/0.1.1a1.json，原始逐例记录随 Release 的 compatibility-evidence.zip 发布。 环境范围 官方普通测试 官方压力测试 Linux 的 10 个普通测试环境：CPython 3.10–3.15、3.14t/3.15t、PyPy 3.11/3.12 每个环境 2,434 passed、24 skipped、1 xfailed 其中 CPython 3.14、3.14t/3.15t、PyPy 3.11/3.12 title: Build, verify and release
body: 基于 zclap 的 Click 参数语义与 Python 预览绑定。 Build, verify and release Local build Install the pinned Rust toolchain with rustup, and use Python 3.10 or newer. The standard development setup is: python -m venv .venv . .venv/bin/activate python -m pip install -r requirements-dev.txt maturin develop --release --locked python -m pytest tests python scripts/audit_dependencies.py On Windows, activate with .venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1. On PyPy or free-threaded CPython, add --no-default-features to the Maturin command. Those interpreters need their own extension build, rather than the ordinary CPython stable ABI. The Rust core can be checked independently: cargo test -p zclick-core --locked cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings cargo check -p zclick-core --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --locked The last command requires rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown. It verifies the core's no_std + alloc boundary; it does not describe the Python extension. Reproduce compatibility evidence compatibility/target.json locks the original Click commit, distribution checksums, documentation and test sources. The harness verifies the checkout, prepares a namespace-only migration and runs both packages. It does not import original Click from the runtime package. Report identifiers normalize package names, three platform-dependent program paths, and five explicitly listed Enum parameter display IDs in the fixed upstream test_choice_default_rendering test. Python 3.10 displays those members by name, while newer interpreters display their values; the upstream test also substitutes Enum for StrEnum on Python 3.10. The original parameter values, assertions and skips remain unchanged. Duplicate canonical IDs within a report are rejected, and the fixed 33,459-case inventory checksum remains unchanged. python scripts/run_compatibility.py --output reports/normal -- -m 'not stress' python scripts/run_stress.py --output reports/stress --workers 4 --batch-size 500 python scripts/api_inventory.py --source .cache/click-source --output reports/api-reference.json python scripts/api_inventory.py --compare reports/api-reference.json --output reports/api.json python3.12 scripts/check_subinterpreters.py --output reports/subinterpreters python scripts/release_gate.py --reports reports/normal/summary.json reports/stress/summary.json --api reports/api.json --boundary reports/subinterpreters/summary.json The stress runner uses exact original node IDs in smaller subprocesses. This limits how many pytest collection objects its repeated GC tests must traverse. It checks the union for missing, extra and duplicate cases. This changes test batching, not assertions, parameter counts or skips. The pager function retains the upstream full-suite collection imports on which its fixture relies. The API inventory is generated on the same interpreter as the candidate audit. This matters for inherited standard-library methods: an Enum constructor's signature can change between Python versions even when the same Click source commit is used. Tests compare both packages under the same interpreter. CI also runs the original typing examples and the focused native, mutation, platform and shell regressions. A passing Linux job does not stand in for a Windows or macOS result. Individual results and unchanged upstream platform skips remain visible in the workflow artifacts. compatibility/test-manifest.json records the count and SHA-256 fingerprint of all 33,459 canonical upstream test IDs. The release gate requires that exact set. It also checks every report's source commit against the immutable release commit. Per-file source hashes identify locally tested changes that have not yet been committed. A normal compatibility run fails if those files change while its tests are running. The dedicated Shell job installs Fish and PowerShell archives from the URLs and SHA-256 checksums in compatibility/shell-runtime-lock.json, uses Bash and Zsh on the runner, and requires all four executables. It then executes the generated completion sources. See Shell completion for the exact integration boundaries and reproducible commands. Reproduce benchmarks maturin build --release --locked --out dist python benchmarks/compare.py --candidate-wheel dist/*.whl --iterations 1000 --repeats 12 --seed 20261111 --affinity auto --output reports/benchmarks.json The driver compares fixed Click 8.5.1, the published zclick 0.1.1a2 baseline and the candidate wheel. Baseline wheel checksums are locked; both zclick versions are installed in separate minimal virtual environments using the same Python interpreter. Candidate source edits cannot alter the installed baseline. Each round uses fresh isolated worker processes; six rounds contain every ordering of the three implementations once, and the default twelve rounds repeat that balanced block. Cold scenarios have independently seeded balanced orders. To reproduce the older a1 comparison, pass --baseline-lock benchmarks/baselines/0.1.1a1.json. Historical snapshots require their matching lock when supplied through --baseline-manifest; selecting a different zclick baseline never changes the pinned Click target. The driver checks each workload's result before timing and compares full output checksums across all three implementations. It records every wall and CPU sample, import latency, Python allocation sample and process peak RSS. CPU model, affinity, observed frequency, load, interpreter and per-round order are retained. --affinity auto selects the first allowed CPU on Linux; omit it on platforms without affinity control. Frequency and shared-host activity are not controlled. The warm invoke workload reuses an already-defined command and includes context creation, parser-plan setup, conversion, callbacks and Python binding costs. parse uses an already-created Python parser. Fresh-process measurements additionally include import and Command/Option construction. These boundaries remain separately reported. Ratios greater than one mean that zclick was faster in that workload. Python tracemalloc does not measure all Rust allocations. The old fixed-order measurements retain their original method and raw files; they are not rewritten as measurements from this protocol. See the benchmark protocol for boundaries, integrity checks and a short harness-only diagnostic command. Interpreter compatibility boundary Subinterpreter compatibility is UNFINISHED. Click 8.5.1 works in the tested CPython 3.12 subinterpreters; zclick's native binding is restricted to the main interpreter. This includes worker threads in that interpreter. It does not include isolated or legacy shared-GIL subinterpreters. The pinned PyO3 0.30.1 binding keeps Python-object caches that cannot safely be shared across interpreters. zclick rejects child-interpreter initialization before entering those caches. The diagnostic compares both packages in fresh processes, checks both import orders and verifies that the main interpreter still works afterward. Its report distinguishes safe_rejection from compatibility_passed; safety does not remove the compatibility difference. The known gap list remains part of the release evidence. While any item is unfinished, the release gate rejects a version without an a, b or rc suffix. A disclosed prerelease still requires all original tests, API contracts, actual Shell tests and interpreter safety checks. No upstream tests are removed, weakened or marked xfail for this gap. Distribution and release gates Build and inspect distributions locally with: maturin build --release --locked --out dist maturin sdist --out dist python scripts/check_wheel.py dist/*.whl python -m twine check dist/* The release workflow first pins the exact release commit. It then requires the compatibility, typing, dependency and platform gates, builds Linux glibc/musl, macOS and Windows wheels for x86-64 and ARM64, and builds a source distribution. Publishing uses those artifacts, not a second unverified build. Every wheel is installed and executed outside the source checkout. The checks call the native parser, render help, dispatch a group, preserve a Python integer larger than 64 bits and capture Unicode-capable output. The musllinux wheels run in an official Python Alpine container pinned by its multi-architecture manifest digest. The source archive is independently rebuilt, installed and executed before it can be published. The eight ordinary wheel targets use CPython's stable ABI from Python 3.10. Linux x86-64 also has separate interpreter-specific wheels for PyPy 3.11 and 3.12, and free-threaded CPython 3.14 and 3.15. Other PyPy or free-threaded platforms require a source build with --no-default-features; a successful CPython stable-ABI wheel does not establish support for those runtimes. The exact platform results remain in the CI artifacts and release evidence archive. Version changes use bump_version.py. It updates the Python project, Rust workspace packages and lockfile together. The workflow supports prerelease, patch, minor, major and explicit PEP 440 versions. A tag must exactly match the project version. A release entry records whether the version is a prerelease. Release automation accepts a matching version tag, a workflow dispatch, or a push to main whose first commit-message line is exactly release: VERSION. The branch trigger is useful when an authorized repository connector can push commits but cannot dispatch workflows. It still requires the same source, compatibility, Shell, type, build and artifact-execution gates. Alpha, beta and release-candidate versions are marked as GitHub prereleases. GitHub release assets include the distributions, per-case evidence archive and raw benchmark JSON. GitHub artifact publication and PyPI publication run as separate jobs so PyPI authentication failure does not hide downloadable GitHub artifacts. PyPI publication uses its GitHub Trusted Publisher configuration or the repository's PYPI_API_TOKEN secret. Repository write access alone does not establish PyPI publishing ownership. A publication failure remains a visible failed job and must not be described as an available pip install release.

title: 第三方 Click 扩展的迁移边界
body: 基于 zclap 的 Click 参数语义与 Python 预览绑定。 第三方 Click 扩展的迁移边界 仅修改应用自己的导入，不能保证第三方扩展同时迁移到 zclick。本次检查了三个真实发布包，它们都在自身源码中导入原版 click。原版 Click 与 zclick 同时安装时，这些导入仍然指向原版 Click；应用中的 import zclick as click 只改变应用当前模块里的变量绑定。 已验证的具体行为 下面的实验固定原版 Click 为 8.5.1，扩展保持发布包原样。每个扩展先运行原版 Click 对照，再运行只调整应用导入的混合场景。测试文件为 integration_tests/test_extensions.py，依赖固定在 requirements-extensions.txt。 扩展及版本 原版 Click 对照 zclick 混合场景的观察 迁移结论 click-didyoumean==0.3.1 拼错子命令时返回退出码 2，并显示候选命令。 @zclick.group(cls=DYMGroup) 仍然构造原版 click.Group 子类；简单命令可以执行。加入 @zclick.pass_context 后，调用因没有活动的 zclick 上下文而失败。 简单示例能运行，不足以证明已使用 Rust 解析。该扩展的类继承和上下文调用需要一致迁移。 click-plugins==1.1.1.2 能把入口点加载的命令注册到原版 click.Group 并执行。 with_plugins([])(zclick.Group(...)) 立即抛出 TypeError，因为扩展检查原版 click.Group 的类型身份。 未修改的发布包不接受 zclick 的 Group。 click-repl==0.4.1 注册 REPL 后，从输入流执行 hello 和 :exit 成功。 注册到 zclick Group 后，扩展包装的原版 click.pass_context 从原版 Click 的上下文栈取值，调用 REPL 时抛出 RuntimeError。 注册成功不等于可执行；上下文装饰器、命令类型判断和补全类型判断需要一起验证。 这些是兼容性诊断测试。其中一些测试明确断言混合场景会失败，测试通过表示观察到的边界可以复现，不能把其通过数计入“第三方扩展已经兼容”的数量。原版 click-repl 对照还会触发其使用 MultiCommand 产生的弃用警告；测试明确捕获该警告，未修改扩展源码或 Click 的警告行为。 为什么导入别名不能解决这些问题 Python 的导入别名只作用于写下该导入语句的模块。应用把名称 click 绑定到 zclick 后，扩展文件中的 import click 会继续独立查找名为 click 的包。两者拥有不同的类对象，因此 isinstance(zclick.Group(...), click.Group) 为假。 上下文同样具有各自的状态。zclick 调用命令时把自己的 Context 放入自己的上下文栈；原版 Click 的 get_current_context() 不会从这个栈取值。诊断测试双向检查两个栈相互独立，这也确保 zclick 没有通过修改全局 sys.modules 或替换原版 Click 偷偷改变其他库。 复现 在仓库根目录创建专用开发环境。下面的安装会构建当前仓库，要求已安装项目声明的 Rust 工具链；第三方扩展和原版 Click 只安装到这个隔离环境。 python -m venv .venv-extensions .venv-extensions/bin/python -m pip install -r integration_tests/requirements-extensions.txt .venv-extensions/bin/python -m pip install --no-deps . .venv-extensions/bin/python -m pytest integration_tests/test_extensions.py -q Windows 将解释器路径替换为 .venv-extensions\Scripts\python.exe。常规 pytest tests 不包含这个独立的扩展实验；选中 integration_tests/test_extensions.py 时缺少任何固定依赖都会直接报错，不会用跳过测试代替结果。 实际迁移方式 先把应用的 import click 改为 import zclick as click，把 from click.xxx 改为相应的 from zclick.xxx。随后检查每个扩展内部的导入、继承、isinstance 判断、异常捕获和上下文装饰器。只有经过实际执行验证的扩展版本，才适合在迁移清单中标记为支持。 对于上表三个未修改的版本，本项目不宣称自动兼容。可以向扩展维护者提交显式支持 zclick 的改动，或在许可证允许且能够维护的前提下迁移应用自己的扩展副本。更改扩展导入之后仍需测试成功路径、失败路径、上下文传播和补全；本轮未把未经执行的修改方案标记为已支持。 来源与证据 click-didyoumean 0.3.1 的发布说明 和 项目源码描述其自定义 Group 用法；本仓库测试进一步检查实际构造出来的类和上下文行为。 click-plugins 1.1.1.2 的发布说明 和 项目源码说明入口点注册方式；测试覆盖真实 with_plugins 装饰器的类型检查。 click-repl 0.4.1 的发布说明 和 项目源码说明 register_repl 和上下文复用；测试运行真实 REPL 注册函数及原版输入流对照。 证据范围限于固定版本和列出的路径。它证明了三个具体的导入边界，未穷举所有第三方扩展、交互终端、插件加载器或提示工具包配置，也没有提出扩展性能提升的结论。 自审 贡献：提供三个真实扩展的可复现迁移边界，未把示例运行成功等同于 Rust 后端已经生效。 清晰度：固定版本、测试入口和隔离环境命令齐全，解释了类型身份与上下文栈两个直接原因。 实验强度：同一扩展同时运行原版 Click 对照与混合导入场景；结论由类型、退出码、输出和异常支撑。 评估完整性：明确列出未测试的扩展和交互场景，没有从三个样本推断整个生态。 方法正确性：保留扩展源码、原版 Click 安装和各自的模块身份；不使用运行时替换、全局导入劫持或断言修改。

title: Measured performance: 0.1.1a2
body: 基于 zclap 的 Click 参数语义与 Python 预览绑定。 Measured performance: 0.1.1a2 Two independently recorded Linux hosts show a large improvement over published zclick 0.1.1a1 in reused parsing: the 1,000-option median ratios are 2.535× locally and 2.354× in release CI. Complete warm invocation at that size measured 1.771× and 2.017× relative to Click 8.5.1. Its improvement over a1 is much smaller: 1.042× locally and 1.050× in CI. The parser comparison with Click differs between hosts. The local 1,000-option ratio of 1.236× was not reproduced in CI, which measured 0.975×. Parsing with 1, 10 and 100 options, the one-option warm invocation and the nested-command case remained slower than Click on both hosts. Unicode/ANSI wrapping measured 7.404× locally and 9.314× in CI relative to Click. These are workload comparisons, not a universal application speedup. The local schema-2 report and release-CI schema-2 report preserve all samples and distribution identities. Their results are presented separately below; neither replaces the other. The published a1 wheel was measured again alongside the candidate in each run. The 0.1.1a1 report retains its original historical measurements. All eighteen warm workloads on both hosts, showing reference median divided by candidate median The chart shows all eighteen warm workloads from both reports. A ratio above one means lower a2 latency. Its source is plot_results.py; exact values and boundaries remain in the tables below. Local source, distributions and environment Measured source: c949d301f815c882acce9a96fe2a0c3b8da9bded, version 0.1.1a2. The working tree was clean before and after measurement. Reference: Click 8.5.1 at the fixed target; published baseline: zclick 0.1.1a1 from commit 3281e18f215dec976c3ce0c4b5dd933ad4d62616. Time: 2026-11-11, 15:41:54–15:42:47 UTC; approximately 53.31 seconds for the complete run. Interpreter: CPython 3.12.14, built with Clang 22.1.3; ordinary GIL build. Host: Linux 6.18.57 x86-64, glibc 2.41, AMD EPYC 9V74 80-Core Processor. Nine logical CPUs were available to the process; the orchestrator and every recorded warm worker used CPU affinity [0]. Method: twelve rounds, two complete blocks of all six implementation orders, seed 20261111, five warmup calls per case and normal garbage collection enabled. Build dependencies: Rust 1.99.1 / Edition 2024, registry zclap 0.1.4 and PyO3 0.30.1. The raw report retains Cargo.lock and native-file hashes. The published baseline is a manylinux_2_17 wheel; the candidate was built on this host as manylinux_2_34. Python, measurement host and execution ordering were controlled, while the wheel build environments were not identical. This is a comparison of these distributions; their entire difference cannot be attributed to source changes alone. The separate release-CI section below uses the distribution build environment and keeps this local result intact. Distribution Wheel SHA-256 Click 8.5.1, py3-none-any 8bb5376d2006950386f8c6427613334a2acadc5f559cb80e638d00b4df957e37 zclick 0.1.1a1, cp310-abi3-manylinux2014_x86_64.manylinux_2_17_x86_64 457e6d01343ccc39cc925ac86ab0e43b6c85e45a165af14e06f37c827ee13a98 zclick 0.1.1a2, cp310-abi3-manylinux_2_34_x86_64 c4ca0d46e04d23647f9798c823bd65464a2a46312bed650f13bebc30ef39aaa2 Local complete warm measurements Times are median microseconds per call across the twelve rounds. Ratios are reference median divided by a2 median: above one means lower a2 latency. The last two columns compare a2 separately with Click and the published a1 wheel. Each sample is a batch average; 1,000 base iterations are scaled to 100 for 100 options and 10 for 1,000 options. Help uses one fifth as many iterations, with a minimum of five. Its median ratio against a1 ranges from 1.231× at one option to 2.535× at 1,000 options. At 100 options, the 2.370× version improvement still leaves a2 behind Click: 64.755 µs versus 56.213 µs. Reusing an owned schema removes repeated setup, while validation, Python object creation and the current parser actions remain part of the call. The measurement does not assign a separate time to each of those costs. Complete invocation includes more than parsing. With 1,000 options, a2 took 5.642 ms, compared with 9.990 ms for Click and 5.878 ms for a1. Context creation, parameter processing, conversion and callbacks remain timed. The 1.042× a1/a2 ratio is considerably smaller than the parser-only ratio, and its paired round ratios range from 0.861 to 1.424. It is not evidence of a large new improvement in complete invocation over the previous release. Small differences need the same restraint. One-option construction measured 1.020× relative to Click; one-option invocation measured 0.973× relative to Click and 1.012× relative to a1. Their sample ranges overlap substantially. The nested-command median remains slower than Click at 0.886×, despite a 1.096× ratio relative to a1. Process CPU time The driver also records process CPU time in microseconds per call, with the same workload boundaries. The 1,000-option command measured 43.584 ms versus 58.250 ms for Click and 57.386 ms for a1; the corresponding help process measured 45.922 ms versus 58.043 ms and 56.828 ms. Individual runs varied substantially, as shown below, so these medians do not imply that every startup is faster. Import-only startup The import interval starts immediately before importing the package; only time is imported beforehand. The whole-process interval additionally includes interpreter startup, reporting the timing and process exit. Boundary Click ms a1 ms a2 ms Click / a2 a1 / a2 Import interval 21.830 21.980 15.776 1.384× 1.393× Whole import-only process 37.732 38.169 29.158 1.294× 1.309× The a2 import interval ranged from 13.826 to 19.960 ms, compared with 18.742–27.341 ms for Click and 18.355–26.606 ms for a1. Whole import-only process ranges were 25.148–38.470 ms, 32.285–45.852 ms and 31.643–51.145 ms respectively. Operating-system caches were not flushed. Local Python allocation observations and process RSS Each cell below is current / peak Python-managed bytes, taking the median of the twelve observations. tracemalloc starts after a collection, observes one call and keeps its returned value alive for the current-byte reading. It does not count all Rust allocations or all memory in a retained schema. Complete invocation recorded 832,314 bytes for a2, below a1's 919,413 and above Click's 780,943. These are Python allocation observations for the stated calls, not total native memory or a zero-allocation result. Peak RSS measures the whole worker process, including imports, package hash verification, tracemalloc and the full workload sequence. It cannot be attributed to one parser call. Values below use MiB, where 1 MiB is 1,048,576 bytes. Local variability and limits of the comparison The following ranges preserve all twelve warm samples for representative large, small and regressing workloads. Paired ratios divide a1 by a2 within each round; they differ from the ratio of the two overall medians. These observations support the stated workload comparisons while retaining their variability; they are not confidence intervals or guarantees for another machine. Fresh-process samples show larger outliers. The table includes every cold workload's observed range in milliseconds and a2's coefficient of variation (CV: sample standard deviation divided by the sample mean). Click's one-option command reached 131.940 ms and a1's 100-option command reached 184.678 ms. These samples were retained. A claim that every invocation or cold start is faster would conflict with the recorded data. Affinity kept the measured workers on CPU 0, but frequency was not locked and no frequency readings were available. The host's one-minute load observation rose from about 0.46 to 1.33. Shared-host activity, scheduling, file caches and GC can affect the run; balanced implementation order reduces one source of bias without removing those conditions. Hash seeds also vary across isolated Python processes. No statistical significance claim is made for the small median differences above. The build-target difference is another attribution limit. Comparing the published a1 manylinux_2_17 wheel with a host-built a2 manylinux_2_34 wheel measures their delivered behavior under this interpreter, including build differences. Component-level attribution and portability require their own comparisons. The historical report and this local run remain intact alongside the separate release-CI result below. Independent release-CI measurement The second run used the release build environment and a different host and Python version. It confirms the direction of the large parser improvement over a1, the large full-invocation advantage over Click, and faster wrapping. It does not reproduce the local 1,000-option parser advantage over Click: the CI median ratio is 0.975×, versus 1.236× locally. The two runs are retained separately because a change of processor, interpreter and build environment prevents attributing that difference to any one factor. CI source and distribution identity Source: 7e3d597873b737bbfc8c2df090773aad56d9bd73, version 0.1.1a2, from Release run 43052475382. The tree was clean before and after timing. Time: 2026-11-11, 15:54:30–15:55:42 UTC, approximately 72.64 seconds for the complete run. Host: AMD EPYC 7763 64-Core Processor, Linux 7.0.0-1019-azure x86-64, glibc 2.43; four logical CPUs were available and all recorded measurement workers used CPU 0. Interpreter: ordinary-GIL CPython 3.14.10, built with GCC 15.2.0. The same interpreter was used for Click, the published a1 wheel and a2. Build: pinned Maturin 1.16.0 and Rust 1.99.1 through the release's manylinux build configuration. Both zclick distributions use cp310-abi3-manylinux2014_x86_64.manylinux_2_17_x86_64 wheels. Protocol: the same twelve rounds, two balanced order blocks, seed 20261111, five warmup calls, normal GC and separately ordered fresh-process boundaries as the local run. Raw evidence: complete CI JSON, SHA-256 4e6fcaddeae2e2c0c3d932b000d649e622408f64261b895d0b81c31a7505afbd. The independently built benchmark wheel and release Linux GNU wheel have different archive hashes. Their 18 Python and native runtime files have identical content, including the native binary. This connects the measured runtime to the release artifact without claiming byte-identical wheel archives. The file-by-file comparison retains every matched runtime hash and the comparison scope. It does not by itself establish publication or performance on another architecture. Both reference ratios use the CI medians; no values are mixed between hosts. Click took 836.866 µs, so a2's parser median was slightly higher. Complete invocation took 7,023.316 µs versus Click's 14,169.504 µs and a1's 7,377.726 µs: 2.017× relative to Click, but only 1.050× over a1. Reducing one part of invocation does not give the complete command the same ratio. All four parser sizes, the one-option invocation and the nested-command case remain slower than Click in this CI run. The report retains all eighteen current/peak observations. tracemalloc does not account for all Rust allocation or total process memory. The table below gives a2's observed warm ranges and coefficient of variation, and each reference's within-round ratio range. The much smaller dispersion in this CI run does not erase the local outliers or turn two hosts into a general performance guarantee. Warm workload a2 range µs a2 CV Paired Click/a2 range Paired a1/a2 range Reuse parser (1) 4.543–4.847 1.99% 0.602–0.659 1.228–1.334 Reuse parser (1,000) 830.166–895.415 2.04% 0.938–1.065 2.240–2.463 Command.main (1) 68.330–71.134 1.19% 0.957–1.028 1.015–1.083 Command.main (1,000) 7,000.795–7,101.010 0.53% 1.955–2.111 1.034–1.075 Nested command 128.380–135.708 1.57% 0.880–0.954 1.005–1.062 Unicode/ANSI wrapping 68.172–72.966 1.97% 8.884–10.063 0.999–1.110 The CI 1,000-option parser's paired Click/a2 ratios cross one, from 0.938 to 1.065. Every paired a1/a2 ratio for that parser remained above one, from 2.240 to 2.463. The full-invocation a1/a2 ratios were 1.034–1.075, a modest change alongside the larger Click comparison. These are observed ranges, not confidence intervals. Affinity selected CPU 0; frequency was not locked and no frequency readings were available. One-minute host load changed from about 1.53 to 1.40. Isolated process hash seeds, GC, scheduling and file caches still affect measurement. Both hosts support faster reused parsing than a1 and faster large full invocation than Click for these workloads. They do not establish uniformly faster parsing than Click, lower process memory, or a speedup for all existing Click applications. Reusing parser structure A parser schema is the Rust representation of option spellings and argument consumption rules. Each command or parser retains at most its most recent owned schema. Before reuse, the binding reads the current definitions and compares their structural fields. Matching definitions reuse the schema; changed definitions produce a replacement. This removes repeated construction of the same owned names and lookup tables while keeping definition validation inside each measured invocation. The implementation is in plan.rs. The following diagram shows the schema decision within one invocation. Both branches use fresh parsing state. flowchart TD A["Current parameter definitions"] --> B{"Match retained schema?"} B -->|Yes| C["Reuse owned schema"] B -->|No| D["Build replacement schema"] C --> E["Parse with fresh call state"] D --> E The retained schema contains Rust structural data. Defaults, environment values, contexts, callback results and Python application objects remain outside it. Parameter registration, parser actions, conversion and callbacks continue through the current Python methods. These boundaries let an application change an alias, arity, callback or type method between invocations without reusing an earlier result. Reentry creates separate invocation state. The schema tests and command mutation tests exercise these distinctions, including copying and pickling a warmed command. Parameter ordering retains the same live Python behavior at its extension points. For exact lists containing at least 512 declared parameters, ordinary CPython objects may use a guarded Rust ordering operation. It records each parameter's first invocation position in a lookup table, then performs a stable sort. This avoids repeated linear list.index searches; the complete operation is not claimed to be linear, since sorting can require O(n log n) work. Smaller lists, custom protocols and PyPy use Python's sorted and index operations. The ordering regressions cover repeated object identities, equality, eager getters and custom containers. This selection is part of the timed invocation rather than an excluded preparation step. Input ownership and Python adapter work The native binding borrows an ordinary argument's interpreter-provided UTF-8 buffer for the duration of the call. It retains the Python owner and records argument indices so that an existing argument can be returned with its original identity. Strings containing surrogate code points use a reversible surrogatepass representation. Preparing an interpreter's UTF-8 representation, handling surrogate strings and creating Python results can still allocate. The native boundary tests cover Unicode, surrogates and distinct empty string subclasses. The Python adapters also avoid work whose result is already known. Built-in type selection uses identity checks and reads the current public type singleton on each call. An exact string can pass through string conversion unchanged; string subclasses continue through their Python conversion methods. Plain text width and ANSI removal avoid a native call when their guarded conditions hold, and formatting wrappers retain observation of replaced native functions. These changes are covered by surface regressions. Help preparation keeps its common single-line path small. It imports inspect only when the running standard library is needed to determine the result, including the whitespace behavior that differs between Python 3.12 and 3.13. Styling and help-table assembly reduce temporary helper objects while preserving output and callback evaluation order. Integer conversion continues to use Python integers, with the same arbitrary precision and current custom conversion methods described in the architecture. These mechanisms explain which work changed. A complete version comparison measures their combined effect together with parsing, binding and Python execution. Assigning a measured percentage to one mechanism would require a separate component comparison. What the benchmark measures Every workload uses the same public Python entry point and checks its result across all three implementations. The driver retains construction, repeated use and fresh-process execution as distinct boundaries. The full workload definitions are in compare.py. Boundary Sizes Work inside the measurement Command construction 1, 10, 100 and 1,000 options Public Option and Command construction Reused parser All four sizes parse_args, a fresh argument-list copy, definition validation, parsing and parser actions Warm command invocation All four sizes Command.main, context creation, parser setup, conversion and the command callback Warm help rendering All four sizes get_help, help assembly, widths and wrapping Nested command One parent and child Group resolution, child invocation and result handling Unicode and ANSI wrapping One fixed paragraph Public wrap_text on the same text and width Fresh-process import Each implementation Import interval and whole-process elapsed time, reported separately Fresh-process command and help All four sizes Interpreter startup, import, command construction, invocation or help, output capture and exit The warm invocation reuses an already-created command. Its schema validation and Python hooks remain timed; command construction has its own row. Fresh-process rows include construction and startup, so they also show whether a change helps a CLI that runs once and exits. The fixed command callbacks sum converted integer values. Application-specific I/O, interactive prompts and expensive business callbacks need additional application measurements. Reproducing a formal comparison Build the candidate from a frozen checkout. The following Linux example reproduces the protocol and uses a dedicated output directory so that the wheel argument identifies the intended candidate: maturin build --release --locked --out dist/benchmark-candidate python benchmarks/compare.py \ --candidate-wheel dist/benchmark-candidate/*.whl \ --iterations 1000 --repeats 12 --seed 20261111 --affinity auto \ --output reports/benchmarks-0.1.1a2.json Use the exact wheel filename if the directory contains more than one wheel. Omit --affinity auto on platforms without Linux affinity control. The driver selects the first allowed CPU when that option is used and records the original and selected affinity. Frequency and shared-host activity remain observed conditions rather than controlled constants. The driver installs the published baseline and candidate into separate environments using the same interpreter and Click wheel. It verifies the published wheel hashes and installed package contents. Formal runs also require the candidate version and Python source files to match the checkout. Reports retain the source commit, native-file hashes, Cargo.lock hash, benchmark source hashes and environment observations. See the measurement protocol for the complete provenance checks and the separate harness diagnostic mode. Each of the twelve rounds uses a fresh isolated worker for each implementation. Within every six-round block, all six implementation orders occur once, in a seeded order. Each cold workload has its own seeded schedule. The driver checks results before warm timing and compares complete help and wrapping output hashes. It records all wall-time and process-CPU samples, keeps normal garbage collection enabled and verifies the package snapshots again after measurement. The worker processes run outside the source checkout with isolated Python. Operating-system caches are not flushed, and the order of workloads inside a worker remains fixed. The report records these conditions. A quiet local measurement interval excludes concurrent project builds and tests, while the retained host observations describe activity outside the project's control. Claim and evidence record The measurement establishes performance only for the recorded workload, distributions, interpreter and host. The following mapping separates the mechanism evidence from the numerical conclusions. Claim Evidence Scope Current definitions are checked before an owned schema is reused plan.rs, test_native_plan.py, test_cached_command_semantics.py Implemented mechanism and focused regression cases Python callbacks, comparisons and conversion changes remain observable test_dynamic_semantics.py, test_native_ordering.py, test_native_parameter_hooks.py, test_native_parameter_guard_edges.py Specific covered behaviors; release verification is tied to its source commit Input handling preserves surrogate data and argument identity test_native_kernel.py, test_native_plan.py Covered native-boundary cases Reused parsing at 1,000 options improved relative to the published a1 wheel Local parse/1000: 1,602.245 µs to 632.171 µs, 2.535×; CI: 2,019.259 µs to 857.956 µs, 2.354× All paired a1/a2 rounds favored a2 on both recorded hosts Warm invocation at 1,000 options has a lower median than Click Local invoke/1000: 1.771×; CI: 2.017× The change over a1 is much smaller, at 1.042× locally and 1.050× in CI Reused parsing at 1,000 options is consistently faster than Click Local parse/1000: 1.236×; CI: 0.975× Unsupported across these two hosts; the local advantage did not reproduce The measured CI runtime corresponds to the release GNU wheel File-by-file comparison of all 18 Python/native runtime files Identical runtime contents; different wheel archive SHA-256 values Every Click application becomes substantially faster Small parser, one-option invocation and nested-command results; cold outliers Unsupported; no universal speedup is claimed Performance conclusions remain separate from compatibility completion. The subinterpreter compatibility gap remains open, so 0.1.1a2 is a prerelease. The release completed its full validation workflow and is available on GitHub and PyPI, with tag v0.1.1a2 fixed to 7e3d597873b737bbfc8c2df090773aad56d9bd73. The release validation record records the fixed upstream inventory, API contracts, original platform skips and actual shell checks. The publication verification records the 12 wheels and source archive, their matching PyPI/GitHub hashes, and an isolated PyPI installation. Passing these checks does not close the disclosed subinterpreter gap or expand the performance conclusions beyond the measured workloads.

title: Measured performance: 0.1.1a3
body: 基于 zclap 的 Click 参数语义与 Python 预览绑定。 Measured performance: 0.1.1a3 Published preview: zclick 0.1.1a3 is available from PyPI and GitHub Releases. The published tag points to 9afcc7537212563f66a5d99c9f08f99bfa692731; release validation records all 61 workflow jobs succeeding. Public installation verification confirms the published package separately from the benchmark environments. The known subinterpreter compatibility gap remains open. Two independent Linux runs compare the measured a3 build with fixed Click 8.5.1 and the published zclick 0.1.1a2 wheel. The local run uses CPython 3.12.14 at commit 2a9e2c3; release CI uses CPython 3.14.10 at 9afcc75. Both hosts identify as AMD EPYC 9V74, but their interpreter, operating system and build environments differ. Each result is kept as its own twelve-round experiment. Small full invocation improved relative to a2 on both runs. One-option Command.main ratios are 1.079× locally and 1.097× in CI; the nested-command ratios are 1.166× and 1.143×. The larger version changes are in reused parsing: one option measured 1.615× and 1.674× relative to a2. These results do not establish a universal large improvement in complete applications. The comparison with Click depends on the workload and environment. One-option parsing is slower locally (0.890×) but slightly faster in CI (1.023×); 100-option parsing goes from 1.057× locally to 0.872× in CI. Ten-option parsing remains slower than Click in both runs. The 1,000-option full-invocation ratios against Click are 1.776× locally and 2.128× in CI, while their ratios against a2 are only 1.042× and 1.033×. Most of that advantage over Click predates this revision. Regressions remain visible. One-option help and Unicode/ANSI wrapping have higher median latency than a2 on both runs; ten-option help also regresses in CI. Four of eight complete fresh-process medians are slower than a2 in each run, though the affected cases differ. Import-only medians are almost unchanged locally and differ only slightly in CI. Wrapping is 7.507× and 9.055× faster than Click for the measured input, but its a2/a3 ratios of 0.978× and 0.988× show that this is an existing advantage rather than a new improvement in a3. The local schema-2 report and release-CI schema-2 report retain every sample and distribution identity. The published a2 wheel was measured again alongside the candidate in each run. The a2 report and a1 report retain their original historical results. An earlier local candidate run predates the PyPy import correction and is superseded by the fixed local run. Its samples are not pooled with either new run, and timing differences between the two local runs cannot be attributed to the import correction alone. Ratios mean reference median time / candidate median time. Above one means lower candidate latency; below one means higher candidate latency. A ratio of 1.10 means approximately 9.1% less time, not 10% less time. The opening table collects the comparisons needed to interpret the findings; all eighteen warm workloads and all eight cold workloads appear in the complete tables below. Exact medians, variance and measurement boundaries remain in the tables. Local source, distributions and environment The experiment fixes the Click behavior target and the published version control independently of the candidate. Package file hashes are recorded and checked before and after measurement. This prevents a local source edit from silently changing the published baseline. Distribution Wheel filename Wheel SHA-256 Click 8.5.1 click-8.5.1-py3-none-any.whl 8bb5376d2006950386f8c6427613334a2acadc5f559cb80e638d00b4df957e37 Published zclick 0.1.1a2 zclick-0.1.1a2-cp310-abi3-manylinux2014_x86_64.manylinux_2_17_x86_64.whl dd69bc1b014559a0c77319f52334811951e49fb134f916a3e76f5b7abd493a0c Candidate zclick 0.1.1a3 zclick-0.1.1a3-cp310-abi3-manylinux_2_34_x86_64.whl 154c50dfd6659089a959075570bea30ab3eb93a0d0bbf3644b0c859ef871bc51 The published a2 wheel targets manylinux_2_17; the candidate is a host build targeting manylinux_2_34. The interpreter, measurement host and execution schedule are controlled, but the build environments are not identical. The entire measured difference cannot be attributed to source changes alone. A later distribution build on another host needs its own measurement and provenance; the independent CI section below keeps that measurement separate. What changed and what the measurements cover The main change reduces the number of Python-to-Rust calls in reused parsing. The parser previously validated its current definitions and then entered native parsing separately. The new entry point performs those operations in one call while preserving publication of the owned plan and the order of normalizer lookup, Python state construction, flag evaluation and resource release. Dynamic hooks still execute. This mechanism is documented in the architecture and implemented in plan.rs and parser.py. The experiment compares the complete distributions; it does not isolate the number of microseconds contributed by this change alone. Smaller changes reduce repeated work without caching application results. The binding reuses a finite set of literal protocol names such as process and nargs; user-defined names and values remain owned. Exact lists of parameter definitions use a live cursor, so mutation during an attribute lookup remains visible, and list subclasses keep their Python iterator protocol. Each zclap candidate command uses one-argument presence storage, while successful matches still require zclap's event and final validation. These changes are described in the ownership section and parse.rs. Group dispatch reuses the same fixed protocol names and context-stack push performs one thread-local lookup. The implementation continues to use threading.local: an attempted direct _thread import was reverted to keep the pinned upstream light-import behavior. Error-only helpers are imported when needed. Context managers, Python overrides, conversion and callback calls remain observable; there is no cache of default values, environment results, contexts or callback results. The relevant source is dispatch.rs, globals.py and core.py. This revision also fixes observable help and parameter behavior. It preserves the target's parameter-container identity, help-option cache and dynamic attribute access order, constructor truthiness and duplicate-parameter warnings. Those are compatibility changes, not evidence of a speedup. Their paired regression cases are in test_command_help_protocols.py. The tables retain the help regressions instead of removing this cost from the comparison. Measurement boundaries The driver measures four distinct operations at each of four sizes. Keeping the boundaries separate shows where a parser improvement affects a complete command and where other work dominates. Boundary Included work Construct Public option and command construction for 1, 10, 100 or 1,000 options Reuse parser A fresh argument list, live definition validation, token processing and current parser actions through an already-created parser Command.main Invocation of an already-created command, including context creation, parsing, conversion, callback binding and return; standalone_mode=False Render help Public help generation for an already-created command and context Nested command A group resolving and invoking a child with one integer option and a checked result Unicode/ANSI wrapping Public wrapping on fixed Unicode and ANSI-containing text with a checked complete output Fresh-process command or help Interpreter startup, import, construction, invocation or --help, output capture and exit Each warm worker starts in an isolated interpreter with -I, outside the source checkout. Its imports and file hashes are verified before and after measurement. Every round starts a new worker per implementation; each six-round block contains all six implementation orders once. Cold workloads have their own balanced order schedules. The warm driver checks and retains full help and wrapped-text hashes, parsed values, option object identity and callback return values across implementations. Cold-process output is also validated by the driver, but the report does not retain a separate stdout hash for every cold sample. The complete method is in the protocol and compare.py. Scope of the conclusions Both sets of measurements test repeated synthetic option lists, a small nested command and a fixed wrapping workload. They include bindings and context costs at the named boundaries, but they do not represent interactive prompts, filesystem work, completion, expensive application callbacks or every custom subclass. A user's elapsed time also includes their own work. There is no basis here for a claim that every Click application becomes substantially faster after changing its imports. The comparison is with both a fixed behavioral reference and an actual published zclick release. It is not a component ablation: changes in call boundaries, protocol-name reuse, zclap setup and compatibility corrections are measured together. Their individual causal contributions cannot be read from the tables. The substantial wrapping and large-command advantages over Click predate this revision, while the a2 comparison exposes the smaller new changes. Runtime correctness remains a separate requirement. The performance worker checks its outputs, not the entire Click API or all platform behavior. The earlier PyPy import failure was corrected before these frozen runs, but the CPython measurements do not themselves validate PyPy or the complete release matrix. The project's declared main-interpreter restriction also remains an unfinished compatibility item in COMPATIBILITY.md; benchmark success does not remove it. Publication and completed validation do not establish unrestricted Click compatibility; the release manifest explicitly retains that incomplete status. Claim–evidence review Claim Evidence Status and scope One-option and nested full invocation have lower medians than a2 and Click Tables 2–4 and 11–13, complete Command.main boundaries Reproduced in direction; local Click/a3 paired ranges still cross one All parser sizes improve relative to a2 by median Tables 2–4 and 11–13; all paired CI rounds favor a3 Supported in both runs; the Click comparison differs by size and environment Large invocation and wrapping are much faster than Click Tables 2 and 11 with both references Supported for these workloads in both runs; mostly existing gains Every operation improves over a2 Help, wrapping and cold counterexamples in both runs; small import differences Rejected zclick always uses less memory Python traces omit native allocations; Tables 10 and 19 are above Click Rejected Each optimization causes a known fraction of the gain No independently frozen component ablation in this report Not established; no numerical attribution Successful benchmarks and publication establish full Click compatibility The release manifest retains the subinterpreter gap Rejected; release validation and unrestricted compatibility are separate Five-question self-review Contribution: Is this a new large speedup everywhere? No. The strongest relative version change is reused parsing at small sizes; complete invocation improves more modestly and several operations regress. Clarity: Can a reader tell which work each number includes? Tables 2–8 separate construction, parser reuse, warm invocation, help and complete process startup; units and reference direction are explicit. Experimental strength: Are the controls immutable and the reversals visible? Both runs retain distribution, source and native hashes, all eighteen warm cases, all eight cold cases, raw samples and paired ranges. The local and CI results are separate; neither is selected because it is faster. Evaluation completeness: What evidence is missing? Final release validation is linked separately from these measurements. Component ablation and application-specific measurements would be needed for stronger causal or general claims. Two environments are reported, and the earlier candidate's data remains separate. Design soundness: Is less work obtained by removing public behavior? The design retains live definitions, dynamic Python methods and context cleanup. Its behavior must pass the separate compatibility checks; the corrected PyPy import was checked in the separate release matrix, outside this CPython performance experiment. Subinterpreter compatibility remains unfinished. Reproducing the local comparison Use a separate clean checkout of the recorded commit and the same CPython interpreter for both controls and the candidate. The protocol validates the candidate's version and Python file hashes against that checkout. The baseline is selected by baseline-lock.json, which pins the published a2 and Click wheels. The earlier a1 lock remains available for reproducing its own reports and must not be silently substituted here. maturin build --release --locked --out dist/benchmark-candidate python benchmarks/compare.py \ --candidate-wheel dist/benchmark-candidate/zclick-0.1.1a3-cp310-abi3-manylinux_2_34_x86_64.whl \ --iterations 1000 --repeats 12 --seed 20261111 --affinity auto \ --output reports/benchmarks-0.1.1a3.json The example wheel filename is the one measured on this host; use the actual filename produced by the local build, and pass exactly one candidate. On Linux, --affinity auto selects the first CPU in the allowed set. Omit affinity control where it is unavailable and retain that difference in the report. Run timing without competing local builds or tests, preserve the complete JSON and review its source, native hashes and sample ranges before interpreting results. Keep later builds or platforms in separate immutable timing records. Publication and verification Version 0.1.1a3 was published as a preview on 2026-11-13. The GitHub release was created at 06:26:17 UTC, and the release workflow completed successfully with 61 successful jobs. The tag resolves to 9afcc7537212563f66a5d99c9f08f99bfa692731. Exact per-environment project and upstream results, original skips, API and typing checks, shell runs and installation checks are recorded in the release manifest. The PyPI verification records 12 wheels and one source distribution. Every published file's SHA-256 and size match the corresponding GitHub release asset. All thirteen public PyPI provenance responses identify GitHub repository LIghtJUNction/zclick, workflow release.yml and environment pypi, and their subject hashes match the distributions. This is verification of PyPI's public publisher records and artifact hashes; it is not an independent cryptographic verification of Sigstore signatures. A fresh environment outside the repository installed zclick==0.1.1a3 through the normal public PyPI index and ran the prompt-and-greeting example in isolated Python mode with no original Click installed. The check passed at 06:30:38 UTC, and the installed native file's SHA-256 is 32a51fda3373d6168b68c8ec4b790a264e1943466b4613f21af43b3efc21d07b, the same native contents timed in CI. The first installation attempt encountered index propagation delay; a second fresh-environment attempt succeeded. The initial failure log was retained, so this is not reported as first-attempt success. The runtime payload comparison connects the CI measurement with the published GNU distribution at the level of all 18 Python and native files. Wheel archive hashes differ, as documented in the CI section. The publication evidence therefore identifies the measured runtime without claiming identical archive bytes or extrapolating the GNU measurement to macOS, Windows, PyPy or free-threaded binaries.

title: Measured performance: 0.1.1a1
body: 基于 zclap 的 Click 参数语义与 Python 预览绑定。 Measured performance: 0.1.1a1 This page preserves the 0.1.1a1 measurements and their original protocol. The 0.1.1a2 performance document describes the current implementation changes and the separate three-way measurement protocol. For the final measured 0.1.1a1 snapshot, the 1,000-option Command.main workload was 1.706× faster than Click 8.5.1 and the Unicode/ANSI wrapping workload was 7.344× faster. Small warm invocations and reused-parser calls were slower. A fresh process that imported the package, constructed and invoked a 1,000-option command was 1.183× faster in this run. These results are workload-specific and do not establish a universal speedup. Source and environment Date: 2026-11-11. zclick: 0.1.1a1 at 86bab2a8de3092155a912a4028382aba8188e6db. Reference: Click 8.5.1; target.json pins its source, release and documentation. Interpreter: 3.12.14 (main, Aug 25 2026, 14:00:49) [Clang 22.1.3 ]. Host: Linux-6.18.57-x86_64-with-glibc2.41; 9 logical CPUs reported to the process. Build: release extension, Rust 1.99.1 / Edition 2024, zclap 0.1.4 and PyO3 0.30.1. Samples: 9 per workload. Warm measurements use 1,000 base iterations, scaled to 100 for 100 parameters and 10 for 1,000 parameters; help uses one fifth as many, with a minimum of 5. Cold measurements use 9 separate fresh interpreters for each package, size and action. Final raw measurements retain every sample, runtime/native-file hashes, Cargo.lock hash, Python allocation observations and process peak RSS. Earlier 0.1.0 development measurements are retained as history. They are not substituted for the final measurements when an earlier number was more favorable. Warm Python API measurements Values are median microseconds per call. Ratio = Click time / zclick time; above 1 means lower zclick latency. CPU ratios use process CPU time. Wall time also includes scheduling delays. Workload Click wall µs zclick wall µs Wall ratio CPU ratio Construct command (1 option) 3.410 3.981 0.857× 0.856× Reuse parser (1 option) 1.558 3.867 0.403× 0.403× Command.main (1 option) 23.453 33.813 0.694× 0.694× Render help (1 option) 53.449 35.509 1.505× 1.504× Construct command (10 options) 29.481 38.888 0.758× 0.758× Reuse parser (10 options) 6.389 17.415 0.367× 0.367× Command.main (10 options) 70.954 86.287 0.822× 0.822× Render help (10 options) 103.318 74.396 1.389× 1.389× Construct command (100 options) 292.765 367.733 0.796× 0.796× Reuse parser (100 options) 60.797 167.109 0.364× 0.364× Command.main (100 options) 606.239 528.201 1.148× 1.148× Render help (100 options) 525.247 452.839 1.160× 1.160× Construct command (1000 options) 4781.334 3478.570 1.375× 1.374× Reuse parser (1000 options) 1000.769 1516.540 0.660× 0.660× Command.main (1000 options) 11176.295 6552.579 1.706× 1.707× Render help (1000 options) 4899.930 4896.697 1.001× 1.001× Nested command 51.620 53.222 0.970× 0.969× Unicode/ANSI wrap 471.700 64.231 7.344× 7.272× The 1,000-option warm invocation took 11.176 ms with Click and 6.553 ms with zclick, about 41.4% less elapsed time per call. It reuses an already-defined Command: the timed work includes a fresh invocation context, parser-plan setup, argument processing, integer conversion and the command callback. Command and Option construction, process startup and terminal I/O are outside this warm invocation measurement. The reused-parser result is a material limitation. That workload constructs its parser before timing and measures parse_args plus a fresh argument-list copy. Inspection of that 0.1.1a1 runtime shows that it reconstructs the native definition while preserving mutable option objects and original argument identities. The timings do not separate schema construction, zclap work, allocations and binding overhead from each other. A future optimization must retain those mutation and identity guarantees. Whole fresh-process commands Each sample creates a new interpreter, imports the selected package, constructs all Option and Command objects, then invokes the command or renders --help. The interval ends after process termination and includes output capture. These measurements answer a different question from repeated calls in an already-running Python process. Fresh process action Click median ms zclick median ms Ratio Invoke command (1 option) 44.227 41.522 1.065× Render help (1 option) 44.435 41.370 1.074× Invoke command (10 options) 39.195 40.491 0.968× Render help (10 options) 47.201 41.713 1.132× Invoke command (100 options) 44.755 40.799 1.097× Render help (100 options) 46.028 41.057 1.121× Invoke command (1000 options) 62.046 52.450 1.183× Render help (1000 options) 74.022 57.461 1.288× The roughly 3–10% differences in small fresh-process cases should not be treated as significant or guaranteed improvements. Process scheduling, CPU frequency and filesystem caches can affect measurements of this size. Full sample ranges are preserved in the raw JSON. A CLI with expensive user callbacks or filesystem work can show a different ratio. Import-only startup These samples start a fresh interpreter and import the package without constructing a command. Only time is imported before the inner import interval. The whole-process interval includes interpreter startup and printing the timing. Operating-system filesystem caches are not flushed. Boundary Click median ms zclick median ms Ratio Import package 21.352 26.043 0.820× Fresh process + import 40.251 46.862 0.859× Import-only timing does not establish the performance of an actual command. Use the fresh-process command results for that boundary. Memory observations tracemalloc observes Python-managed allocations during one call after a collection; returned objects remain alive through the sample. It does not count every Rust allocation. RSS is a separate process high-water mark across the worker's complete workload set, including the interpreter and benchmark driver. Workload Click Python peak bytes zclick Python peak bytes Construct command (1 option) 3,290 3,458 Reuse parser (1 option) 2,488 1,330 Command.main (1 option) 7,274 7,160 Render help (1 option) 5,288 2,996 Construct command (10 options) 20,252 20,420 Reuse parser (10 options) 2,792 2,522 Command.main (10 options) 14,857 14,891 Render help (10 options) 7,102 4,850 Construct command (100 options) 189,828 189,996 Reuse parser (100 options) 6,584 16,362 Command.main (100 options) 93,387 98,625 Render help (100 options) 25,999 23,729 Construct command (1000 options) 1,887,972 1,888,140 Reuse parser (1000 options) 54,560 163,850 Command.main (1000 options) 780,943 919,413 Render help (1000 options) 215,608 213,339 Nested command 9,810 9,951 Unicode/ANSI wrap 42,128 8,126 Worker peak RSS was 22.78 MiB for Click and 23.82 MiB for zclick. This is not an isolated measurement of native parser allocations. Text wrapping uses fewer observed Python bytes, while large option invocation uses more. The extension allocates Python and Rust objects; no zero-allocation claim is made. Reproduce and interpret the historical run These commands use the driver from the pinned 0.1.1a1 source snapshot above. Use that checkout and its own development environment to reproduce this method. The current driver uses the schema-2 protocol, including three implementations and at least twelve balanced rounds. maturin develop --release --locked python benchmarks/compare.py --iterations 1000 --repeats 9 --output reports/benchmarks.json The driver verifies outputs before warm timing and validates every fresh-process result. The two packages run in separate worker processes. Normal interpreter GC remains enabled. Command construction uses the public Option and Command constructors; each long option receives an integer value, and the callback sums the converted values. Dynamic defaults, prompts, user business logic and application filesystem work are outside these workloads. Packages run in a fixed order: Click, then zclick. The shared host is not isolated with CPU affinity or frequency locking, and package order is not randomized or interleaved. A quiet interval was used, but other host activity remains possible. Nine samples show variability; they are not a statistical guarantee. Small differences and differences between the earlier and final snapshot can reflect both code and measurement conditions. Release CI independently runs this driver on its immutable commit and publishes its raw JSON. Earlier release CI comparison (a8bc735) The release pipeline measured commit a8bc735a3df168b62b2e11d99b34e7ab40530ba7 on a separate runner. Its runtime code is the same as the locally measured 86bab2a snapshot; the release-trigger commit adds documentation and release-note generation. The host and interpreter differ, so the two sets remain separate measurements. CI interpreter: 3.14.10 (main, Oct 26 2026, 14:17:03) [GCC 15.2.0]. CI host: Linux-7.0.0-1019-azure-x86_64-with-glibc2.43; 4 logical CPUs reported. CI raw JSON and release workflow retain source hashes, all repeated samples and the exact environment. Ratios below are Click median / zclick median. All listed boundaries use the same driver and parameters on both hosts. Boundary Local CPython 3.12 ratio CI CPython 3.14 ratio Warm Command.main / 1 option 0.694× 0.939× Warm Command.main / 10 options 0.822× 1.006× Warm Command.main / 100 options 1.148× 1.185× Warm Command.main / 1,000 options 1.706× 2.013× Reused parser / 1 option 0.403× 0.464× Reused parser / 1,000 options 0.660× 0.425× Nested command 0.970× 0.886× Unicode/ANSI wrapping 7.344× 9.038× Fresh-process command / 1 option 1.065× 0.952× Fresh-process command / 10 options 0.968× 0.945× Fresh-process command / 100 options 1.097× 0.961× Fresh-process command / 1,000 options 1.183× 1.067× Fresh-process help / 1,000 options 1.288× 0.953× The larger warm invocation and text-wrapping gains appear on both hosts. The reused parser remains slower on both. Small warm commands and whole-process startup show mixed results. The local 1.288× fresh-process help result did not reproduce on CI, where that boundary measured 0.953×. It must not be presented as a portable help-startup improvement. On CI, the 1,000-option warm invocation was 14.713 ms for Click and 7.309 ms for zclick. Whole-process invocation was 71.540 ms and 67.020 ms respectively; whole-process help was 73.347 ms and 76.995 ms. The approximately 6.7% invocation difference is small relative to the scheduling and frequency limitations of this method and is not claimed to be statistically significant. Neither host's results replace the other. The source archives and release assets retain the original measurements, including regressions. Final release commit (3281e18) The release pipeline for 3281e18f215dec976c3ce0c4b5dd933ad4d62616 generated another complete measurement as part of its required validation. This commit fixes the report-only normalization of five Python 3.10 Enum test IDs and permits independent builds to run alongside validation. It does not change the zclick runtime from either the local 86bab2a measurement or the earlier a8bc735 CI attempt. The earlier release attempt stopped at evidence aggregation; its benchmark remains archived above. The final runner reports CPython 3.14.10, GCC 15.2.0, Linux 7.0.0-1019-azure, glibc 2.43 and four logical CPUs. Final CI raw JSON retains every sample, memory observation, source hash and environment field; the release workflow records how it was produced. This is a separate automatically required run, not a replacement chosen for a better result. Boundary Local 86bab2a ratio Earlier CI a8bc735 ratio Final CI 3281e18 ratio Warm Command.main / 1 option 0.694× 0.939× 1.058× Warm Command.main / 10 options 0.822× 1.006× 1.151× Warm Command.main / 100 options 1.148× 1.185× 1.169× Warm Command.main / 1,000 options 1.706× 2.013× 1.997× Reused parser / 1 option 0.403× 0.464× 0.520× Reused parser / 1,000 options 0.660× 0.425× 0.435× Nested command 0.970× 0.886× 0.889× Unicode/ANSI wrapping 7.344× 9.038× 8.724× Fresh-process command / 1,000 options 1.183× 1.067× 1.148× Fresh-process help / 1,000 options 1.288× 0.953× 1.017× On this final CI runner, the warm 1,000-option invocation measured 11.149 ms for Click and 5.582 ms for zclick. Whole-process invocation measured 63.205 ms and 55.066 ms; whole-process help measured 63.471 ms and 62.415 ms. The warm interval reuses the command definition; the whole-process interval includes interpreter startup, import, command construction, invocation or help rendering, output capture and process exit. The same runtime code shows different small-workload ratios across these runs, including changes from slower to faster. Neither CPU model and frequency nor process affinity and host activity are controlled, the local interpreter differs from CI, and package timing order is fixed. Even identical CI platform strings do not establish identical machine conditions. The final 1.017× cold-help result does not turn the earlier mixed cold-help measurements into a reliable improvement. Large warm invocation and wrapping gains, slower reused parsing, and variable small or cold workloads are the conclusions supported by the complete record; the best individual ratio must not be generalized to every Click application.

title: 概览
body: 转换模型请求、响应与流式事件，让宿主连接不同协议。 zconv Allocation-free AI protocol conversion in stable Rust. zconv converts model requests, complete responses and incremental SSE events. The library is always #![no_std], uses only core, forbids unsafe Rust, and has zero normal, development, build, optional or target-specific dependencies. Input is borrowed. Every output buffer, JSON index, IR arena and stream workspace belongs to the caller. There is no allocator, runtime, I/O, global cache or background work in the library. MSRV: Rust 1.99.1. The same crate builds for Linux, macOS, Windows, aarch64, WASM and bare-metal targets. Benchmarks, examples and tests may use std. Own stream state without borrowing buffers stream::EventEncoderState keeps protocol state without storing references to the caller's buffers. Pass EventEncoderBuffers and response identity context to encode for each event batch. After a capacity error, grow the indicated buffer while preserving its contents and retry the same batch; discard provisional output on error. This supports application-owned growable buffers without unsafe lifetime tricks or another dependency. Supply choice-end and finish events only when the application is ready to publish a successful terminal response.
