Start here Install the current minor release: cargo add zconv@0.4 This complete request conversion is also available as examples/convert.rs: use zconv::ir::Record; use zconv::json::Token; use zconv::{convert, Operation, Options, Protocol, Workspace}; fn main() -> Result<(), zconv::Error> { let input = br#"{"model":"example-model","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hello"}]}"#; let mut tokens = [Token::EMPTY; 64]; let mut records = [Record::EMPTY; 16]; let mut nested_tokens = [Token::EMPTY; 64]; let mut scratch = [0; 512]; let mut output = [0; 1024]; let result = convert( Protocol::OpenAiChat.into(), Protocol::OpenAiResponses.into(), Operation::Request, input, &mut output, Options::default(), Workspace { tokens: &mut tokens, records: &mut records, scratch: &mut scratch, nested_tokens: &mut nested_tokens, }, )?; assert_eq!(result.path, zconv::Path::Direct); assert_eq!(result.resources.ir_records_used, 0); assert_eq!( core::str::from_utf8(&output[..result.written()]).unwrap(), r#"{"model":"example-model","input":[{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"Hello"}]}]}"#, ); Ok(()) } The example capacities are explicit choices for a small request. A successful direct call can use empty IR storage. Auto callers that need IR fallback must provide enough records for their supported inputs. A capacity error never silently allocates a larger buffer. Choose a conversion path Strategy Contract Auto Use an applicable direct implementation; use IR only on a capability miss. Direct Require direct support for this operation and these input features; otherwise return DirectUnavailable. Ir Always decode and encode the semantic representation, even for identical formats. Conversion.path reports Identity, Direct or Ir. Same protocol, version and profile can preserve the original bytes after complete JSON validation and the adapter's source-semantic checks. Invalid JSON, invalid known fields, missing context, forbidden losses and capacity errors are never hidden by fallback. Direct requests and complete responses read borrowed protocol views without constructing normalized IR. Direct streams invoke an event sink without filling the Event IR arena. The implementation shares JSON validation, semantic mapping rules and writer primitives between routes. For deliberate inspection and edits, use protocol::decode_request or decode_response, modify the public IR, then call its encoder. The JSON token tape can be reused immediately after decoding: IR fragments borrow input bytes, not token storage. See examples/edit_ir.rs. Six distinct protocols Adapter Requests Complete responses SSE events OpenAI Completions Text prompt and legacy controls Text choices and usage Text chunks and [DONE] OpenAI Chat Completions Messages, old functions and new tools Messages, tools, choices, refusal, usage Text/tool/refusal deltas, choices and usage OpenAI Responses Input items, instructions, tools and context references Output items, status and usage Typed item/content/tool events and required final snapshots Anthropic Messages Content blocks, system, tools and media Blocks, stop state and cache-aware usage Message/block lifecycle, partial tool JSON and cumulative usage Gemini GenerateContent Contents/parts and function declarations Candidates, functions and usage streamGenerateContent with alt=sse Gemini Interactions v1 Independent interaction input and context Independent steps and status interaction.* and step.* events The six Chat ↔ Responses / Anthropic / GenerateContent directions implement direct requests, complete responses and supported stream events. Remaining directions use IR. A direct direction can still reject a feature and let Auto select IR; for example, most nonstream media paths currently use IR. The support and fidelity matrix distinguishes faithful conversion, caller-supplied context, explicit downgrade and unrepresentable features for each protocol and operation. Anthropic citation, redacted-thinking, server-tool and detailed-usage events have an explicit same-origin representation; they do not become local function calls. Other unsupported event families return errors. Gemini Interactions is not an alias for GenerateContent. Stored response, interaction and provider file handles retain their source namespace. An OpenAI compatible provider must select an explicit Profile; its extensions are not automatically injected into another provider. Resource APIs api provides independently implemented wire contracts for Batch, Files, Embeddings and Images. These are resource messages, not new conversation protocols. They use the same caller-owned JSON tokens and output buffers: Resource Implemented wire operations Batch Create/retrieve/list/cancel metadata, input/output JSONL envelopes, error records and pagination Files Multipart upload with binary contents and expiry, retrieve/list/delete metadata, content-download endpoint Embeddings Text/token batches, dimensions, float/base64 encoding, typed request/response builders and borrowed vectors Images Generation and JSON/multipart edits, response metadata/usage, partial/completed image SSE events; legacy variation wire format api::parse validates known fields and retains unknown fields. Document::encode preserves validated JSON bytes. encode_object constructs and validates resource objects, while EmbeddingsRequest, EmbeddingsResponse and FileUpload provide typed builders. Endpoint writes method/path metadata; the caller performs HTTP, authentication, retries, pagination and provider operations. File content is arbitrary bytes and deliberately does not pass through a JSON parser. See resource contracts and examples and the runnable examples/resources.rs. No upstream SDK is linked or re-exported, so adding these contracts does not change the dependency graph. Strict fidelity and explicit context The default Policy rejects semantic loss. Narrow options can permit dropping extensions, reasoning, provider context or nonportable metadata. The conversion report counts these losses and identifies metadata fields. For per-field details, retain the decoded IR and use Request::losses or Response::losses. Streaming has its own exact DroppedField mask. Missing, null, empty text, empty lists and numeric zero are distinct. Numbers stay as original JSON spans where possible; integer usage never passes through floating point. Anthropic cache counters and Gemini thought counters are normalized with checked integer arithmetic, then separated again when required by the target. Supply facts absent from a source through Context / StreamContext: model, response ID, timestamps, required output limits, tool ID/name bindings and Responses output item IDs. No clock or random ID generator is hidden inside the converter. GenerateContent model/stream selection is returned as transport metadata because those settings do not belong in its JSON request body. Chat-compatible reasoning accepts reasoning_content or reasoning, including ordered string arrays, only under an explicit compatible profile. Raw reasoning maps to Responses reasoning.content; summaries stay in reasoning.summary. Targets that cannot preserve that distinction reject the conversion unless the caller explicitly drops reasoning. Signatures retain their source identity. Incremental streams and memory examples/stream.rs feeds seven-byte input fragments into a Chat → Responses converter and drains thirteen-byte output fragments. The API requires no async runtime: let step = converter.step(input_fragment, output_fragment, eof); // Advance input by step.consumed; commit output[..step.written]. // NeedInput / NeedOutput / NeedBuffer / Done / Failed are explicit. SSE framing handles CR, LF, CRLF, BOM, comments, multiple data lines and arbitrary network splits. Output backpressure and workspace growth preserve consumed bytes and never replay committed events. Stream routing is fixed before the first output. StreamConfig::usage_emission = UsageEmission::Continuous emits currently observed usage alongside Chat/Completions chunks and emits usage-only updates. The default remains Final. Cumulative values replace prior values; they are never summed per chunk. Missing counts remain unknown. Request stream_options are typed in IR and returned as EncodeReport::transport_stream_options for targets without a matching request field; the application selects the stream encoder's output mode from that preference. Text paths without target snapshots do not retain the entire answer. Tool arguments need bounded storage for validation at completion. Responses targets must emit complete final snapshots, so their aggregate space grows with the answer. This cost is supplied and measured separately; it is not omitted to claim fixed memory. The streaming contract explains lifecycle, EOF, usage, snapshots, profiles and buffer replacement. Conversion.resources and StreamConverter::memory() distinguish input/output, reserved capacities, state size, IR records and observed high-water usage. OutputTooSmall provides an exact output size; token/IR capacity errors provide a lower bound. JSON input size, nesting, tokens and object members have explicit limits. Duplicate keys, including escape-equivalent names, are rejected. Build, verify and measure cargo test --all-targets --locked cargo +1.99.1 test --all-targets --locked cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings cargo run --example convert cargo run --example edit_ir cargo run --example stream cargo run --example memory cargo run --example resources cargo bench --bench convert -- --full cargo bench --bench json -- --full cargo bench --bench stream -- --full cargo bench --bench resources -- --full python3 scripts/check_package.py The main crate's tests and benchmarks have no third-party dependencies. Optional comparison/ and fuzz/ workspaces contain the external serde_json/libFuzzer oracles and are excluded from both the crate dependency graph and release package. CI also runs Miri, MSRV/stable on three operating systems, cross-target checks and a package audit. Measured performance and memory Validation evidence and reproduction Architecture, borrowing and recovery Version bump and registry release workflow Changes Sources and scope Official protocol documentation was checked on 2026-11-15. Adapter versions, source URLs and interpretation rules are recorded in SOURCES.md. The historical design study uses cortexfs-protocol at commit 84f349c97bc2f6a611109686a02e21de3800042a. This implementation is independent and does not depend on that crate. The crates.io API confirmed that zconv did not exist before initialization. The release gate rechecks name ownership and version availability immediately before publication; that earlier result does not reserve the name. The library's boundary is wire data and event semantics. Networking, authentication, connection pooling, retries, model execution and server resource management belong to the caller. License MIT OR Apache-2.0.

title: Resource API contracts
body: 转换模型请求、响应与流式事件，让宿主连接不同协议。 Resource API contracts The api module validates and writes OpenAI resource messages without importing an SDK. A conversation converter changes the representation of model messages; a resource contract describes the bytes sent to a file, batch, embedding or image endpoint. Those are separate jobs, so the six Protocol variants are unchanged. Every input is borrowed. Token arrays, multipart boundaries, output buffers and HTTP transport belong to the caller. The crate performs no network operation, allocation, tokenization, image decoding, base64 decoding or provider-side task. The source specifications are linked in SOURCES.md. Contract inventory API Request support Response support Caller responsibility Embeddings Single text, text arrays, token IDs and token batches; model, dimensions, float/base64 and user Ordered embedding items, indexes, float/base64 vectors, model and integral usage Tokenize text when token IDs are desired; choose model-supported dimensions; decode base64 if needed Batch Create; retrieve/list/cancel method/path metadata; nonstream input JSONL Batch state, counts, file IDs, errors, usage, lists and result/error JSONL Upload source file, ensure unique custom IDs across the file, validate endpoint-specific bodies, poll and download output Files Binary multipart upload, purpose and optional expiry; retrieve/list/delete/content method/path metadata File metadata, nullable byte count, expiry, pagination and delete confirmation HTTP transfer; treat content-download bytes according to their actual MIME type Images Generation JSON; image edit JSON references or binary multipart; legacy variation multipart URL/base64 output, revised prompts, metadata and usage; partial/completed generation/edit SSE payloads Model capabilities, media limits, actual image processing and network streaming Endpoint::request_schema() returns a JSON contract where one exists. Image edits also accept multipart; Files upload and legacy variations are multipart-only. FileContent has no response JSON schema. It is a raw byte response. The legacy variation endpoint is retained for wire interoperability, not an availability claim about a retired provider operation. Parse, inspect and preserve use zconv::api::{self, Schema}; use zconv::json::{Limits, Token}; let input = br#"{"object":"file","id":"file_1","filename":"input.jsonl","purpose":"batch","bytes":null,"created_at":1,"future_field":{"x":1}}"#; let mut tokens = [Token::EMPTY; 64]; let doc = api::parse(Schema::File, input, &mut tokens, Limits::default())?; assert!(doc.id().unwrap().eq_str("file_1")); assert!(doc.field("bytes").unwrap().is_null()); let mut output = [0; 512]; let n = doc.encode(&mut output)?; assert_eq!(&output[..n], input); # Ok::<(), zconv::Error>(()) Document borrows the input and token tape. Do not reuse that tape while using the view. Document::raw() detaches a validated JSON fragment which borrows only the input bytes. Fields that are unknown to this release remain available through field/value and survive raw encoding; that does not assert their semantics are understood. Known fields and required resource discriminators are checked. JSON duplicate keys, including escape-equivalent names, remain invalid. encode_object constructs arbitrary supported resource objects from FieldValue entries, then validates the result against a chosen schema. FieldValue::Json requires an already parsed RawValue; arbitrary bytes cannot masquerade as JSON. On any error, discard provisional output. OutputTooSmall reports the exact size needed; token limits and semantic errors do not cause hidden buffer growth. Typed embedding builders EmbeddingsRequest::new accepts an EmbeddingInput: Text, Texts, Tokens or TokenBatches. It writes JSON directly into caller storage. Empty inputs, empty token batches and zero dimensions are rejected. Optional Encoding::Float and Encoding::Base64 select the requested vector representation. EmbeddingsResponse writes borrowed Embedding items. EmbeddingVector::Floats contains f32 values; non-finite values fail instead of producing invalid JSON. Base64 preserves the supplied string. A parsed response exposes each vector through Document::embedding, and the raw JSON number spellings are unchanged. These APIs do not normalize vector lengths or claim to validate a model's shape. Batch JSONL encode_batch_input(custom_id, url, body, output) accepts a parsed JSON object, requires a nonempty custom ID and API path, and writes a POST envelope. It rejects stream:true. Whitespace outside JSON strings is compacted so a pretty-printed input still produces one physical JSONL line. String escapes and content remain unchanged. Append a newline when assembling the file. JsonLines yields borrowed lines, accepts LF/CRLF and a terminal newline, and rejects blank records. Parse each line as Schema::BatchInput or Schema::BatchOutput using a reusable token tape. Envelope validation does not validate the entire model request inside body; use the relevant conversation or resource adapter. File-wide ID uniqueness and request-count limits require caller state and are not invented by a stateless line iterator. Multipart and binary content FileUpload provides a typed upload with filename, MIME type, bytes, purpose and optional expiry seconds. encode_multipart also supports image edits and the legacy variation format using borrowed Part values. A filename-bearing part is binary and is never decoded as UTF-8. Ordinary fields must contain UTF-8. Choose a boundary of 1–70 allowed RFC 2046 characters and send a matching header, for example Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary="chosen-boundary". Boundaries that occur at a potential delimiter in a part are rejected before any output is written. Header control characters, quotes and backslashes are rejected; choose an acceptable transport filename rather than inserting raw quoted header text. Repeated image[] parts are allowed; duplicate scalar fields are rejected. Use Endpoint::write_path to build paths. IDs are percent-encoded as one segment, so an embedded slash does not alter routing. ListQuery::encode writes escaped pagination fields starting with ?; a zero limit is invalid. The caller combines these bytes with a provider base URL and chooses appropriate endpoint-specific pagination limits. Image streaming Parse image_generation.partial_image, image_generation.completed, image_edit.partial_image and image_edit.completed as Schema::ImageStreamEvent. Partial events require an index. Document::encode_sse frames the validated payload with an event discriminator and data: lines, including when the source JSON contains formatting newlines. The existing sse framer can decode fragmented transport input; these resource events are separate from conversation StreamConverter events. Unknown image event types fail explicitly so they cannot be mistaken for successful completion. Verification tests/resource_api.rs exercises realistic response shapes, JSONL, unknown-field preservation, malformed known fields, path escaping, binary multipart content, image SSE and exact output capacities. tests/allocation.rs measures the builders, parse/encode paths and multipart upload with a positive-controlled allocator. examples/resources.rs combines an embedding request, Batch JSONL and Files upload. benches/resources.rs measures resource parse/validation/encoding; its results describe local CPU work, not model latency or remote API availability.

title: Architecture and contracts
body: 转换模型请求、响应与流式事件，让宿主连接不同协议。 Architecture and contracts Why storage belongs to the caller A protocol converter must inspect structure, remember stream lifecycle, and write new syntax. Those operations do not require a heap allocator. zconv borrows input bytes and asks the caller for each storage region explicitly. An exhausted region produces a recoverable capacity result rather than allocating a hidden fallback buffer. Layer Representation Storage owner Purpose JSON Validated UTF-8 spans and subtree-end token indices Caller token slice Complete syntax validation and cheap subtree navigation Native views json::Value over input and token tape Borrowed Direct field lookup without owned values Request / response IR Separate headers and a typed record arena Caller record slice Inspection, editing, extension isolation Direct conversion Native view and JSON writer Caller output Avoid semantic arena construction Event IR Typed events with payload-relative spans Caller event slice Explicit streaming IR and edits Stream lifecycle Converter state and item/checkpoint slices Caller IDs, indices, usage, completion, backpressure Aggregation Append-only linked segments Caller byte slice Required complete snapshots and object tool arguments The token tape is a compact index, not an owned general-purpose DOM. JSON keys are sorted through index links solely to detect duplicate decoded names. Original object order and byte spans remain unchanged. Duplicate detection is bounded by O(k log k) comparisons for an object with k keys; it does not repeatedly scan all earlier keys. Routing flowchart TD A["Validate JSON"] --> B{"Strategy"} B -->|"Ir"| C["Decode semantic IR"] B -->|"Auto or Direct"| D{"Same protocol, version and profile"} D -->|"Yes"| E["Validate source and copy identity bytes"] D -->|"No"| F["Inspect direct feature support"] F -->|"Applicable"| G["Native view to target writer"] F -->|"Capability miss and Auto"| C F -->|"Capability miss and Direct"| H["Structured error"] C --> I["Encode semantic IR"] Only DirectUnavailable allows Auto fallback. A syntax error, invalid known field, policy rejection, missing context, or capacity error never triggers a second conversion attempt. A Direct capability failure still validates source semantics before returning, so unsupported fields cannot hide malformed input. The direct implementation consumes borrowed wire values and never constructs request/response records. Forced IR always decodes and encodes, including for identical formats. Identity validates the complete JSON document and the source adapter's declared semantic contract before copying bytes. It preserves unknown extension bytes because the source and target protocol, version and provider profile are equal. Lifetimes and editing A native Value borrows both input and the token tape. RawValue detaches a validated fragment: it borrows input only. Request and response IR use detached fragments, so their token tape can immediately be reused. Text is either a borrowed JSON string or a caller-supplied UTF-8 replacement. A replacement must outlive encoding. The caller owns the IR record arena and may inspect or modify its public semantic fields; encoding validates record ranges and rejects invalid structure instead of indexing unchecked memory. Stream event spans borrow the associated payload logically rather than storing self-referential pointers. decode_event writes caller event records; stage_events validates spans and encodes an edited event batch transactionally. After a stream callback or step advances, callers must not retain a view into a reused input workspace. Rust's ordinary borrowing rules govern native views. Faithfulness and provenance The default policy rejects unrepresentable semantics. Narrow permissions allow dropping provider extensions, reasoning, provider context, or nonportable metadata. Reports distinguish these categories and include metadata field bits; the IR loss iterator identifies extension names, owner records and source formats. Tool call IDs, usage, errors, safety/refusal state and context IDs are not generic metadata that can silently disappear. An OpenAI previous-response handle and a Gemini previous-interaction handle belong to different namespaces. The converter never translates their strings into each other. A caller must materialize the relevant history or explicitly permit dropping the reference. Provider file IDs obey the same ownership rule. Gemini GenerateContent carries model selection in a URL and streaming selection in its method. EncodeReport.transport_model and transport_stream retain those facts separately from the JSON body. zconv performs no transport, authentication, model calls, retries, or server-side resource lookup. Numbers and usage Unmodified numbers retain their original JSON byte spans. Integer token counts never pass through floating point. Where one provider's accounting differs, checked integer arithmetic makes the conversion explicit. Anthropic usage updates are cumulative: a new present counter replaces its prior value. A field absent from an update retains its last known value. If both canonical input and output are known, a missing total can be computed with checked addition; counters that cannot be supplied or derived remain unknown. Repeated updates are not added together. Capacity recovery and output commitment For nonstream conversion, bytes in the output buffer are provisional until a successful return. On error discard them. OutputTooSmall.needed is exact after counting the complete output. Enlarge the output and retry the same input. Token/IR capacity errors report the first required capacity as a lower bound. Increasing that capacity and retrying may reveal a later requirement. Streaming stages one converted source event before exposing its bytes. A short output slice drains the pending event over multiple calls. Each step reports consumed input and written output. Resend only the unconsumed suffix. Capacity failures roll back semantic state and preserve the framed event; replace the named caller buffer and resume. Successfully committed output is never replayed. The path is fixed before the first output. Direct and IR streaming share the same primitive event semantics: Direct invokes the sink immediately; IR first materializes the caller event tape. A later unsupported event fails explicitly. Resource limits JSON defaults limit input to 16 MiB, nesting to 64, tokens to 262,144, and object members to 16,384. The caller may lower these limits. Nesting has an independent hard ceiling of 64, so passing usize::MAX does not disable stack safety. No core module hides a giant fixed array or performs heap allocation. Conversion.resources reports input and written output separately from reserved token, IR, scratch and nested-token capacities. StreamConverter::memory adds state size, framing/data/pending capacities, item checkpoints, event IR and aggregation, with observed high-water counters. Capacity is reported as capacity; it is not labeled measured peak usage.

title: Performance and memory measurements
body: 转换模型请求、响应与流式事件，让宿主连接不同协议。 Performance and memory measurements Version 0.4 resource contracts — 2026-11-15 cargo bench --bench resources -- --full measures JSON parsing, semantic validation and byte-preserving output together. Each row is the median of nine batch-average durations, with fixture construction and allocation outside the timed loop. The run used Rust 1.100.0, Linux x86_64 and the repository's thin-LTO bench profile. Concurrent work in this shared workspace affects scheduling and these results do not set a release performance threshold. Resource fixture Input bytes Median per operation Input throughput 1536-element float embedding 17,618 204.347 µs 82.22 MiB/s Completed batch metadata 214 8.620 µs 23.68 MiB/s File metadata 97 2.072 µs 44.66 MiB/s Completed image event 140 2.779 µs 48.04 MiB/s Raw results: resources-0.4.0.csv. Zero-allocation behavior is checked separately by the positive-controlled allocation oracle. Historical protocol measurements — 2026-11-10 These are reproducible measurements of the library, not model/network latency or a comparison with another product. The measured code is commit e227184715ba53e827d5435974de88c1f7533c3f. Documentation and the corpus initialization script were added afterward without changing the measured kernel. Environment and method Measured on 2026-11-10, Linux x86_64, Intel Xeon Platinum 8573C, Rust 1.99.1 (58cf8f9c3, LLVM 23.1.1). Cargo's bench profile uses thin LTO, one codegen unit and its default optimized level. This is a shared environment; CPU affinity, frequency and other tenants were not controlled. Small differences and tail outliers should not be treated as stable guarantees. Local compilation, tests and fuzzing were stopped during the final conversion/stream measurements. Fixture creation, allocation and output formatting are outside the timed loops. The input bytes and result are passed through black_box. Conversion includes complete JSON syntax/UTF-8/duplicate-key validation, source feature checks and target writing. Output is actually generated; a parser-only result is not labeled conversion throughput. Complete request conversion Run cargo bench --bench convert -- --full. The harness takes 15 batches of 10,000 conversions (312 per batch for the long fixture). The CSV's median_ns and p95_ns describe batch-average time per conversion, not individual-call latency percentiles. Input throughput uses input bytes, not target byte count. Chat source fixture → target Input Direct median IR median IR / Direct Small → Responses 127 B 3.702 µs 4.122 µs 1.11× Small → Anthropic 127 B 2.908 µs 4.973 µs 1.71× Small → GenerateContent 127 B 2.558 µs 4.187 µs 1.64× Function definition → Responses 280 B 4.571 µs 5.095 µs 1.11× Long mixed text → Responses 57,435 B 73.363 µs 72.615 µs 0.99× Long mixed text → Anthropic 57,435 B 71.033 µs 77.278 µs 1.09× Long mixed text → GenerateContent 57,435 B 71.544 µs 75.720 µs 1.06× For the long fixture, Direct input throughput is approximately 747–771 MiB/s. Direct removes semantic record construction, but long inputs are dominated by validation and byte handling shared with IR. It is not faster on every measured case. Default Auto prefers an applicable Direct path because that is the API contract; it does not promise the lowest latency for every input. Tool requests to Anthropic/GenerateContent currently require IR. Auto spends about 0.8 µs more than forced IR on these fixtures while checking direct applicability. Callers with a known IR-only workload can select Strategy::Ir. Direct and IR may emit different legal JSON shapes, such as explicit default item type fields; the differential tests compare semantics and loss reports. The throughput harness reserves generous reusable buffers for all cases. Its *_reserved columns are capacities, not minimum requirements or measured peaks. Use the separate capacity example below for the small-footprint case. Raw results: convert.csv. Incremental streaming Run cargo bench --bench stream -- --full. There are 24 cases: two targets, three strategies, one-byte or whole-stream input, and 17-byte or whole-result output slices. Each stream contains 16 text chunks, UTF-8 and escapes, a finish event, usage and [DONE]: 3,348 input bytes and 848 decoded text bytes. The harness uses 21 calibrated batches, aiming at about 20 ms per batch. It also samples individual streams separately. batch_* statistics and single_* statistics are intentionally distinct. First-write latency includes converter construction and ends when the first step call returns written > 0. Selected Auto cases, all using Direct and a 17-byte output slice: Target Input slice Batch-average median / stream Individual first-write median Output Anthropic Whole 3,348 B 67.844 µs 3.455 µs 3,490 B Anthropic 1 B 119.102 µs 5.360 µs 3,490 B Responses Whole 3,348 B 84.284 µs 3.727 µs 9,173 B Responses 1 B 131.907 µs 5.647 µs 9,173 B These numbers measure conversion work after bytes are available. They do not measure time to the first generated model token. With both entire-stream input and sufficient output space, one step can finish the whole conversion before returning, so first caller-visible output time can approach total stream time. Direct and IR streaming use the same semantic sink. Their timing differences are small and noisy on these fixtures; the clear Direct storage saving is the absence of the Event IR arena. The full CSV includes all latency percentiles, step counts, actual paths and memory regions. It has a timing table followed by a separately headed memory table; lines beginning with # explain the schema. Raw results: stream.csv. Zero allocation and small storage are separate checks tests/allocation.rs installs a counting allocator only in the std test binary. A positive allocation control verifies the oracle. Thread-local counters exclude unrelated test-runner activity. Parsing, Identity, Direct, IR, and Direct/IR streaming all produce zero allocation calls and zero allocated bytes in the measured section. The library itself forbids unsafe Rust; the test's allocator wrapper delegates unchanged contracts to System. Run cargo run --example memory for a fixture-specific storage measurement. It determines token/record capacities and exact output length before the final conversion. Those probe allocations are outside the conversion and are released before its buffers are prepared. Small Chat → Responses resource Direct IR Borrowed input 72 B 72 B Output capacity 100 B 117 B JSON token storage: 10 × 20 B 200 B 200 B Semantic IR storage 0 B 432 B: 2 × 216 B Scratch / nested token storage 0 / 0 B 0 / 0 B Provided buffers, excluding input 300 B 749 B Input plus provided buffers 372 B 821 B These are slice capacities for this exact fixture, not process RSS, stack usage, allocator bookkeeping or a universal bound. Larger structures need more tokens and IR records. The output shapes differ legally, accounting for the 17-byte output difference. Streaming storage and aggregation On the measured x86_64 build, StreamConverter is 832 B, ActiveItem 88 B, Event 216 B and Token 20 B. The table below describes the same 848-byte answer fixture. Each number comes from memory() or the caller's declared storage. Region Anthropic target Responses target Converter state 832 B 832 B Framing capacity / high water 189 / 188 B 189 / 188 B Data capacity / high water 181 / 181 B 181 / 181 B Pending capacity / high water 512 / 475 B 4,592 / 3,336 B JSON token capacity / high water 1,280 / 400 B 1,280 / 400 B Item and rollback checkpoint capacity 88 + 88 B 88 + 88 B Direct Event IR capacity 0 B 0 B IR Event arena capacity / high water 432 / 432 B 432 / 432 B Aggregate capacity / high water 64 / 25 B 1,161 / 1,129 B Direct state + workspace capacity 3,234 B 8,411 B IR state + workspace capacity 3,666 B 8,843 B Input and the caller's output slice are separate: a one-byte input fragment and a 17-byte output slice can be reused. The benchmark happens to hold its whole source fixture for repetition. No full-source buffer is owned by the converter. Anthropic conversion retains 25 bytes of response ID/model metadata and does not accumulate the answer. Responses conversion retains text, fragment links and metadata to produce required final snapshots. This is a real cost that grows with content. Tool arguments also require bounded aggregation and may temporarily need a contiguous validation copy at completion. workspace_high_water_sum adds separately observed region high waters; those maxima need not occur at the same instant. It is not labeled a simultaneous peak or RSS. Stack frames and the caller's storage placement are additional costs. JSON recursion has a hard depth ceiling of 64 and can be lowered through json::Limits; lower limits reduce both accepted nesting and recursive stack requirements. Stack cost is additional An independent diagnostic build records compiler-emitted static stack frames. It uses Rust 1.102.0-nightly (ac8310ba6 2026-11-09), LLVM 23.1.5, x86_64, opt-level=3, one codegen unit and -Z emit-stack-sizes, producing a relocatable object without final linking/LTO. It does not change the crate's stable-Rust or MSRV requirement. Function Static frame in the diagnostic object json::parse 168 B JSON recursive value / array / object 72 / 88 / 264 B Top-level convert 1,864 B Direct request / response writer 1,320 / 1,544 B IR request decoder / encoder 1,400 / 1,016 B IR response decoder / encoder 920 / 1,000 B StreamConverter::step 1,640 B There are 231 records; the largest individual record is the content-block decoder at 3,128 B. Frames on an active call chain add together, and recursive JSON levels repeat frames. Inlining, ABI and application LTO can change these numbers. This is not a measured whole-call stack peak or a proven total memory bound. The 300-byte Direct buffer example must therefore not be described as 300-byte total conversion memory. Embedded callers should select nesting limits for their stack budget and measure their final linked application. Full records: stack-sizes.csv. Reproduce on a little-endian ELF64 Linux target with Rust nightly and GNU c++filt available: rustc +nightly --crate-name zconv --crate-type lib --edition 2021 \ -C opt-level=3 -C codegen-units=1 -Z emit-stack-sizes \ --emit=obj src/lib.rs -o /tmp/zconv.o python3 scripts/measure_stack.py /tmp/zconv.o Measured JSON optimization The retained optimization skips an initial ordinary string prefix using safe, portable 64-bit byte tests. Quotes, backslashes and control bytes return to the scalar validator; UTF-8 validation still covers the complete input. It uses no unsafe loads or architecture-specific intrinsics. Boundary tests cover every byte value at positions around word boundaries, including controls and escapes. An isolated A/B harness builds the pre-optimization JSON kernel from 96fa6fc606e265d58b60a20073f2354f7564169e and the current kernel with the same types, benchmark and compiler flags. Two passes reverse before/after order. Each result is the median of nine batch averages. The second pass gives: JSON fixture Bytes Before After Ratio Long ASCII 65,560 78.558 µs 13.834 µs 5.68× Long Unicode 98,328 184.454 µs 101.162 µs 1.82× Escape-dense 73,752 84.226 µs 72.596 µs 1.16× Across both passes, long ASCII improved 4.89–5.68× and long Unicode 1.66–1.82×; the escape-dense case did not regress in these measurements. These ratios apply to this JSON kernel benchmark, not to end-to-end model calling or every protocol conversion. Raw results: before 1, after 1, before 2, after 2. Reproduction cargo bench --bench convert -- --full > convert.csv cargo bench --bench stream -- --full > stream.csv cargo bench --bench json -- --full > json.csv cargo run --example memory python3 scripts/compare_json.py --output /tmp/zconv-json-comparison Run benchmarks separately from compilation, tests and fuzzing. Retain compiler, architecture, fixture and capacity details with any new results. CI runs quick benchmark smoke tests for correctness; noisy timing thresholds are not release gates.

title: Protocol and design sources
body: 转换模型请求、响应与流式事件，让宿主连接不同协议。 Protocol and design sources Conversation documentation was reviewed on 2026-11-10 and the 0.4 compatibility and resource contracts were checked on 2026-11-15. Adapter versions are explicit in Format. Adapter Wire version Primary specification OpenAI Completions v1, legacy prompt API https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/completions/methods/create OpenAI Chat Completions v1, legacy functions and current tools https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/chat OpenAI Responses v1 https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/responses Responses events v1 https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/responses/streaming-events Function strict defaults Chat versus Responses https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/function-calling Responses migration semantics Tool schema defaults and item identity https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/migrate-to-responses Anthropic Messages 2023-06-01; explicit newer version checks https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/messages Anthropic version differences 2026-10-21 https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/migration-2026-10-21 Anthropic streaming versioned Messages events https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/streaming Gemini GenerateContent v1beta JSON REST mapping https://ai.google.dev/api/generate-content Gemini Interactions v1, step-based resource https://ai.google.dev/api/interactions-api-v1 Gemini Interactions events interaction / step events https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/streaming Gemini thought accounting Visible output versus thought tokens https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/thought-signatures SSE framing WHATWG Living Standard, 2026-11-09 revision https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/server-sent-events.html JSON grammar RFC 8259 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8259 Batch resource v1 https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/batches/methods/create Batch JSONL v1 https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/batch Files resource/upload v1 https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/files/methods/create Embeddings v1 https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/embeddings/methods/create Image generation v1 https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/images/methods/generate Image edits v1 https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/images/methods/edit Image events and output v1 https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/images Multipart boundary grammar RFC 2046, section 5.1 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2046#section-5.1 Pinned design study Repository: https://github.com/LIghtJUNction/cortexfs Commit: 84f349c97bc2f6a611109686a02e21de3800042a Directory: crates/cortexfs-protocol Read: borrowed.rs, bridge.rs, direct.rs, context.rs, event.rs, request.rs, response.rs, semantic.rs, openaichat.rs, openairesponses.rs, gemini.rs, and the crate README. Borrowed wire views, a separate semantic model, explicit context ownership and provider namespaces are the design ideas reused. zconv is independently implemented with caller-owned storage and has no dependency on cortexfs-protocol. Identity conversions validate their input. Automatic fallback is restricted to capability errors; malformed input and capacity errors remain errors. Registry check Before initialization, GET https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/zconv?nocache=20261110 with an identifying User-Agent returned HTTP 404 and {"errors":[{"detail":"crate zconv does not exist"}]}. The sparse registry entry https://index.crates.io/zc/on/zconv was also absent. The initial no-User-Agent request returned HTTP 403; that response was not treated as evidence of name availability. The release gate repeats the API check before publication; name availability is not a reservation. Interpretation rules Gemini Interactions is a separate resource: its previous_interaction_id belongs to its provider namespace. It cannot become an OpenAI previous_response_id. Current Interactions uses steps, including model_output, thought, function_call, and function_result, and step-based streaming events. Anthropic 2026-10-21 removes sampling parameters. Adapters must reject requests that would emit temperature, top_p or top_k for that version, even if a value matches an earlier default. These are protocol version differences, not vendor extensions. Specifications define the supported wire contract. Additional model-specific validation and network headers remain the caller's responsibility. The new resource module is an independent implementation of wire contracts, not an upstream type re-export. Embedding vectors remain floating JSON values or base64 strings; numeric token accounting remains integral. Files bytes may be null, and binary file content has no JSON schema. Batch JSONL validates individual envelopes but cannot establish file-wide custom ID uniqueness without caller state. Legacy image variation encoding preserves a historical wire format and does not assert that a retired endpoint or model is available on a provider. Defaults and token-accounting differences Chat function definitions without an explicit strict setting use best-effort calling. Responses attempts schema normalization into strict mode when possible, otherwise falls back to best effort. Cross-conversion from Chat therefore writes strict:false; a Responses source with unresolved missing/null strict requires the caller to resolve the mode in IR before cross-conversion. Same-format IR retains the source's field-presence state. Explicit boolean settings are retained only where the target can express that guarantee. Anthropic's input_tokens excludes its separately reported cache read/write counts. The IR's input total includes them. Gemini's visible output count excludes thought tokens; the IR/OpenAI output total includes them. These conversions use checked integer addition/subtraction. The Interactions v1 reference example with input 7, visible output 23, thought 49 and total 79 is a regression fixture: canonical output is 72, and encoding back to Gemini restores visible output 23. The documented OpenAI Responses SSE union includes completed, incomplete and failed lifecycle events. A similarly named cancellation webhook is not reused as a stream event. Length and safety finishes preserve distinct incomplete reasons instead of being labeled successful completion.

title: Streaming conversion
body: 转换模型请求、响应与流式事件，让宿主连接不同协议。 Streaming conversion StreamConverter converts an SSE response as bytes arrive. It consumes arbitrary input fragments, stages one source event, and drains the resulting target events into arbitrary output fragments. It owns no heap allocations. Every growing region is supplied in StreamBuffers. The runnable example is examples/stream.rs. The conformance and recovery tests are tests/stream.rs and tests/sse.rs. Calling contract Construct StreamConfig::new(source, target), supply any missing target context, and initialize the buffers. Call step(input, output, eof) repeatedly. Advance the input cursor by Step.consumed and use only output[..Step.written]. Status Caller action NeedInput Supply the next input fragment. NeedOutput Supply more output space and resend only the unconsumed input suffix. NeedBuffer Enlarge the named workspace with the corresponding replacement method, then resume the same unconsumed suffix. Done The source terminated and all staged output has drained. Failed(error) Stop conversion. Previously returned bytes remain committed; this converter cannot restart or choose another path. eof=true means the supplied fragment is the last fragment. If output fills before all of it is consumed, keep eof=true while resubmitting its unconsumed suffix. A zero-length output slice is supported: it applies backpressure and can return NeedOutput without writing anything. NeedBuffer.needed is an exact size for decoded event data and completed pending output. For a partially received event, token tape, item slots, IR events or an aggregate arena, it is a lower bound. The caller can choose a larger growth factor or impose an application limit. A configured JSON depth, input or token limit is a hard error; supplying a larger slice does not bypass that limit. Each completed source event is a transaction. On a capacity failure, item records, aggregate links, counters and output sequence numbers are restored to their pre-event state. The framed event remains available. Growing a buffer does not require refeeding bytes already counted as consumed. The zero-capacity recovery test exercises all seven replaceable workspace classes. Routing and event IR Direct invokes the target writer from validated source views without creating an Event record. Ir first fills the caller's events slice, then encodes those records. Tests compare the emitted bytes for both implementations, including interleaved tools and one-byte output buffers. Direct streaming exists for Chat ↔ Responses, Chat ↔ Anthropic Messages, Chat ↔ Gemini GenerateContent, and same-protocol conversion. Other directions use IR in Auto; explicit Direct rejects them. The stream's route is fixed before any output is committed. A later unsupported event is an error and never causes replay through another route. The supported features of these direct directions and their IR counterparts are the same because both use the same semantic sink contract. There are no additional IR-only streaming features hidden behind a late fallback. Protocol version, profile and policy are validated before conversion; source event semantics are validated as events arrive. Same-protocol streaming validates and re-encodes events; it does not claim byte-preserving Identity. For manual IR inspection, decode_event decodes a single standard-profile JSON payload. decode_event_format also accepts an explicit vendor profile. Each EventText references a byte span in that payload, and declares whether it is a JSON string or decoded UTF-8. The caller can inspect or modify the event records and call stage_events on an IR converter. The payload is borrowed only for that call. Staged output is then drained with step(&[], output, false). Edited spans are bounds-checked; edited strings are validated again. Event IR represents starts, text/tool/reasoning/refusal deltas, signatures, block endings, cumulative usage, choice endings, final status, failures and final snapshots. Usage.input_basis distinguishes total prompt tokens from an uncached count with separate cache reads and writes. output_basis distinguishes inclusive output from visible output with a separate thought count. These distinctions are explicit in the IR rather than inferred from an undocumented vendor assumption. Context requirements Target or source feature Required external information Target requires an ID/model absent from the source StreamContext.response_id / model. Chat, Completions or Responses target, source has no integer creation time StreamContext.created. No clock is read. Responses target item_id_prefix, used with the target item index to create local item IDs. Anthropic target from another source initial_usage.input, known before the first emitted event. Cache details can also be supplied. Legacy Chat function_call or Gemini call without an ID A matching ToolId entry. An explicitly present partial usage set cannot populate a required target usage object Supply the missing counters; they are not guessed. Context input-token counts use the canonical total, including separately reported cache reads and writes. The Anthropic writer subtracts these details when populating its uncached input_tokens. Its initial output-token count can be zero because no target output has yet been emitted. Final counters use actual supplied or parsed values. Response IDs are correlation data. A copied response ID is not authorization to resume a conversation on another provider. Local Responses item IDs are scoped by the caller's prefix. Actual tool call IDs are preserved independently of these generated item IDs. Server-side conversation references belong to the request/context API, outside the SSE response converter. Implemented stream coverage The transport framing for all adapters is SSE. Gemini GenerateContent uses the API's alt=sse response representation; a bare JSON array or newline-delimited JSON is not SSE input. Protocol Input/output streaming support Limits that produce explicit errors OpenAI Completions Text choices, integer indices, finish reasons, usage, [DONE], error envelopes Tool calls, media and non-null logprobs cannot be represented by this text protocol. OpenAI Chat Completions Text/refusal deltas, new tool_calls, legacy function_call with caller ID, multiple choices, usage and [DONE] A tool header must supply a complete function name before its argument deltas. Unknown vendor fields require an implemented profile. OpenAI Responses Created lifecycle, text/refusal content parts, raw reasoning and summary parts, function-call items and arguments, final snapshots, usage and completion/incomplete/failure status Server-side tools and streamed media outside the declared subset are rejected. Complete final snapshots are emitted when this is the target. Anthropic Messages Message/content-block lifecycle, text, tool input JSON fragments, thinking/signatures, redacted thinking, citations, server tools/results, detailed usage, stops, ping and errors Provider-only content requires the same source/target Format; multiple choices cannot be encoded. Gemini GenerateContent Candidates and indices, text/thought parts, complete function-call objects, finish reasons, usage and stream EOF Streamed media, server-tool parts, function-bound signatures and partial-argument extension schemas are rejected. Gemini Interactions v1 Independent interaction.created, step.start/delta/stop, interaction.completed model-output, thought and function-call steps; usage/errors/final statuses Agent/server-tool steps and streamed media are rejected. The older content-event schema is not accepted as v1. These rows describe stream features, not a promise that every target can express every source feature. Multiple choices are representable in Chat, Completions and GenerateContent. Anthropic, Responses and Interactions reject nonzero choice indices. Refusal deltas are representable in Chat and Responses. Textual reasoning can be represented in Anthropic, GenerateContent, Interactions and explicitly profiled compatible Chat. Opaque signatures cannot cross provider/profile identities. BlockKind::Reasoning is raw thought; ReasoningSummary is a summary. Responses raw reasoning uses reasoning_text and content indexes, while summary text uses its separate summary indexes. Items retain both parts in final snapshots. A target that only represents raw thought cannot silently receive a summary, and a target that only represents summaries cannot silently receive raw thought. The caller may explicitly permit reasoning loss under the normal policy. EventKind::ProviderBlock, ProviderDelta and ProviderUsage preserve declared Anthropic-only payloads as validated raw JSON with source provenance. They are not ordinary function events. In particular, server_tool_use is work performed by the provider and must never become a local tool execution request. These payloads can be replayed only to the identical source Format; unsupported cross-provider use is an error. Profile::OpenAiCompatible("provider-name") is supported for Chat streaming. It enables the recognized reasoning_content / reasoning extensions. Standard Chat rejects those fields. The writer emits reasoning_content only for an explicitly compatible Chat target; it never injects that field into the standard profile. Arbitrary vendor field names remain unsupported. Usage and explicit losses Usage events replace the counters they contain. They are not summed across events. In particular, an Anthropic output-token update from 2 to 7 produces 7, not 9. Arithmetic is integer-only and checked. Cache reads and writes are included when normalizing Anthropic prompt totals; encoding Anthropic reverses that normalization. Gemini visible output and thought counts are added for canonical/OpenAI output, then separated again for Gemini targets. Source bases are retained so a partial cache/thought update can recompute the total without double-counting. StreamConfig::usage_emission and the owned encoder's equivalent select UsageEmission::Final (default) or Continuous. Continuous mode attaches the latest observed usage to Chat/Completions chunks and flushes usage-only updates; fragmentation, capacity retries and output backpressure do not duplicate counters. No counts are inferred from text length. allow_partial_usage remains the caller's explicit policy when only a partial count set is known. Request IR separately carries StreamOptions { include_usage, continuous_usage_stats }. Chat/Completions write the request field; other targets return EncodeReport::transport_stream_options. This metadata lets an HTTP adapter choose how to configure its response encoder without inserting a foreign field into a provider request. Parsing a request never mutates a stream encoder. The default policy rejects losses. drop_reasoning permits dropping unsupported textual reasoning, with the number of dropped deltas in Report.dropped_reasoning. drop_extensions permits only the field classes listed below. The report includes both a count and a dropped_fields bit mask using DroppedField. Bit Dropped field SystemFingerprint system_fingerprint ServiceTier service_tier SafetyRatings Gemini safetyRatings FinishMessage Gemini finishMessage AverageLogprobs Gemini avgLogprobs CacheCreationTokens Separate cache_creation_input_tokens detail in a target without this counter; the canonical total still includes these tokens. The opt-in policy does not permit unknown events, malformed JSON, namespace-bound signatures, fabricated usage or silent tool/result removal. Errors retain their classification and never trigger IR fallback. Memory accounting memory() separates the converter structure, every caller buffer's capacity, and observed utilization. Capacity fields are bytes except that items_used and tokens_peak are record counts. aggregate_peak includes transient contiguous tool-argument validation space; aggregate_used is the retained arena length. Region Growth and purpose framing One source SSE event, normalized line delimiters. data That event's joined and UTF-8-decoded data payload. pending Target events generated by one source event. Required final snapshots may make this larger than one incremental event. tokens Compact JSON indices for the current event; reused to validate completed tool arguments. items Bounded item identities, indices, lifecycle and aggregation links for one response. checkpoints One copy of the item slots for transactional rollback. events IR records for one source event; Direct does not use this slice. aggregate IDs, names, tool JSON and target-required final snapshots; optional exact source snapshot verification. Text paths without required snapshots do not accumulate the answer. The regression test compares short and 4096-byte Responses→Chat answers and finds identical retained aggregate usage. Tool arguments are retained until completion for strict JSON validation; interleaved tools use append-only linked fragments. Final validation temporarily needs a contiguous copy when a tool has multiple fragments. This storage cost is explicit. Responses targets must emit complete text and argument snapshots, including the final response object's output. Their aggregate storage therefore grows with those contents. validate_snapshots=true additionally retains source Responses text for byte-for-byte final-snapshot checks even if the target does not need it. With the default false, deltas are authoritative, final snapshots are not appended, and their lengths and lifecycle are checked. A target that already requires aggregation performs exact checks. Framing does not rescan already consumed input. Fragment append is constant work plus the newly decoded bytes; the final snapshots traverse the retained fragments. Active-item lookup is linear in the caller-bounded item count. It is not a function of the number of network fragments. No giant internal stack array substitutes for caller-provided storage. EOF, failures and signatures The standalone SSE decoder follows the WHATWG rule that EOF does not dispatch a partial event. It accepts CR, LF and CRLF, one leading BOM, comments and multiple data lines. Its payload and *_into metadata methods apply UTF-8 replacement decoding. Raw metadata views are also available. Last-Event-ID persistence and reconnect scheduling belong to the transport caller. The protocol converter adds a stricter completion contract. Completions/Chat require [DONE]; Anthropic requires message_stop; Responses and Interactions require a terminal lifecycle event. GenerateContent completes at EOF after finish reasons for its choices. Premature EOF or a residual incomplete SSE event returns TruncatedStream. This includes an unterminated trailing comment; a completed comment event is harmless. Repeated terminal events or new data events after termination return AlreadyFinished. An upstream error event is converted to the target's error envelope and ends the stream. A library parsing, semantic or capacity error is never formatted as an invented upstream model failure. Cancellation is an explicit Event IR final status; a target without a representable terminal status reports Unsupported. In particular, response.cancelled is not a Responses SSE terminal event in the documented stream union. Cancellation cannot be encoded by borrowing the similarly named webhook event. Length and safety endings do map to response.incomplete, retaining max_output_tokens versus content_filter in incomplete_details. Protocol evidence The implementation was checked against official documentation retrieved on 2026-11-10: WHATWG SSE parsing and interpretation, Living Standard last updated 2026-11-09: line handling, BOM, data joining, UTF-8 and EOF rules. Anthropic streaming messages: content-block lifecycle, partial tool JSON, thinking signatures and cumulative usage. Gemini Interactions streaming: step-based events and partial argument strings. Gemini Interactions v1 reference: independent interaction resource, steps, usage and statuses. OpenAI and GenerateContent references, together with the exact historical design-reference commit, are recorded in SOURCES.md. Evidence review Claim Executable evidence Arbitrary fragmentation and backpressure preserve bytes All tested split sizes 1–97 and one-byte output match the unfragmented result. Direct bypasses Event IR Direct reports zero IR events; forced IR records events and produces identical bytes. Capacity recovery is atomic Every workspace starts empty, grows on its classified error, and matches the pre-sized conversion. Tool IDs and argument order survive interleaving Two interleaved calls round-trip through Responses, Anthropic, GenerateContent and Interactions. Usage is not double-counted Cumulative output updates and cache-read/write round trips have exact expected integers. Final snapshots are not duplicated Text appears once after round trips; exact mode rejects altered final content. Vendor fields remain explicit Standard reasoning extensions fail; compatible-profile output is tested separately. Public edited IR is safe Invalid span arithmetic and bounds are rejected before encoding. The design review checks API clarity, representation limits, memory costs, adversarial input and claim/evidence alignment. Unsupported cells remain explicit errors; the tests do not justify claiming support for streamed media or managed-agent events.

title: Support and fidelity matrix
body: 转换模型请求、响应与流式事件，让宿主连接不同协议。 Support and fidelity matrix The release implements six distinct adapters. Support means parsing, conversion and tests exist. It does not mean every vendor feature can be expressed in every target. The default policy is strict. F = faithful within the documented portable subset. C = caller context is required. D = explicit permission and a concrete loss report are required. X = the target has no supported equivalent; conversion fails. An implemented adapter may return Unsupported for a feature outside its declared subset. Requests Source adapter Implemented input Faithful cross-protocol subset Context / downgrade / rejection OpenAI Completions String prompt and generation controls; identity validates string/token batches F: one user text prompt C: token-ID prompts need tokenizer and batches need caller expansion before IR; X: flattening arbitrary chat history into a prompt OpenAI Chat Ordered messages, text blocks, legacy functions/function_call/function role, tools/tool_calls/tool results, media, generation controls F: text and function semantics; schemas to Responses C: target-required max_tokens or item IDs; D: provider-only fields; X: unsupported role/order/target features OpenAI Responses String or item input, omitted/null message content, message/function_call/function_call_output items, typed result content, tools, output constraints, text verbosity and server context F: ordered items and function semantics; raw reasoning distinct from summaries C: materialized provider history when changing namespace; D: explicit reference removal; X: server-managed built-in tools without a declared representation Anthropic Messages System content, ordered content blocks, tool_use/tool_result, text/thinking/media, generation controls F: portable text/tools/media C: missing tool names in target results; D/X: signatures and provider controls; version 2026-10-21 rejects removed sampling controls Gemini GenerateContent contents/parts, systemInstruction, functionDeclarations, functionCall/functionResponse, inlineData/fileData, generationConfig F: portable text/tools/media C: model from transport context; C: missing call IDs/names; model/stream returned separately for target transport Gemini Interactions Independent v1 input/steps model, user_input/model_output, function_call/function_result, tools, generation_config, previous_interaction_id F: portable model-call semantics C: materialized stored history; D: explicit context removal; X: agent/background/server-tool features outside model-call conversion Content and structured output Semantic feature Preservation rule Text Original JSON strings stay borrowed; modifications are escaped correctly Missing / null / empty Represented separately; same-format IR retains declared supported distinctions; cross-format shape differences follow target semantics Images URL/base64 mappings exist; OpenAI data URLs are split into native MIME/base64 fields without a session-sized temporary buffer Audio Chat wav/mp3 input and native MIME/base64/URI descriptions where supported; incompatible target forms fail Audio/video URLs Typed media references retain URLs without fetching; native targets require a representable MIME/source form Files URL/native file descriptions where supported; provider file IDs never cross namespaces implicitly JSON Schema output Chat ↔ Responses normalized JSON object/schema conversion; same-GenerateContent schema controls preserved; other dialect guarantees fail explicitly Function strict defaults Chat missing/null maps to explicit false in Responses; unresolved Responses missing/null needs a caller IR edit before converting to another protocol; explicit strict true cannot map to a target without the same guarantee Reasoning Compatible Chat accepts ordered strings/arrays under reasoning_content or reasoning; Responses content is raw thought and summary remains summary; raw thought cannot be relabelled as a Gemini summary; standard Chat rejects undocumented fields Typed tool results Nested text/media arrays map across Chat, Responses and Anthropic; Gemini uses native functionResponse parts where representable; missing IDs/names/MIME, unsupported media and impossible ordering fail explicitly Agent input defaults Missing/null Responses content is empty content; null/absent summary becomes an empty summary list; null/empty annotations are accepted; missing/null image detail defaults to auto Text verbosity Retained independently of structured-output format; targets without a supported verbosity representation require explicit loss policy Stream options Typed include_usage and continuous_usage_stats survive Chat/Completions encoding; targets without the field return transport_stream_options for the caller Signatures Opaque provider-owned data stays in its originating format; cross-provider use requires explicit reasoning loss or fails Refusal / safety Dedicated refusal blocks and finish states retained where the target can express them; no successful answer substituted Extensions Source protocol/version/profile retained; unknown fields never injected into another provider by default Complete responses Source adapter Implemented representation Faithful subset Caller context / explicit loss / rejection Completions choices[index].text, finish_reason, usage F: ordered text alternatives and exact counters C: required target IDs/timestamps; X: multi-choice to a single-result API Chat choices/message, modern and legacy tool calls, refusal, finish and usage F: text/tools/alternatives C: Responses output item IDs; D: timestamp metadata when target lacks a field Responses output items, status/error/incomplete_details, tool calls, usage F: message/tool semantics and completion status where representable D: item metadata when target lacks it; X: failed/cancelled status in a success-only envelope Anthropic content blocks, stop_reason/stop_sequence, usage and cache counters F: text/tools and checked accounting conversion C: OpenAI timestamp; D/X: source-only metadata and unsupported stop semantics GenerateContent candidates/index/content, finishReason, usageMetadata, prompt feedback F: portable candidates and usage C: required target timestamp/IDs; D: vendor diagnostics; X: multiple candidates in a single-result target Interactions independent steps, id/model, ISO created/updated, status/error, usage F: portable steps and status C: target timestamp representation; D: incompatible timestamp metadata; X: server execution steps without an equivalent Output IDs are caller facts. Context.response_id identifies the overall result; Context.item_ids supplies distinct Responses output item IDs by ordinal. A tool call_id is never substituted for an output item ID. Context.tool_calls supplies missing name/ID bindings when the source omits a value required by the target. Usage stays integral. Anthropic uncached input plus cache-read/write counters is normalized before conversion. Gemini visible-output/thought accounting is normalized before mapping to inclusive OpenAI counters. Nonportable accounting details are retained as extensions or rejected/reported under the explicit policy. Streaming events Source adapter Implemented stream Termination Important boundaries Completions SSE text choices and usage [DONE] Legacy prompt API has no tool-block semantics Chat SSE delta text, function/tool argument shards, choices, usage, errors [DONE] Reasoning extension requires explicit compatible profile Responses Typed response/item/content/text/function-argument events, separate reasoning text/summary events and final snapshots completed / incomplete / failed Final snapshots are not appended as deltas; required target snapshots use caller aggregation; cancellation has no documented SSE terminal variant Anthropic message/block lifecycle, thinking, redacted thinking, citations, server-tool blocks/results, detailed usage, ping/error message_stop Provider-only payloads preserve source Format and fail cross-provider conversion; server-owned tools never become local function execution GenerateContent streamGenerateContent with alt=sse, candidates/parts/tool calls/usage finish reasons plus explicit EOF The raw streamed JSON-array transport is outside the SSE adapter Interactions interaction.created, step.start/delta/stop, interaction lifecycle/error interaction terminal event Separate v1 step lifecycle, independent of GenerateContent Text, tool calls/arguments, reasoning in declared profiles, usage, choices, errors and terminal state have event-level implementations and tests. Version 0.3 adds explicit event representations for Chat-compatible image URL arrays, GenerateContent grounding metadata and continuation tokens, and Anthropic matched stop sequences. These are source-owned extensions: a target without an equivalent must reject them or use an explicit loss policy, never silently approximate them. Version 0.4 adds same-origin Anthropic provider blocks, deltas and usage fields. Other streamed media generation blocks and provider event families outside this matrix remain unsupported. Images resource SSE is handled separately by api. Usage includes observed cache lifetime buckets and compatible-provider receipt fields without assigning prices, granting authority or deciding charges. Missing counters remain unknown. Applications retain financial policy and any deliberately chosen partial-usage presentation. UsageEmission::Continuous attaches the latest observed usage to Chat/Completions chunks and emits usage-only updates. The default Final mode retains terminal usage behavior. Neither mode fills in unknown counts. Reasoning events distinguish raw thought from summary, including two part indexes within one Responses item. EventEncoderState offers the same event encoder with non-borrowing persistent state. The caller retains and may grow item/aggregate storage between calls; capacity retries discard provisional output and restore committed state. This API performs no allocation and does not schedule tasks. Successful terminal emission remains an explicit caller action, so an application can settle before submitting choice-end and finish events. Resource APIs api owns Batch, Files, Embeddings and Images wire contracts. These types are implemented locally to preserve the zero-dependency contract; they are not SDK re-exports. Parsing, validated encoding, endpoint paths, JSONL, multipart and image SSE are supported as detailed in RESOURCE_APIS.md. Networking, file storage, remote job execution and model-specific limits belong to the caller. Direct paths All six Chat-centric directions implement direct requests, complete responses and supported streams. Common nonstream text, generation and usage shapes use direct views. Chat ↔ Responses requests also directly map supported function definitions, selection and tool history. Complete tool responses still use IR. Other nonstream tools/media/reasoning enter IR when the direct feature preflight rejects them. All other protocol pairs use IR. Direct and IR obey the same semantic and loss policy. A capability miss can select IR only before output commitment. A later unsupported stream event fails without replaying already emitted data. Evidence tests/protocol.rs covers all 36 request directions and all 36 complete-response directions, plus all 25 modern-protocol tool request and response directions. tests/direct.rs compares direct and IR semantic results for the six direct pairs. tests/stream.rs checks fragmentation, interleaving, lifecycle, backpressure, workspace growth and direct/IR output equality. Unsupported semantics have negative tests; ordinary success is never used as a substitute for a loss report. tests/api_compatibility.rs, tests/stream_compatibility.rs and tests/resource_api.rs cover the 0.4 additions and malformed/ambiguous inputs.

title: 概览
body: 统一语言构建与发行格式生成，检查输出制品。 zdistro 一个模板，连接语言构建、文件暂存和各平台的打包工具。 zdistro 把软件包拆成三个可组合步骤：先调用 Cargo、Python、npm 或你声明的构建命令；再把产物映射到统一暂存目录；最后交给目标格式的原生工具，生成包并校验。核心运行时使用 Python 3.11+ 标准库。 内置 17 个输出后端，涵盖 Debian/Ubuntu、Arch、Windows、macOS、Android、Python、Rust、npm、浏览器扩展和容器。其他语言与格式通过显式 argv 配方接入。每个后端都保留自己的 SDK、签名和格式要求。 开始使用 git clone https://github.com/LIghtJUNction/zdistro.git cd zdistro python -m pip install . zdistro init demo --name hello-package --target deb,arch,zip zdistro doctor --manifest demo/zdistro.toml zdistro plan --manifest demo/zdistro.toml zdistro build --manifest demo/zdistro.toml --target zip init 生成可编辑的 zdistro.toml、最小样例和明确的前置条件。把文件映射改成自己的软件，填写维护者、版本和许可证后即可构建。已有文件会保留。支持 ubuntu、rust、python、安卓、浏览器插件、容器 等常用别名。 zdistro init multilingual --target python,rust,浏览器插件,安卓,容器 zdistro build --manifest multilingual/zdistro.toml --available --available 构建当前主机已满足条件的目标，并逐项列出跳过原因。默认构建遇到前置条件缺失会返回非零退出码。 六个入口 命令 做什么 输出 init --target … 生成统一模板及对应最小样例 TOML 与源文件 doctor 检查当前主机、工具、项目文件和 SDK；容器目标检查引擎 文本或 --json plan 展示构建器、文件映射、原生命令和缺失条件 JSON；不运行构建命令 build 私有目录构建、生成包、调用验证器 产物与 receipt.json verify RECEIPT 检查配置指纹、产物 SHA-256/大小并重新验证格式 JSON matrix --format svg 根据模板、主机工具和实际收据生成矩阵 SVG、JSON 或 Markdown 构建结果放在 dist/zdistro/<格式>/<本次构建>/。失败记录为 failure.json；只有成功生成并验证的非空产物才有成功收据。收据同时记录主机、源配置指纹、命令结果、文件摘要和验证范围。 README 打包矩阵 zdistro matrix --manifest demo/zdistro.toml \ --format svg --output demo/docs/packaging.svg 在自己的 README 中嵌入： ![Packaging matrix](docs/packaging.svg) 矩阵从实际数据计算。Native verified 表示产物通过原生格式工具检查；Integrity verified 表示归档、元数据或内容摘要检查通过；Recipe verified 表示用户声明的验证命令成功。Tools found 是当前主机的前置条件结果，Native tools needed 表示另一主机需要相应工具。已有收据对应的产物缺失时显示 Receipt only。配置指纹变化或产物被修改会撤销对应验证状态。 本项目使用的样例验收入口是 tests/native_smoke.py。三平台 CI 上传实际包、收据、SDK 检查结果和矩阵，见 Actions。产物校验、安装测试、签名和商店提交分别记录，矩阵展示产物校验范围。 Linux packaging acceptance snapshot 上图是本机实际产物校验时生成的快照，数据见 packaging.json。其他系统的正式构建证据在 Actions 制品中；这个 Linux 快照不会把其他系统的工具适配标成已经实测。 统一模板 schema = 1 source_date_epoch = 1700000000 [package] name = "my-app" version = "1.0.0" description = "My application" maintainer = "Maintainer <maintainer@example.org>" license = "MIT" identifier = "org.example.myapp" [build] kind = "cargo" project = "rust-app" [[files]] source = "{build}/cargo/release/my-app" destination = "usr/bin/my-app" mode = "0755" [targets.deb] architecture = "amd64" depends = ["libc6"] [targets.arch] architecture = "x86_64" release = "1" depends = ["glibc"] [targets.zip] files = [{source = "{build}/cargo/release/my-app", destination = "my-app"}] 语言构建器在独立的源副本中运行；{build} 指向这次构建的私有目录。files 只接收项目内的源文件或本次构建产物，目标路径使用相对 POSIX 路径。每个目标可以覆盖 files，因此同一个程序可以使用不同的安装布局。架构字段描述装入包内的程序，跨编译由语言工具链及其 build.target 负责。 crate 调用正常的 cargo package，保留其拆包后构建验证；wheel/sdist 调用 PEP 517 前端 python -m build；npm 调用 npm pack --ignore-scripts。Python 打包需要在运行 zdistro 的环境安装 build，项目后端依赖由 PEP 517 的隔离构建处理。Cargo · Python packaging flow · npm pack 扩展语言和格式 build.kind = "command" 接入任意已经存在的语言构建工具。新包格式通过 recipes 登记，并与内置后端共用暂存目录、检查和收据： [targets.custom] [recipes.custom] hosts = ["linux", "macos", "windows"] tools = ["my-packager", "my-package-check"] artifact = "my-app.bundle" build = [["my-packager", "--root", "{stage}", "--output", "{artifact}"]] verify = [["my-package-check", "{artifact}"]] 把配方中的工具换成该生态实际使用的构建器和验证器即可。两组命令都必填；命令失败、产物缺失或为空都会结束构建。参数按数组传递；占位符包括 {python}、{project}、{stage}、{build}、{work}、{out}、{artifact}、{name} 和 {version}。模板和构建脚本是可执行的项目配置，应在 plan 中审阅后运行。 独立 verify 会按原来的 targets.<target>.project / build.project 重新复制配方项目；{work}、{build}、{stage} 是新的临时目录，先前的中间产物不会恢复。验证命令应检查 {artifact}，需要的辅助脚本放在 {project} 中。 具体原生工具、格式规则和官方来源见 格式指南。 开发与验收 python -m unittest discover -s tests -v python tests/native_smoke.py --targets deb,arch,zip,tar-gz 测试覆盖路径和文件映射、真实归档、扩展资源引用、配方产物/验证契约、嵌套项目重验、收据篡改、配置变更失效、可重复 ZIP 和矩阵状态。原生构建工作流负责 Linux Deb/Arch、macOS PKG/DMG、Windows MSI/MSIX，以及使用现有 SDK 的 Android APK/AAB 检查。Android 还检查真实应用标识和版本，拒绝版本不符的有效 APK。SDK 或工具缺失会显示具体前置条件。 日常修改在本机验收；GitHub 工作流仅用于显式启动或版本标签触发的正式原生制品构建。仓库自身的 zdistro.toml 可生成 zdistro 的 wheel、sdist、可运行 zipapp、Deb 和 Arch 包： python -m pip install build python -m zdistro build --manifest zdistro.toml --target wheel,sdist,zip 本项目属于 Project Z。公共接口或依赖变更按反向依赖传播：维护者负责协调、更新并验证直接及间接消费者，再提交相关变更。 许可证 zdistro：MIT，见 LICENSE。被打包的软件及调用的外部工具保留各自的许可证。

title: Format backends and verification
body: 统一语言构建与发行格式生成，检查输出制品。 Format backends and verification zdistro delegates package construction to the ecosystem's own tools. A format backend has four responsibilities: declare prerequisites, describe a plan, produce an artifact, and verify that artifact. Language compilation happens before file staging; cross compilation remains a language-toolchain setting. Built-in formats Target Builder / required tools Verification performed deb dpkg-deb Package/version identity and payload listing arch makepkg, fakeroot, pacman, bsdtar Native package inspection and .PKGINFO, .BUILDINFO, .MTREE zip, tar-gz Python standard archive libraries Member boundaries, readable archive; ZIP CRCs crate cargo package Cargo's default unpack/build verification, normalized manifest identity wheel python -m build --wheel Core metadata and every wheel RECORD digest/size sdist python -m build --sdist Source distribution archive and PKG-INFO identity npm npm pack --ignore-scripts Tar structure and package.json identity extension, xpi ZIP library Root manifest, required fields, local scripts/pages/icons, ZIP CRCs pkg macOS pkgbuild, pkgutil Expand native metadata and payload without installing dmg macOS hdiutil Image integrity and format inspection without mounting msi Windows WiX 4+ CLI Native MSI database decompilation msix Windows SDK MakeAppx ZIP/block-map metadata and native unpack apk Android AAPT2 + platform android.jar, or existing Gradle project AAPT2 parsing and actual application ID/version matching aab AAPT2 or Gradle project, Java and bundletool Bundle module validation and actual manifest identity/version matching docker Docker Buildx or Podman Docker/OCI archive references and OCI blob digests/sizes These are artifact checks. Installation/upgrade behavior, application behavior, code signing, notarization and store review require their own workflows and are not marked complete by an artifact receipt. Linux packages Debian and Ubuntu packages are created with dpkg-deb --root-owner-group --build. zdistro generates DEBIAN/control from the package metadata and records runtime dependencies from targets.deb.depends. This follows the native tool's binary package directory contract. See dpkg-deb. Arch packages use a generated PKGBUILD whose package function copies the staged files. makepkg generates the ALPM metadata and compressed archive.
