title: Architecture and resource ownership
body: 基于 Project Z 的原生 Minecraft 启动器。 Architecture and resource ownership zmcl separates portable launch planning from operating-system work. The goal is to keep the launcher's own installation and process lifetime small while providing practical Minecraft workflows. The functionality target remains XMCL v0.73.1 at a fixed commit; implemented commands, controlled tests and real game outcomes have separate acceptance records. VALIDATION.md records functional evidence, and PERFORMANCE.md records the measured process trees and storage populations. Project Z boundary The portable zmcl-core crate uses no_std + alloc and forbids unsafe Rust. It parses bounded JSON through Project Z zconv, represents Minecraft metadata and inheritance, evaluates rules, constructs download/launch plans and supplies incremental SHA-1, SHA-256 and MD5. Filesystem access, networking, process creation, native windows and credentials remain in the application. A core launch plan is an executable plus an argument vector; it is never a shell command. The application uses Project Z zclap for command parsing and the unified zgpui package for the optional desktop frontend. Window creation, input, Canvas drawing and widgets call zgpui::native; the dependency enables native and linux-software. On Linux this renders on the CPU and submits pixels through X11, without a GL context or renderer worker. This is an actual backend integration. The core remains no_std + alloc; zgpui also retains its separate no_std scene API when native features are disabled. Other OS backend code does not imply native acceptance on those systems. Exact dependency versions and gitlinks are maintained in Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock and .gitmodules. Release settings use size optimization, LTO, one code-generation unit, aborting panics and stripped symbols. Component Responsibility Persistent ownership Core Bounded JSON, hashes, safe relative paths, manifests, rules, inheritance and argv plans None Runtime Official metadata, loader profiles/installers, assets/natives, Java selection and game launch Instance installation state and launch records Network / store Bounded HTTPS transfers, expected-digest checks and conventional Minecraft paths Shared verified objects and metadata cache Java Adoptium runtime selection, verification, extraction and version check Versioned managed JREs and selector records Content Modrinth mods, dependency resolution, mrpack and pack catalogue Mod lock, import state and mod transaction journal Resources Resource/shader ZIP lifecycle and recoverable revisions Resource lock, journal and retained history Worlds / backup Save metadata, safe file transfer and checksummed mutable-data snapshots World directories, backup archives and restore state Instance lifecycle Independent writable clone and reversible trash/restore Instance directories and trash records Servers Official Java server installation, explicit-EULA start, status/stop and TCP ping Server configuration, logs and process identity Horizon Signed official launcher component as a separate provider Versioned verified payload and provider data Accounts Device authorization, token refresh and account selection Public account metadata; tokens in an OS secret store GUI Native views, bounded worker output, cancellation and optional exit User choices and activity state while open Process lifetime The native GUI waits for input and worker events instead of maintaining a web runtime or a launcher service. A user operation starts a short-lived CLI worker. Its stdout/stderr are captured with limits, cancellation targets its own process group, and completion returns a bounded result to the interface. Archive, credential and verification helpers also run only for the operation that needs them. A successful game launch redirects output to files, starts Java in a separate process group on the supported Unix path and returns its PID. The Java process therefore does not depend on the GUI worker's lifetime. The optional gui --exit-after-launch launch flag is disabled by default; enabling it exits the GUI only after an uncancelled launch operation returns success and valid JSON containing a positive PID. Normal operations, malformed results, cancellation and errors leave the interface available. The direct CLI's --wait mode deliberately keeps the calling process alive. flowchart TD G["Native GUI"] --> W["Short-lived CLI worker"] W --> P["Verified launch plan"] P --> J["Java: separate process group and logs"] P --> R["Success result with PID"] R --> C{"Exit flag enabled?"} C -->|Yes| E["GUI and worker finish"] C -->|No| G The Linux lifecycle acceptance observed the GUI exit successfully while its real Java game process continued running independently. That run checked process lifetime and native window properties; it did not capture a game menu and is not a performance benchmark. Zero launcher residency means the participating launcher processes have exited. Java, a managed server, Horizon's own launcher/game processes and another independent zmcl session remain separate consumers and must be counted when reporting total machine usage. Data layout The application chooses an OS-appropriate data root, with explicit --root and ZMCL_HOME overrides. The layout below is relative to that root; source code uses validated identifiers and confined joins before accessing it. Relative location Contents and lifecycle instances/<id>/instance.json Version, loader, Java preference, memory and installation state instances/<id>/game/ Writable Minecraft game directory, including saves, options and installed content instances/<id>/mods-lock.json / resources-lock.json Provider identities, versions, filenames and expected file digests for managed content instances/<id>/resources-history/<revision>/ Retained originals and before/after resource-lock snapshots instances/<id>/ installation/logging files Generated loader profile, native extraction, game logs and last-launch identity shared/objects/ Digest-addressed verified file objects shared/versions/, shared/libraries/ and shared/assets/ Standard Minecraft paths backed by shared objects; logging configurations live under assets runtimes/<major>-<os>-<arch>/ Immutable release/hash directories and the selected managed Java runtime backups/<id>/ Retained ZIP snapshots with SHA-256 manifests servers/<id>/ Server JSON, verified JAR, EULA/properties files, logs and owned-process record providers/horizon/installed/<id>/ Verified provider installation manifest and extracted payload providers/horizon/ provider data Horizon-owned persistent data, separate from Java instances trash/<token>/instance/ and item.json Reversible instance removal and its identity accounts/, cache/ and locks/ Account metadata, bounded-operation cache/staging, and advisory lock files The shared store reduces duplicate immutable downloads. Successful materialization uses hard links where supported and a file copy where linking is unavailable. A hard link shares an inode, not an independent writable file, so objects are made read-only and file identity matters when measuring disk usage. Active resource/shader files are independent writable copies: editing one must not alter the verified cache. Instance cloning also copies writable game files instead of linking them. Retained backups, resource revisions, trashed instances, old Java releases and provider payloads consume real storage. Staging can temporarily hold both old and new data. The project does not claim those bytes disappear after installation, and it has no general automatic history-retention policy. Storage reports must identify their dataset and distinguish logical path bytes from allocated bytes of distinct files. Installation and provider trust The download layer receives a bounded destination, expected size where available and an expected digest. Provider metadata is obtained over HTTPS; bytes are checked before the store publishes them. Minecraft and Modrinth commonly use SHA-1, while managed Java uses SHA-256. A cached file must pass the same expected-value checks before reuse. Real acceptance includes corruption of both a conventional library path and its cache object, followed by successful redownload and restoration of verified shared materialization. A Minecraft installation resolves the official version and inheritance, selects or provisions the required Java major, merges the loader profile and repeats the Java requirement check. The resulting plan determines libraries, client, natives, logging configuration and assets. Explicitly configured Java paths are checked and their errors are surfaced. Automatic Adoptium installation is available only when the instance has no explicit Java preference and no suitable discovered runtime. Direct launch selects an installed runtime and does not download one. Managed Java installs into a new release/hash directory. The archive's SHA-256 and size are checked, bounded ZIP/tar extraction rejects escaping or unsafe entries, and java -version must report the requested major before publication. Valid internal tar links are handled under confinement checks. A selector switches future launches without replacing a runtime directory that a running game might still use. Linux acceptance covers explicit Java 21 installation and automatic Java 25 provisioning during a Minecraft 26.3 installation, followed by a real Minecraft 26.3 main menu. World play, Realms and multiplayer remain separate acceptance targets. Horizon has a separate trust and compatibility boundary. Its provider verifies the GitHub release asset digest, the official signed SHA256SUMS manifest and hashes of extracted files. The signing key and message format are fixed to the official release-signing source; the helper uses system OpenSSL for Ed25519 verification. Managed files are checked again before launch, and the official launcher's self-update is disabled so it cannot replace the verified payload. The accepted Linux result is installation and --version execution of launcher 0.2.84. Account authorization, legitimate Minecraft preparation, actual Horizon gameplay and Java-mod compatibility are separate unaccepted paths. Locks, stopped-instance checks and recovery The operation lock holds an open file with File::try_lock. The operating system releases the lock when the owning process exits; the filename can remain without representing a live lock. Per-instance operations serialize changes. Multi-instance operations acquire their locks consistently, and provider operations use their own named locks. Mutation guards check recorded game identity and world session locks before changing instance data. Linux checks use the recorded PID and process start identity together with the expected game directory; a bare PID is insufficient because operating systems reuse PIDs. World copying/export also holds the world's OS session lock while reading, and rechecks file identities to detect a changing source. On platforms where a recorded launch cannot be established as stopped, the guard refuses instead of assuming the game exited. These are process/file coordination controls, not permission to modify a live world. A pending content, backup or resource journal blocks unrelated installation, launch and instance/world mutations that could invalidate recovery. Recovery operates under the appropriate lock and handles its own journal, while conflicting operation journals remain a blocker. Ambiguous state or modified files are preserved for review. The modules use different publication boundaries because a mod-directory update, a resource ZIP change and a full game-data restore own different files. Operation Publication and recovery boundary Mod add/update/remove Fresh files are downloaded and checked before the managed mods directory/lock transition. Version-2 journals record enough identity for conservative recovery. Legacy journals lacking that identity are refused and retained. Manual or unrecognized files are preserved. Resource add/update/remove/toggle A per-file journal records the intended transition. New files publish without overwriting a conflicting destination; old managed files and lock snapshots remain in a revision directory. Resource restore The selected revision must match the current expected after-state. Restoring creates a reverse transaction, preserving the current revision as recoverable history. Changed or ambiguous files stop the operation. World import/clone/export Confined private staging, bounded copy/extraction, source checks and exclusive final publication. Existing destinations are refused. The code does not rewrite world chunks. Backup restore Verify all snapshot bytes into staging, preserve excluded managed roots, create a pre-restore snapshot and journal the game-directory swap. A later create/restore can recover an interrupted swap conservatively. Instance clone Copy writable game files and managed-content lock metadata into a new instance. Mark it uninstalled so shared installation artifacts, profiles and natives are recreated by install. Instance trash/restore Move the complete instance into a retained trash container. Restore refuses an occupied target and preserves the recorded data. Shared cached objects remain available. The Modrinth resolver is intentionally bounded: at most 512 projects, dependency depth 32 and 32 rounds of exact-version pin propagation. Required-version conflicts, incompatible projects and unsupported required filename-only external dependencies produce errors. It does not implement exhaustive SAT/backtracking across arbitrary release combinations. Resource-pack/shader requirements are reported rather than silently installing additional projects or a shader engine. Mrpack hash behavior differs by direction. Download/import recomputes SHA-1 and verifies size, while preserving supplied SHA-512 metadata. Export streams each file to recompute SHA-1 and SHA-512, checks the expected SHA-1/size and emits both fields. The reader accepts older inputs that omit SHA-512, so it is deliberately more permissive than the current format's required fields. File formats and bounded work World metadata reads selected fields from gzip-compressed Java level.dat/Data, including display name, last-played time, game mode and version. It does not expose seed/player-position data or offer an NBT/chunk editor. Import accepts a directory or ZIP with one identifiable world root; export preserves ordinary world bytes and excludes the active session-lock file. Corrupt metadata remains visible as an invalid entry rather than being presented as a valid world. Archive helpers reject unsafe paths, collisions under portable path rules, unsupported links/special files and decompression beyond their budgets. JSON, metadata, helper output and directory traversal are bounded before or during allocation. Limits are deliberate product boundaries and can reject unusually large valid content; a limit error must not be reported as successful installation. Boundary Representative current limit Source Core JSON 32 MiB input, 1,048,576 tokens, 131,072 fields JSON helper Instance clone 50,000 entries, 512 MiB per file, 4 GiB total, depth 32 Instance manager World transfer 50,000 entries, 1 GiB per file, 16 GiB total World helper World NBT 8 MiB compressed and 16 MiB decoded World helper Server-list response 1 MiB packet and bounded VarInt, DNS/connect/read deadlines Server protocol Local Java server start is separately guarded. Creating a server does not accept the Minecraft EULA: eula=true must already be explicitly present before start. Managed start/stop currently uses Linux procfs and pidfd identity checks, with the expected executable, command, working directory and start identity. Stop sends a bounded graceful termination only to the verified owned process; uncertain identity is an error. Portable installation and modern Java server-list ping do not imply portable managed process control. The server CLI acceptance installed the official Minecraft 1.21.1 JAR, independently checked its SHA-1/size, queried status/list and observed an explicit refusal with unchanged eula=false and no server Java process. The reproducible script never accepts the EULA or requests an accepted live-server start. The ping tests use local fake TCP peers; they do not contact arbitrary external servers. Accounts and system dependencies Microsoft authentication uses an explicitly configured registered application ID and the device authorization, Xbox/XSTS and Minecraft entitlement/profile flow. Refresh tokens belong in the OS credential store; a plaintext token file is not the fallback. Launch-plan output redacts credentials, and provider secrets are kept out of process arguments where the system helper interface allows it. Live licensed-account authorization and every platform's credential adapter still need their own acceptance result. A small Rust dependency graph does not remove operating-system dependencies. The application uses the following capabilities on demand; their processes, libraries and installed bytes are part of honest resource accounting. Capability Runtime dependency Native GUI Project Z native-window implementation, platform window libraries and OpenGL/driver stack; accepted on Linux X11/XWayland with a private Xvfb/software-driver setup HTTPS download System curl Safe archive and metadata work Python 3.8+ standard-library helpers for ZIP/tar, gzip/NBT handling and operation-specific validation; one actual-interpreter resolver handles Windows py -3/python/python3, Unix python3/python, or the literal ZMCL_PYTHON executable path. Helpers use isolated UTF-8 execution; only successful discovery is cached. Horizon signature verification System OpenSSL with Ed25519 support Account secrets OS credential services and their platform adapters Minecraft Java A compatible system or managed JRE; its memory is separate from launcher residency Horizon The verified upstream launcher and whatever legitimate game data/preparation it requires Windows and macOS source paths, archive mappings or generated argument plans are not equivalent to native execution acceptance. The current managed-server process boundary is Linux-only; uncertain game-stop identity on other platforms fails conservatively. The native GUI has no accepted native Wayland or hardware-driver result in this dataset. Exact platform and user-flow limits are maintained in FEATURES.md. Evidence and remaining work The current implementation is supported by bounded-core unit tests, operation-specific Rust/Python tests and named real provider/GUI/game workflows. The resource CLI script exercises official small downloads, update/history/restore and manual-file/process protection in an isolated home. The lifecycle CLI script completed 21 commands against a fresh home containing synthetic NBT and opaque region bytes: world roundtrips, SHA-256 backup/restore with a retained pre-restore snapshot, independent instance cloning and reversible trash. Three protective refusals were expected. Those fixtures prove command and file boundaries; they do not prove that a real Minecraft world loads. Public-pack installation plus a launch dry run proves resolution and plan construction, not successful gameplay. Architecture review follows five questions: whether each module supplies a concrete user operation, whether ownership and process boundaries are clear, whether claims have named evidence, whether missing platform/game outcomes remain visible, and whether failure leaves recoverable data. Those questions drive the open acceptance work: licensed-account flows, more real worlds and loaders, native Windows/macOS runs, resource/shader rendering, remote and collaborative services, and complete GUI coverage. Performance changes must use the matched protocol in PERFORMANCE.md, including helper/driver and retained-data costs.

title: 用 zdistro 分发 zmcl
body: 基于 Project Z 的原生 Minecraft 启动器。 用 zdistro 分发 zmcl zmcl 的发行端使用固定版本的 zdistro 创建归档和系统软件包。最终 tar.gz、ZIP 和 DEB 的文件由 zdistro 生成；zmcl 的包装脚本负责核对输入二进制、源码身份、运行库要求和输出文件。zdistro 不进入启动器的运行时，也不承担应用更新服务。 固定工具与环境 zdistro：v0.1.0，源码提交 6a54a137fc697d372b54ef85105315f2ce522b3d。 官方 zipapp SHA-256：a30a4580254a6510c2019e3e7a684c31d4e435b69f32f33d3813ef6264544908。 发行端需要 Python 3.11 或更新、Git；Linux 需要 readelf，DEB 另需 dpkg-deb。 用户端的安装器与文件助手仍要求 Python 3.8 或更新。构建工具的版本要求不等于用户端要求。 包装脚本必须显式接收 --zdistro，执行前核对固定摘要，不会自动下载或执行其他版本。 生成发行包 先在最终源码提交上完成本地 Cargo 测试、严格 Clippy、修改过的 Python 测试及实际使用流程，再构建原生程序： cargo build --release --locked ./target/release/zmcl --version git rev-parse HEAD sha256sum target/release/zmcl 记录完整提交与二进制摘要。Linux x86_64 示例： python3 scripts/zdistro_package.py \ --binary target/release/zmcl \ --source-root . \ --source-commit FULL_SOURCE_COMMIT \ --expected-sha256 FROZEN_BINARY_SHA256 \ --zdistro /path/to/zdistro-0.1.0.pyz \ --target tar-gz \ --target deb \ --output /path/to/new-release-directory 输出目录必须尚不存在。重复验证应使用新的目录，保留第一次执行的证据。 包装脚本检查源码 checkout 的 HEAD、运行时代码、Cargo 与工具链配置、依赖 gitlink，以及实际入包的安装器、文档、图标和桌面文件。检查范围内的未跟踪或被 Git 忽略文件也会拒绝；应在干净的打包 checkout 中执行，构建输出放在 target/。它还检查二进制的原生 ELF/PE 架构、摘要及实际 --version 输出。这些检查用于防止混装。二进制的编译来源仍须由构建记录提供，不能只凭版本字符串证明。 每次执行依次调用 zdistro 的 doctor、plan、build、verify 和 matrix。请求的目标必须全部产生且完成校验；缺失、重复、跳过目标都会失败。不会用 --available 将不支持的目标静默省略。 产物与校验记录 路径 内容 public/ 带版本、操作系统和架构的最终软件包、各包的 SHA-256 文件及 SHA256SUMS release-result.json 源码、二进制、工具、目标和发布副本的摘要映射 evidence/zdistro.toml 此次实际执行的 manifest evidence/artifacts/ zdistro 的原始软件包及原始 receipt evidence/legacy/ 原有 payload 生成器的归档与文件、依赖证据，供追溯使用 evidence/legacy/ 是输入和校验材料；用户下载的软件包来自 public/ 中对应的 zdistro 输出副本。原始软件包、manifest 与 receipt 保留原始字节，不改写校验状态。发布副本改用唯一文件名，摘要必须与原始产物完全相同。 zdistro 的 receipt 会包含打包机器的绝对路径。可公开的原始证据应在固定的通用容器路径中生成，例如 /workspace/zmcl 与 /workspace/releases。先检查记录，不公开私人路径或原始会话日志。 receipt 中的 installed: false、published: false 和签名状态表示该工具自身的工作范围。实际安装、发布和界面验收另立记录，不能事后把原 receipt 改成已安装或已签名。SHA-256 可核对文件是否一致，本身不证明发布者身份。 软件包布局和运行条件 便携包保留原有根目录和 scripts/install.py 入口。DEB 将程序放在 /usr/bin/zmcl，同时提供桌面入口、图标、许可证和说明文件。游戏实例、存档、账号资料及 Java 不打进启动器软件包。 DEB 的 glibc 与 Fontconfig 下限来自实际二进制引用的符号；动态库名映射到 Debian 包名，遇到未映射的依赖会明确失败。还显式声明 curl、CA 证书（ca-certificates）、Python 与图标主题依赖，安装时禁用推荐包也会安装必需的 CA 证书。当前未从 GCC/GLIBCXX 符号推导 Debian 包版本下限，不能据此宣称任意旧系统兼容；真实安装和动态链接检查另行验收。Microsoft 凭据操作需要额外的 libsecret-tools 与桌面 Secret Service，Horizon 验签需要支持 Ed25519 的 OpenSSL。不能为了使安装通过而降低实际 ABI 下限。 DEB 目前只接受数字形式的 X.Y.Z 版本，拒绝尚未转换的 SemVer 预发布或构建后缀，防止 Debian 与 SemVer 不同的排序规则改变升级顺序。GitHub 上将数字版本标为开发预览不会改变软件包版本本身。 每个软件包在 share/zmcl/distribution.json（DEB 为 /usr/share/zmcl/distribution.json）提供应用、版本、格式、打包工具及固定官方发行页等说明。该文件用于展示安装来源，不授权自动改写程序，也不代替包管理器的所有权记录。 Arch 继续使用仓库中维护的 AUR 配方，并消费 zdistro 生成的官方 tar.gz，以保留 provides、conflicts 与可选依赖声明。DEB 的成功打包不表示所有 Debian 或 Ubuntu 版本都能运行，实际系统版本与安装结果应单独记录。 用户安装信息与更新入口 用户安装器仍使用 Python 3.8 或更新。在解包目录执行 python3 scripts/install.py install --prefix "目标目录"；Windows 可使用 py -3。Linux 的程序目标为 bin/zmcl，Windows 为 bin/zmcl.exe。完成提示给出可验证的版本、位置、直接启动命令和更新方式。若 PATH 优先选择另一份程序，同时展示两个路径，不修改 PATH 或用户的 shell 配置，也不删除另一份安装。 用户安装生成 share/zmcl/installation.json，字段为 schema: 1、application: "zmcl"、version、channel: "portable"、executable、prefix 和 release_url。版本优先使用经过 payload 摘要校验的发行元数据；合法旧包缺少完整信息时可以安装，但不能从目录名称推测版本。install.json 保留原有的严格列表格式，每项只含 path 和 sha256。带 distribution marker 的新便携安装明确管理程序、图标、桌面文件、distribution marker 与 installation receipt 五个文件；marker 和 receipt 的修改也会触发保护。 GUI 的 Settings 展示当前程序版本、路径与安装来源，并提供手动 Check for updates。只有通过校验的 distribution marker 才用于识别对应的打包来源；缺失 marker 时，合法 portable receipt 可以说明用户安装，但不自动标记为 zdistro。损坏、悬挂链接或与当前程序不匹配的 marker 不会被另一份 receipt 覆盖。更新结果提供官方发行页与适合当前平台的资产信息，不自动替换文件；AUR 和 DEB 仍由各自包管理器更新。 用户级升级检查旧清单与实际摘要，只覆盖确认受管且未修改的文件。卸载同样只移除匹配的受管文件；修改过的文件、非受管文件和已有游戏数据保留。详情与可复制命令见安装说明。 0.1.4 实际发行验收 0.1.4 从源码 25c243a 生成 Linux x86_64 tar.gz、DEB 和 Windows amd64 ZIP。文件大小、摘要、二进制身份与完整流程记录在发行报告和结构化回执；面向用户的入口为 v0.1.4 发行页。 Linux 在 Debian forky/sid 容器完成旧 0.1.3 升级、重装、卸载，以及带空格前缀、PATH 遮蔽、九组原生 GUI 夹具和数据保留检查。最小原始镜像没有 CA 证书；正常 apt 安装 DEB，即使使用 --no-install-recommends，也会安装所需证书。随后 GitHub HTTPS 请求返回 200、证书验证结果为 0；一次真实手动更新查询识别本机版本高于当时线上 0.1.3，查询没有修改二进制。 正式 Windows workflow 44739704182在原生 build 26100 runner 上完成 MSVC 构建、ZIP 打包、私有前缀安装、版本输出、Win32 窗口、五项受管文件与卸载数据保留检查。此结果不扩大为所有 Windows 版本、真实账号或实际游戏流程验收。首次 Windows 验证器 PATH 解析失败，以及 Linux 容器默认排除文档导致的首次完整性检查失败，均保留在原始记录；修正验证环境后的成功另行记录。 平台边界 Linux 原生包装支持 tar.gz、ZIP 和 DEB；Linux ZIP 的名称必须明确为 Linux。Windows 原生包装入口仅接受 ZIP，并要求在 Windows 执行对应二进制的版本检查。不能把 Linux 上生成 ZIP 的成功当作 Windows 应用运行验收。 本 wrapper 尚未实现 macOS 应用分发、MSI/MSIX 安装体验、RPM、AppImage、Flatpak、签名或自动更新。框架的平台支持、软件包结构验证与完整启动器的实机流程应分别报告。 回归与已知工具行为 ZMCL_TEST_ZDISTRO=/path/to/zdistro-0.1.0.pyz \ python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_zdistro*.py' 测试使用小型原生 ELF、真实固定 zipapp 和真实软件包格式，检查文件、权限、来源身份、依赖下限、重复目标、篡改以及输出冲突。它不替代真实 zmcl 的安装、原生窗口和游戏流程。 固定 v0.1.0 zipapp 的入口未传播 CLI 返回码，失败时可能返回进程状态 0，同时向 stderr 写入错误 JSON。包装脚本因此同时检查错误记录、结构化结果、目标完整性和文件摘要，拒绝这种假成功。没有修改固定工具来掩盖问题；最小复现与测试应随验收记录保存。

title: XMCL compatibility record
body: 基于 Project Z 的原生 Minecraft 启动器。 XMCL compatibility record 0.1.4 distribution and installation The source connects the fixed zdistro 0.1.0 packager to Linux tar.gz/DEB and native Windows ZIP preparation. Distribution instructions describe the artifact and runtime-dependency checks. Availability and native acceptance belong to each published release; no macOS application package is provided. Settings now shows the running launcher version, platform, executable location and advisory installation source. A manual Check for updates action and zmcl update check --json inspect official GitHub releases, compare semantic versions, and select packages for the current OS and architecture. A newer local build is reported as ahead of the published package. Failures can be retried, and release links can be opened or copied; installation remains with the selected installer or package manager. The portable installer reports the installed version, prefix, direct launch command and same-prefix update command. If PATH selects another zmcl, it identifies both copies. Validated distribution metadata and the generated installation receipt join the existing strict file/digest manifest. Upgrades refuse modified or unmanaged installation files; removal preserves modified files and game data. Windows installations use bin/zmcl.exe, and user-facing Python requirements remain 3.8+. The wrapper-to-installer roundtrip uses a real small ELF, the fixed zipapp and private prefixes with spaces. It verifies distribution/installation metadata, installed file digests, removal and synthetic game-data preservation. The Windows distribution workflow records its native build, install, window and removal results separately. These source-level improvements do not relabel the earlier application, account, game or memory evidence below. 0.1.3 management and distribution iteration The 0.1.3 report records source 9ef89bb92d46d324172d6ea8b13054c81434e178, 97 Rust tests, 51 affected Python tests, real CLI file roundtrips, two six-flow native GUI observations, and another six-flow check of the AUR-installed binary. GitHub v0.1.3 and AUR 0.1.3-1 are published; normal host upgrade and public-index readback passed. Helpers load modules on demand, backup list entries release full archive indexes between inspections, and JSON output avoids a complete encoded duplicate. This reduces observed large-backup query peaks in the fixed paired fixture; the complete GUI below-10-MiB target remains unmet. No new Windows/macOS, real-account or game/server-launch acceptance is inferred, and the fixed XMCL baseline and feature gaps below remain unchanged. 0.1.2 iteration The implementation and evidence report records application source e86b5841532ef04cc74cea5585ae396150452408, 97 Rust tests, strict Clippy, native creation/management fixtures and explicit Windows/macOS limits. Archive, metadata and Horizon helpers now share actual Python 3.8+ discovery, isolated UTF-8 execution and retry after a missing interpreter is installed. Windows background helpers suppress extra console windows while preserving output/error streams. Large-library and empty-window measurements identify their separate pre-release candidates; they are not relabelled as final 0.1.2 performance measurements. zmcl targets the functional scope of XMCL v0.73.1, commit aeb52403945f017a17f4014cb6542f73fa47dd15. The fixed service interfaces define the comparison baseline. The official feature catalogue provides product context and may describe newer upstream work. Full coverage remains a development target; the gaps below remain part of the acceptance work. This record separates implementation, local fixtures and live results. Implemented identifies a reachable code path. Fixture accepted identifies tests with controlled files, synthetic NBT, fake network peers or process fixtures. Live accepted identifies a named provider download, native interface interaction or real game outcome. Each result applies to its stated environment. Build identities, current test totals and sanitized outcomes belong in VALIDATION.md; process-tree and storage measurements belong in PERFORMANCE.md. Runtime, interface and accounts Area Implemented behavior and source Recorded acceptance Remaining scope Native GUI Native desktop interface: Library, Discover, Modpacks, Accounts, Settings, activity and cancellation. Instance Manage opens Worlds, Backups and Resources; Servers has its own sidebar entry. Creation includes asynchronous official-release selection, exact ID filtering, collision-free names, vanilla/Fabric/Quilt/Forge/NeoForge choice and default create-and-install. Forge/NeoForge require explicit loader versions; create-only and failed-install retry preserve the instance. Linux private-display interaction includes the original instance/mrpack flow and six management window/file checks at 1120×760. The 0.1.2 frozen application passed four creation fixture groups and six management scenarios with real native Linux window interaction, plus a normal Windows GNU full-GUI cross-build. GUI world cloning/details, resource search/history restore, server configuration/ping, Horizon, complete keyboard/accessibility, gamepad and Windows/macOS interface acceptance remain open. CLI Command entry points cover instances, installs, launches, accounts, mods, packs, resources, worlds, backups, Java, local servers, Horizon and diagnostics. Operations use explicit arguments and JSON results. Named command workflows are recorded below and in the validation report. CLI availability and GUI availability are tracked separately. Launcher exit after launch Optional GUI launch flag gui --exit-after-launch. The GUI exits after an uncancelled launch worker succeeds and returns valid JSON with a positive PID. The default keeps the GUI open. PID/result gate tests and real Linux lifecycle accepted: the GUI exited successfully while its separately grouped Java game process continued running. This check did not capture a game menu. Report launcher-session residency separately from the continuing Java/game process. launch --wait intentionally keeps the calling CLI alive. Official metadata and vanilla Runtime fetches version manifests, verifies version JSON and installs client, libraries, assets, logging configuration and natives. Game-menu acceptance: real Linux Minecraft 26.3 main menu with Java 25; the earlier fresh Minecraft 1.21.1 run reached the welcome screen. Actual world play/save, Realms and multiplayer were not exercised. Portable launch planning Core handles inheritance, legacy/modern arguments, OS/architecture/features rules, Maven paths, native classifiers and Java requirements. It creates argv vectors. Unit tests, a no_std target check and official old/current manifest plans for multiple OS configurations. Real execution across the historical version range and each OS remains open. Fabric Official loader profile and dependency installation, merged with the Minecraft version. Real Linux Minecraft 1.21.1 main menu, Fabric API and Mod Menu; a Mod Menu screen was captured. Broader loader/game/mod combinations remain to be accepted. Quilt Official loader metadata, semantic loader-version ordering and profile inheritance. Real Linux Minecraft 1.21.1 main menu with Quilt 0.30.2 after the automatic-selection fix. Broader Quilt loader/game/mod combinations remain to be accepted. Forge Official installer execution, generated profile discovery and locally produced artifact handling. Linux Forge 52.1.20 installation, launch plan and real Minecraft 1.21.1 main menu accepted after the local-artifact fix. Representative old/new Forge versions and mod combinations remain open. NeoForge Official installer with an explicitly selected compatible loader version. Implementation and shared installation checks. Fresh installation and real game launch across supported versions. Managed Java Java manager lists/discovers runtimes, downloads an official Adoptium JRE using SHA-256 and size, extracts it in staging, checks java -version, and retains immutable version directories. Real Linux installation of Temurin jdk-21.0.13.1+2; archive size 52,190,567 bytes. Unsafe archive and link fixtures are tested. Windows/macOS runtime execution and the supported major-version range. Automatic Java during install The install path checks the version's required Java major and can provision a missing managed runtime when no explicit Java path is configured. Java selection itself remains a selector; direct launch does not download a runtime. Real Minecraft 26.3 installation automatically added Temurin jdk-25.0.5.1+2 to a home that previously contained only Java 21. The resulting launch dry run selected Java 25, and a real Minecraft 26.3 launch reached the main menu. Keep explicit Java configuration, installation-time provisioning and launch-time selection distinguishable in reports. Microsoft accounts Device authorization, refresh, Xbox/XSTS and Minecraft profile/entitlement flow, account selection and OS secret storage adapters. A registered application ID is required. Code and local validation paths. A live licensed-account sign-in/refresh/launch result; adapters on each OS. Offline single-player profile Explicit user name and compatible offline UUID in the launch plan. The recorded Linux vanilla/Fabric launches used explicit offline names. Online ownership authentication is handled through the account flow. Diagnostics Runtime/tool discovery, Java reporting and shared-storage statistics. CLI diagnostics and GUI Settings paths. Redacted crash analysis, AI providers and authorized automated repair. The current 0.1.2 application source uses the published zgpui 0.1.5 package and its zgpui::native window, input and drawing API, with native and linux-software enabled. Linux renders into a client CPU surface and submits it through X11. The former zui-native dependency and alias are removed. Version 0.1.5 separates text measurement from rasterization, bounds ellipsis probes and accelerates software rectangle spans. Hidden management lists are released; hidden Activity logs remain bounded and drained without per-chunk repaint. Nine unchanged English titles borrow static strings through zi18n 0.1.0; a language selector and translated catalogues are not implemented. Historical v0.1.0/AUR 0.1.0-1 evidence retains its original backend and artifact identity. See the manifest, pinned submodules and architecture. Content and distribution Area Implemented behavior and source Recorded acceptance Remaining scope Verified downloads and shared storage HTTPS transport, bounded concurrency/retry and digest-addressed storage. Downloads require expected digests and limits. Conventional Minecraft paths reuse cached objects. Real Minecraft, mod, resource, Java and Horizon downloads; repair after both a library path and its cache object were corrupted; an edited active resource ZIP leaves its cache object unchanged. Byte-range resume, mirror selection, broader network settings and additional damaged-cache cases. Modrinth mods Content management searches with game/loader filters; installs required dependencies; lists, toggles, updates and removes tracked mods; exposes transaction recovery. Required-version conflicts and incompatible projects are rejected. CLI acceptance: real Mod Menu 11.0.4→11.0.5 update with Fabric API and Placeholder API; required-dependency remove/disable refusal; toggle, update, remove and v2 recovery checks. Existing Fabric/Mod Menu game-menu evidence is recorded separately. Optional dependency selection, groups and exhaustive version-combination solving. The resolver has explicit graph/iteration bounds. Modrinth pack catalogue Search official modpack projects and install a selected project release through the mrpack importer. Pack acceptance: real sop-continued project IpYIvkPB, release TAU7qd8y: search, install, instance inspection and launch dry run. The pack installed 19 files totalling 15,962,909 bytes with Fabric 0.19.3. The named pack's game launch remains unverified. Existing game-cache reuse is part of this result, not a fresh-install timing benchmark. Mrpack import/export Safe fresh-instance import, staged overrides and export. Dependency identifiers include minecraft, fabric-loader, quilt-loader, forge and neoforge. ZIP/path fixtures, GUI export/import of a small vanilla instance and the named public-pack install. Representative Forge/NeoForge/Quilt pack launches and unavailable-file cases remain open. Mrpack hashes Download/import verifies SHA-1 plus size; received SHA-512 is retained as metadata. Export streams the files, checks SHA-1/size and computes SHA-512 for the output index. Archive helper and format tests. The reader accepts legacy inputs without SHA-512; strict conformance to every current format rule is not claimed. Resource packs Resource manager: exact project/game filtering, add/list/update/remove, availability toggle, revision history and restore. Native Resources exposes lists, project-ID/slug addition, enable/disable, update, confirmed removal and transaction recovery. Only tracked, unchanged ZIP files are modified. 20-command real CLI acceptance, including a No Pumpkin Blur download and older-release upgrade. New native fixture acceptance verifies that unmanaged files remain unchanged. New GUI network install/update paths still need live acceptance; catalogue search and historical revision restore remain CLI paths. In-game selection/rendering is separate; options.txt selected packs remain unchanged. Shader packs Same tracked-file lifecycle in shaderpacks, with upstream loader requirements returned to the caller. Actual Terder's Potato Shader download, verified size/hash/catalogue, list output and unchanged game configuration. Shader-engine installation and in-game shader compilation/rendering. Downloading a shader ZIP does not install Iris or OptiFine. Resource transaction recovery Per-file journal, retained originals and before/after lock snapshots; ambiguous or manually changed files are preserved. Interrupted and repeated recovery fixtures; live remove/history/restore workflow; refusal with a recorded live-PID fixture. Windows/macOS failure-recovery acceptance. Non-Unix ambiguous identity cases are left for explicit recovery. Historical archives currently remain on disk. The current Modrinth format specification requires both SHA-1 and SHA-512 fields. Field preservation, download verification and export computation are separate behaviors. Resource-pack/shader dependencies are reported; these commands do not silently install additional projects or shader engines. Instance data, local services and Horizon Area Implemented behavior and source Recorded acceptance Remaining scope Instance lifecycle Create/list/show/configure, independent game-data clone, trash/list/restore. A clone is marked for installation so shared binaries/profiles/natives can be recreated. Trash retains shared objects. Local tests cover independent writable copies, trash/restore, collisions and symlink refusal. The synthetic-data CLI lifecycle also verifies separate inodes, occupied-target refusal and retained clone edits. Large-instance acceptance, groups, directory relocation and migrations from other launchers. World management List/info/path/import/export/clone. Reads bounded gzip Java NBT metadata without editing chunks. Native Worlds lists saves, imports a folder or one clearly rooted ZIP, exports ZIP and copies a verified path. Synthetic save fixtures, CLI file roundtrips and native import/export flow, including occupied-target refusal. GUI clone/details, playing an imported real world, data-pack management, previews, NBT editing, chunk tools and 3D blueprints. Backup/restore Manual snapshots with SHA-256 manifests, safe staged restore, a pre-restore snapshot and interruption journal. Native Backups lists/creates snapshots and confirms restore with the actual label and ID. CLI hash/restore checks and native confirmed restore using synthetic files; changed bytes were restored and the pre-restore copy remained available. Scheduled backups, retention controls, remote/cloud backup and broad real-world recovery acceptance. Local Java server management Create/install/start/status/stop/list, verified official JARs, Java selection, logs and process identity. Native Servers exposes create/install/start/stop and refreshed state. Start requires explicit eula=true; creation leaves it false. Original six-command CLI acceptance downloaded the official JAR. The new native fixture creates a server and verifies visible EULA refusal with no process started. Live server installation/start/stop through the new GUI, GUI config editing/ping and a user-authorized real server/world lifecycle. Managed start/stop remains Linux-only with procfs/pidfd. Server status ping Bounded Java server-list-ping handshake, status JSON and ping/pong over TCP, with DNS/connect/read limits. A real local TCP fake server exercises the wire protocol and malformed packets. External servers, older legacy ping protocols and broader timeout/network cases. Horizon launcher provider Separate provider manages the official Horizon launcher component. It verifies GitHub asset digest, signed SHA256SUMS and extracted-file hashes; launch rechecks managed files. Actual Linux x86_64 launcher@0.2.84 download (35,123,939 bytes), signature/manifest verification, extraction and verified --version execution. Horizon sign-in, legitimate game preparation and entering a game. Java mod-loader support is not transferred to Horizon. Other OS archives have fixtures, not native execution acceptance. Recorded resource acceptance The reproducible resource script uses a new test home and two small official releases. Its sanitized acceptance record retains the command outcomes and explicit limits: Project Kind Accepted release Archive bytes No Pumpkin Blur (iQRsGaVM) Resource pack kcDL19Mv 768 Terder's Potato Shader (j8vzmojd) Shader IEpWGvCX 24,189 The upgrade test seeds a previous managed state from the official compatible release 1BoGsbLr, updates through the real CLI to kcDL19Mv, and verifies that the previous archive remains recoverable. Expected failures for manual collisions, edited managed content and a sleeping-process fixture with a live PID are part of the accepted command sequence. No Minecraft world or shader renderer is started by this script. Recorded lifecycle acceptance scripts/test_lifecycle_cli.py ran 21 recorded real CLI commands in a new isolated data root. Three commands deliberately tested and received protective failures: importing over an existing world, exporting over an existing ZIP, and restoring an instance into an occupied target. The successful commands checked world directory/ZIP/clone roundtrips, backup manifests and pre-restore snapshots, independent writable instance copies, and trash/list/restore. The source world contains three files totalling 2,111 bytes: generated gzip NBT, an explicitly opaque region fixture and a fixture marker. It is not a game-loadable world. No Java/game/server process or network download is requested. The acceptance establishes command routing, response fields and file preservation; playing and saving a real imported world remains a separate target. Platform acceptance Surface Linux Windows macOS Java client and native GUI X11/XWayland path; 0.1.2 creation/management fixtures passed. Earlier real vanilla/Fabric/Forge/Quilt outcomes retain their original identities. Full GUI cross-build passed on the normal GNU target; native zmcl runtime acceptance pending. Source paths and generated launch plans; native zmcl build/runtime acceptance pending. Managed Java Official x86_64 JRE installation accepted. Platform selection/extraction paths; native execution pending. Platform selection/extraction paths; native execution pending. World, backup and resource mutation Process-record checks plus session-lock safeguards; named fixture/CLI scenarios accepted. Conservative refusal when an existing launch record cannot establish exit; transaction and filesystem behavior need native acceptance. Conservative launch-record handling and native filesystem acceptance pending. Local managed server Start/stop implementation uses procfs and pidfd identity checks. Managed start/stop explicitly unavailable; installation/ping have portable code paths. Managed start/stop explicitly unavailable; installation/ping have portable code paths. Horizon provider Linux x86_64 glibc launcher component accepted. x64/arm64 archive mappings, pending native execution. x64/arm64 archive mappings, pending native execution. The upstream zgpui 0.1.5 release independently ran Windows/macOS native probes; those results do not establish zmcl application acceptance on those systems. No native Wayland backend or hardware-driver result is inferred from the Linux private-display run. Process, archive and account-provider prerequisites are described in ARCHITECTURE.md. Capabilities still outside the implemented scope These remain visible acceptance targets from the fixed XMCL baseline: OptiFine/LabyMod installation; alternate Yggdrasil, Ely.by and LittleSkin authentication. CurseForge/FTB distribution and unavailable-file handling; CurseForge, MCBBS, Packwiz, offline/server-pack workflows beyond the implemented mrpack path. Mod/content groups, optional-dependency UI and creator project/gallery/version publication. World/data-pack editing, chunk visualization and 3D blueprint workflows. Scheduled/remote backups and retention management; remote SSH/SFTP servers, deployment and service credentials. P2P LAN discovery, ICE/STUN/relay traversal and two-client acceptance; Together-specific service integrations. AI crash diagnosis and model-provider/tool permissions beyond basic local diagnostics. Full desktop file associations, shortcuts, notifications and accessibility; themes/backgrounds; controller-only Big Picture and virtual keyboard. Windows Bedrock management; a signed launcher self-update/rollback channel; complete OS/game/loader acceptance. Claim–evidence review Review dimension Question and current answer Contribution Which useful paths exist? The tables identify concrete commands and native flows, with source links. Full XMCL coverage remains the goal. Clarity Can readers distinguish file operations, GUI exposure and game execution? Separate columns and named outcomes provide that distinction. Experimental strength What ran against real software? Named Minecraft, Modrinth, Adoptium and Horizon outcomes are recorded in VALIDATION.md. Performance claims use the matched protocol in PERFORMANCE.md. Evaluation completeness What remains? Synthetic-world tests, untested OS paths, account authorization, shader rendering and missing services remain explicitly scoped. Design soundness What is protected? Expected digests, staged publication, operation locks and retained revisions are backed by the cited code/tests. Recovery limits and history storage cost remain documented. Upstream references XMCL v0.73.1 release and fixed service interfaces. Modrinth project search, version files and mrpack specification. Adoptium API cookbook. Horizon installation and first launch, official source and pinned release-signature implementation.

title: 性能测量与可复核记录
body: 基于 Project Z 的原生 Minecraft 启动器。 性能测量与可复核记录 0.1.3：大备份查询下降，完整 GUI 目标仍未完成 相对已经完成按需导入的 af14e2c 候选，固定两份各含 10000 个文件的备份、系统 Python、三对交错实际 CLI 查询中，完整树观测峰值均下降。各组三轮最大值为 RSS 45,692 → 35,368 KiB（约 −22.6%），PSS 35,099 → 24,824 KiB（约 −29.3%）。2000 个世界的列表查询峰值有重叠，未证明稳定下降；同一种查询的前后规范 JSON 响应逐轮一致。逐轮数据与夹具 最终 0.1.3 二进制 SHA-256 为 02620a8ec4fac34e63fcbe483268149b2ed4032ac2d7bf42975ff6b19b72a1aa。以下为六组原生管理流程，包含启动和流程间等待，单位 KiB。10 MiB = 10,240 KiB；不是空首页静置统计。 环境 主 RSS 中位 / 峰值 主 PSS 中位 / 峰值 相关树 RSS 峰值 相关树 PSS 峰值 默认 PATH，含 mise shim 11,316 / 17,780 7,300 / 13,326 59,884 48,651 ZMCL_PYTHON=/usr/bin/python3 11,020 / 17,040 6,783 / 12,528 37,948 19,306 两组 GUI 分别有 116/2820、132/2767 个含缺读样本；查询共 73/1193 个。完整树中位数为 null，峰值为采样下界；未知内存没有填零。成功读取的样本中 Swap/SwapPss 为零，缺读仍未知。默认环境中一部分名为 python3 的进程实际映像为 mise；这些开销保留在相关树中，选择系统 Python 不是代码优化。完整 GUI 数据 私有 Xvfb 为 1280×900×24，窗口 1120×760；GUI 实际采样间隔中位约 8.24/8.18 ms。显示服务 RSS 中位数 38,992/38,732 KiB、PSS 32,746/32,496 KiB 单列，观察线程 CPU 为 9.83/9.31 秒。GUI 控制器内存未独立采样。共享主机、未清缓存、缺读和不同原型身份均在完整报告说明。主进程和完整树都存在超过 10 MiB 的状态，不能用局部查询收益宣称整体目标完成。 本版程序 1,473,752 字节，官方 tar.gz 679,517 字节，展开的 7 个常规文件合计 1,527,273 字节。文件体积与运行内存分开，系统库、Python、Java、游戏及缓存不包含在发布文件中。发行记录 2026-11-20 0.1.2 GUI 迭代：分开报告两项对照 固定场景 基线 → 候选 结果 空库窗口，6 秒内请求 360 次 Expose，三对交错运行 GUI CPU 中位数 2.65 → 1.47 秒 −44.53%；请求频率不是渲染帧率 2000 个世界，Library → Worlds → Library，两对交错运行 返回 Library 的 GUI PSS+SwapPss 7,940 → 6,110 KiB −23.05% 同一大列表返回阶段 GUI RSS 12,808 → 10,948 KiB −14.52% 同一阶段，应用加单列显示服务 逐样本合计 PSS+SwapPss 39,952 → 38,742.5 KiB −3.03% CPU 对照冻结到一个 renderer 候选，大列表对照冻结到另一组合候选；都不是最终 0.1.2 二进制重新实测。大列表收益不能全部归因于离页清理，释放对象也不保证分配器立即归还 RSS。空库 idle RSS 基本不变、PSS 未下降；管理动作完整树峰值没有稳定降低。全状态低于 10 MiB 的目标仍未完成。 两项均在有其他构建任务的共享 Linux 主机运行。保留 swap、外部显示服务、观察器与短命进程缺读，不将缺读填成零。详见分析与测量方法、空库逐轮汇总、2000 世界逐轮汇总及公开源码等价证明。renderer 的本地实测候选可用公开基线和已发布补丁精确重建。 最终 0.1.2 Linux GUI 的大小为 1,473,144 字节（1.40 MiB），Windows GNU 跨编译为 1,366,528 字节（1.30 MiB）。构建、功能与对应哈希见最终应用验收；这些是文件大小，不是内存值。 v0.1.1：历史冻结实测 空库默认首页静置 RSS 的本次中位数为 9.55 MiB；完整 GUI 内存目标仍未完成。 启动、连续重绘和管理操作均存在超过 10 MiB 的 RSS。PSS 与 RSS 分别报告；按需启动后退出的 CLI/Python 仍计入相关进程树。 冻结应用源码为 35eb8a3，消费正式 zgpui 0.1.2 / 5b268da。主程序1,439,712字节，SHA-256 a28998952b42d09f652ac95da47ddb15930cd556b6fa4e9b7e7ebbd23a4ac2e9。统计和每轮结果见当前测量汇总。 主进程与相关进程树 单位为 KiB；10 MiB = 10,240 KiB。静置取每轮11样本的中位数，再取三轮中位数。峰值均为采样观察下界，各列分别取最大值。 场景 主 RSS 主 PSS 相关树 RSS 相关树 PSS 空库首页静置中位数 9,784 4,647 9,784 4,647 空库静置样本最大值 9,864 5,085 9,864 5,085 连续重绘观察峰值 13,192 8,256 13,192 8,256 管理测试启动阶段峰值 16,972 9,989 16,972 9,989 六项动作阶段峰值，排除启动 13,892 9,306 60,860 49,269 空库与重绘期间只观察到一个应用进程；管理操作最多同时三个。管理全程主 RSS 中位数为10,424 KiB，不能把空首页的数字推广到其他页面。三轮活动进程的 VmHWM 为17,204、16,540、15,832 KiB，管理进程为17,064 KiB；这些生命周期计数包含启动。 最大相关树样本出现在备份/恢复阶段，该条读取完整：GUI RSS/PSS为10,420/5,260 KiB，GUI派生的CLI为5,256/1,454 KiB，CLI派生的Python为45,184/42,555 KiB，合计60,860/49,269 KiB。这里是同一条样本的相加，并非把各进程不同时间的最大值叠加。 条件、显示服务与换页 在2026-11-20 15:48:13–15:50:49（Asia/Taipei）运行，Linux x86_64、1120×760窗口、私有Xvfb、zgpui原生CPU后端。每轮先预热20秒，再记录11个一秒间隔的静置样本；随后6秒内以60 Hz请求360次Expose，事件可能合并，并记录重绘后静置。没有清空系统缓存，没有启动Minecraft/Java。 三轮活动样本完整。六项管理流程共有2,938条样本，其中129条包含已退出或不可读的相关进程；这些条目保留，完整树中位数和完整CPU总量为 null，管理内存状态为 needs_review。功能六项通过与测量完整性分别判断；未知进程的值不作为零。 显示服务单列：启动前Xvfb RSS为37,620–37,900 KiB；运行时静置RSS增量为1,248–1,512 KiB，PSS增量为1,061–1,269 KiB。管理流程Xvfb RSS/PSS中位数增量为584/270 KiB。显示服务不是应用子进程，其绝对值、before/during差值及负增量都保留在汇总中。优化未增加常驻后台绘制进程。 第二轮重绘后静置发生换页：该阶段应用PSS中位数为3,301 KiB、SwapPss中位数为1,336 KiB，逐样本相加后中位数为4,637 KiB；Xvfb SwapPss为8,432 KiB。不能把这一轮驻留下降视为优化收益。空库idle、drawing和管理阶段已读取到的SwapPss为零；缺读仍是未知。 33个宿主快照都观察到外部Cargo/Rustc等任务。MemAvailable最低2,009,508 KiB，memory PSI avg10最高some=4.34、full=3.87。这是共享开发机的限定实测，不是独占安静机器上的普遍性能结论。 CPU与观察器成本 6秒重绘轮次 GUI/树CPU秒 Xvfb CPU秒 控制器CPU秒 1 3.38 0.60 3.18 2 3.21 0.56 3.11 3 2.68 0.46 2.82 GUI重绘CPU中位数为3.21秒。管理观察窗约30.94秒，主进程CPU为10.04秒，树共同身份增量的观察下界为10.96秒；观察线程自身使用15.55秒CPU。频繁读取 /proc 会扰动被测程序，未把观察成本省略。 测试端xdotool、ImageMagick、夹具CLI和测试端ZIP回导CLI不属于已部署应用，已单列其范围；这些外部驱动的RSS/PSS没有由现有脚本独立采样。GUI自己派生的CLI/Python则完整纳入应用树。最后核对32个观察到的应用/显示进程身份均已退出。 为什么下降，仍缺什么 原版本的OpenGL软件驱动和字体匹配状态占据了大量驻留内存。本版直接使用CPU绘制，字体匹配后释放临时状态，并在X11复制帧后释放客户端像素页；重绘仍需要完整四字节像素表面，1120×760即3,404,800字节。原生实现与生命周期检查见上游源码。 首次CPU接入开发构建 fcc214bf / 二进制 99ea0d70… 的同类活动脚本基线为RSS/PSS 17,560/9,846 KiB。当前构建的空库值更低，但两批共享宿主压力不同，不据此给出通用节省倍数。后续重点是字体初始化峰值、绘制期间的像素与文字缓存，以及管理任务的Python常驻工作集。仅降低首页或把操作移至后台，都不能完成完整口径目标。 复测入口为 scripts/bench_gui_activity.py 和 src/gui/manage_smoke.py --memory-output，先固定实际构建版本、源码提交和二进制哈希，再运行默认参数。完整复现命令及数据字段在脚本 --help 和当前汇总中。 v0.1.1 发行文件 官方Linux预览包为664,850字节，SHA-256 c61a83ce918d7fe3d58a080bc41bc1c5f301c259396cc4a96a5acf81c3ee9f0b；展开后7个常规文件、内容合计1,490,322字节。程序本身1,439,712字节。实际预编译ABI要求glibc≥2.39、Fontconfig≥2.17.0，直接ELF不依赖OpenGL。系统库、Java、Minecraft、账号和缓存不包含在这些分发文件数字中。 v0.1.0 与 XMCL 的历史对照 以下保留v0.1.0原始身份、软件图形环境和固定XMCL v0.73.1比较；不改标为本次0.1.1的测量。 本次记录对应 zmcl 源码 0337762 和 XMCL 官方 0.73.1 Linux x64 发行版。2026 年 11 月 20 日，在同一台 Linux 开发机上，使用同一份 schema 4 脚本，各运行三轮默认空首页。zmcl 的主程序为 1,412,176 bytes；空闲 PSS 的三轮汇总值为 89,946 KiB（87.84 MiB），XMCL 为 376,722 KiB（367.89 MiB）。zmcl 原始样本 · XMCL 原始样本 这些数值只描述本次软件渲染环境中的默认首页。 两款应用开始测量时，主机可用内存分别为：XMCL 1,894,756 KiB，zmcl 6,492,216 KiB。XMCL 样本存在明显换页，两个默认首页的内容也不同。以下表格同时保留驻留页、换出页和合计值，不据此推导相同功能下、所有机器上的性能倍数。zmcl 仍在补齐功能，当前范围见功能矩阵。 v0.1.0 冻结结果 内存单位为 KiB。每轮先取 11 个完整样本的中位数，再取三轮中位数；下表不是单次最低值。 指标 zmcl 0.1.0 / 0337762 XMCL 0.73.1 PSS：按份额计入共享驻留页 都没有增加。内核 CPU 计数频率为 100 Hz，每 tick 为 10 ms，因此这里的 0.00 秒表示有限观察窗内未观察到计数增加，不表示任意时段都没有 CPU 消耗。CPU 单核占用率由 CPU 时间除以各轮实际经过时间计算；不是全机 24 个逻辑 CPU 的总百分比。 各轮数据与范围 应用 / 轮次 PSS 中位数 SwapPss 中位数 逐样本合计中位数 RSS 中位数 CPU 秒 zmcl XMCL 0.73.1 主程序 ELF（bytes） 1,412,176 224,836,856 压缩发行包（bytes） 648,849（tar.gz） 85,934,576（tar.xz） 展开后的常规文件合计（bytes） 1,453,865 293,657,164 展开后的常规文件数 7 23 zmcl 的 v0.1.0 Linux x86_64 开发预览 包含七个常规文件：主程序、README、功能文档、许可证、图标、安装器和 release.json。648,849 bytes 是最终 tar.gz 的实际大小；1,453,865 bytes 是七个文件的内容字节之和，不包括归档头或文件系统分配。压缩方法及两款产品包含的内容不同，本页不由发行包体积推导等功能节省比例。清单与安装验收 该 v0.1.0 预编译包要求 Linux x86_64、glibc 2.43 或更新。 2.43 是此 ELF 直接引用的最高 GLIBC 符号版本，不是所有 Linux 发行版都兼容的证明；系统图形、字体库和外部工具还有自己的要求。其它环境可按源码构建说明构建，并自行验证运行依赖。该分发包的内容与安装验收只覆盖 Linux x86_64。 zmcl 是动态链接的原生程序；系统图形、字体与其它动态库不包含在 ELF 数字中。上表也不包含 Java、Minecraft、mods、账号配置、下载缓存、构建目录或实例数据。展开文件合计没有按设备号与 inode 去重，不等于实际物理磁盘块占用。XMCL 官方包记录 窗口出现与首帧 同一脚本以约 250 ms 间隔轮询 X11 窗口，记录“窗口被发现”的时间。zmcl 三轮为 292.377、296.835、296.322 ms；XMCL 为 1,621.568、3,334.413、1,066.178 ms。各自中位数为 296.322 ms 与 1,621.568 ms。这是轮询发现窗口的时间，受到调度和轮询粒度影响，不是首个可交互画面时间，也不能视为严格冷启动成绩。 zmcl 另有进程内首帧标记，本次为 277、271、298 ms。它从 GUI 入口计到第一帧提交，起点与外部窗口检测不同；XMCL 没有对应标记，因此不对这一数值作跨应用比较。操作系统缓存没有清空，顺序运行可能影响时间。 环境与测试协议 条件 本次设置 操作系统 Omarchy / Linux 7.3.4-arch1-1，x86_64 CPU Intel Core i9-12900HX，24 个逻辑 CPU 物理内存 16,090,532 KiB，约 15.35 GiB 显示 独立 Xvfb，1280×800×24；应用窗口 1024×720 图形环境 LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1；X server 报告 llvmpipe（LLVM 23.1.1，256 bits） 其它驱动覆盖 LP_NUM_THREADS、GALLIUM_DRIVER、MESA_LOADER_DRIVER_OVERRIDE、MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE 均未设置 桌面会话变量 XDG_SESSION_TYPE=x11、SDL_VIDEO_DRIVER=x11，移除 WAYLAND_DISPLAY 场景 每轮全新应用数据和缓存目录，未登录、无实例、默认首页 暖机 / 采样 窗口出现后等待 20 秒；11 个样本，间隔设为 1 秒 顺序 XMCL 连续三轮，然后 zmcl 连续三轮；没有随机化或交错 主机背景与缓存 共享开发机，未做系统级隔离；没有清空操作系统缓存 进程范围 启动器进程树、会话和此前观察到的存活子进程；排除 Xvfb、测试控制器、Java 与 Minecraft X server 的 renderer 是测试显示服务的记录。相同 Xvfb 和环境变量不保证两款应用内部使用相同图形后端；该记录不能单独证明 XMCL 的 ANGLE 后端。本次 zmcl 自身的首帧记录也报告 llvmpipe。硬件 GPU title: zmcl project site
body: 基于 Project Z 的原生 Minecraft 启动器。 zmcl project site A static Chinese documentation page for GitHub Pages. It uses system fonts, local assets and a small command-copy helper. Installation, current capabilities and measurement limits remain readable without JavaScript. There is no application framework, analytics or third-party script. Preview and validation From the repository root: python3 site/check.py python3 -m http.server 8080 --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory site Check desktop and mobile widths, the three current asset links, installation disclosures, command-copy feedback and keyboard focus. The copy helper selects the command if clipboard access is unavailable. Current release: 0.1.4 The primary download section presents exactly three official assets for the development preview: Target File Bytes SHA-256 Linux x86_64 user installation zmcl-0.1.4-linux-x86_64.tar.gz 700244 8265e672ef7914362c1038b71ed382d18efafe49668d7791005713faa5f580f1 Debian x86_64 system package zmcl-0.1.4-linux-x86_64.deb 571108 c19afcdd4e567ffcb580f60fbe5812d6915c12b484e9751518c3f0b790c5b7b8 Windows amd64 user installation zmcl-0.1.4-windows-amd64.zip 670411 48bd7dc7ce0eb799fed225678b6a6d9c4ed518f7ee96482b2c5c1f0f516271cf The fixed release page is /releases/tag/v0.1.4; all asset paths use /releases/download/v0.1.4/. Source is 25c243a593b187b0f0835e740665e1fce96d3621. Linux executable identity is 1504616 bytes / 586968d15c5187c0223d5223294ddcba585789d93934e6a37a3c7e1c516a3615; Windows executable identity is 1382912 bytes / 33164565b43bf2f9db63da8e61db2a211318ca2fa682fd29ef988e910612910f. These file sizes do not measure runtime memory. Linux requirements remain glibc >=2.39, Fontconfig >=2.17.0, FreeType and X11/XWayland. Python >=3.8, curl and CA certificates are used by installation and requested helper operations. The native Linux CPU executable has no direct OpenGL dependency. The DEB explicitly requires CA certificates even with --no-install-recommends; this is not a compatibility claim for every stable Debian or Ubuntu release. AUR zmcl-bin 0.1.4-1 is publicly available at source commit a769068256b4aa0803ab08b7f0691a8a4024a464. Public recipe verification is distinct from installation acceptance: the fresh public clone build, normal host upgrade and installed native update-window acceptance have passed. The real official check reports current 0.1.4. Previous AUR versions and their original identities stay in historical_releases; they are not the current primary download route. Acceptance and boundaries Claim Evidence Scope Three 0.1.4 asset identities and reproducible user commands docs/validation/zdistro-release-0.1.4.json, docs/INSTALL.md Exact files, hashes, source and named platforms Linux DEB upgrade, reinstall and uninstall docs/reports/2026-11-20-zdistro.md Debian forky/sid container, real 0.1.3 to 0.1.4 upgrade and data preservation Portable installation and interface Same release report and structured receipt Prefix with spaces, PATH shadowing, nine native GUI fixture groups; no real account or game claim Minimal Debian can verify official HTTPS Same release receipt Initially missing CA certificates, normal apt installation of required CA, HTTP 200 and certificate verification result 0 Manual update checking does not alter the executable Same release receipt One real query before publication reported local 0.1.4 ahead of online 0.1.3; binary unchanged Windows native packaging and window workflow 44739704182 MSVC, ZIP, private prefix, version, Win32 window, five managed files, uninstall and data preservation on build 26100 Full Windows version matrix, actual Windows games and accounts Not established by this run Keep separate from native runner packaging/window acceptance macOS distribution, signed automatic updates and complete XMCL coverage Not established Remain planned The first Windows validator PATH lookup failure and Linux container documentation-exclusion failure retain their own original records. title: 概览
body: MCP 客户端与服务端原语，连接工具调用和宿主传输。 zmcpio Bounded MCP client/server primitives for applications that own authorization and scheduling. The protocol core is no_std, allocation-free and forbids unsafe Rust. zcall is its only direct third-party dependency; zconv is transitive. The optional std feature adds blocking stdio process I/O and bounded HTTP/1.1 I/O over caller-supplied TCP or verified TLS streams. The crate is named zmcpio on crates.io and the Rust API is imported as zmcpio. The former project name, zmcp, belongs to a different crates.io publisher and must not be used as a dependency for this implementation. Install [dependencies] zmcpio = { version = "0.5.1", default-features = false } To use the stdio and HTTP/1.1 I/O adapters, enable the optional std feature: [dependencies] zmcpio = { version = "0.5.1", default-features = false, features = ["std"] } The protocol core and zcall bridge do not require an allocator. Process/socket setup may allocate. HTTPS requires a caller-supplied verified TLS stream. Development follows the internal Git default branches; Cargo.lock records the exact zcall and zconv commits and package versions. Registry releases use the separate release staging workflow. The shared model contract and resource codecs are available through zmcpio::zcall. The zcall standard-library server remains opt-in; zmcpio keeps its dependency defaults disabled. The MCP bridge still accepts only complete JSON object tool arguments and preserves the full MCP result envelope; resource codecs do not execute MCP or HTTP operations. Boundary zmcpio parses complete JSON-RPC messages and returns borrowed actions. Action::CallTool does not execute anything. An application checks policy, runs its tool, then calls Server::tool_result. No agent loop, TLS engine, OAuth login flow, database, model runtime or automatic network requests are included. Shared model types and provider-format conversion come from zcall. zharness and zmcpio remain independent components, sharing the zcall contract: application +-- zmcpio MCP client/server, stdio, zcall tool bridge | +-- zcall shared model/tool types (re-exported as zmcpio::zcall) +-- zharness tool registry, execution boundary, model bridge +-- zcall model lifecycle +-- zconv Client encodes requests and correlates replies using bounded caller-owned pending slots. bridge converts discovered MCP tools into zcall::v1::ToolDefinition, accepts complete Content::ToolCall or streaming ReadyTool, and appends results through Request::append_tool_result. MCP IDs and model call IDs remain distinct. Use from the source checkout cargo test --locked --all-targets cargo run --locked --example basic cargo run --locked --example mcp_stdio cargo run --locked --example zcall_tools cargo build --locked --features std --example mcp_stdio --example mcp_client target/debug/examples/mcp_client target/debug/examples/mcp_stdio echo '{"text":"hello"}' The stdio example implements only an explicitly allowlisted echo tool. It uses bounded LF framing and keeps diagnostics off stdout. See MCP, architecture, and security. See the client and zcall guide for lifetimes, cancellation, pagination, error policies and custom transports. On Windows use .exe paths. Implemented boundaries Boundary Provided primitives Tool client/server Discovery, list/call, pagination, multimodal results, progress, cancellation, ID correlation Streamable HTTP Modern POST-only and legacy POST/GET/DELETE envelopes; JSON/SSE; sessions and resume metadata for legacy only SSE Incremental caller-buffered decoder, encoder, comments, BOM/UTF-8 handling, backpressure and exact capacity errors Legacy batches Caller-bounded 2025-03-26 request/response arrays, per-item errors and no response for notification-only batches Legacy HTTP+SSE Same-origin endpoint negotiation and separate message stream; no implicit credential forwarding or tool replay Other MCP methods Explicitly enabled resource/prompt/completion/logging routes, callback and MRTR envelopes, subscription validation, version-specific task messages Optional I/O Real stdio process adapter and bounded HTTP/1.1 framing over supplied streams Streamable HTTP, legacy SSE and the opt-in extension APIs ship in 0.3.0. See HTTP and extensions for their contracts and executable examples. See validation for reproducible tests and benchmark limits. A local modern HTTP server and client can be run in separate terminals: cargo run --locked --features std --example mcp_http -- server 8080 sse cargo run --locked --features std --example mcp_http -- client 127.0.0.1:8080 Use json instead of sse to exercise a single-JSON HTTP response. The example binds only to loopback and exposes only echo. For remote HTTPS, inject a verified TLS stream or connect the no-std protocol adapter to an existing HTTP stack. Legacy single-message negotiation covers 2024-11-05, 2025-03-26, 2025-06-18 and 2025-11-25. Modern requests use 2026-07-28. This is a set of protocol and transport primitives, not an automatic agent, OAuth client, task worker or storage service. It is not a certification that every optional extension or third-party server conforms. Bounded JSON-RPC batches are supported only for 2025-03-26, through an explicit batch API; other revisions reject arrays. Application-owned callbacks, task execution, policy, replay storage and timers remain explicit. Memory contract Input, token tape, output, framing and request slots are caller-owned. Parsing borrows input and token storage. Retain both while an action or tracker ID uses them. No hidden growth occurs. Error reports a category, byte offset and required capacity when known. On serialization failure discard partial output and retry serialization only; never repeat a side-effecting tool just to grow output. JSON accepts valid UTF-8 and paired Unicode escapes, rejects duplicate decoded object keys, enforces byte/member/string/token/depth bounds, and preserves number lexemes. Request IDs use signed 64-bit integers or strings; out-of-range integer IDs are rejected rather than rounded. Nesting has a hard ceiling of 64 containers. Full JSON Schema validation is an application responsibility. License: MIT OR Apache-2.0.

title: MCP client and zcall integration
body: MCP 客户端与服务端原语，连接工具调用和宿主传输。 MCP client and zcall integration zmcpio can act as the client of an MCP tool server. The default core encodes requests and validates replies without I/O or allocation. The optional std adapters start a real stdio server process or frame HTTP/1.1 on supplied streams. zcall is the only direct dependency; the exact same types are available through zmcpio::zcall::v1. Run a real server connection [dependencies] zmcpio = { version = "0.2", features = ["std"] } From this source checkout: cargo build --locked --features std --example mcp_stdio --example mcp_client target/debug/examples/mcp_client target/debug/examples/mcp_stdio echo '{"text":"hello"}' Use .exe executable paths on Windows. The client example starts the selected server, performs the legacy handshake, follows tools/list pages, checks that the explicitly selected tool exists, calls it, prints its result and closes the child. It never chooses a tool on its own. Server command arguments follow the JSON argument. In an application, pass a configured std::process::Command directly to stdio::StdioTransport::spawn; no shell is inserted by the library. The executable is an integration example, not a hardened long-running agent. Its 32-message reply budget and 128-page discovery budget bound loops, not elapsed time. Blocking stdio reads do not have a response deadline. For cancellation or timeouts during a blocked read, supply application-owned asynchronous/deadline I/O through MessageReader, MessageWriter or your own loop. Protocol client Create a Client with a borrowed identity, an explicit Era, and caller-sized Pending storage. A new client identity starts its numeric request IDs at one; do not reset it on an existing legacy connection. The client retains no request or response payload and allocates no dynamically growing request table. Legacy mode starts with initialize. A supported initialize response moves to AwaitInitialized; encode and successfully send initialized before requesting tools. Client negotiation accepts the single-message tools baselines 2025-11-25, 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26 and 2024-11-05. Use initialize_with_version for an explicit initial revision. Only 2025-03-26 supports the opt-in bounded batch API; receive still takes one message, so batch consumers explicitly iterate entries. protocol_version() exposes the selected version; unknown revisions are rejected. Modern mode uses 2026-07-28 metadata on every request and is immediately ready. discover is optional and exposes supported versions, capabilities and optional server identity. There is no automatic legacy fallback or retry of tools/call. with_client_capabilities explicitly declares callbacks implemented by the host; the default declares none. Advertised capabilities do not authorize execution. list_tools returns one borrowed ToolPage at a time. Its cursor is opaque: decode it into retained caller storage before reusing the response input/tokens. Applications own cross-page duplicate handling, tool namespaces, page limits, authorization, JSON Schema validation and caching. No schema/resource URL is fetched. call_tool accepts a validated JSON object and returns Outgoing { id, len }. Send only output[..len]. A too-small output or full pending table reserves no ID and changes no state. A successful encode does reserve a slot before network I/O, because a partial send is ambiguous; explicitly close or abandon rather than silently issuing the side effect twice. receive takes exactly one complete JSON-RPC message and returns a typed Event. Only a matching, well-formed response completes a pending request. Numeric and string IDs are distinct; duplicates and late/unmatched responses are rejected. Input/token-capacity errors leave pending state intact for re-parsing with larger storage. Notifications and uncorrelated errors do not complete requests. Bridge to model calls The bridge uses zcall's actual public types rather than parallel look-alikes: Input Adapter Output Discovered MCP ToolView bridge::tool_definition zcall::v1::ToolDefinition for RequestBuilder::tool / Request::append_tool Complete Content::ToolCall bridge::prepare_call Validated PreparedCall with caller-buffered escaped arguments Streaming ReadyTool bridge::prepare_ready The same PreparedCall; partial deltas are not accepted Streaming ReadyTool with later Session mutation bridge::prepare_ready_detached Copies only ID/name into caller storage so the retained Invocation does not borrow Session Authorized PreparedCall PreparedCall::start MCP request bytes plus a retained Invocation identity binding Completed MCP CallResult Invocation::content zcall::v1::Content::ToolResult with the original provider call ID Completed MCP CallResult Invocation::append_result Checked update to a zcall Request history Run cargo run --locked --example zcall_tools for the complete executable discovery -> model tool definition -> MCP tool call -> next model request example. This example uses in-memory transport and a supplied completed model call; it does not make a real model API call. The same byte/state APIs are used with stdio. An Invocation binds the model's call ID to the independent MCP request ID. Retain it until the response arrives, and pass the actual response ID to the result adapter. The adapter rejects mismatches. Request::append_tool_result then rejects unknown, ambiguous or duplicate model call results. For streaming sessions, explicitly retain the result before calling the model session's submit_tool_result; the bridge does not prematurely advance a model lifecycle. Use prepare_ready_detached when that Invocation must outlive a borrow of the session: it copies identity bytes into caller storage but still borrows arguments until they have been encoded. This permits a later mutable Session transition without allocating Strings or bypassing Rust's borrowing rules. Results and provider differences The default ResultEncoding::Portable retains the entire MCP result object as zcall::Data::Json, including content, structuredContent, isError and metadata. It omits the separate provider-native error flag because several zcall protocol adapters cannot encode that field. Actual tool failures remain visible inside the JSON envelope. The model receives that JSON representation, not provider-native image/audio tool-result blocks. Nothing is automatically flattened or fetched. This full-envelope adapter is not a privacy filter: _meta and nested metadata also reach the model. If a server/application contract marks any data as client-only or confidential, do not pass that result through the convenience adapter unchanged. Construct an application-filtered zcall::Content::ToolResult instead, retaining the original model call ID and the tool-failure indication. NativeErrorFlag is an explicit opt-in through content_with_encoding or append_result_with_encoding for a format supporting it, such as Anthropic. An unsupported destination still fails in zcall rather than silently dropping the flag. MCP tool annotations/output schemas remain on ToolView; they are not input schemas or permission grants. MCP schemas do not imply a provider's strict schema mode, so discovered definitions explicitly set strict=false. JSON-RPC failures and modern input_required are not completed tool results. Handle them separately. The client validates the input-required envelope and exposes it without executing callbacks. See extensions for explicit continuation using the original parameters, opaque request state and caller-approved input responses. The bridge cannot consume it as a successful CallResult. Ownership, transports and limits Retain discovery/result bytes and their MCP token tapes while borrowed views or zcall requests reference them. Escaped model IDs/names use caller identity storage; escaped JSON-string arguments use separate argument storage. After encoding, argument storage can be reused while identity storage remains retained. Conversion into zcall validated JSON uses its public checked constructor and caller token scratch; it does not introduce an unchecked lifetime shortcut. The core works with complete messages supplied by any transport. The http, sse and legacy_sse modules now supply bounded protocol handling; optional http_io supplies blocking HTTP/1.1 framing on generic I/O streams. See HTTP for real TCP examples, buffer ownership and TLS integration. There is no bundled TLS implementation, OAuth login UI, HTTP/2/3 wire stack, background reconnect loop, or unbounded remote-URL client. Close the response stream to cancel a modern HTTP request. For legacy HTTP or stdio, send the cancellation notification instead. A legacy disconnect alone does not cancel work. Resume a legacy stream with GET and a committed event ID; never repeat a side-effecting POST as a substitute for resumption. The client keeps a request pending after encoding cancellation because the peer may already have completed it. abandon is an explicit local timeout/cleanup decision and never reuses that ID. Neither operation proves remote effects were undone. Child-process cleanup manages only the direct child, not a process tree. Evidence and boundaries tests/client.rs checks state transitions, capacity retries, IDs, pagination, notifications, malformed results and explicit error paths. tests/bridge.rs checks real zcall request encoding across five tool-capable protocols, full result preservation and separate model/MCP identities. tests/stdio.rs checks framing and actual child lifecycle; scripts/client_smoke.py uses both the Rust example server and an independent Python JSON-RPC peer. These are tools-profile tests, not a full official MCP conformance certification or a network latency guarantee.

title: Architecture
body: MCP 客户端与服务端原语，连接工具调用和宿主传输。 Architecture Each module owns one boundary. json validates once into caller-sized offset tokens; field iteration subsequently follows token indexes without reparsing. rpc distinguishes message categories. mcp checks version/lifecycle and returns actions. tools encodes definitions and results. tracker accounts for in-flight IDs and cancellation. transport frames stdio or defines complete-message I/O. client owns only protocol state and caller-sized pending slots. Request IDs are monotonic integers and are not reused during a client lifetime. Successful encoding reserves a slot; successful response validation releases it. Malformed or unrelated replies cannot complete a different operation. Notifications never complete requests. Client construction is for a new protocol connection/identity, not a way to reset ID counters on an existing legacy connection. bridge uses the public zcall v1 contract rather than inventing parallel model types. A retained Invocation binds the independent MCP and provider call IDs. Validated MCP values are revalidated through zcall's public JSON constructor at the type boundary; this avoids unsafe constructors or a second direct dependency. Default bridging retains the whole result envelope as JSON for portability. The optional stdio module owns a spawned child and its pipes. Framing remains bounded and caller-buffered; std process creation is not allocation-free. It is blocking, with bounded graceful shutdown but no response-read deadline. Async I/O runtimes, TLS verification, credentials and scheduling remain application responsibilities. Offsets use u32 to keep each token compact. Inputs larger than u32::MAX are rejected. Recursive descent is bounded to at most 64 container levels even when a caller sets a larger limit. Duplicate-key detection is quadratic in the number of fields of one object and is bounded by max_members. This tradeoff avoids an unbounded hash map; adversarial wide-object performance remains a benchmark case. Server identity is borrowed. Modern capability metadata is borrowed per request and never cached across requests. Legacy lifecycle changes occur only after a successful response encoding, so growing a too-small output does not consume the initialization transition. Initialization starts a protocol connection, not an agent or model session. The application must track concurrent requests, retain borrowed storage until completion, authorize execution, schedule or cancel work, and deliver exactly one response. The server exposes these pieces; it does not secretly do them. Calls may finish in a different order because response IDs are retained explicitly. HTTP and extension boundaries http validates the MCP HTTP envelope independently from socket ownership. sse turns incremental body bytes into complete events with bounded storage; legacy_sse validates the old two-endpoint handshake without granting access to an arbitrary returned URL. http_io is optional blocking HTTP/1.1 framing with Content-Length/chunked/close-delimited bodies and an explicit reuse policy. extensions identifies standard methods, validates required wire fields and provides subscription/task/callback envelope helpers. Servers opt into exact handlers; clients keep bounded request correlation. Returning an action does not read a file, invoke a model, prompt a user, create a task worker, or grant permission. Each such operation is an application decision. Modern HTTP has no protocol session or GET resume stream. Legacy HTTP has optional identity-bound sessions and optional event replay. Keeping these rules separate prevents a network disconnect from being interpreted as the wrong protocol's cancellation signal.

title: Explicit MCP extension boundaries
body: MCP 客户端与服务端原语，连接工具调用和宿主传输。 Explicit MCP extension boundaries The crate provides a bounded wire boundary for optional MCP methods. The host implements resources, prompts, models, user interaction, subscriptions and tasks. Only enable methods your application actually serves; a capability is not an authorization decision.
