A 64-byte echo round trip took 176.627 ns and a 1 MiB round trip took 78.186 µs under the aggregation below. These numbers include fuel metering and the input/output memory boundary. They describe this guest and machine, not arbitrary plugin workloads, and do not imply native-call performance or zero-copy behavior. The benchmark source is clean commit e957b45e6f9a071a8ce3030fd75d3ca34334c71b. Later release changes update versions and evidence; the measured adapter and benchmark are identified by this immutable source. The native ABI's prior measurements remain in the 0.2.0 report. Method The host was Linux 6.18.57, x86_64, glibc 2.41 on an AMD EPYC 9V74 80-Core processor. Each benchmark process was pinned to CPU 0. Rust was 1.100.0 (0ef1bc386059596dada8fb65b50425aab2ea637a, LLVM 23.1.5). The release profile uses optimization level 3, thin LTO, one codegen unit and host panic=unwind. It owns its store on one thread, uses the same Wasmi 2.0 engine, finite fuel, memory/table/stack limits, scratch negotiation, zeroing, copies and lifecycle. zplugin adds its public error handling, size checks and poisoning. title: Untrusted Wasm plugins
body: 原生插件 ABI、动态库加载与可选 Wasm 沙箱。 Untrusted Wasm plugins Trust boundary zplugin::wasm::Plugin executes untrusted Wasm32 code in Wasmi 2.0. The backend validates the module, denies every import and start section, checks its interface, and meters guest execution. Native Plugin::load remains an unsafe operation for trusted machine code. Loading a native library never acquires Wasm isolation. The boundary passes bytes through checked linear-memory offsets. No native function pointer, Rust reference, allocator, task, waker, or resource handle is exposed to the guest. Each instance owns its memory and state. No filesystem, network, environment variable, clock, process or WASI API is linked. An interface ID is a compatibility label, not proof of identity or permission. The wasm feature is optional and implies alloc, not std. Native/default features retain their zero-third-party-runtime dependency policy and share the Project Z zsys loader. All configurations require Rust 1.95. The Wasm host uses Wasmi 2.0.0 with default-features = false and explicit stable, validate, portable-dispatch, and libm. Its locked runtime graph adds eight packages: Wasmi, wasmi_core, wasmi_ir, wasmi_collections, wasmparser, spin, libm, and bitflags. No JIT compiler, text parser, WASI implementation, or third-party executor is enabled by this feature. The guest SDK needs only the default zplugin crate and core. Build and call The runnable guest implements wasm_guest::Guest. Its state has a const initializer and its input/output scratch arrays have fixed capacities. export_wasm! supplies the exports and checked status/length adapter: zplugin::export_wasm!(Demo, constructor = Demo::new(), interface = 0x7a70_6c75_6769_6e01_u64, version = 1, input = 1_048_576, output = 1_048_576); A standalone guest crate uses crate-type = ["cdylib"], a default-features-disabled zplugin dependency, and panic = "abort". Compile with cargo build --release --target wasm32-unknown-unknown. A no_std guest supplies its own panic handler and, only if needed, allocator. A guest can also use Rust std facilities that work without imports; unsupported I/O/WASI imports are rejected at load. The example has no allocator and traps on panic. Its build script sets a 64 KiB guest linear-memory stack with -C link-arg=-zstack-size=65536. This is a size choice for this small example, independent of the host interpreter-stack limit; applications choose an adequate guest stack for their own code. Scratch capacities are also compile-time choices. The host example reads at most the module-size limit plus one byte, calls the safe wasm::Plugin::new(bytes, interface, limits), and then calls plugin.call(operation, input, output). The constructor validates, compiles and binds once. Repeated calls use cached typed exports and reusable guest buffers. No text or structured serialization is imposed; application interfaces define their own byte encoding, such as explicit little-endian values. rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown python3 scripts/wasm.py cargo run --release --example wasm_host --features wasm,std -- target/wasm-pinned/demo.wasm scripts/wasm.py also accepts --guest-toolchain and --host-toolchain to verify independent compilation. The example's operations are echo (0), uppercase (1), stateful counter (2), application error (3), fuel loop (4), trap (5), and denied memory growth (6). Failure operations are deliberate test cases, not host APIs. Frozen byte-buffer protocol v1 This protocol is separate from native zplugin_entry_v1. A compatible core Wasm binary exports the three required items below; unrelated exports are ignored. The engine rejects imports, start sections, shared memory, and multiple memories. The adapter additionally rejects memory64 even if another Cargo dependency enables that engine feature. A module may have one bounded internal table. Export Wasm signature Purpose memory Non-shared Wasm32 memory Instance-local data zplugin_wasm_info_v1 (i32) -> i64 Versioned metadata query zplugin_wasm_call_v1 (i32, i32, i32) -> i64 Operation, input length, output capacity Metadata uses unsigned bit patterns in the integer results: Query field Result 0 Protocol version, exactly 1 1 Application-defined 64-bit interface ID 2 Application interface version; must fit u32 and exactly match 3, 4 Input scratch offset and capacity; each fits u32 5, 6 Output scratch offset and capacity; each fits u32 All seven queries share one fuel budget. Binding checks both complete scratch ranges against current linear memory and host transfer limits. Nonempty buffers must not overlap. Byte alignment is sufficient; offset zero is legal, including for nonempty storage. Empty ranges must still identify an in-bounds position. The negotiated offsets and capacities are cached for the instance lifetime. Before each call the host copies the input and zeroes the granted output range. The guest receives the operation number, actual input length, and min(host_output.len(), negotiated_output_capacity). It returns the signed status in the low 32 bits and the output byte count in the high 32 bits. Status zero means success. Nonzero statuses use the native status-number convention (-3 is short output, -7 unsupported, positive codes are application errors) but are surfaced as wasm::Error::GuestStatus(i32). Output length is ignored on failure. On success it must not exceed the granted capacity. The host copies output only after successful status and length checks. Caller output is unchanged on any error. A trap, engine failure, or invalid success length permanently poisons the instance. Application statuses and oversized host input leave the instance usable; application code must document whether it modifies its own state before an error. Calls use a fresh budget, never an accumulating fuel balance. Dropping the plugin releases its store and allocations without executing a guest destructor. Any language that emits these exports can implement this protocol. The delivered Wasm SDK and independently compiled example are Rust; the existing generated C/C++/Zig native ABI headers describe native libraries, not Wasm memory offsets. Arbitrary WASI programs, browser/wasm-bindgen modules requiring JavaScript imports, Component Model binaries and native dynamic libraries are not accepted by this ABI. Limits and lifecycle Default limits are explicit and customizable per instance: Resource Default limit Enforcement point Binary module bytes 4 MiB Before parsing Guest linear memory 16 MiB, one memory Instantiation and every growth Table elements 4,096, one table Instantiation and every growth Input / output capacity 1 MiB each Binding and calls Guest execution 10,000,000 fuel Combined metadata queries; each subsequent call Interpreter value stack 64 KiB Execution Guest call depth 128 Execution Store instances 1 Instantiation Wasmi's strict validation/compilation limits and eager compilation are always enabled. Over-limit memory.grow and table.grow return Wasm's normal failure sentinel; guests can handle it and continue. Actual traps stop the call. A plugin may be dropped immediately after failure because it has no external callbacks, threads or host resources to drain. The host type is deliberately !Send + !Sync; all operations are serialized through &mut self. Construct separate instances on worker threads to obtain independent state. Reuse also retains guest knowledge: a malicious stateful plugin can remember earlier inputs within its own memory. Use a fresh instance for a new tenant or confidential session. No host-side instance/module cache is created implicitly. The application controls the number of resident instances and aggregate budgets. To switch implementations, construct and validate a new instance first, then replace the active instance at a request boundary. Keep the current instance if the replacement fails. Native hot::Generations is not a Wasm manager. Security boundaries The memory limit covers guest linear memory, not whole-process RSS. The parser, compiled representation, store metadata, host buffers, allocator and interpreter stack add memory. The binary-size cap and strict engine limits constrain accepted input, but they do not impose a process memory quota. The host must bound input file reads and the number/rate of module compilations and active instances. Fuel limits metered guest execution, including the metadata queries and dynamic bulk-memory operations. It is not a wall-clock timeout for validation/compilation, and different Wasmi releases may meter differently. No host callbacks are present whose execution could evade the guest budget. This version does not implement asynchronous Wasm tasks, WASI capability grants, or host-call bridges. Isolation depends on the correctness of Wasmi and its dependencies. This adapter uses safe engine APIs and forbids unsafe Rust in the host module. Its tests do not certify immunity to engine defects, hardware side channels, or host OOM. For high-risk multi-tenant execution, add a separate OS process/container with its own memory/CPU/syscall policy. That additional boundary is outside this library. Primary references: WebAssembly security, Wasmi 2.0, engine configuration, resource-limiter scope. The Wasmi project lists audits of older releases; this document makes no audit claim for the new adapter or Wasmi 2.0. Claim and evidence review The binary conformance suite uses no third-party fixture generator. The independent build runner executes the real Rust guest; CI uses Linux, macOS and Windows native hosts. Run both locally: cargo test --locked -p zplugin --features wasm --test wasm cargo test --locked -p zplugin --features wasm,wasmi/memory64 --test wasm python3 scripts/wasm.py Review dimension Claim and evidence Boundary Contribution Import-free safe Wasm load/call path; real guest round trips Does not retrofit native isolation Clarity Export table, scratch rules, defaults and complete examples above Only this protocol, not arbitrary Wasm applications Experimental strength Traps, fuel, memory/table growth, buffers, malformed modules, mutation cases Regression tests, not exhaustive formal verification Evaluation completeness MSRV, native-host CI, cross-compiler guests, feature-unification regression CI evidence identifies actual runner targets Design soundness Safe engine APIs, mandatory limits, poisoned-state handling, no guest Drop code In-process engine and allocator remain trusted

title: zplugin 0.2.0 交付报告
body: 原生插件 ABI、动态库加载与可选 Wasm 沙箱。 zplugin 0.2.0 交付报告 日期：2026-11-13，Asia/Taipei。 本轮范围 zplugin 0.2.0 与 zplugin-macros 0.2.0 已正式发布到 crates.io，并完成公开包的独立安装验收。 本轮新增跨库异步任务、C/C++/Zig 接口生成，以及稳定结构体、枚举、拥有型资源和回调。 最终提交通过全部三平台门禁，tag、Release 和两个公开包使用同一已验证版本。 核心仍是默认 no_std、无需分配器、零第三方运行时依赖的原子化库，不包含执行器、 插件市场、目录监听器或业务框架。 能力 已交付实现 明确边界 跨库异步 OwnedTask<T>、Task<T>、poll/cancel/release、可 retain 的线程安全 waker，宿主可 .await T: AbiValue；不传递原生 Future/Waker 布局，不安装异步运行时 跨语言生成 共享 Rust trait 生成完整 C 头文件、布局、方法签名与描述符初始化器；Zig 翻译该头文件 同一目标平台 C ABI；不是跨平台通用二进制 稳定值 #[abi_type] 结构体、嵌套结构体、无载荷及带载荷枚举，完整递归 schema 检查 首版不接受泛型、引用、数组、拥有型容器、bool/char/usize/isize/128 位字段 拥有型资源 OwnedResource、宿主 Resource、资源 ID/版本、原库释放函数和独立存活凭据 应用定义操作码及缓冲协议；不跨边界传 Rust 分配器或 trait object 反向回调 Callback/CallbackRef、显式 retain/release、重入检查和 panic 污染状态 普通回调限创建线程；只有 waker 的通知操作允许跨线程 旧入口 zplugin_entry_v1、既有同步描述符和方法签名未改变。扩展表使用独立的长度与 版本前缀；应用新增方法仍应升级业务接口版本，不能偷偷改变已冻结的函数表。 使用与复现 安装时按需要显式启用功能： cargo add zplugin@0.2.0 --features std,macros,hot-reload 只需要协议或手工句柄时，可以关闭所有默认功能；alloc 提供 Rust future、闭包回调、 拥有型资源等便利适配，std 额外支持可展开 panic 的捕获。过程宏的 syn、quote、 proc-macro2 及其传递依赖只用于编译，不是运行时依赖。 完整独立项目与构建步骤： Rust 异步共享接口、插件和宿主。 C/C++/Zig 插件和 Rust 宿主。 扩展 ABI、所有权、线程和取消协议。 python3 scripts/check.py python3 scripts/check.py --cross-version python3 scripts/legacy.py python3 scripts/foreign.py --install-zig python3 tools/bench/run.py docs/benchmarks/v0.2.0 python3 tools/bench/extensions.py 测试证据 本地使用 Rust 1.100.0 和 MSRV 1.85.0；edition 为 2024。1.100.0 已核对 Rust 官方发布记录。 两版本均通过完整本地检查，新增基准也通过两个版本的 Clippy；最终 Python 套件为 23 项。 验证项 结果及覆盖 运行时/契约测试 45 项通过，覆盖所有权、错误输出、描述符长度、重入、panic、waker 失败和资源清理 宏单元测试 7 项通过 文档测试 3 项通过；3 个依赖独立共享 crate 的片段由完整示例工程覆盖 core-only 测试 9 项通过；不与全功能测试重复相加宣传总量 编译失败诊断 36 个案例通过，包括不支持的签名、生命周期与 Send/Sync 限制 feature 组合 8 种显式组合通过 同步动态库 8 组真实动态库契约，另有示例自检 异步动态库 10 组契约，包含工作线程唤醒、取消、析构、旧新代并存和 32 轮唤醒/取消竞态 独立 Rust 编译 同步和异步宿主/插件分别使用 1.85.0 与 1.100.0，覆盖四种组合与 debug/release 旧版兼容 对固定 v0.1.0 源码进行旧宿主/新插件、新宿主/旧插件双向真实加载 Python 验证/发布工具 23 项通过，覆盖版本计算、候选一致性、发布恢复、UTF-8、超时及平台链接命令 打包 本地两 crate 联合打包、解包编译及 publish dry-run 通过；正式候选由发布门禁重新验证 嵌入式 thumbv7em-none-eabi 和 wasm32-unknown-unknown 检查的是无分配器协议的 编译能力，不代表这些目标可以加载本机 .so、.dylib 或 .dll。 最终候选的完整三平台门禁已全部通过： Release 工作流 43376384241 共 7 个验证作业，连同计划和发布作业共 9 项成功。 实际执行 target Rust 1.85.0 Rust 1.100.0 C11/C++17/Zig 原生库 x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu 通过 通过 三个 .so 通过，Zig 0.17.1 aarch64-apple-darwin 通过 通过 三个 .dylib 通过，Zig 0.15.2 x86_64-pc-windows-msvc 通过 通过 三个 .dll 通过，Zig 0.17.1 原生 CI 机器分别是 Linux/glibc 2.43、macOS 26.7.2 arm64、Windows Server 2025。 C/C++ 编译器分别为 GCC 15.2.0、Apple Clang 21.0.0、Zig Clang 22.1.8。 跨语言测试分别耗时 70.36、41.50、202.03 秒，包含工具准备、编译与实际加载，不是调用性能数字。 原始机器记录和校验值保存在 机器可读验收证据。 实测性能 所有数字来自 Linux x86-64、AMD EPYC 9V74、Rust 1.100.0、release/thin LTO 的三次独立进程。 下表是三次运行中位数的中位数；普通 p50/p95/p99 是批次平均耗时的分位数，不是单次请求 的尾延迟。同步基准与异步基准没有并行运行，也没有与本任务编译任务重叠。 操作 实测中位数 Rust 堆分配 同步完整代理，标量 3.474 ns/次 0 同步代理，64 B 13.370 ns/次 0 同步代理，4 KiB 174.716 ns/次 0 同步代理，1 MiB 38.279 µs/次 0 异步缓存 C poll 12.216 ns/次 0 异步完整代理 poll，复用 C waker 14.018 ns/次 0 Rust Future poll，复用执行器 waker 14.740 ns/次 0 Ready 任务创建/销毁 20.741 ns/次 1 次，56 B 每轮更换 C waker 45.153 ns/次 1 次，40 B 每轮更换 Rust waker 73.983 ns/次 2 次，80 B 加载、绑定、创建、切代、回收 26.386 µs/次 3 次宿主分配；不含独立插件计数 异步代理在相同 C waker 和生命周期语义下比缓存 C poll 多 1.802 ns/次。工作线程 创建/取消/join/释放的三次 p50 为 8.478–14.242 µs；这些结果受调度影响，不构成取消时限。 异步测量每行净存活字节增量为零，结束时插件计数字节归零，并验证协作式关闭成功。 创建、首次桥接和更换 waker 会分配，不能把“稳定 poll 为零分配”扩展成“所有异步操作零分配”。 计数器不覆盖系统加载器或 OS 线程内部的分配。4 KiB/1 MiB 的运行间波动明显，不据此宣称 比所有缓存函数指针或 libloading 普遍更快。 完整性能报告 包含全部对照、分配/内存、加载、绑定、创建/销毁、热切换、延迟测量方法和六份原始 CSV。 测量在版本号递增前完成；最终发布仅做版本同步，运行时及示例的功能源码没有另行替换。 安全与支持边界 加载本机代码仍是明确的 unsafe/信任边界。ABI 检查发现不兼容，不隔离恶意代码、 内存破坏、panic=abort 或本机崩溃。插件自己负责网络、文件、运行时、线程及业务状态。 普通代理、任务的 poll/cancel/drop、资源和一般回调均采用创建线程模型，不声明 Send/Sync。 waker retain/wake/release 可以跨线程。异步任务必须拥有调用结束后仍需要的数据，不能把 调用期借用保存到 future。异步结果目前限 AbiValue，不直接返回拥有型缓冲或资源。 默认固定驻留最保守。物理卸载依赖显式的协作式安全承诺：必须释放对象、资源、任务和回调， 并等待所有工作线程、注册项以及最后一次回调/析构的返回路径退出。示例通过 join 实现； 不能因为引用计数为零就假定任意外部执行器已经停机。清理失败时保留库，不用超时强制卸载。 C/C++/Zig 示例使用平台系统 ABI。Zig 验证固定 Linux/Windows 0.17.1、macOS 0.15.2； macOS 由 Zig 生成 PIC 对象，再由当前 Apple SDK 的 C 驱动链接。测试某一系统版本不代表 已验证所有更旧系统，交付插件必须遵守自己的目标架构、部署版本和系统库要求。 发布与归档 发布时间为 2026-11-13 14:13:05（Asia/Taipei）。 项目 结果 已验证版本提交 9870ed1873019063b61fdfb3bb2bd9a5ecb858ad Tag v0.2.0 GitHub Release zplugin 0.2.0 运行时 crate zplugin 0.2.0 编译期宏 crate zplugin-macros 0.2.0 registry 返回的版本均未撤回，下载包与发布记录的 SHA-256 一致： 包 SHA-256 zplugin 2376c2084d78c80311487ea9658db1e5d999a05374264318f9869ae56725d14e zplugin-macros 8b38bdcb1dc20733d9f4ea369fa45cd8576d3bf7bfc03bb48d34068880904a99 发布由同一工作流完成版本校验、工作区和内部依赖同步、最终候选验证、原子提交/tag 推送、 依赖顺序上传、registry 可见性等待与校验、GitHub Release 创建。CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN 只注入上传步骤；保留 patch/minor/major/custom、dry_run、互斥及部分发布恢复。 本轮已分阶段推送，主要实现记录为： abf2511：任务、稳定值、资源和回调协议。 290ab2e：Rust 异步及 C/C++/Zig 示例、独立版本兼容和跨平台测试。 577e631：分配计数任务基准、三次实测原始数据和性能报告。 1601d41：macOS 原生链接链路及对应回归测试。 发布后的 registry-only 独立共享接口/插件/宿主工程也已通过。它从 crates.io 下载两个 0.2.0 包，确认 Cargo source 为 registry、两个校验值匹配，并通过 release 构建、fmt、 Clippy 和 8 组动态调用。覆盖嵌套结构体、载荷枚举、异步 Pending/wake/Ready、取消、 保留回调、资源超出代理生命周期存活、恰好一次释放和最后一个库存活凭据退出。 没有使用本地 zplugin 路径覆盖来代替公开包。 云盘归档：zplugin-0.2.0-delivery-2026-11-13。 归档包含本报告、性能报告、ABI/扩展协议、六份原始 CSV、机器可读 CI 证据，以及独立 公开包消费工程和验收记录。GitHub 保存源码和报告，云盘提供交付副本。 结论与证据自检 功能贡献：提供稳定边界与生命周期原语，不包装成完整异步框架。 表达清晰：接口、ABI、crate 和业务版本分开；借用、拥有、通知和执行分开。 实验强度：保留静态/缓存 C/libloading 对照，初始化与稳定调用分测，公开不利波动。 验证范围：真实原生库、跨 Rust 版本、错误与资源退出路径均有可执行测试；最终原生矩阵和公开包安装均已通过。 设计正确性：不承诺自动关闭任意执行器、强制卸载、不可信代码隔离或未测平台性能。 文档依据 Research-Paper-Writing-Skills 的结论—证据对应原则整理：实现、实测和支持边界 分别陈述；未经执行的能力不记为通过。

title: Performance evidence
body: 原生插件 ABI、动态库加载与可选 Wasm 沙箱。 Performance evidence Measured on 2026-11-12T01:55:00+08:00 (Asia/Taipei), Linux x86-64. This report records actual runs of the included benchmark; macOS and Windows performance remains unmeasured. Result The full typed proxy completed the scalar fixture in 3.644 ns/call, using the median of three run medians. This is approximately 274.4 million calls/second for this tiny workload. The equivalent libloading baseline measured 3.665 ns/call. Their difference is small relative to shared-machine variation. These results support low dispatch overhead, without a general speedup claim over cached function pointers or libloading. Every measured borrowed scalar/byte call recorded zero host and plugin Rust heap allocations. Creating an example object allocated 16 bytes in the plugin; ordinary calls then reused that object, its cached methods and caller buffers. Reproduce From the repository root with the pinned toolchain installed: python3 tools/bench/run.py The runner builds demo-plugin and zplugin-bench in artifacts/benchmark-target, with --release --locked and the plugin's instrument feature. It writes three raw CSV files under docs/benchmarks. An optional first argument selects a different output directory. On Linux it pins the process to the first CPU in its permitted affinity set. The three fresh processes rotate the order of the six dispatch baselines by 0, 2 and 4 positions. Recorded machine: AMD EPYC 9V74 80-Core Processor, pinned CPU 0, a shared execution environment. Compiler: rustc 1.99.1 (58cf8f9c3 2026-10-13), LLVM 23.1.1, target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu. Build: opt-level=3, lto=thin, codegen-units=1, panic=unwind, no additional RUSTFLAGS. The runtime has std, macros and hot-reload; libloading 0.8.9 belongs only to the unpublished benchmark package. Dispatch and buffer processing Each cell is the median of three independent run medians. Scalar, 64 B and 4 KiB columns use nanoseconds; the 1 MiB column uses microseconds. The byte operation uppercases ASCII into a reused caller-owned output buffer. Path Scalar ns ↓ 64 B ns ↓ 4 KiB ns ↓ 1 MiB µs ↓ static-inline 1.354 3.733 159.725 38.607 static-noinline 1.635 3.929 160.989 38.678 cached-extern-C 2.508 5.755 158.503 39.003 cached-generated-adapter 3.789 13.211 163.718 38.089 libloading-cached 3.665 13.280 167.496 38.023 zplugin-proxy 3.644 13.523 169.580 37.770 The scalar proxy run medians ranged 3.418–3.657 ns. For the proxy's larger transfers they ranged 13.194–13.642 ns (64 B), 167.324–170.772 ns (4 KiB), and 31.980–38.917 µs (1 MiB). The large-transfer variation is material; the raw runs are preserved without discarding the slower result. All six paths execute the same arithmetic or byte transformation and update a per-object call counter. Static inline, static noinline and the thin C function pointer are lower-bound controls: they omit plugin validation, panic containment and instance guards. The cached-generated-adapter, libloading and typed-proxy paths use the same generated adapter, plugin object contract, creating thread and live library ownership. The libloading control resolves an exported function-pointer data symbol once; it never performs symbol lookup in the timed loop. All foreign-call controls rebuild the same repr(C) argument record on every call, matching the proxy's packing work. black_box protects inputs, results and buffers from dead-code elimination. The fixture's final call counter and transformed output are also consumed. The generated proxy methods have #[inline], exposing small packing/status wrappers to downstream optimization. Method pointers are cached at binding; individual calls perform no registry lookup, lock, serialization or reference count clone. This design is visible in the generated code and supported by the allocation measurements; no numerical improvement is attributed to a single optimization without an isolated experiment. Loading, lifetimes and switching These figures use nanoseconds per operation. The range covers the three run medians. Rust allocation counts cover host and plugin for object/buffer rows; load and hot-switch rows count host Rust allocations only. Operation Median ns ↓ Run-median range ns Allocations/op lifecycle/remap-load-drop 35188.150 34675.280–35429.500 2 lifecycle/warm-load-drop 3099.050 3069.410–5087.140 2 lifecycle/core-warm-load-drop 163.340 161.940–209.610 0 lifecycle/interface-bind 29.832 29.536–30.039 0 lifecycle/create-drop 17.759 17.424–17.864 1 lifecycle/owned-64B-create-release 43.189 42.754–44.314 1 hot/request-lease 0.706 0.706–0.706 0 hot/session-reused-call 3.469 3.466–3.592 0 hot/switch-load-bind-create-collect 29318.050 27065.650–29761.700 3 remap-load-drop closes the only live handle each iteration, then loads again; filesystem page caches are warm. warm-load-drop retains another handle, so it measures acquiring/releasing an already mapped image plus the std path helper. core-warm-load-drop reuses a NUL-terminated path and calls the no-allocator loader. The std helper canonicalizes a path, which explains its two host allocations. No cold-storage claim follows from these measurements. create-drop includes both construction and destruction. The 64 B owned-return row includes plugin allocation, copying the requested data, host wrapping and release in the originating plugin. Instrumentation uses counting allocators, which add atomic operations to allocation/free paths and can change their absolute timings. OS loader allocations made inside libc are outside these Rust allocator counters. The hot-switch measurement uses two independent copied library files and a resident-old-generation limit of two. Each iteration loads, validates, constructs a new typed instance, commits the new generation, drops the instance and collects the old image. File copying happens before timing. A request lease is acquired once; the reused-session-call row then makes repeated calls without cloning that lease. Hot rows count host allocations because every copied image owns a separate, independently retired plugin allocator. Latency distribution Ordinary rows contain 41 samples of batches: scalar 200,000 calls, 64 B 100,000, 4 KiB 4,000, 1 MiB 16, bind/create/owned-release 10,000, load 100, and full switch 20 operations per sample. CSV p50/p95/p99 values for those rows are quantiles of batch means, not individual request latencies. Up to 1,024 operations warm each row before timing. A separate 20,001-sample, one-call measurement records individual elapsed times. The timer floor is shown alongside it; these values include timer overhead. Run Timer-floor p50 ns Proxy p50 ns Proxy p95 ns Proxy p99 ns Proxy max ns 1 20.000 21.000 30.000 31.000 431.000 2 20.000 21.000 30.000 31.000 143976.000 3 20.000 21.000 30.000 31.000 320.000 The timer floor is much larger than the batched scalar call time. Use batched results for dispatch cost and the raw latency distribution to observe scheduling and timer effects. Do not subtract medians to manufacture per-call tail latency. Memory On this build, Plugin occupies 32 stack bytes, Binding 64, Instance 72, and the eight-method DemoProxy 136. These are Rust-side observations for this feature/target combination, not frozen C ABI sizes. Borrowed instance creation adds zero host heap bytes and requests 16 plugin heap bytes. The 1,024-instance experiment requests exactly 16,384 plugin bytes, then returns to its prior plugin live-byte count after destruction; the host vector's preallocated storage is excluded from that delta. These counts exclude the system allocator's own bookkeeping and reserved arena capacity. The three process-first loads took 107.081, 644.143, 250.086 µs, and increased Linux RSS by 208, 224, 228 KiB. RSS includes code/data pages and loader/runtime effects. It is coarser than the allocator counts and depends on OS paging. Repeated data-buffer calls allocate neither boundary buffers nor serialization storage. Evidence and review Raw data: run 1, run 2, run 3. Measurement implementation: benchmark, runner, plugin allocator. Claim Evidence Status Borrowed calls force no Rust heap allocations Both allocators record zero across all scalar/byte rows Measured on Linux Full proxy has low dispatch overhead Three scalar medians and equivalent cached adapter controls Measured for this workload Plugin resources are released in their origin Owning buffer release row, object byte accounting, integration tests Implemented and exercised Request leases avoid per-call reference counting Reused-session benchmark and proxy implementation Implemented and measured Performance generalizes to other CPUs and OSes No measurements here Future measurement Review: the contribution is typed ABI/lifetime management with small measured cost; terminology and units are explicit; all reported numbers map to raw data; controls cover dispatch, buffers, allocation, memory, loading and hot switching; the shared-machine variance and narrower semantics of thin controls remain visible. No asynchronous workload or cross-platform performance result is claimed.

title: 概览
body: 管理原生 PTY、ConPTY 与所属子进程。 zpty Independent Project Z PTY library. Version 0.2.2 separates repository and package metadata; the five production Rust files are byte-for-byte identical to ztty source f2db31d7ea35bf1a0554e76d69d2e44faafd0cab. See SOURCE.json. The 0.2.1 API is unchanged. Native pseudo-terminal ownership for Rust programs that do not link the Rust standard library. zpty uses core and alloc, has no Cargo dependencies, and exposes bounded, nonblocking reads and writes with explicit child-process ownership. Version 0.2 adds macOS PTYs and a Windows ConPTY implementation. The caller owns terminal emulation, rendering, executable lookup, environment policy, and its event loop. The operating-system APIs differ, so the constructors and readiness handles make those differences explicit. Platform Session API Readiness System boundary Linux unsafe Pty::spawn Pty::fd() for poll/epoll C runtime and libutil macOS Pty::spawn_with_helper; legacy unsafe Pty::spawn Pty::fd() for poll/kqueue Darwin C runtime Windows 10 build 17763+ Pty::spawn_utf16 output_event() and process_event() for native wait sets ConPTY and Win32 worker threads macOS hosts with active threads Use Pty::spawn_with_helper when the host may already have threads, including AppKit workers. The executable must call run_spawn_helper before configuration, cwd changes, UI initialization or starting its own threads. Ordinary launches return immediately from that entry; a helper launch configures the terminal and replaces itself with the requested program. # #[cfg(target_os = "macos")] { use std::ffi::{CStr, CString}; use std::os::unix::ffi::OsStrExt; use zpty::{Pty, Size}; // At executable entry, before host initialization: let owned: Vec<CString> = std::env::args_os() .map(|argument| CString::new(argument.as_bytes()).unwrap()) .collect(); let arguments: Vec<&CStr> = owned.iter().map(CString::as_c_str).collect(); zpty::run_spawn_helper(&arguments); // This operation can also run later, after host worker threads have started. let helper = zpty::current_executable().unwrap(); let pty = Pty::spawn_with_helper( &helper, c"/bin/sh", &[c"sh", c"-c", c"printf hello"], &[c"PATH=/usr/bin:/bin", c"TERM=xterm-256color"], Size::new(80, 24), ).unwrap(); // Register pty.fd() with the host's native event loop. # } current_executable uses the kernel-reported absolute executable path, independent of argv[0] or cwd. Darwin's posix_spawn starts a fresh image with a new session; the helper establishes its controlling terminal, foreground group and initial dimensions before executing the target. Arguments and the complete environment retain their original bytes. A successful helper becomes the target with the same child PID. The parent receives real spawn, terminal-setup and exec errors through a private close-on-exec pipe. A fixed ready frame must arrive before EOF is accepted as exec handoff. The handshake has a five-second deadline after posix_spawn returns; failure closes the descriptors and cleans up only the directly owned child. Kernel creation and kill/reap completion are not hard-real-time bounded. The caller must retain exclusive child-reaping ownership and must not enable automatic SIGCHLD reaping. All private descriptors are moved above fd 2 before standard-stream file actions. POSIX_SPAWN_CLOEXEC_DEFAULT excludes unrelated and concurrent-spawn descriptors. Darwin's pipe followed by fcntl has a short close-on-exec setup gap; unrelated foreign fork/exec code must manage its own inheritance policy. This guarantee is specific to the new API and does not change the unsafe legacy constructor's contract. The native cargo test --locked -p zpty --test darwin_spawn gate checks Apple SDK ABI declarations, active worker threads, concurrent spawns, controlling-terminal semantics, exact argv/environment, dimensions, descriptor inheritance, errors, timeout, reaping and all seven initially closed-stdio combinations. It requires real macOS; cross-target checks and the non-macOS skip are not native acceptance. Legacy fork-based Linux and macOS constructor Supply a resolved executable path, argv including argv[0], a complete environment, and descriptors that must be closed in the child. Argument pointer arrays are prepared before the fork. After forkpty returns, the child uses only close, execve, write, and _exit; it does not allocate Rust memory or search PATH. # #[cfg(unix)] { use zpty::{Pty, Size}; // Run before other process threads are started. Read the full safety contract // on Pty::spawn before embedding this operation in a multithreaded host. let pty = unsafe { Pty::spawn( c"/bin/sh", &[c"sh", c"-c", c"printf hello"], &[c"PATH=/usr/bin:/bin", c"TERM=xterm-256color"], Size::new(80, 24), &[], ) }.unwrap(); pty.resize(Size::new(100, 30)).unwrap(); // Register pty.fd() with the host's native event loop. # } forkpty itself is not specified as async-signal-safe. The unsafe constructor therefore has a process-wide safety contract: callers must establish that forking is safe for their host, C runtime, allocators, and signal handlers. A host that cannot establish this contract needs a separate process launcher. An execve failure appears as child exit code 127. The returned master has O_NONBLOCK and FD_CLOEXEC. A closed slave produces a zero-length read; Linux's slave-hangup EIO is normalized to EOF. Unix Drop closes the master, sends SIGHUP to the child session if still live, and attempts a nonblocking reap. It does not force-kill jobs that ignore hangup or wait indefinitely for them. Windows spawn_utf16 accepts a resolved executable path, argv including argv[0], an optional Windows environment block, and character dimensions. Argument strings exclude their NUL terminator. The library builds a mutable command line using Windows CRT escaping rules and rejects commands exceeding 32767 UTF-16 units. None inherits the environment; a supplied block must be sorted case-insensitively and end with two NUL units. # #[cfg(windows)] { use zpty::{Pty, Size}; // Replace this with the host's resolved executable path; do not assume every // Windows installation uses C:\Windows. let program: Vec<u16> = r"C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe".encode_utf16().collect(); let option: Vec<u16> = "/D".encode_utf16().collect(); let pty = Pty::spawn_utf16( &program, &[&program, &option], None, Size::new(80, 24), ).unwrap(); pty.resize(Size::new(100, 30)).unwrap(); // Wait on pty.output_event() and pty.process_event() in the native event loop. // Handles are borrowed; callers must not close them. # } ConPTY requires synchronous pipe endpoints. Two native workers service these pipes so the public read and write methods do not block the UI on pipe I/O. Each direction has a queue capped at 1 MiB, plus a 16 KiB worker buffer. Queue storage grows on demand. This bound describes the library's queues, not the memory used by Windows, OpenConsole, or the child application. The output readiness event is manual-reset. Drain read until is_would_block() before waiting again. write accepts only the prefix that fits; callers retain and retry the suffix. process_event is signaled when the directly owned child exits. reap, wait, and wait_timeout query that child's handle and cannot consume an unrelated process's status. Windows hangup closes the pseudoconsole and its attached console processes. The reader keeps draining the final console output during this operation, including when its public output queue was full. Windows Drop then cancels outstanding worker I/O, joins the workers, and closes their handles. This teardown can block while Windows closes the console; it has different lifetime semantics from the nonblocking Unix destructor. Microsoft's pseudoconsole session guide explains the underlying pipe-drain requirement. Optional official ConPTY redistribution The library prefers an adjacent conpty.dll and OpenConsole.exe pair supplied by the application. It obtains the executable's absolute directory and loads the DLL with LOAD_LIBRARY_SEARCH_DLL_LOAD_DIR | LOAD_LIBRARY_SEARCH_SYSTEM32; it does not search PATH or the current working directory. If the pair is absent or cannot provide the required exports, the library uses the inbox Windows API. uses_bundled_conpty() reports which backend the session selected. The ztty repository's tools/package_windows.py packages the executable with Microsoft's 1.25.261109001 ConPTY redistribution, pinned to an exact package SHA-256, and includes its MIT license and a file-hash manifest. The official package supports Windows build 17763 and later. Microsoft describes the redistribution model in terminal discussion 17608. ConPTY version affects escape-sequence transport. A successfully linked Windows executable alone does not establish Kitty Graphics compatibility, cursor behavior, or native rendering correctness. Run the native acceptance test against the actual packaged pair; no behavior is inferred from an undocumented passthrough flag. I/O and validation On every platform, a successful write may accept fewer bytes than supplied. Preserve the unwritten suffix, and use is_would_block() to distinguish a temporarily full channel from a permanent error. wait deliberately blocks; use reap or wait_timeout when the caller needs a bound on child-status collection. cargo run -p zpty --example capture The example selects /bin/sh on Unix and native PowerShell on Windows. It verifies round-trip text, the resized 100-column by 30-row console, successful child exit, and a separately owned process exiting with code 7. Its timeout and printing harness uses std; the library remains #![no_std]. The capture example validates PTY I/O, dimensions and owned-child status. Terminal emulation, native-window pixels and application packaging remain consumer responsibilities. Library build checks do not establish those application behaviors. Independent candidate validation Run python3 scripts/check.py from this repository. It preserves the existing unit tests, documentation tests, capture example and native Darwin fixture; it adds no new PTY behavior tests. A platform with zero unit or documentation tests reports zero. Darwin runtime acceptance runs only on macOS. The library supports Linux/macOS/Windows, so a bare-metal no_std target is not claimed. The validation workflow is manual/reusable and requires a full commit SHA. Pushes do not start CI. The separate Release workflow selects or resumes an immutable candidate, waits for all three native-platform gates, then publishes that same crate. Publication requires credentials supplied by the repository owner; candidate validation does not.

title: 概览
body: 组合编辑器与终端工具的原生配置，供 zdot 预览和部署。 zrc A small configuration framework for oh-my-ztty. One warm palette, native application settings, and one reviewable zdot deployment. zrc gives Neovim a complete editing environment and applies the same Ink colors to terminals and command-line tools. Applications read their own configuration formats. There is no configuration daemon, startup download, or additional plugin manager. Install and compose cargo install zrc --version 0.1.2 --locked zrc --list zrc --list --json zrc --modules nvim,fzf,bat,ripgrep,git,shell --output /path/to/new-profile The parent directory must already exist, and the output directory must be new. The installed Rust executable contains all reviewed configuration assets, including hidden .config directories. It can compose from any working directory without Python, a source checkout, or a network connection. Installing the crate does not deploy configuration or install the applications listed below. For a source checkout, cargo install --path . --locked builds the same executable. Cargo needs Rust 1.100 or newer. The Python entry remains available as python3 scripts/compose.py with the same selection and output arguments. Modules Module Configuration Neovim 0.11+ Ink colors, welcome page, native fuzzy picker, status line, search, LSP, local extensions Kitty, Foot, Ghostty Warm palette, spacing and cursor tmux Compact status line and low-contrast dividers fzf Matching native finder colors bat ANSI theme that inherits the terminal palette ripgrep Smart-case search and warm match colors Git Display-only include, with no identity or signing settings Shell Builtin environment assignments for editor and tool defaults registry.json is the module catalog. profiles/ink/profile.zdot is the complete static profile. Choose a subset by composing a new profile directory: zrc --modules nvim,fzf,bat,ripgrep,git,shell \ --output /path/to/new-profile zdot plan --root /path/to/new-profile --target "$HOME" --json zdot apply --root /path/to/new-profile --target "$HOME" --backup Review the plan before deployment. --backup lets zdot preserve replaced settings. Use zdot remove with the same root to restore them. Compose into a new, stable directory: moving a deployed profile breaks its links. The native CLI composes profiles without an interpreter. Python is needed only for the optional source entry and development checks. Neither entry is part of shell or editor startup. zdot owns deployment, backup and rollback; zrc does not duplicate those mechanisms. Neovim Open Neovim with no file to see the welcome page. Space is the leader key. Keys Action Space f f Find files with a native floating fuzzy picker Space f g Search project text and open quickfix results Space f r Recent files Space b b Open buffers Space e Native file explorer Space w Save Space c a / c r / c f Code action / rename / format Space d Line diagnostics Space a c Show local editor context as JSON Space a s Start ssmcp explicitly in a terminal split Space ? Search the shortcut list Ctrl-Space Native completion The picker starts one ripgrep process when opened, then filters in memory. It does not run a new process for each keystroke. File results are bounded to 4,000 entries and 512 KiB; text search uses a 2 MiB output bound and 1,000 quickfix entries. Truncated results are labelled. Each search has a five-second deadline. Searches use the current project and respect ignore files; no indexer runs at startup. When started from the home or filesystem root, the finder asks for a project directory before scanning. LSP starts when a matching file is opened in a recognized project and its language server is already installed. Rust, C/C++, Go, Python, Lua, shell, JavaScript and TypeScript have native adapters. Existing executables in Neovim's stdpath("data")/mason/bin are reused when absent from PATH. zrc does not install servers or launch one for a loose file without a project root. :ZrcHealth shows optional executables. Files over 1 MiB enter large-file mode before reading: persistent undo, syntax highlighting, Treesitter and LSP are skipped for that buffer. Buffers over 20,000 lines also skip highlighting after reading. Swap-file recovery stays at Neovim's normal setting. These limits can be adjusted. Local extensions Put local settings in ~/.config/zrc/nvim.lua, outside the managed Neovim directory: return { large_file_bytes = 2 * 1024 * 1024, max_files = 4000, lsp = true, extensions = { { event = "InsertEnter", setup = function() -- Use an already installed optional native package. -- vim.cmd.packadd("my-local-package") end, }, }, } An extension may specify event, pattern, once and setup. Its setup runs through pcall, so one failing extension does not abort editor startup. Use Neovim's native packages for local plugins; no registry or lockfile is downloaded. :ZrcContext displays only the current file path, cursor, file type, working directory, modified flag and diagnostic counts. It does not send anything or read buffer contents. :ZrcConnect starts the already installed ssmcp only when invoked. Activating optional tools The suite sources ~/.config/zrc/shell.zsh for fzf, bat, ripgrep and editor defaults. Standalone users can source that file from their interactive zsh configuration. Git's module is an include file. Add its path once after reviewing existing includes: git config --global --add include.path ~/.config/zrc/git.inc It changes color output only. Existing identity, credentials, signing, transport, hooks and repositories are not copied into zrc. The tmux profile is ready for tmux when installed; composition never installs packages. Extension contract The registry schema defines module IDs, required executables, optional activation guidance and source-to-destination mappings. Source paths are repository-relative; destinations are target-relative. Modules must own disjoint destinations. The crate build rejects source symlinks and special files before embedding assets; the Python entry checks sources when composing. Registry validation rejects path traversal and overlapping destinations. Both entries reject unknown modules, existing outputs (including dangling links), missing parents and symlink parents. Repeated module names keep their first position. Composition finishes in a staging directory beside the output, then renames it into place. The result contains files/, profile.zdot and zrc-profile.json for one zdot deployment. Add native configuration under profiles/ink/files, register disjoint destinations, update the static profile, and validate the application parser before publishing. No application binary, personal configuration, secret, or device identifier belongs in this repository. Local verification python3 scripts/check.py python3 scripts/check_cargo.py --package python3 scripts/benchmark.py --runs 30 Checks use isolated XDG directories. They exercise profile safety, Neovim's palette, picker, welcome page, large-file behavior and LSP selection, plus configuration parsers for installed applications. Missing optional application validators are separate from successful checks. The Cargo gate checks formatting, strict Clippy and Rust tests; compares every module and generated metadata against Python; verifies crate asset inclusion; and installs the extracted crate offline into a temporary directory. It runs that installed binary outside the checkout with an empty PATH. It also checks preserved existing outputs, unknown modules, parent-directory rules and argument errors. Development and release scripts use Python 3.11 or newer. Measurements record commands, versions and limitations. They describe a particular machine and workload; zrc makes no unmeasured ranking claim against other configurations. References Neovim LSP and Lua API Kitty configuration Ghostty configuration zdot design and recovery MIT license. Library The crate exposes zrc::registry() for validated module metadata and zrc::compose(&["nvim", "git"], output) for the same staging and output rules as the CLI. JSON parsing and string escaping use the published Project Z library zconv. Configuration bytes stay embedded in the crate; neither API deploys to HOME or invokes an external program. Releasing python3 scripts/bump.py patch updates VERSION, registry.json, Cargo.toml and the zrc entry in Cargo.lock together. --publish runs the local Python and Cargo checks, then commits, tags and atomically pushes from main. A tag starts the existing archive-and-checksum workflow; ordinary pushes do not start CI. Crates.io publication is a separate, explicit local step using the maintainer's existing Cargo login. Release instructions cover the exact-commit dry run, full package/install gate, publication and registry verification. A GitHub archive alone is not evidence that cargo install zrc is available.

title: Local measurements
body: 组合编辑器与终端工具的原生配置，供 zdot 预览和部署。 Local measurements Measured on 2026-11-20 (Asia/Taipei), x86_64, Neovim 0.12.6. Source data: benchmark-2026-11-20.json. Case Median p95 Neovim without configuration 5.863 ms 16.707 ms zrc welcome page 11.600 ms 34.912 ms zrc opening a small Lua file 22.402 ms 78.471 ms Each case ran 30 times after two warmups, interleaved to reduce drift from other development processes. Measurements are end-to-end process wall time in isolated XDG directories, ending after the VimEnter handlers and welcome page completed. Filesystem caches were warm. The source-file case had no language server. The welcome page adds about 5.7 ms to the empty baseline on this machine. Lua file startup also includes Neovim's native filetype and syntax work. Tail latency was variable on the shared development machine. These data do not establish a cross-machine ranking, cold-start performance or interactive rendering speed. Peak RSS was not collected in this initial record because the system time executable was absent. Validation Six profile tests cover composition, existing-output preservation, invalid modules, path validation, symlink rejection and overlapping destinations. Native Neovim checks exercise Lua loading, palette, local-only context, lazy LSP, picker filtering and selection, welcome-window lifecycle, large-file mode and reuse of installed Mason language servers. Real asynchronous ripgrep is checked for filenames with spaces, ignored .git paths and exact match coordinates; a home-directory search is verified to request a project before starting any process. Kitty, Foot 1.28, Ghostty, fzf, bat, ripgrep, Git and zsh configurations passed their installed parsers or execution checks. tmux was not installed and is listed as an unvalidated optional profile on this machine. Review of claims Contribution: native configurations share a palette and one zdot profile; registry and composition tests demonstrate this. Clarity: installation, activation and recovery are separate operations. Evidence: startup claims cite the command, raw results and workload. Completeness: LSP and tmux limitations are explicit; no editor plugin or server downloads are counted as startup. Design: there is no background updater or duplicate deployment engine.

title: 概览
body: 在字节切片中正向或反向查找字节和子串，并返回原始位置。 zscan Byte and substring search with no dependencies, no allocation and an always no_std library. Rust 1.70 or newer; MIT licensed. [dependencies] zscan = "0.1" The API consists of four functions and one borrowed searcher: use zscan::{find, rfind, find_byte, rfind_byte, Finder}; assert_eq!(find_byte(0, b"ab\0cd"), Some(2)); assert_eq!(rfind_byte(b'a', b"aba"), Some(2)); assert_eq!(find(b"ababa", b"aba"), Some(0)); assert_eq!(rfind(b"ababa", b"aba"), Some(2)); let finder = Finder::new(b"aba"); assert_eq!(finder.find(b"xxaba"), Some(2)); assert_eq!(finder.rfind(b"ababa"), Some(2)); All inputs are byte slices, including NUL and invalid UTF-8. Returned positions are byte offsets in the original haystack. An empty needle matches at 0 forwards and haystack.len() backwards. An overlong needle returns None. Complexity and implementation Byte search takes O(n) time. Substring search takes worst-case O(n + m) time and O(1) extra space, where n and m are the haystack and needle lengths. Finder::new takes O(m) time, borrows its needle, and caches fixed-size metadata for both directions. It never copies or reverses the input. A Finder can be shared between threads; searches do not mutate it. Short haystacks avoid preprocessing. Longer searches filter candidate starts using two needle bytes, then verify the full candidate. A failed verification can replace an unhelpful probe with the first mismatching byte. Verification spends a single search-wide budget: initially 2m, replenished only by newly skipped positions, with m charged per candidate. When that budget is exhausted, search falls back once to Two-Way. This bounds verification work by O(n + m), including repeated and periodic data. CPU support and safety Target Generic build x86-64 AVX2 after cached CPUID, OSXSAVE and XCR0 checks; otherwise SWAR AArch64 with target-guaranteed NEON NEON Other targets Portable SWAR/scalar The x86 AVX2 path aligns its byte-scanning bulk loop and uses complete, in-bounds overlapping vectors at the slice boundary. It also uses SSE2 for 16-byte candidate ranges. No vector load crosses either end of a supplied slice; unaligned slices are supported. Safe public functions require no caller feature detection. A build using -C target-cpu=native or explicit target features must run on a compatible CPU and OS, as with any Rust binary built with those flags. No std feature detector, allocation, FFI, build script or third-party dependency is used by the library. Unsafe code is confined to architecture intrinsics and their private checked dispatch; each block records its feature and access preconditions. Linux protection-page tests use libc FFI in the test executable only. Verification cargo test --locked cargo test --release --locked cargo test --doc --locked cargo +1.70.0 test --locked python3 scripts/audit.py python3 scripts/test_backends.py Tests include independent naive references, exhaustive small alphabets, seeded random inputs, every short match position, binary data, offsets, SIMD tails, direct scalar/vector comparisons, and guarded pages. CI runs stable and MSRV on x86-64 and AArch64, fmt/Clippy, native builds, scalar Miri, and bare-metal thumbv7em-none-eabi / aarch64-unknown-none library builds. Benchmarks The isolated comparison project pins memchr 2.8.3 and memx 0.2.2. The fixed protocol includes 607 short, binary, structured-text, alignment, tail, and adversarial workloads. One-shot timing includes preprocessing and dispatch; Finder construction and reuse are measured separately. All measurements are ns/op, including early returns. Raw samples, source snapshots, hashes, build settings and failed comparator answers are retained. See baseline correctness notes. On the recorded Xeon Platinum 8573C / Rust 1.99.1 generic build, the geometric mean speedups against the fastest correct baseline in each case were: Workloads One-shot substring forward One-shot substring reverse Short (238 cases) 1.21x 1.68x Typical binary (195 cases) 1.34x 7.67x HTTP / JSON / logs (48 cases) 1.92x 5.27x The overall 2x research target was not met. Typical byte searches were 0.98x/0.91x the fastest forward/reverse baseline, and some short/reused searches regressed. These repeated-buffer, warm-cache measurements on shared hardware are observations, not a universal performance guarantee. The current full report includes all cases, slower results and native builds. The round-2 review compares the previous implementation with matched memchr controls, explains the warmup-calibration correction, and retains regression investigations. The earlier component ablations remain available with their original source snapshots; they were measured before this revision. Release The Release workflow supports current, patch, minor, major, and custom version selection, plus existing-tag recovery. Use Actions → Release → Run workflow on main, or commit an explicit .github/release-request.json request as described in the maintenance guide. A bump updates the manifest and both lockfiles, then atomically pushes the version commit and its immutable tag. Existing vX.Y.Z tag pushes are also supported. The workflow checks the tag's exact commit through the full CI matrix, verifies the package contents, packages and dry-runs before publishing. Only the publish step receives the repository Secret CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN. An exact crates.io archive checksum must be confirmed before a GitHub Release is created. Ambiguous upload errors are checked against the registry before any manual recovery; an existing version is never overwritten.

title: Baseline versions and correctness
body: 在字节切片中正向或反向查找字节和子串，并返回原始位置。 Baseline versions and correctness Versions were queried from the registry on 2026-11-09, before optimization: Baseline Version Upstream commit Registry checksum memchr 2.8.3 5fdb40c054e1fff359a2f7bdf7f87a13b34b465d cf8baf1c55e62ffcace7a9f06f4bd9cd3f0c4beb022d3b367256b91b87513d98 memx 0.2.2 c52c59209caa169054a4b2f8533d9ad646c59dd4 b34799f4a1d8693a53c36c100211735052ea2193eabdd03c3aa304319a39978c Commits were read from the published crates' .cargo_vcs_info.json. Checksums are also in the independent comparison/Cargo.lock. memchr keeps its default features and runtime SIMD detection; disabling std would weaken the baseline. memx reverse substring mismatch The first correctness smoke run, before optimized zscan measurements, found that memx 0.2.2 can omit the candidate at haystack.len() - needle.len(). Its first-byte reverse path initializes curr_idx to that index but searches the exclusive slice [..curr_idx]. When both slices have the same length, it skips the search entirely. The issue appears in both its scalar and x86 paths. Minimal reproduction with the pinned dependency: let haystack = b"\xffA"; let needle = b"\xffA"; assert_eq!(memchr::memmem::rfind(haystack, needle), Some(0)); assert_eq!(zscan::rfind(haystack, needle), Some(0)); assert_eq!(memx::memrmem(haystack, needle), None); // comparator bug The harness does not patch memx or remove cases. It retains memx/rfind timings and records each result's correct flag, but marks all memx/rfind rows eligible=false so that an incomplete search cannot win a speed comparison. Other memx operations, zscan, and memchr must match independent reference loops or the run stops. The remaining forward and byte memx results provide a second optimized baseline; memchr remains the primary baseline for every API. Source: memx 0.2.2 reverse implementation and scalar implementation.

title: Fixed comparison protocol
body: 在字节切片中正向或反向查找字节和子串，并返回原始位置。 Fixed comparison protocol This plan was written before optimized zscan measurements. The workload generator in src/main.rs fixes the cases, seed, alignments, and lengths; --list prints every case with its content fingerprint and expected answers. Keep failed and slower cases in every report. A timing run may not silently discard a case. Baselines Use crates.io's current stable releases, checked on 2026-11-09: memchr 2.8.3 (upstream commit 5fdb40c054e1fff359a2f7bdf7f87a13b34b465d) and memx 0.2.2 (c52c59209caa169054a4b2f8533d9ad646c59dd4). Commits come from each published crate's .cargo_vcs_info.json; Cargo.lock records package checksums. memchr's default std feature remains enabled to permit its strongest runtime dispatch. memx provides another independently maintained SSE2/AVX2 implementation. Both operate on arbitrary bytes. Independent naive loops are correctness oracles, not timed competitive baselines. Workloads, fixed before tuning Seed: 0x6a09e667f3bcc909, xorshift64 (13, 7, 17). Short: haystack lengths 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 15, 16, 17, 31, 32, 33, 63; needle lengths 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 16, 32. For fitting nonempty needles test first, last, and absent matches; empty and overlong needles are separate cases. Typical: haystack lengths 128, 512, 4,096, 65,536; needle lengths 2, 4, 8, 16, 31, 32, 33, 64, 127, 256 where they fit. Test first, last, absent, dense, and sparse matches. The data between matches uses all byte values except the needle's sentinel, including NUL and invalid UTF-8. Large: 1,048,576-byte haystacks, needle lengths 4, 16, 64; last and absent. Alignment: every actual pointer residue modulo 64, not merely an allocation offset; lengths and needle lengths vary deterministically with the residue. SIMD tails: every tail length modulo 32, with a nonzero pointer residue. Adversarial: all-equal, periodic ab, and a two-byte low-entropy alphabet; matching and near-matching needles of lengths 8, 32, 128, 257 in 65,536-byte haystacks. A near miss changes a middle byte while preserving equal endpoints. The primary short and typical result groups are fixed above. Report each direction separately, and compare each zscan cell with the fastest semantics-equivalent measured competitor in that cell. Report both medians and the distribution of per-case ratios; a geometric mean does not establish that every case is faster. The research target is at least 2x, not a claimed result. What is timed byte_find, byte_rfind, find, and rfind call the public one-shot API inside the timed loop, including that API's preprocessing and dispatch. Arguments and results pass through std::hint::black_box on every iteration. The byte is the first needle byte (255 for an empty needle). reuse_find and reuse_rfind construct each library's borrowed searcher before timing and include its public search method in timing. build_both compares one bidirectional zscan Finder with the pair of memchr Finder and FinderRev needed for the same two directions. No memx reuse rows are fabricated: it exposes only the one-shot operations used here. Construction returns are black-boxed. The timed loop uses statically specialized closures; algorithm selection happens outside that loop. Each cell has warmup and adaptive batching, followed by seven retained raw samples. Engine order rotates between samples. The default target batch time is 100 microseconds; --smoke uses one small batch solely to exercise the harness. Correctness is checked before timing, against independent forward/reverse loops and both baseline libraries. Further fixed-seed differential inputs run first. Only nanoseconds per operation are reported; no unscanned bytes are credited as throughput. The process has steady-state CPU dispatch caches after warmup. One-shot calls still execute each API's dispatch path. --cold is a separate fresh-process, single-call observation, including first-use dispatch; it is noisy and is not used for the 2x target. Configurations and retained evidence Run generic and -C target-cpu=native, then independent generic ablations --cfg zscan_scalar, --cfg zscan_no_short, and --cfg zscan_no_prefilter. These cfgs affect zscan only; the exact RUSTFLAGS are captured for every run. Finder reuse versus one-shot isolates caching. This is an observational suite: shared/cloud hardware is not a release performance gate. run.py saves every CSV row (gzip), cases manifest, compiler/OS/CPU metadata, Cargo metadata and lockfile, compile flags, git commit and worktree state, source SHA-256 hashes, command lines, and stderr. summarize.py derives tables without deleting outliers. Re-run the whole suite on fixed idle hardware before using a timing difference as a product guarantee. Pre-timing addendum: structured text and baseline eligibility Before any full timing run, add a separate text group with HTTP header, JSON, and log-line fragments. Each has 128, 512, 4,096, and 65,536-byte haystacks with first, last, absent, and dense matches, using ASCII needles content-length:, "request_id":", and level=error. These 48 cases supplement all 559 original cases unchanged; they avoid relying only on synthetic sentinel-byte data. The original short/typical groups remain separately visible in every summary. Initial correctness-only smoke detected a memx 0.2.2 reverse substring bug. Retain all memx reverse timing cells and their correctness flags, but mark the entire operation ineligible for performance ratios. This prevents incomplete searches from being counted as fast. See baseline-notes.md for the minimal reproduction and source. No zscan or memchr discrepancy is accepted, and no case is removed or rewritten in response to this finding. Round 2 calibration correction The first round and the first same-session round-2 baseline used one warmup pilot per batch size. A scheduler pause during that pilot could underestimate the necessary iteration count. One observed fast byte search consequently used one iteration per retained sample and reported 73–196 ns, dominated by timer overhead. Those runs remain available as diagnostic evidence. Corrected runs use the minimum of three warmup pilots at each candidate batch size. Only warmup chooses the batch size: all seven actual measurement samples, including slow ones, remain unfiltered. The 607 workloads, random seeds, algorithms, semantics, and sample count are unchanged. The corrected before source is an isolated checkout of fbe6bcb91989e45d4bf6805c6888863c57554cb5 with this same corrected harness; after runs use the identical harness.

title: Independent comparison project
body: 在字节切片中正向或反向查找字节和子串，并返回原始位置。 Independent comparison project This project is excluded from the published crate and has its own workspace, dependencies, and lockfile. Read cases.md for the fixed protocol and baseline-notes.md for a discovered comparator correctness failure. The production crate has no dependency on any of this code. cargo run --release --manifest-path comparison/Cargo.toml --locked -- --smoke python3 comparison/run.py --config generic native scalar no-short no-prefilter --output comparison/results/experiment-1 python3 comparison/summarize.py comparison/results/experiment-1 Run one timing process at a time on an idle machine. run.py refuses to overwrite an existing configuration directory. It preserves raw samples (gzip), every case's fingerprint, exact source snapshot and SHA-256 hashes, compiler and CPU metadata, commands, build logs, and correctness diagnostics. Set CPU affinity outside the script when the machine permits it. Shared CI timings are only observations; the smoke job validates the harness and results, not a speed gate. --list prints the fixed case manifest without timing. --cold OP ENGINE observes the first public call in a fresh process, including CPU initialization; the clock and process startup state make it noisy. Capture seven fresh-process observations for all one-shot functions with: python3 comparison/run.py --mode cold --config generic --output comparison/results/cold-1 python3 comparison/summarize.py comparison/results/cold-1 All latency is ns/op. The summarizer uses the median of seven retained samples, then divides the fastest correct, eligible baseline median by zscan's median. The full per-case table remains next to each raw run. Construction compares one bidirectional zscan Finder with a forward/reverse memchr Finder pair. Reuse measurements keep construction outside both timed loops. Each one-shot loop includes its API's preprocessing and CPU dispatch.

Ratios are the fastest valid competitor's median ns/op divided by zscan's median ns/op; above 1 means zscan is faster. Every sample is retained, including outliers, slower cases, and the diagnostic timings of an incorrect comparator. memx 0.2.2's reverse substring implementation omits a valid final candidate on some inputs. title: Round 2: bounded vector tails and byte scanning
body: 在字节切片中正向或反向查找字节和子串，并返回原始位置。 Round 2: bounded vector tails and byte scanning The bounded-tail changes improved the targeted medium-size cases, while the broad 2x short/typical performance target remains unmet. The headline results below use the primary corrected after run. A second unchanged run diagnoses severe localized regressions; it does not replace the primary run or supply a selectively better headline. All 607 predeclared cases, every slower result, and all seven measurement samples are retained. Each full configuration has 76,482 raw samples. memchr 2.8.3 is always a strict baseline; memx 0.2.2 contributes eligible byte/forward results. Its known incorrect reverse operation is retained but excluded from speed ratios. Calibration correction and source control The original single-pilot calibration could size a fast operation at one iteration after a scheduler pause during warmup. For example, the diagnostic native text-http-first-n65536-m15 byte_rfind run used one iteration per measurement and reported 73–196 ns, dominated by timer overhead. The original round2-before directory and all round-1 data remain intact. They are historical/diagnostic observations; round-1 ablations were not rerun on the new code. Corrected calibration uses the minimum of three warmup pilots at each candidate batch size. This only sizes the batch: none of the seven actual measurement samples is filtered. The corrected before production source is an isolated checkout of fbe6bcb91989e45d4bf6805c6888863c57554cb5. Before, primary after, and repeat use the identical corrected harness and identical case fingerprints, compiler, profile, and per-configuration RUSTFLAGS. The only production source change is src/bytes.rs. Complete source snapshots and hashes accompany every run. Build Before minimum median batch ns After minimum median batch ns Repeat minimum median batch ns generic 13514 9267 14245 native 6785 7985 4275 Across the corrected runs, the smallest engine/case median batch was 4.275 microseconds. The three-pilot correction prevents one unusually slow pilot from determining the batch size; it does not guarantee a minimum batch duration or eliminate shared-machine timing instability. These data are observations, not a fixed-hardware release gate. Complete group comparison Best-baseline speedup is fastest eligible competitor median / zscan median, geometrically averaged across every case in the group. Above 1 favors zscan. The own-improvement column is before zscan / primary-after zscan. The unchanged memchr control uses before memchr / primary-after memchr.
