title: Verification and release maintenance
body: 在字节切片中正向或反向查找字节和子串，并返回原始位置。 Verification and release maintenance The scripts use Python 3.11+ and its standard library. They are excluded from the published crate. audit.py reads Cargo metadata, including normal, build, dev, optional, and target-specific dependencies; every entry must be absent. python3 scripts/audit.py python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py' -v python3 scripts/test_backends.py Release Set the repository Secret CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN, then open Actions → Release → Run workflow on main. Choose one mode: Mode Effect current Release the version already in Cargo.toml; use this for the first release. patch For example, 0.1.0 → 0.1.1. minor For example, 0.1.3 → 0.2.0. major For example, 0.1.3 → 1.0.0. custom Set the optional version field to a greater plain X.Y.Z version. existing-tag Set tag to an existing vX.Y.Z tag to resume its release. Leave unused fields empty. Older dispatch clients supplying only tag still work. Plain release versions are required; leading zeroes and prerelease suffixes are rejected. New release preparation is restricted to main. Release through a committed request When workflow dispatch is unavailable, commit a deliberate change to .github/release-request.json on main. For the first 0.1.0 release: {"mode":"current","expected_version":"0.1.0"} Only changes to this exact file initiate branch-based publication. Ordinary source pushes do not. expected_version must match the request commit's Cargo.toml, preventing an old request from causing a different bump. The JSON accepts only mode, expected_version, optional version or tag as above, and an optional request_id of 1–80 letters, digits, dots, underscores or hyphens. A fresh request_id allows a deliberate retry commit. Unknown or duplicate keys, empty or non-string values, conflicting selectors, symlinks, and requests over 4 KiB are rejected. To resume an existing release, for example: {"mode":"existing-tag","expected_version":"0.1.0","tag":"v0.1.0","request_id":"retry-1"} Here expected_version refers to the branch source, even when the selected tag is older. Create or edit the request file only when intending to initiate a release. Version commit, checks, and publication Preparation updates only Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, and the path zscan entry in comparison/Cargo.lock. It prints the diff and builds a deterministic release commit with a fixed bot identity and the source commit's timestamp plus one second. current makes an empty release commit so the branch and tag can be advanced in one atomic operation. The script checks registry availability before changing refs, then performs one non-force atomic push of main and vX.Y.Z. Concurrent branch or tag changes cannot partially advance these refs; no tag or published version is overwritten. A matching existing release commit/tag can be resumed without another push. GitHub-token pushes do not launch new Actions runs. This workflow explicitly calls the full CI matrix on the resolved commit and then publishes in the same run. Direct pushes of existing-commit vX.Y.Z tags remain supported. Every CI checkout uses the tag's exact commit. Publication checks the local HEAD, tag, remote tag, manifest version, clean tracked files, and archive VCS identity again. The publication job starts only after the full CI matrix succeeds, then repeats packaging and dry-run before uploading. Release packaging and publication use pinned Rust/Cargo 1.99.1, recorded in scripts/release-toolchain.txt. The resolver reads this file from the tagged commit, so a manual run from a newer branch still uses the older tag's pin. Regular CI continues to check rolling stable and the MSRV. This prevents a later stable update from silently changing normalized manifests or archive bytes during manual recovery. The publication script checks the actual rustc --version --verbose and cargo --version --verbose identities and records them in target/release-evidence.json, without credentials. For a previously published archive, these identify the current verification tools, not the historical publisher's tools. Checksum equality remains mandatory; matching source commits alone never establish archive equality. Only the publication step receives CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN. It invokes cargo publish --locked once. A missing Secret, failed check, unavailable registry preflight, or conflicting published checksum stops the run. No token is passed in arguments or written to a file. After an upload error, read-only registry checks determine whether the exact archive was published. The workflow does not upload again automatically. If confirmation remains unavailable, inspect crates.io before manually rerunning the same tag. A rerun recognizes an identical existing archive by SHA256 and proceeds without republishing. A different archive or a yanked version requires manual investigation. GitHub Release creation happens only after the registry confirms the matching crate, version, and checksum. test_release.py exercises publication failures with isolated mocks. test_prepare_release.py checks version changes and uses temporary local Git remotes to exercise branch/tag races, atomic pushes and idempotent recovery. Neither test suite contacts GitHub or uploads a crate. Configuring this workflow or passing its tests is not evidence of a real publication. Action pins The official tag refs were checked on 2026-11-09: Action Tag Full commit actions/checkout v7.0.1 3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 actions/upload-artifact v7.0.2 cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 The crates.io version/checksum response schema was checked against its official response snapshot. Updates should resolve and review a new full commit before changing either pin. Hosted-runner benchmark smoke results are observations, not a performance gate.

title: 概览
body: 原生 zsh 配置框架，按需加载插件并显式提供上下文。 zshard A small zsh framework for Project Z. Completion, history suggestions, command highlighting, a warm copper prompt, and explicit AI handoff fit in ordinary zsh scripts. Part of oh-my-ztty. Use it on its own with zsh 5.9 or newer: git clone https://github.com/LIghtJUNction/zshard.git ~/.local/share/zshard source ~/.local/share/zshard/zshard.zsh Add that source line to your zsh configuration when ready. Remove the line to uninstall the framework; configuration and history remain yours. The complete suite provides managed installation and removal. The shell stays small The prompt reads Git's HEAD directly. Its palette is shared with command highlights, suggestions and completion headings; all eight colors can be configured. It shows the directory, branch, exit status and slow-command duration. There is no prompt subprocess, network request, background watcher or required icon font. A real process trace tests that contract. Completion initializes on the first Tab, with zsh's security audit. Cache validation checks the current completion inputs and audit exclusions before reusing a dump. History suggestions inspect a bounded recent window; Right or Ctrl-F accepts the text. Highlighting recognizes the first command token. This is a small editor integration, not a full shell grammar checker. # Set before source: ZSHARD_KEYMAP=vi # default: emacs ZSHARD_COMPLETION=eager # default: lazy; also supports off ZSHARD_SHELL_INTEGRATION=1 # optional OSC 7 / OSC 133 source ~/.local/share/zshard/zshard.zsh See configuration and extension APIs and the measured release results. Startup, first completion, memory and comparison measurements are reproducible with the benchmark script. Faster startup partly comes from deferring completion; compare the feature-ready results as well. Add only the plugins you want zshard load ~/.config/zsh/my-plugin.zsh zshard defer ~/.config/zsh/after-prompt.zsh zshard lazy expensive-command ~/.config/zsh/tool-init.zsh Remote plugins require a full commit SHA and an explicit entry file. Installation never sources downloaded code. Review a plugin, install its pin, then load it with zshard use NAME. The complete example includes a command, a hook and cleanup. AI is an explicit action zai context # local JSON: directory, shell, last exit zai connect # run Project Z ssmcp here zai propose 'git status --short' # stage text for review; Enter runs it Context excludes environment variables, history and file contents. No model or account is configured implicitly. For an existing provider CLI, configure an argv array and run zai ask: ZSHARD_AI_COMMAND=(my-provider-cli --read-stdin) zai ask 'Explain this directory context' That command receives the context and request on stdin. Provider output is displayed; it is never evaluated. bin/zshard ai context also works outside an interactive shell. Develop make check make bench python3 scripts/bump.py patch --release make check runs isolated runtime and PTY checks. Benchmarking is separate. The release command tests locally, commits the version, tags it, and pushes an atomic release update. GitHub Actions builds a source archive and checksums on release tags; routine checks are manual. MIT licensed. zshard adds no compiled helper or Rust standard-library dependency. It uses the system zsh runtime; ssmcp remains a separately installed Project Z companion.

title: Configure and extend zshard
body: 原生 zsh 配置框架，按需加载插件并显式提供上下文。 Configure and extend zshard Set options before sourcing zshard.zsh. The framework can be sourced twice without registering duplicate hooks. Option Default Effect ZSHARD_KEYMAP emacs vi selects zsh's vi editor ZSHARD_COMPLETION lazy eager initializes immediately; off leaves completion alone ZSHARD_PROMPT minimal off leaves PROMPT and RPROMPT alone ZSHARD_SUGGESTIONS 1 0 disables history suggestions ZSHARD_HISTORY_SCAN 200 Maximum history events inspected for a suggestion ZSHARD_HIGHLIGHT 1 0 disables command-token highlighting ZSHARD_SHELL_INTEGRATION 0 1 enables OSC 7 cwd and OSC 133 command boundaries ZSHARD_CACHE_DIR XDG_CACHE_HOME/zshard Dedicated completion cache directory ZSHARD_PLUGIN_DIR XDG_DATA_HOME/zshard/plugins Installed plugin checkouts and locks HISTFILE XDG_STATE_HOME/zshard/history Existing user value is preserved XDG defaults follow the usual ~/.local/share, ~/.local/state and ~/.cache locations. Completion uses a private cache directory and runs compinit -i for every new shell; insecure completion directories are skipped. It never uses compinit -C to bypass the audit. Dump files and compiled dumps must be owned by the current user, not symlinks, and not writable by group or others; unsafe caches are bypassed. Colors One palette controls the prompt, command highlighting, history suggestions and completion headings. Set these variables before sourcing zshard.zsh: Variable Default Purpose ZSHARD_COLOR_PATH #e8ded2 Warm white directory label ZSHARD_COLOR_ACCENT #d4a373 Copper branch and prompt symbol ZSHARD_COLOR_MUTED #a3978b Command duration ZSHARD_COLOR_ERROR #e59a91 Failed commands and unknown command tokens ZSHARD_COLOR_COMMAND #e8ded2 Recognized command tokens ZSHARD_COLOR_KEYWORD #c5a4b6 Shell keywords ZSHARD_COLOR_SUGGESTION #a3978b History suggestion text ZSHARD_COLOR_COMPLETION #d4a373 Completion group descriptions Values use zsh color syntax: default, standard color names, palette indices 0–255, or #RRGGBB. The default RGB colors require a terminal with truecolor support, including ztty. For an older terminal, set palette indices before loading the framework. Custom prompt callbacks can use the same variables. The prompt reads Git HEAD through zsh builtins. Changing directories refreshes repository discovery; creating a repository in the current directory or removing the cached checkout refreshes it before the next prompt. No Git process, file watcher or network request runs as part of this refresh. Warm completion during installation Run zshard cache warm [COMPLETION_DIR ...] from the standalone CLI or an existing shell to prepare the audited completion dump. Installers can call this after installing files, so the first interactive Tab uses the warm cache. This operation performs work explicitly during installation; normal startup still defers completion. Pass extra completion directories in the same order used by the interactive configuration. ZSHARD_CACHE_DIR can keep a suite cache separate. Added or removed completion files can require a later rebuild. Local loading zshard load FILE sources the canonical file path once. defer FILE queues it for the next ZLE editing line. lazy COMMAND FILE installs a command wrapper, loads the file once when invoked, then forwards the original argument boundaries. A lazy plugin must define that command or make its external executable available. Each deferred batch attempts every queued plugin once, even when another plugin fails. The batch returns its first nonzero status. Plugins queued while that batch runs wait for the next editing line. Failed plugins are not marked as loaded and are not retried automatically; after correcting a failure, use zshard load FILE to retry it explicitly. A failure does not undo shell changes already made by that plugin. Plugins execute with the user's shell privileges. They are explicit trusted configuration. Startup does not search the network or load every installed plugin automatically. Pin a remote plugin zshard plugin add NAME HTTPS_OR_SSH_URL FULL_COMMIT_SHA RELATIVE_ENTRY_FILE zshard plugin verify NAME zshard use NAME NAME allows letters, digits, underscores and hyphens. The Git commit must be the full 40-character SHA. An entry must resolve inside the checkout. Git file transports and repository hooks are disabled during installation. A checkout and its .lock file record the resolved pin. verify checks HEAD and uncommitted files with Git; this explicit integrity check is separate from shell loading. Export exact pins for your dotfiles repository and restore them explicitly on another machine: zshard plugin export > plugins.lock zshard plugin restore plugins.lock Restore does not load code. It verifies matching installed checkouts, installs missing pins, and refuses a different existing pin. A failed batch keeps successfully installed entries so a retry can continue. Change a pin by removing and reinstalling a reviewed version: zshard plugin remove NAME zshard plugin add NAME URL NEW_FULL_COMMIT_SHA ENTRY Removal affects files installed under the dedicated plugin directory. It does not undo functions already loaded into a running shell. Open a new shell or use the cleanup API. Hooks and cleanup Use zshard hook EVENT FUNCTION and zshard unhook EVENT FUNCTION. Registration uses zsh's standard hook arrays and preserves other functions. Supported events are chpwd, precmd, preexec, periodic, zshaddhistory, zshexit and zsh_directory_name. The hello plugin is a usable template. Its cleanup function is zshard_plugin_hello_unload. A plugin named my-tool defines zshard_plugin_my_tool_unload. zshard unload NAME calls that function and clears the loaded-file record, so the plugin can be loaded again. It refuses to claim success when no cleanup function exists. A plugin owns and removes only its own hooks, variables, widgets and functions. Completion and themes Before the first Tab, call zshard completions DIRECTORY to add a directory of standard zsh _command files. Use #compdef command in those files. Late registration returns an error instead of silently missing the completion. Call zshard theme FUNCTION to use a prompt callback. The callback receives the last exit status and elapsed whole seconds, and assigns PROMPT and RPROMPT. The compact theme demonstrates this. Keep external commands out of prompt callbacks if you want the default latency contract. ZLE integration uses add-zle-hook-widget. Its highlight entries carry a memo=zshard marker, so unrelated regions survive redraws. Suggestions yield when another widget owns POSTDISPLAY. Right and Ctrl-F accept a suggestion at the end of the buffer; otherwise they move forward normally. Repeated redraws reuse the previous history result, including an empty result, only while the input, history event and scan limit remain unchanged. Finishing an editing line drops that cache. Changed input still performs the bounded history search. AI contracts zai context produces one zshard.context.v1 JSON object. Its fields are cwd, shell, shell_version, last_exit, capabilities, history_included and environment_included. It does not read files or emit the previous command. In a fresh standalone process, last_exit starts at 0; the active interactive shell supplies its recorded previous status. The current directory can itself be private; sharing happens only when the user explicitly runs a provider or ssmcp. zai connect forwards arguments to the actual ssmcp binary. It does not start a model. ZSHARD_AI_COMMAND must be an array; zai ask passes each element as an argv entry and sends context plus the request on stdin. It never evaluates strings as shell code. zai propose requires an interactive TTY and one printable command line. It pushes text into the editing buffer. Review, edit or cancel it; only an explicit Enter runs the command.

title: Completion cache compatibility
body: 原生 zsh 配置框架，按需加载插件并显式提供上下文。 Completion cache compatibility zshard 0.1.2 keeps the native zsh security audit on every completion initialization. It adds a small compatibility layer around cache generation and invalidation; it does not use compinit -C, change users' fpath, or disable permission checks. Why the cache needed more than a file count The zsh 5.9 functions compinit, compaudit and compdump do not always derive the same count after rejecting completion paths. Their treatment of symlinks and permitted private groups also differs. A stable set of inputs can therefore regenerate an identical dump on every shell launch. A stock Ubuntu 24.04 container with zsh 5.9-6ubuntu2 reproduced this with a foreign-owned completion directory: compinit compared 968 candidates with a dump recording 966. The patched candidate reused its corrected dump without changing either its hash or nanosecond modification time. Separate fixtures cover a safe symlink and an allowed private-group directory alongside a rejected world-writable directory. Counts also miss changes that preserve the total. In an isolated root fixture, two previously owned completion files changed to another UID. A native warm dump retained both executable mappings. Another fixture replaced one completion file with another while keeping the total unchanged. zshard now rebuilds in both cases. What changes during initialization The scoped audit wrapper calls the original compaudit and observes its ordered directory and candidate lists plus rejected paths. These inputs become an escaped signature in a comment inside the dump. The signature is compared as data and is never evaluated. A literal line feed or carriage return in the encoded signature disables disk caching for that initialization; tests also cover real filenames containing both characters. When the signature differs, native compinit -i builds at a new private staging path. The scoped dump wrapper retains compinit's actual candidate count and writes the signature beside the header. The complete file is published atomically, so its metadata and completion definitions cannot come from different concurrent writers. A stale compiled dump is removed before publication. Failed metadata writes or publication return failure; both original functions are restored and staging files are removed. When inputs and audit exclusions match, native compinit -i performs its usual audit and loads the warm dump. File additions, same-count replacements, changed rejected paths and different completion directories invalidate it. As with native compinit, editing a #compdef line without changing the file list requires explicitly rebuilding the dump. Evidence and reproduction Ubuntu fixture results preserve the baseline and patched traces. Runtime tests cover reuse, unsafe ownership changes, equal-count replacements, line-safe metadata, function restoration and write failure. The formal release workflow runs the ownership-transition test with an isolated temporary home as root. make check python3 scripts/diagnose_completion.py # The ownership test needs an isolated root container; it never uses real dotfiles. docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/src:ro" -w /src ubuntu:24.04 \ bash -ceu 'apt-get update >/dev/null apt-get install -y zsh python3 >/dev/null python3 tests/test_runtime.py RuntimeTests.test_changed_completion_file_ownership_invalidates_cache' The extra signature work occurs when completion first initializes, including explicit zshard cache warm. Default startup and prompt rendering still create no child process. See measured timings for the resulting first-completion cost.

title: Performance and validation
body: 原生 zsh 配置框架，按需加载插件并显式提供上下文。 Performance and validation zshard starts with ordinary zsh code and no background process. Its default startup defers completion, plugin management and AI helpers until needed. The complete startup measurement below includes audited completion and keeps that distinction visible. 0.2.0 palette and interaction measurements The warm copper defaults keep real first-prompt delivery near 4.1 ms in a 31-sample interleaved comparison with 0.1.3. Repeated redraws of unchanged input reuse a bounded history result: that specific miss case measured 0.0695 ms instead of 0.7254 ms. Changing-input misses measured 0.7210 ms instead of 0.6939 ms, so the cache benefit is not a per-keystroke speed claim. Default initialization measured 3.655 ms median; initialization with audited completion ready measured 17.601 ms. Default idle shell PSS was 1478 KiB. The 0.2.0 validation record contains exact source revisions, all timings, memory boundaries, 37 local runtime contracts and reproducible commands. Earlier measurements below retain their original source and scope. Earlier 0.1.2 measurements Source commit: 3367c8dadef1a06a047ce9b47aa9446fe219550c. zsh: zsh 5.9.2 (x86_64-pc-linux-gnu). CPU: 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-12900HX. Raw timestamp: 2026-11-19T20:06:22.203002+00:00. Configuration Initialization median, ms p95, ms Idle PSS, KiB Vanilla zsh 1.679 2.005 767 zsh + audited completion 12.291 15.236 2308 zshard, completion deferred 4.106 5.114 1161 zshard, completion ready 19.185 24.213 2500 Oh My Zsh, git + robbyrussell 28.403 33.335 2824 The baseline-to-zshard elapsed-time ratio was 6.92 for default initialization and 1.48 with completion ready. This compares these configurations on one workstation; it does not rank all shells or terminals. The first completion in each shell took a median of 15.848 ms with a warm disk dump. Creating a new dump took 147.310 ms. The cold cost occurs on the first Tab of a fresh cache; it is not included in the deferred startup figure. Installers can explicitly run zshard cache warm [COMPLETION_DIR ...] to pay that cost during installation. Native compinit still rebuilds when its audited completion inputs change. The script measures 31 interleaved process launches after three warmups, using an empty temporary home. It invokes zsh -f -i -c and measures process launch plus initialization; first-prompt rendering is excluded for every variant. PSS comes from five idle processes per variant through /proc/PID/smaps_rollup; terminal-emulator memory is excluded. All measured zshard idle processes had zero child processes. Oh My Zsh is pinned at c0140703a53eb0d22be44f7bac318d0baacc927c with the git plugin, robbyrussell theme and automatic updates disabled. The baseline does not add separate suggestion or highlighting plugins. Warm filesystem state, system load, distribution completion files and shell configuration affect these values. Raw samples and environment include all startup, completion and memory samples. Reproduce make check python3 scripts/benchmark.py --samples 31 --output artifacts/benchmark.json # Optional comparison against your reviewed, pinned upstream checkout: python3 scripts/benchmark.py --samples 31 --omz /path/to/ohmyzsh --output artifacts/with-omz.json Runtime evidence The 28 runtime contracts passed through local checks and the isolated root ownership-transition test. The tests use temporary homes and actual zsh PTYs. They cover suggestion acceptance, Tab completion, AI proposal staging without execution, JSON escaping, argument-preserving lazy loading, hook coexistence, themes, completion registration, pinned plugin integrity, unload, lock restoration, CLI warming with additional completion directories and a dedicated cache, secure dump reuse, and rejection of a writable dump. A Linux strace check verifies no child process is created by default startup or the built-in prompt. The public HTTPS example-plugin path was exercised against commit 6ef55fe94dcf0f5f17c8f749041dc2cad6df0590: install, verify, load, execute the hello command, unload, export, remove, restore and verify all succeeded. No downloaded plugin was loaded by the installation operation. The 0.1.2 compatibility layer validates the current completion file list and native audit exclusions before reusing a dump. This adds work at first completion compared with 0.1.1; the published measurements include it. Cache compatibility evidence explains the Ubuntu rebuild loop, ownership-transition regression and atomic publication checks. PSS varies with other processes sharing mapped pages, so compare configurations within one recorded run. Claims and review Review question Evidence and boundary What was created? A zsh framework with a small default path and explicit extension APIs; zsh remains the shell. Is the behavior clear? Deferred initialization and feature-ready initialization have separate measurements; AI actions are explicit. Are performance claims supported? Raw samples, exact revisions and a reproducible script support this workstation comparison. Is evaluation complete? Runtime regressions cover Arch zsh 5.9.2 and Ubuntu 24.04 zsh 5.9. Workstation timings describe this recorded configuration; other machines and plugin combinations need their own measurements. Does the design uphold its boundaries? PTY and process-trace checks cover no automatic command execution and no default child process; plugins remain trusted shell code.

title: 概览
body: 为 Typst 标记、代码和数学内容构建语法树。 zsyn An independent, zero-dependency Rust parser for Typst markup, code, and math. zsyn builds lossless syntax trees in caller-owned memory, exposes exact UTF-8 byte ranges, and supports incremental editing. Its core is always #![no_std] and forbids unsafe code. The optional alloc feature provides an owning tree. The minimum supported Rust version is 1.74.0. The published crate has no normal, build, development, optional, or target-specific third-party dependencies and no build script. Linux, Windows, macOS, WebAssembly, AArch64, and a bare-metal ARM target are covered by CI. Parse without an allocator [dependencies] zsyn = "0.1.0" use zsyn::{parse, Diagnostic, Limits, Mode, Node}; let source = "= Greeting\nHello *world*! $x^2$"; let mut nodes = [Node::EMPTY; 256]; let mut diagnostics = [Diagnostic::EMPTY; 16]; let tree = parse( source, Mode::Markup, &mut nodes, &mut diagnostics, Limits::default(), )?; for node in tree.descendants() { // Every text slice borrows source. Offsets are UTF-8 bytes. let _ = (node.kind(), node.span(), node.text()); } for diagnostic in tree.diagnostics() { let _ = (diagnostic.kind, diagnostic.span); } # Ok::<(), zsyn::ParseError>(()) Mode::Markup parses a document, Mode::Code parses an expression/statement sequence, and Mode::Math parses mathematical notation without surrounding dollar signs. Embedded mode changes are handled by the parser. parse_bytes validates UTF-8 before parsing raw bytes. Lexer exposes individual mode-specific tokens and errors. parse_into returns arena lengths and the root index for applications that manage the tree lifetime themselves. Owning trees and edits [dependencies] zsyn = { version = "0.1.0", features = ["alloc"] } use zsyn::{Limits, Mode, OwnedTree}; let mut document = OwnedTree::parse( "Hello ordinary world.", Mode::Markup, Limits::default(), )?; let stats = document.edit(8..9, "Z", Limits::default())?; assert_eq!(document.source(), "Hello orZinary world."); assert!(!stats.full_reparse); let tree = document.as_tree(); assert_eq!(tree.root().text(), document.source()); # Ok::<(), zsyn::ParseError>(()) An edit uses a half-open byte range in the old source. Invalid ranges and non-boundary UTF-8 offsets return InvalidEdit. Owning edits are transactional: an error leaves the previous source and tree intact. EditStats reports the reparsed range, reused nodes, and whether a complete parse was required. The allocation-free reparse function accepts the old tree, the new source, an Edit, and a separate caller-owned output arena. The caller owns source editing and allocation policy. Tree representation Each arena node occupies 24 bytes and stores a syntax kind, two byte offsets, and three integer links. Nodes borrow the original source instead of copying token text. Children, parents, and depth-first descendants are available through read-only NodeRef views. Iteration uses no heap and no recursive traversal stack. Node indices are local to a tree revision; retain byte spans across updates. The concrete syntax tree retains whitespace, comments, delimiters, and error nodes. Leaf text reconstructs the original source exactly. Nodes represent expressions and statements, including precedence, calls, closures, destructuring, rules, conditionals, loops, imports, math attachments, fractions, and roots. The crate handles parsing; evaluation and document layout belong to consumers. Identifier classification uses checked-in Unicode 18 XID tables generated from the Unicode Character Database. This keeps the published crate independent of Unicode helper crates. The generator and its source URL are in scripts/generate-unicode.py; the data license is included in the package. Recovery and resource limits Incomplete input returns a tree with located diagnostics when the parser can recover. Resource exhaustion returns ParseError without exposing a partially initialized tree. Caller buffer sizes are hard limits in addition to Limits: Limit Default Source bytes 64 MiB Nodes 4,000,000 Diagnostics 4,096 Recursive parser depth 96, hard ceiling 128 Parser work steps 134,217,728 Set smaller limits for constrained devices. Depth counts parser nesting levels; one nested expression can consume several levels. Source length is also restricted to the u32 byte-span domain. The owning interface uses fallible reservation; the core requires no allocator at all. Correctness and performance The independent comparison/ workspace pins typst-syntax 0.15.1. Its strict differential gate compares every node's kind, byte range, and depth, including trivia and error nodes. Throughput comparisons run only after the complete trees match for both the original and edited documents. No benchmark substitutes lexical scanning for tree construction. The suite includes fixed short, large, code-heavy, math-heavy, and malformed documents; one-character edits; deterministic random Unicode input; boundary conditions; invalid UTF-8; resource limits; and incremental/full-parse equality. Unicode identifier classes are compared across every valid scalar value. See the measured performance report for the recorded latencies, throughput, requested heap usage, repeated runs, and remaining limits. See comparison/README.md for the exact compiler flags, corpus definitions, timing protocol, and memory accounting. Performance depends on the source, CPU, allocation policy, and edit shape. Only measured, equivalent workloads should be used for speed claims. cargo test --all-features cargo test --manifest-path comparison/Cargo.toml cargo test --manifest-path comparison/Cargo.toml --no-default-features --test core cargo +nightly miri test --manifest-path comparison/Cargo.toml --no-default-features --test core --test incremental --test resources RUSTFLAGS='-C target-cpu=x86-64' cargo run --release \ --manifest-path comparison/Cargo.toml --bin benchmark CI and releases CI runs the OS matrix, stable Rust, actual MSRV core tests, cross-target checks, rustfmt, clippy, documentation tests, Miri, dependency/package checks, cargo package, and cargo publish --dry-run. To release, open Actions → Release → Run workflow on the default branch and select none, patch, minor, or major. A default-branch push that changes Cargo.toml also checks the committed version and releases it if unpublished. The same workflow calculates the candidate version, runs the complete reusable CI workflow, updates the manifest and lockfiles, pushes the version commit and annotated tag, publishes to crates.io, verifies its package checksum, and creates the GitHub Release. The release job reads CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN from GitHub Actions secrets. PRs, forks, and non-default branches cannot publish. An automatic check skips an already published version; a manual release requires a new version or a retry of the same interrupted run. Release serialization and same-run recovery protect against duplicate or partially completed publication; generated tags do not need to trigger another workflow. License Project code: MIT OR Apache-2.0. Unicode data: Unicode License V3.

title: Reproducible parser comparison
body: 为 Typst 标记、代码和数学内容构建语法树。 Reproducible parser comparison This independent Cargo workspace checks complete syntax trees and measures parsing against typst-syntax 0.15.1. Its registry dependencies and Cargo.lock belong only to this workspace. The published zsyn package contains none of them. Correctness gate tests/differential.rs compares every node's syntax kind, UTF-8 byte range, and depth in preorder. This preserves parent/child structure, trivia, delimiters, and error nodes. Node text follows directly from the shared source and matching ranges. There is no token-only comparison, ignored whitespace, or wrapper normalization. benchmark runs the same gate before timing each corpus and its edited form. A mismatch emits equivalent=false and withholds its speedup. The gate establishes equivalence for the exact tested documents. It does not establish language-wide compatibility. The grammar cases cover markup, code, math, malformed input, and mode transitions; the deterministic fuzz tests independently check bounded execution, valid byte ranges, complete source retention, and incremental/full-parse consistency. cargo test --manifest-path comparison/Cargo.toml cargo test --manifest-path comparison/Cargo.toml --no-default-features --test core cargo +nightly miri test --manifest-path comparison/Cargo.toml --no-default-features --test core --test incremental --test resources core.rs imports only std and zsyn, so the MSRV job can compile it directly with rustc --test without resolving a newer oracle dependency graph. The root crate retains an empty third-party dependency tree in every feature configuration. Fixed workloads Corpus Source Repetitions Purpose short corpus/short.typ 1 Small document latency and fixed overhead large corpus/large-unit.typ 2,048 Prose, Unicode, formatting, lists, math code corpus/code-unit.typ 256 Expressions, calls, bindings, rules, control flow math corpus/math-unit.typ 512 Attachments, fractions, functions, delimiters errors corpus/errors-unit.typ 256 Incomplete expressions and recovery Workload construction is deterministic and occurs before measurement. CSV rows include the exact byte count and an FNV-1a fingerprint so that compared runs can be matched. The fingerprint identifies the input and is not a security checksum. Measurement protocol Run on an x86-64 machine with the exact release flags below. Record the compiler, CPU, OS, and commit alongside the output. rustc --version --verbose RUSTFLAGS='-C target-cpu=x86-64' cargo run --locked --release \ --manifest-path comparison/Cargo.toml --bin benchmark > timing.csv RUSTFLAGS='-C target-cpu=x86-64' cargo run --locked --release \ --manifest-path comparison/Cargo.toml --features allocation-stats \ --bin benchmark > memory.csv python3 comparison/merge-results.py timing.csv memory.csv benchmark.csv Full-parse and hot-edit timings perform eight warm-up calls, calibrate a batch to at least 15 ms, and report the median of nine equal-sized batches. First-edit timings use the independent-tree procedure below. std::hint::black_box surrounds inputs and results. Complete parsed results are dropped inside the timed region. Equivalence-check trees and canonical records are released before timing, so their allocations do not remain live during measurement. The release profile uses optimization level 3, thin LTO, and one codegen unit for both implementations. Full parsing reports two zsyn interfaces. zsyn-arena reuses caller-allocated node and diagnostic buffers, measuring the core parser's advertised allocation-free API. zsyn-owned includes source ownership and allocations on every call. Both build the same verified complete tree. The separate rows show the cost of owning the source and allocating storage; the arena row assumes the application already has reusable buffers. Single-character editing has two separately named measurements. edit-first prepares eight independent, freshly parsed source trees outside the timed region, times the first edit to each, and reports the median of nine batches. edit-hot alternates a fixed ASCII character and its replacement at the same byte position with the existing tree, allowing an editor's cursor locality to benefit from cached lookup. Initial source/tree construction happens outside timing in both cases. Both edited states pass the complete-tree gate before measurement. The reparsed_bytes column records the affected region returned by each implementation. typst-Source also maintains Typst's source line index and numbered spans; zsyn maintains its documented syntax-tree state. These interfaces have different supporting metadata, which should be considered when interpreting edit latency. The mib_s value for a full parse is source MiB divided by elapsed seconds. For an edit it expresses document-size throughput; edit latency and reparsed bytes are the meaningful incremental metrics, since the parser is expected to reuse most of the document. Memory accounting A counting wrapper around Rust's System allocator records allocation calls, requested bytes, and peak live requested bytes during one operation. It is confined to this unpublished benchmark executable. All tree comparisons and formatting happen outside the measurement window. The default timing executable uses Rust's ordinary allocator directly; the counting wrapper is not compiled into it. A second build with allocation-stats measures memory without reporting timings. merge-results.py checks all 35 rows, the complete-tree gate, source fingerprints, node counts, storage capacities, and reparsed ranges before joining the two runs. Timing rows from an instrumented executable are rejected. Both raw CSV files should be retained alongside the joined results. retained_arena_bytes counts zsyn's initialized nodes and diagnostics. reserved_bytes includes unused storage capacity reported by the interface. The core arena's capacity is allocated before timing and is reported even though its parse operation performs no allocations. Typst rows expose allocator measurements; a zero in an arena-specific column means that metric is not applicable. Requested heap bytes exclude allocator bookkeeping, rounding, call stack, and executable pages; they are not process RSS. Incremental allocation counts and allocated-byte totals exclude initial construction. The incremental peak includes the already retained document: the counter is enabled during construction, then allocation totals are reset before editing while the live-byte count is preserved. This accounts for old storage freed or replaced during an edit. Baseline design The pinned baseline's node representation uses owned leaf strings and reference-counted inner nodes with child vectors. Its source wrapper owns the text and line map. The incremental parser reparses code/content blocks or eligible markup ranges, expanding the range when surrounding syntax must be reconsidered. These are implementation observations about version 0.15.1, not performance results. zsyn tests whether a caller-owned flat arena and borrowed source spans reduce allocation and traversal costs. Any claimed acceleration must be read from a row whose complete-tree gate passed. Failure to reach a target speedup is a measurement result, not permission to relax the gate. Review criteria Contribution: the measured operations construct complete trees; tokenization alone is not a performance result. Clarity: latency, full-document throughput, requested heap memory, arena storage, and source metadata are reported separately. Evidence: every published ratio requires a passing complete-tree comparison and a fixed compiler configuration. Coverage: representative fixed corpora are supplemented by grammar cases, malformed inputs, Unicode, resource budgets, and repeated edits; results remain specific to the tested scope. Design: caller-buffer and owned interfaces are measured separately so allocation setup does not disappear from the report.

title: Measured parser performance
body: 为 Typst 标记、代码和数学内容构建语法树。 Measured parser performance The allocation-free parser exceeds 2× typst-syntax 0.15.1 on the code and error corpora in both recorded runs. Short documents, prose, and math also improve, with smaller gains. The 3× full-parse target remains unmet. The owning convenience interface has separate measurements because it copies the source and allocates storage. All results below use source commit 3f0fce64cdcac746a547aec03d6e21b5f1974f37. They cover the five fixed documents in this repository, not every possible Typst program or processor. The first frozen-source timing run supplies the main tables; the second run is retained without selecting its fastest cells. Evidence and setup The joined results, first timing run, repeat, separate memory run, and environment record contain the raw measurements. Both timing runs use the ordinary Rust allocator with no counting wrapper. A different build collects memory, and the merge script rejects instrumented timing rows or mismatched inputs, node counts, capacities, and reparse ranges. The host was Linux x86-64 on an Intel Xeon Platinum 8573C, with the timing process pinned to CPU 8. Rust was 1.99.1. Both implementations used -C target-cpu=x86-64, optimization level 3, thin LTO, and one codegen unit. No local Miri run shared the timed interval. This was a shared execution host; CPU affinity does not make absolute latency portable to another machine. Every corpus passes an exact complete-CST comparison before timing: syntax kind, byte span, and preorder depth match at every node. That also fixes the source text and parent/child hierarchy. Trivia and error nodes are retained, with no token-only comparison or normalization. Canonical comparison records and validation trees are released before timing. Both states of each benchmark edit are checked against complete reparsing. The methodology and harness specify the gate and workload construction. Full parses and hot edits use eight warm-up calls, a batch calibrated to at least 15 ms, and the median of nine batches. black_box surrounds inputs and results. Full-parse result destruction occurs within the timed interval. For first edits, eight independent source trees are created outside timing for each of nine batches; no clone-induced copy-on-write cost is added to the reference. Complete parsing Run 1, complete syntax-tree construction. Lower latency and higher speedup are better. The arena buffers are already allocated. The owning interface includes source ownership, buffer allocation, initialization, and destruction. Corpus Input bytes typst-syntax µs zsyn arena µs Arena speedup zsyn owned µs Owned speedup Short 90 3.368 1.976 1.704× 2.220 1.517× Large 604,160 9,141.122 5,894.961 1.551× 6,436.449 1.420× Code 60,416 3,291.779 1,626.113 2.024× 1,719.680 1.914× Math 64,000 5,033.140 2,606.147 1.931× 2,730.119 1.844× Errors 24,832 1,013.616 471.239 2.151× 523.898 1.935× Full-document throughput from the same run. One MiB is 1,048,576 bytes. Corpus typst-syntax MiB/s zsyn arena MiB/s zsyn owned MiB/s Short 25.48 43.43 38.65 Large 63.03 97.74 89.52 Code 17.50 35.43 33.50 Math 12.13 23.42 22.36 Errors 23.36 50.25 45.20 Corroborating run on the identical executable. These are two observed medians per cell, not confidence intervals or a best-of-run aggregation. Corpus Arena ratio: run 1 Arena ratio: run 2 Owned ratio: run 1 Owned ratio: run 2 Short 1.704× 1.640× 1.517× 1.424× Large 1.551× 1.614× 1.420× 1.519× Code 2.024× 2.026× 1.914× 1.889× Math 1.931× 1.798× 1.844× 1.766× Errors 2.151× 2.064× 1.935× 1.984× The code corpus is just above the 2× threshold in both runs; the error corpus has a larger margin. The final math measurements remain below 2×. The owning interface remains below 2× across these final measurements. The complete parsing goal is therefore met in two of five measured arena workloads, with the remaining cases and the 3× goal reported explicitly. Incremental editing These edit measurements exercise a fixed, equal-width ASCII-letter replacement inside an existing token. edit-first starts with a newly parsed tree and no previously edited-leaf cache. edit-hot repeatedly toggles the same character at the same location after warm-up. zsyn validates that the token kind and boundaries remain stable, then reuses the existing topology; the processed-byte column is the checked token span. The reference is Typst's public Source::edit interface. It also maintains a line index and numbered source spans. zsyn maintains the documented syntax-tree state. The ratios below compare those complete public operations and include this metadata difference; they do not isolate Typst's AST splice cost. Structural insertions, deletions, delimiter edits, and recovery changes have separate correctness tests but are not performance claims from these rows. First edit, run 1. Initial parsing is outside the timed interval. Corpus typst Source first edit µs zsyn first edit µs Measured ratio Typst reparsed bytes zsyn processed bytes Short 1.056 0.096 11.056× 36 8 Large 739.898 0.891 829.947× 144 130 Code 83.029 0.410 202.634× 44 6 Math 82.791 0.497 166.707× 35 5 Errors 32.065 0.867 36.973× 53 41 Repeated edit at the same location, run 1. This table describes cursor locality and the existing leaf cache. Corpus typst Source hot edit µs zsyn hot edit µs Measured ratio Short 1.034 0.069 14.914× Large 655.783 0.356 1840.216× Code 58.729 0.065 902.159× Math 69.660 0.066 1058.165× Errors 24.890 0.576 43.232× All measured zsyn edits in this corpus perform zero heap allocations. The repeat file retains the corresponding second-run edit timings. Small edit latencies should be interpreted with their exact workload and host context; the full-parser table is the basis for the 2× parsing claim. Memory Requested heap bytes and caller-provided arena storage. Memory comes from a separate instrumented executable. Allocation counts describe a single complete parse. A core parse makes zero allocation calls while using the arena shown below. Corpus Nodes Core initialized arena B Core reserved arena B Owned peak heap B Typst peak heap B Owned / Typst allocation calls Short 55 1,320 3,048 2,694 2,983 3 / 28 Large 126,977 3,047,448 3,049,176 4,109,120 7,049,288 3 / 67600 Code 44,545 1,069,080 1,070,808 1,321,748 2,154,568 3 / 33798 Math 67,073 1,609,752 1,611,480 2,197,144 3,317,832 3 / 30733 Errors 13,825 341,016 342,744 473,176 758,088 3 / 9483 The node representation is 24 bytes. Text stays in the caller's UTF-8 source for the core interface. Core initialized arena counts retained nodes and diagnostics; Core reserved arena also includes the unused space supplied by the benchmark. Owned peak heap includes its source string and buffer capacities. Allocation counts and bytes exclude allocator metadata, rounding, stack, executable pages, and shared runtime state; these are not RSS measurements. For the 604,160-byte prose document, the core retains 3,047,448 arena bytes. The owning parser peaks at 4,109,120 requested heap bytes, compared with 7,049,288 for the reference in this memory run. The owning parser uses three allocations on each of the five corpora. Its sparse-markup capacity estimate reduces unused space without adding repeated parse attempts on these workloads. The separate giant-input regression parses 16 MiB of plain text into two caller-owned nodes and a zero-length diagnostic buffer, and rejects the same input when its source-byte budget is lowered below that size. That is a resource test, distinct from the 604,160-byte large benchmark corpus. Miri uses a 4 KiB instance of that same regression to keep interpreter work bounded. Implementation choices and performance limits The measured implementation uses byte-first ASCII scanning, coalesced text runs, a flat arena, cached lookahead, bounded recovery, and a source-sensitive capacity estimate for the owning interface. Trivia lookahead is reused across the scanned interval. Math attachment updates maintain their tail and avoid repeated traversal of an existing child chain. Work-budget tests cover these paths, so their linear behavior is checked alongside syntax equivalence. There is no explicit SIMD or unsafe implementation path in these measurements. The crate forbids unsafe code and keeps the portable MSRV 1.74 implementation. Portable core::simd was rejected as unstable by the tested stable compiler; platform intrinsics were not added without a measured complete-parser benefit. Compiler-generated vector instructions in ordinary optimized Rust are not an explicit SIMD API in zsyn. Node construction and parser control flow remain substantial work in these corpora: the code document produces 44,545 nodes from 60,416 source bytes, and the math document produces 67,073 nodes from 64,000 bytes. Each result retains a complete hierarchy with byte ranges and parent/sibling links. Plain-text scanning therefore accounts for only part of the complete operation. The owning interface also copies the source and prepares its buffers; its run-1 median exceeds the arena path by 93.568 µs for code, 123.972 µs for math, and 541.488 µs for the large document. These measurements quantify the combined public-interface cost. The report's timing resolution is the complete operation, so it provides no per-instruction attribution. Reproduction Use the frozen implementation commit above and the commands in comparison/README.md. Retain both raw timing runs and the separate memory output. comparison/merge-results.py joins only compatible rows and does not choose the faster timing run. The manual performance workflow performs the same separate timing/memory builds and uploads the raw files. The owning API is optional. The published crate's dependency tree remains empty, and the comparison workspace and its pinned reference dependency are excluded from the package. The core MSRV is 1.74; the oracle workspace runs on the current stable compiler recorded in the environment file. Claim and evidence review Claim Evidence Scope More than 2× on code and errors Both final timing CSVs Reused caller arena, fixed corpora, recorded host Complete syntax results match Harness gate and differential suites Every retained kind, byte span, and hierarchy in tested sources Core parsing allocates zero times Separate allocation-count rows and caller-arena API Caller-owned source and buffers Stable token edits reuse syntax Edit statistics, full-parse checks, and first/hot rows Equal-width ASCII replacements used by this benchmark Memory use is bounded Explicit parser budgets and resource regressions Requested limits and caller buffer capacities

title: 概览
body: 按需采集 Linux 的处理器、内存、进程与存储状态，提供可借用的数据视图。 zsys A composable system-information engine for Rust, with zero third-party runtime dependencies. Collect only the information you need, retain sampling state, and read snapshots through borrowed views. The native system-information backend is Linux. CPU, memory, processes, filesystems, block I/O, networks, and optional sysfs hardware information are implemented. Windows, macOS, and other targets currently expose the portable counter models and parsers; their native collectors remain future work. See platform support. Run it From a checkout, with Rust 1.95 or newer: cargo run --release --example basic cargo run --release --example cadence The current development version is 0.1.1; registry publication is confirmed by its version tag and release: [dependencies] zsys = "0.1" Check crates.io and GitHub Releases for completed publications. Before publication, or when developing from this checkout, use zsys = { path = "../zsys" } instead. use std::time::Duration; use zsys::System; fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> { let mut system = System::new(); system.refresh_cpu()?; system.refresh_memory()?; system.refresh_processes()?; std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(250)); system.refresh_cpu()?; system.refresh_processes()?; println!("CPU: {:?}%", system.cpu().and_then(|c| c.aggregate_busy_percent())); if let Some(memory) = system.memory() { println!("Available memory: {} bytes", memory.counters.available_bytes); } for process in system.processes() { println!( "{} {} RSS={} CPU={:?}% {:?}", process.id.pid, String::from_utf8_lossy(&process.name), process.memory_bytes, process.cpu_percent, process.availability, ); } Ok(()) } The first CPU observation establishes a baseline and reports None for usage. The sleep belongs to the application: collectors create no background threads and impose no hidden refresh interval. Detailed timing, error, and counter semantics are documented in sampling semantics. Choose a collector Each type below can be used without constructing System. Linux collectors live in zsys::linux. Collector Explicit operations Returned information CpuCollector refresh, refresh_frequencies Aggregate and online logical CPU counters, utilization, optional scaling frequency MemoryCollector refresh, snapshot RAM and swap counters, freshness, legacy availability-estimate flag Processes enumerate_pids, refresh, refresh_pid, details Retained PID table, identity, lifecycle changes, CPU/RSS, optional executable/arguments/UIDs/GIDs DiskIoCollector refresh, iter, get Device and partition counters, byte deltas, I/O timings Filesystem refresh, capacity, last_error Capacity and inode counters for one path Mounts refresh, iter_mut, refresh_capacities Mount discovery, decoded paths, filesystem types, explicitly requested capacities Networks refresh_counters, refresh_details, refresh Traffic counters; separately refreshed addresses, flags, MAC, MTU, optional link speed Hardware refresh_inventory, refresh_info, refresh_temperatures, refresh_gpus DMI descriptions, thermal/hwmon readings, DRM identification and available driver telemetry For example, process details are an independent operation: use zsys::linux::{Detail, DetailOptions, Processes}; fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> { let mut processes = Processes::new()?; let pid = std::process::id(); let identity = processes.refresh_pid(pid)?.id; let details = processes.details(pid, DetailOptions::all())?; if details.id == identity { if let Detail::Value(path) = details.executable { println!("{}", path.display()); } } Ok(()) } System lazily owns the CPU, memory, process, network, disk-I/O, and mount collectors. Its refresh_basic samples CPU, RAM, processes, network counters, and block I/O in sequence. Each module keeps its own freshness; a combined refresh is not an atomic kernel snapshot. Hardware and potentially blocking filesystem-capacity queries remain explicit. Collectors reuse retained storage as the sampling workload stabilizes. New objects, larger files or fields, discovery, and owned detail results can allocate. Retained capacity reflects earlier workload peaks until the collector is dropped; allocation measurements must state their warm-up and refresh scope. Portable core [dependencies] zsys = { version = "0.1", default-features = false } Feature Meaning No features no_std counter types, delta calculations, procfs parsers, Sample, SystemSnapshot, and Cadence; no allocator required alloc no_std configuration with the allocation capability enabled; it does not enable OS access or add separate collectors std — default Enables alloc and, on Linux, native collectors dylib Allocation-free Linux/macOS/Windows native library loading; independent of std and alloc Core APIs include cpu::CpuTimes, memory::Memory, process::{ProcessId, ProcessCounters, ProcessState}, disk and network counter/parser types, and sampling::Cadence. Parsing operates on caller-provided bytes; the core does not open files. Generate the complete API reference with cargo doc --no-deps --all-features --open. Shared native library loading The opt-in dylib feature provides the system boundary used by Project Z plugin runtimes. It opens trusted libraries, resolves raw symbol addresses and explicitly closes references without requiring std, a Rust allocator or another crate. The wrapper does not allocate Rust memory; the OS loader and native initializers can allocate their own memory. zsys = { version = "0.1.1", default-features = false, features = ["dylib"] } dylib::Library keeps the native mapping loaded when its Rust handle is dropped. Its unsafe close operation is only valid after all code, data, callbacks and background work requiring that reference have stopped. The narrow path API accepts CStr; Windows also provides validated UTF-16 open_wide. Unsupported targets and static musl builds return dylib::Error::Unsupported. This capability does not add Windows/macOS telemetry collectors. The native CI jobs compile a separate shared library and exercise symbol calls, duplicate image references, explicit close and retained mappings in a child process. Current execution evidence belongs to the corresponding CI run. Measure before making a claim BENCHMARKS.md contains the comparison scope, measurements, raw-data locations, and limitations. The independent benchmark package pins sysinfo =0.40.3 as a benchmark dependency. The library itself does not depend on sysinfo, libc, Rayon, or a procfs wrapper crate. cargo build --locked --release --manifest-path benchmarks/Cargo.toml python3 benchmarks/run.py --output benchmark-results/local --samples 1000 Use a new output directory for each run. The harness retains raw samples, environment metadata, distribution statistics, Rust allocation accounting, and process peak RSS. CPU samples with a real sampling interval and rapid calls that may return cached sysinfo values are separate cases. Large-process tests depend on the host's PID and memory limits; consult the report for the scales actually executed. Validation and release cargo fmt --all -- --check cargo test --locked --all-features cargo test --locked --no-default-features cargo check --locked --no-default-features --features alloc cargo clippy --locked --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings cargo doc --locked --no-deps --all-features python3 scripts/check-package.py The Python scripts require Python 3.11 or newer. CI defines stable/MSRV checks, bare-metal no_std, WASM core, Linux x86_64/aarch64, glibc/musl distributions, Windows/macOS core builds, native C-ABI checks, and benchmark builds. Resource soak keeps a process collector alive for the requested duration. Current execution results belong to Actions, not to a static support claim. The Release workflow runs on main. Manual dispatch accepts none, patch, minor, or major; changes to the package manifest or release workflow on main also start validation for the checked-in version. Configure repository secret CARGO_REGISTY_TOKEN, the requested spelling. It takes precedence; CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN is also accepted as a fallback. The selected value is passed to Cargo under its canonical CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN environment variable. Logs identify only the selected secret name, never its value. Tokens are never stored in source files. Release preparation synchronizes the crate version in both lockfiles without upgrading benchmark dependencies, then runs the full CI matrix for the exact candidate commit. A preparation retry reuses an already pushed bump commit only when its parent and file tree match the candidate. Publishing checks the crate checksum in the registry before creating its matching vVERSION tag and GitHub Release with generated notes. To recover a failed publication, rerun the failed jobs so they reuse the prepared commit; dispatch bump=none only when the checked-in version is the intended candidate. Read further Sampling semantics and complete API map Platform support and native-interface boundaries Architecture and evidence Benchmarks Progress and acceptance record Changelog Licensed under MIT OR Apache-2.0.

title: 架构与可验证的设计
body: 按需采集 Linux 的处理器、内存、进程与存储状态，提供可借用的数据视图。 架构与可验证的设计 zsys 把采集分成三个责任：解释字节、读取操作系统、维护采样状态。核心层独立于 OS 和分配器，Linux 采集器拥有缓冲区与历史值，System 仅组合调用。设计的性能收益以 BENCHMARKS.md 为证据入口，本文不赋予未经测量的倍数优势。 模块边界 层次 输入与输出 设计目的 代码与验证 Core 原始计数器、时间间隔 → 有单位的数据与差分 公式可单独测试，解析器可用于 fixture 或其他数据来源 src/cpu.rs、src/process.rs、src/disk.rs、src/network.rs 的单元测试 Parsers 借用的 byte slice → 计数器或借用字段 解析时不创建临时字符串，拒绝缺失字段、溢出和损坏记录 src/linux/parse.rs 与各 core parser 测试 Linux I/O procfs/sysfs/原生 API → 可复用读取存储 降低固定文件重复打开、路径构建和缓冲扩容成本 src/linux/io.rs、C ABI 检查 Stateful collectors 本轮记录＋上次状态 → 新快照、差分、生命周期与失败状态 稳定对象复用存储，识别身份变化，区分新数据和旧数据 tests/processes.rs、tests/collectors.rs、tests/disks.rs Composition 显式刷新请求 → 相应模块的借用视图 按需初始化，保持独立刷新，无后台调度成本 src/linux/system.rs、tests/system.rs 一次读取如何形成快照 公共计数器文件通过缓存的打开句柄读取，数据进入采集器自己的缓冲区。解析器在这些已读取字节上工作，名字或记录只有在需要跨次刷新保留时才复制到拥有型字段。这里仍然存在内核到用户缓冲区的读取复制；“借用解析”描述的是解析阶段的内存行为。 CPU、网络与块 I/O 先验证输入，再更新可见结果。网络与块 I/O 使用复用的暂存记录，重复键或损坏输入会返回错误并保留旧成功快照。CPU 热插拔改变聚合基线，网络 ifindex 变化、设备名称变化或累计值回退会影响相应差分。错误路径的实际行为见 采样语义。 进程读取采用可见 PID 表与代次标记。完整枚举成功后，采集器更新各 PID 的当前记录，记录失败项，最后移除本轮不再可见的项。相同 PID 的启动 tick 改变时，使用新的身份与 CPU 基线。默认 RSS 来自同一 PID 身份下的 statm，stat 的原始 resident 字段仍供检查；详情进一步通过固定 PID 目录和前后身份检查避免跨生命周期拼接。tests/processes.rs 覆盖生命周期、权限、异常输入和身份一致性。 为什么拆开高频计数器与详情 CPU 时间、内存统计、网络流量与进程核心记录适合频繁读取，命令行、可执行文件、用户 ID、网络地址及硬件 inventory 的读取范围和变化频率不同。独立 API 使调用者决定何时付出这些成本。例如 Networks::refresh_counters 不发现 IP 地址，Processes::details 不隐式刷新整个进程表，CpuCollector::refresh_frequencies 不混入每次 CPU 使用率读取。 磁盘容量也单独暴露，因为挂载点可能属于远程或故障文件系统。Mounts 提供发现结果，调用者选择 Filesystem 执行容量查询；System::refresh_basic 保持为明确的计数器组合，不包括所有挂载的容量与硬件详情。这个边界既影响延迟，也影响失败处理方式，参见 statvfs(3)。 内存与原生调用的选择 采集器保留 Vec、HashMap 和读取缓冲容量，避免稳定规模下重复创建整个数据结构。新增对象、名字增长或更大的文件仍然可能分配。保留容量使驻留内存受历史峰值影响；丢弃采集器会关闭其拥有的文件描述符并释放拥有型存储。进程资源测试 检查热路径分配、持续运行的保留字节与描述符，以及反复创建销毁后的资源归还。 PID 枚举有 ScanMode::Native 和 ScanMode::Std 两个实现。原生路径在 x86_64/aarch64 使用 getdents64，目录缓冲从需要枚举时才分配，并有增长上限；标准库路径保留为可测量的对照和其他架构的默认选择。单 PID 刷新无需分配整个目录枚举缓冲。两种路径的输出一致性由 tests/processes.rs 检查，性能差异由独立 benchmark 测量。 原生 FFI 限制在 Linux 后端，结构体布局和常量通过 C 头文件校验与 Rust layout 单元测试约束。文件描述符交给 File 或 OwnedFd，getifaddrs 分配的链表由专用 RAII 对象释放。零第三方运行时 crate 表示依赖关系为空，并不消除 OS 接口、Rust 标准库或平台 C ABI 的职责。依赖门禁见 scripts/check-package.py。 测量与验收依据 benchmark package 固定 sysinfo =0.40.3，只调用双方公开 API。每个实现运行在独立子进程中，记录分位延迟、吞吐、Rust 分配请求、保留堆字节及整个测试进程的峰值 RSS。报告需要保留采样范围与 freshness：同名函数的两次调用可能执行不同工作，系统接口受到权限限制时也可能得到不同集合。 真实 CPU 刷新与可能命中 sysinfo 最小间隔缓存的高频调用分开记录；网络对比先检查双方实际集合和详情；进程比较以实际采集身份、RSS 来源和字段范围为准；磁盘容量使用对应的挂载集合。仅 zsys 支持的原子操作单独报告。该方法将架构选择与可复查的观测关联，而不把单个机器上的结果扩大为所有平台的承诺。 文档主张与证据核对 主张 证据 边界 核心不要求 std 或分配器 no-default-features 测试、bare-metal/WASM 编译门禁 这些目标只验证 core，未实现原生采集 运行时第三方依赖为空 Cargo metadata 与 scripts/check-package.py benchmark 独立使用 sysinfo 开发工具依赖 刷新与详情可独立组合 tests/system.rs 和公开 collector API refresh_basic 是顺序组合，失败可留下跨模块不同 freshness PID 复用与失败状态有明确行为 生命周期 fixture、权限、快速退出测试 可见范围仍由内核权限和 namespace 决定 复用采集器有可检查的资源行为 tests/process_resources.rs 持续运行时长和实际结果以执行日志为准 相对性能可以复现 benchmark 源码、原始数据与 BENCHMARKS.md 依赖硬件、进程规模、采样内容与环境权限 自审 贡献范围： 提供原子采集 API、保留状态和明确差分语义；尚未实现其他 OS 的原生后端。 表达清晰： API、单位、时间原点、错误状态和拥有关系分别说明，术语与公开类型保持一致。 实验强度： README 不引用待验收数字；所有性能判断由 benchmark 数据和采样条件支撑。 评估完整性： fixture、并发、资源、发行版、ABI 与编译矩阵分别覆盖明确的失败模式；环境允许的进程规模由报告记录。 设计边界： 保留容量、近似 RSS、硬件驱动差异、namespace 和可能阻塞的容量调用均有明确说明。

title: Platform support
body: 按需采集 Linux 的处理器、内存、进程与存储状态，提供可借用的数据视图。 Platform support The portable core and native collection backends have different support boundaries. A successful Windows or macOS core build does not provide a native system-information collector on that platform. Implemented capability Target Portable models/parsers Native collection Boundaries Linux x86_64, glibc Yes CPU, memory, processes, disk/mounts, network, optional sysfs hardware Requires accessible kernel files and permitted native calls Linux aarch64, glibc Yes Same Linux backend Native getdents64 number and C ABI have dedicated CI checks Linux x86_64, musl Yes Same Linux backend Alpine CI checks the native headers and runs Linux tests Other Linux architectures Yes Common procfs paths are conditionally available Process construction defaults to ScanMode::Std outside x86_64/aarch64; these architectures do not have the same native test coverage Linux 32-bit Yes Partial platform paths only Filesystem capacity returns Unsupported; no complete backend acceptance claim Windows and macOS Yes Not implemented CI builds/tests the core and verifies Linux code stays gated Android, iOS, FreeBSD Portable core is designed to remain OS-independent Not implemented No native collection or runtime validation is claimed thumbv7em-none-eabi Core compilation None no_std, including the optional alloc configuration, is a compile gate wasm32-unknown-unknown Core compilation None no_std core is a compile gate These rows describe source capabilities and the configured validation scope. Inspect the CI runs and acceptance record for execution results on the commit you use. Shared dynamic-library interface The independent dylib feature implements native loading on Linux, macOS and Windows with no_std and no allocator. Unix uses eager, local symbol loading. Windows uses the platform default DLL search directories and preserves UTF-16 paths through open_wide. Statically linked musl and other unsupported targets return an explicit unsupported error. A handle owns one OS loader reference and is thread-local. Dropping it pins the mapping; unloading is an explicit unsafe operation whose caller must stop every dependent object, symbol, callback and native task first. This is the system primitive used by zplugin; it does not implement plugin ABI validation or platform telemetry collection. The native CI matrix exercises independently built dynamic libraries. The bare-metal/WASM jobs also compile the feature's unsupported-target path. A configured CI job is not a recorded native runtime result; consult its completed run for the tested commit. Feature and compiler requirements The MSRV is Rust 1.95, edition 2024. With default features disabled, the crate is no_std and its counter types and parsers do not require a global allocator. The alloc feature enables that capability without enabling OS access; it currently adds no separate allocation-backed public collection API. Default std enables Linux collection only when target_os = "linux". cargo test --locked --no-default-features cargo check --locked --no-default-features --features alloc cargo check --locked --no-default-features --target thumbv7em-none-eabi cargo check --locked --no-default-features --features alloc --target thumbv7em-none-eabi cargo check --locked --no-default-features --target wasm32-unknown-unknown Install the listed Rust targets before running cross-target commands. Compilation on bare metal or WASM validates the portable core; these commands do not read the host's system information from those targets. Linux native boundary The runtime dependency list is empty. Linux FFI calls the platform C ABI and kernel interfaces directly; the Rust libc crate is not required. The application still uses Rust std and the operating system's normal C runtime/linker environment. getdents64 is used on x86_64/aarch64; ScanMode::Std allows a directly comparable standard-library enumeration path. Filesystem capacity uses the Linux LP64 statvfs layout. Native headers are checked by scripts/check-abi.c, including socket/address layouts and syscall/ioctl constants; corresponding Rust layout assertions run in unit tests. Current glibc and musl declarations for statvfs preserve the offsets used here, including their trailing reserved storage. See statvfs(3) and the musl header. A mounted /proc and /sys can expose a container-specific, restricted, or host-wide view. zsys reports the view it reads: it does not grant permissions, join other namespaces, normalize CPU by container quota, or replace RAM totals with cgroup limits. with_proc_root and with_sys_root support fixtures and alternate mounted views. Cached descriptors are associated with the view used when opened; create new collectors after changing the process's namespace or mounts. Network details use getifaddrs, with a read-only ioctl/procfs fallback when the native address path encounters specified permission/protocol restrictions. Metadata queries still can fail; counter collection remains independently callable. Six-octet MAC addresses are optional, and link speed depends on driver sysfs support. Details use the current network namespace even when the counter collector reads a custom proc root. Hardware inventory depends on exported kernel attributes. A headless container can legitimately have no sensors or DRM cards. Thermal-class temperatures, raw hwmon channels, DMI descriptions, PCI identification, and optional AMDGPU metrics are the current scope. There is no universal GPU telemetry backend, and no hardware-control operation. Validation matrix ci.yml defines Ubuntu 22.04/24.04, Windows/macOS core jobs, a native Ubuntu aarch64 job, Debian/glibc and Alpine/musl containers, MSRV, bare-metal/WASM checks, formatting, Clippy, rustdoc and benchmark compilation. Fixtures cover parsing, stale values, lifecycle and identity changes without requiring a particular physical disk, GPU, or sensor. soak.yml runs an extended process-resource test, with a manually selectable duration and a scheduled run. tests/process_resources.rs checks allocations and descriptor growth for a continuously reused collector. This test's scope is the process collector; hardware-driver behavior and every filesystem implementation remain dependent on the deployment environment. Next native backends Windows, macOS, FreeBSD, Android and iOS require their own native interfaces and semantics. They will be added behind platform-specific modules rather than treating Linux procfs fields as an implementation for other kernels. Their implementation and native testing are pending.

秒／3,968,000 次与 60.006 秒／4,514,816 次；两次热路径分配、保留字节增长、FD 增长均为 0 分支运行、PR 运行 本地最终基准 公平 statm RSS 路径；真实进程数与采样范围记录完整 overview.json、final-table.csv、原始数据 独立远端基准 工作流成功；network／full 可比；失败 repeat 与 PID 数漂移单独保留 运行 43198501217、汇总、原始 ZIP 合并 PR #1 已合并到 main 4a137a3b6918c9307056dbba674345733be84acb 首次发布尝试 11 个验证 job 与打包通过；crates.io 返回 403 Forbidden: authentication failed 运行 43201351434、publish 日志 凭据选择修复 优先 CARGO_REGISTY_TOKEN，fallback CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN，传给 Cargo 使用标准环境变量 6a6f450670ea88353e48c72b7b9bf4a35eab30eb 第二次发布尝试 11 个验证 job 与打包再次通过；确认选择 CARGO_REGISTY_TOKEN 后上传仍被 403 认证拒绝 运行 43201957205、publish 日志 CI 结论对应表中指定的提交，不自动代表未来变更。资源测试只覆盖稳定单 PID 的持续刷新及反复创建销毁；它没有证明所有模块在任意工作负载下永不泄漏。 尚未完成或尚待验收 [ ] 在仓库 Actions secrets 中更新有效的 CARGO_REGISTY_TOKEN，重跑 43201957205 的失败 publish job，保持候选 SHA 6a6f450；随后确认 crates.io zsys/0.1.0 发布、索引与校验和匹配。 [ ] 确认对应 Git Tag 与 GitHub Release 创建成功；两次运行中这些步骤均因上传失败而跳过。 [ ] 本地完整网络与所有模块组合的同范围对比：sysinfo 在当前受限 namespace 返回空接口，公平性门禁阻止生成速度倍率。 [ ] 补充进程数完全匹配的远端 5,000／10,000 规模结果：运行已完成，但背景进程变化使双方采样数量范围不同，当前不报速度倍率。请求 100 的远端组实际为 164，不标为 100 进程结果。 [ ] 调查远端 cold_basic 的一次部分扫描失败并复测；成功工作流不表示每个重复都成功。 [ ] 进一步优化未达目标的 CPU、Memory、块 I/O、500 个及以上全进程刷新和 P99 延迟。 [ ] Windows、macOS、FreeBSD、Android、iOS 原生后端；当前这些平台的 core 可编译能力不等于原生采集完成。 性能判断的范围 本地同范围数据表明，zsys 在内存、进程与限定挂载容量等多条路径上降低了中位延迟，并在已测稳定热路径中消除了 Rust 分配请求。CPU 的真实间隔采样中位数较低，但 P99 为 514.797 μs，高于 sysinfo 的 231.166 μs。5,000 进程全刷新中位数为 43.247 ms，仍远高于 1 ms 目标。CPU／Memory 的保留缓冲也比对应 sysinfo 路径大。因此当前结果不能概括为“所有路径更快、更省内存”，更不能宣布用户的最终发布验收已经全部完成。 独立 AMD EPYC runner 上，完整网络中位延迟为 917.941／1,191.003 μs，完整组合为 3.646／6.383 ms（zsys／sysinfo），有效中位比值分别为 1.30×／1.75×；网络仍未达 30 μs，组合仍未达 1 ms。网络分配次数更少，但请求字节和保留堆更多。数字、采样范围与原始证据见 验收报告 和 BENCHMARKS.md。

title: 采样语义与 API
body: 按需采集 Linux 的处理器、内存、进程与存储状态，提供可借用的数据视图。 采样语义与 API zsys 的一次刷新表示一次明确的读取操作。调用者选择模块、调用时间和需要的详情，采集器保存本模块上次成功观测及可复用存储。所有单位、差分和失败状态都应与对应快照一起使用。 时间、快照与刷新边界 Sample 包含 timestamp_ns 和 sequence。Linux 采集器的时间戳来自该实例创建时建立的 Instant 原点，因此可用于同一实例前后采样的差分。不同采集器的数值没有共同原点；它们也不是 Unix 时间或系统启动时间。若业务需要跨模块时间轴，应在调用刷新前后额外记录应用自己的共享时钟。 CPU、内存、网络计数器、块 I/O、挂载列表和文件系统容量在首次成功采样前没有有效观测。相应计数器快照的 sequence == 0 表示尚未成功采样，读取接口上的 Option 用于避免把初始化零值当作真实数据。硬件字段另用 HardwareValue 区分尚未采样和读取失败，硬件数值的样本序号表示读取尝试，字段可能为 Unavailable。 System::new() 不执行文件系统访问，模块在首次显式刷新时初始化。refresh_memory 不会刷新 CPU；refresh_process 不会扫描其他 PID。refresh_basic 依次刷新 CPU、内存、进程、网络计数器和块 I/O，较早步骤成功后即保留新值；后续步骤失败时，剩余模块仍保留自己的旧值。这种组合保留了每个模块的真实时序。相关断言见 tests/system.rs。 SystemSnapshot 是可由调用者组合的 CPU／内存数据类型，本身不会执行采集，也不会使不同时间的观测变成原子快照。CpuTimes、Memory 等 Copy 数据可以直接复制；进程等含拥有型字段的记录可以按需 clone。借用视图避免在每次读取结果时重新构造整个集合。 CPU 使用率 系统与单核 CPU 百分比来自两次累计 tick 的差。CpuTimes 累计 user、nice、system、idle、iowait、irq、softirq 和 steal；guest 时间已经包含在 user/nice 中，不重复累加。实现将 idle 和 iowait 视为空闲，计算： busy_percent = 100 × (Δtotal − Δidle − Δiowait) / Δtotal 首次观测、累计值回退或 Δtotal == 0 时，使用率为 None。Linux 文档说明 iowait 也可能下降，因此该情况会使当前差分无效。CpuCollector 每次发现当前在线 CPU；在线集合变化时重建聚合基线，仍存在且身份一致的单核可以继续差分。实现和回归测试见 src/cpu.rs、tests/collectors.rs，字段来源见 proc_stat(5)。 进程 CPU 百分比以一颗逻辑 CPU 为 100%，使用成功观测之间的单调时间间隔： cpu_percent = 100 × Δ(user_ticks + system_ticks) / (ticks_per_second × elapsed_seconds) 多线程进程同时占用两颗逻辑 CPU 时可以接近 200%。代码不按机器核数、CPU affinity 或 cgroup 配额再归一化。Processes 为各 PID 保存各自的采样时间；函数执行了多少微秒，不会被用作两次采样之间的时间。第一次读取、PID 复用、前次不可访问、计数器回退或无效时间间隔会得到 None。该公式在 src/process.rs 有确定性测试。 高频读取不会增加内核 CPU tick 的分辨率。短间隔内可能得到零增量、None，或量化明显的瞬时进程百分比；应用可按业务需要延长间隔或对多次结果平滑。CpuCollector::refresh_frequencies 单独读取 sysfs scaling_cur_freq 并转为 Hz；它不修改使用率采样时间，频率也不保证等于芯片此刻的实际运行频率。频率字段没有单独的内置时间戳，调用者如需精确 freshness 应记录调用时间。参见 CPUFreq 文档。 进程身份、可见性与详情 ProcessId 由 PID 和 start_time_ticks 组成，区分同一次系统启动中的 PID 复用。start_time_since_boot(ticks_per_second) 把启动 tick 转为启动后的 Duration，保留可获得的亚秒精度。该值不是墙上时钟日期；跨重启持久化身份时，应用还需要自行关联启动会话。时钟 tick 和页大小由原生 sysconf 读取；fixture 可以通过 with_parameters 显式给定。字段定义见 proc_pid_stat(5)。 Processes::refresh 每次枚举当前可见 PID 并读取选中的记录，复用表项、名称缓冲区和基线。增量体现在状态维护与生命周期变化；它没有订阅内核事件，也没有跳过全部已有 PID 的实时计数器读取。ProcessChanges 的 added、removed、reused、failed 描述生命周期与采样结果，updated 统计成功读取的数量，包含新建和复用 PID，并不表示每个字段发生变化。 情况 全表 refresh 的处理 新 PID 可读取 插入记录，CPU 基线为 None PID 相同、启动 tick 改变 标记 reused，替换身份，重置 CPU 基线 原记录本轮无法访问 保留历史数据和时间戳，标记 Inaccessible、Vanished 或 Invalid，清除 CPU 使用率 原 PID 未出现在成功枚举结果 从可见进程表移除 整个目录枚举失败 返回错误，保留已有表 refresh_pid(pid) 只更新该 PID，发现其已经消失时移除该项，不会顺带清理其他 PID。enumerate_pids() 返回复用缓冲区中的排序去重列表，不读取进程内容、不更新快照。枚举后进程仍可立刻退出，后续读取必须处理错误。failures() 对应最近一次全表刷新；单 PID 调用的错误通过返回值和该记录的 availability 表达。生命周期、权限、快速创建退出与枚举测试见 tests/processes.rs。 权限与 namespace 决定采集范围。hidepid、容器 PID namespace 或挂载视图可以让进程完全不出现在 /proc；从表中移除表示不再可见，业务不能仅据此推断其已在宿主机终止。name 保存内核 comm 的原始字节，它可能被内核截短，也可能不是 UTF-8。线程数量是记录字段；当前 API 不展开每个线程为独立进程对象。 默认进程 memory_bytes 读取 /proc/PID/statm 的 resident 页数并转换为字节。counters.resident_pages 则保留 /proc/PID/stat 的原始近似字段，两者可能不同。Linux 对这类 RSS 统计仍有近似说明；它们没有提供 PSS，也不等同于逐映射计算的精确内存。共享页会出现在多个进程的 RSS 中，不宜直接求和当作系统已用内存。参见 proc_pid_statm(5)。 details(pid, options) 按需读取 executable、NUL 分隔的命令行、四组 UID 和四组 GID，返回拥有型 ProcessDetails。用户／组 ID 顺序为 real、effective、saved-set、filesystem；当前 API 不执行用户名数据库查询。命令行保留空参数和非 UTF-8 字节。每个详情字段为 Detail::NotRequested、Detail::Unavailable(ErrorKind) 或 Detail::Value，空值与读失败各有语义。 详情操作通过同一个打开的 PID 目录读取，并在前后校验身份。它返回读取时的 ProcessDetails.id，不会自动替换进程表中较早的记录。把详情附加到已有快照前，应比较两个 id，如 README 的示例所示。详情读取会分配拥有型结果，适合按需请求而非无条件放入每个高频循环。 内存 Memory 的容量单位均为字节，procfs 的 kB 数值按 1024 转换。used_bytes() 是 total 减 available；swap_used_bytes() 是 swap total 减 swap free。free_bytes 与 available_bytes 分别表示空闲页和内核估计的可用容量，含义不同。 当内核未提供 MemAvailable 时，解析器使用 free、buffers、cached、reclaimable、shared 的已记录近似算法，MemorySample::available_is_estimate 明确标记此路径。已有 MemAvailable 时使用内核值。解析失败保留旧成功快照，测试见 tests/collectors.rs；来源见 proc_meminfo(5)。默认读取所在挂载视图的 /proc/meminfo，不自动替换为容器 cgroup 内存配额。 磁盘、挂载与容量 DiskIoCollector 从 /proc/diskstats 获取块设备和分区计数器。sector 固定按 512 字节计算，与设备物理扇区大小分开；in-flight 是当前进行中的 I/O 数量，属于 gauge。DiskDelta 对支持的累计计数器求差，遇到回退、设备名称变化或溢出时不生成有效差分。物理设备和它的分区可能表示同一批 I/O，混合求和会重复统计。参见 Linux I/O statistics 和 tests/disks.rs。 Mounts::refresh 只发现挂载及其路径、类型、源设备和选项。它解码内核的路径转义，按挂载身份保留仍匹配的容量样本。Filesystem::refresh 才会调用原生 statvfs 获取容量；free_bytes 包含所有空闲块，available_bytes 表示普通用户可用部分。失败会保留上次成功容量与时间戳，并更新 last_error。当前容量 FFI 支持 Linux 64 位 ABI，其他位宽返回 Unsupported。参见 statvfs(3)。 容量查询可能因远程或故障文件系统阻塞。调用者可以使用 iter_mut() 挑选本地挂载点；refresh_capacities() 会遍历所有已发现挂载，并返回成功／失败数量。库不设置内核文件系统访问超时，也不在后台执行这些调用。 网络 Networks::refresh_counters 读取 /proc/net/dev 的全部十六个累计计数器，包含字节、包、错误、丢弃等字段。完整解析和重复接口校验成功后才提交快照，旧接口移除，新接口建立基线。Network.delta 与 interval_ns 可用于应用自己的速率计算；计数器回退时差分为 None。字段来源见 Linux interface statistics。 refresh_details 独立获取地址、掩码、ifindex、flags、MAC、MTU 和可用的驱动链路速率，详情带有自己的 sampled_at_ns。AddressSource::Getifaddrs 表示原生地址列表；明确的 netlink 权限或协议限制会启用 IoctlProcfs 后备：IPv4 通过只读 ioctl 枚举，IPv6 来自 /proc/net/if_inet6。后备 flags 受 SIOCGIFFLAGS 返回范围限制。IPv6 scope ID 保留，六字节 MAC 不适用的硬件类型返回 None。参见 getifaddrs(3)、netdevice(7)。 详情发现 ifindex 变化时清除相关差分，避免跨接口复用计算速率。若同名接口的移除和重建都发生在两次详情刷新之间，纯计数器路径可能无法识别该生命周期；需要更强身份检查的应用应同时安排详情刷新。refresh() 依次调用 counters 和 details，因此详情失败时，计数器可能已是新样本，调用者应分别检查它们的时间。 网络详情始终读取当前进程所在的网络 namespace；with_proc_root 提供的 fixture 路径只替换计数器文件。详情刷新和新接口发现可以分配内存，稳定接口的计数器路径复用存储。 硬件与 GPU Hardware::refresh_inventory 发现 hwmon、thermal zone 和 DRM primary card，connector 与 render 节点不作为重复 GPU。缺失 class 目录表示没有暴露此类设备，其他目录错误保留旧 inventory。refresh_info 读取 DMI 描述，refresh_temperatures、refresh_gpus 分别读取已知设备的可用数值。硬件字段通过 HardwareValue::{NotSampled, Unavailable, Value} 表达结果。 thermal zone 的 raw_input 单位是毫摄氏度，celsius() 提供换算。hwmon 保留驱动原始固定点值：多数驱动使用毫摄氏度，部分 ADC 驱动输出毫伏，因此库不对所有 hwmon 输入统一作温度换算。fault == Value(true) 表示该通道的测量存在硬件故障。hwmon 与 thermal 两个视图可能重复描述同一个物理传感器，inventory 保留来源供应用选择。依据见 hwmon ABI、thermal sysfs API。 GPU 识别包含 DRM card、PCI vendor/device ID、驱动及可用产品名称。VRAM 总量／已用字节和 busy 百分比来自驱动公开的可选 sysfs 文件，当前覆盖 AMDGPU 提供这些属性的情形。缺少属性返回 Unavailable，不会生成零占用数据；NVML、完整 Intel/AMD/NVIDIA 遥测和 GPU 控制不在当前实现内。依据见 PCI sysfs、AMDGPU memory、AMDGPU activity，fixture 见 tests/hardware.rs。 内存复用、并发与调度 采集器拥有自己的缓冲区和状态，通过 &mut self 刷新，通过借用读取快照。新 PID、较长名称、新接口、CPU 热插拔或更大的文件都可能扩容。Vec 和 HashMap 在规模回落后通常保留容量，目的是复用；这部分驻留容量与未释放对象泄漏应分开测量。当前没有自动缩容策略或公共 reserve/shrink 接口，调用者可以丢弃并重建采集器以释放保留容量，同时建立新的时间与差分基线。 公共 procfs 文件复用打开的文件与读取缓冲；进程记录按本次身份读取，文件所有权由 Rust RAII 管理。读取缓冲存在记录大小上限，过大的输入返回错误，避免无限增长；PID 表的内存仍随可见进程规模增长。LinuxCollector::processes() 是早期兼容接口，每次构造 Vec<ProcessRecord>；高频调用应使用保留表的 Processes。 独立实例可以放在不同线程中使用。库没有全局采样锁；同一实例的并发刷新仍需要调用者提供同步。Send + Sync 编译检查和并行独立采集见 tests/system.rs。tests/process_resources.rs 对持续存活的进程采集器检查 Rust 分配、保留字节和文件描述符，并支持 ZSYS_SOAK_SECONDS 延长运行时间。 Cadence 接收调用者提供的单调纳秒时间。先检查 is_due(now)，刷新成功后调用 mark_success(now)；失败不推进成功时间。set_interval_ns 修改采样策略，不改写先前观测；reset 清除调度基线。它不会 sleep、spawn 线程或隐式刷新。示例见 examples/cadence.rs。 公共 API 索引 模块／类型 入口与数据 cpu CpuTimes::total、busy_percent_since；八类累计 tick memory Memory；used_bytes、swap_used_bytes process ProcessId::start_time_since_boot、ProcessCounters::cpu_percent_since、ProcessState parse parse_cpu_stat、parse_meminfo、process_stat／RawProcess、兼容 parse_process_stat、ParseError disk DiskCounters、DiskDelta、DiscardCounters、FlushCounters、Capacity、RawDisk、RawMount、DISKSTATS_SECTOR_BYTES、diskstats/mountinfo 解析与转义解码 network NetworkCounters::delta_since、RawNetwork、parse_net_dev_line snapshot／sampling Sample、SystemSnapshot、Cadence CpuCollector
