Condition Behavior Partial UTF-8 or control sequence Continue normal PTY processing for at most 250 ms to reach a complete parser boundary; otherwise refuse and preserve the partial state for later input Completed stateless Kitty/native UI capability queries, without persistent resources or pending protocol input Allow and retain queued replies Actual Kitty/Sixel graphics or native UI state Conservatively refuse, even after image deletion or a terminal reset Unfinished graphics/query transfer, including a zero-byte pending transfer Refuse while pending state remains Pending OSC 52, paste transfer, active overlay, running text-plugin work or pending child reaping Refuse until normal handling completes or the active UI/operation is closed Checkpoint would exceed 128 sessions or 128 MiB total Refuse before handover Target cannot decode the format/state or does not return the expected acknowledgement Keep the current broker; validator deadline is 10 seconds Ordinary ED2 screen erasure preserves the prior graphics history classification; it does not create external-protocol history or clear an existing unsafe history. Older running brokers may already have marked a stateless query as unsupported. A newer CLI cannot retroactively change that broker's classification. Keep those sessions available and use the updated executable for new work. The CLI waits up to 60 seconds for its response. A parser-boundary refusal does not discard buffered input: when the remaining UTF-8 or sequence bytes arrive, the existing terminal can continue parsing them normally. Native windows and renderer resources are rebuilt after a successful handover. They may briefly disappear; compositor placement and uninterrupted physical frames are not guaranteed. If the new executable restores the sessions but cannot reopen a display, it returns window_error and the CLI exits nonzero. The broker and PTYs remain alive. Restore display access and use ztty attach with the same ZTTY_SOCKET to reopen the retained sessions. This recovery path is implemented but was not exercised by this round of reload tests. Moving from a 0.5.0 broker A broker from the published 0.5.0 release has no checkpoint/restore handover support. A newer CLI receives a safe refusal; it cannot retrofit the capability into the running process. Keep the old windows open until their work finishes. Install or build ztty 0.5.1 with its pinned dependencies, then start a new independent broker pool separated from the old executable for new work. An existing broker for the same new ELF may be reused. From an older ztty shell, clear its inherited socket only for this new launch: env -u ZTTY_SOCKET /absolute/path/to/new-ztty --name new-work -e /bin/bash The new window inherits its new broker's address. Reload-capable brokers can then use ztty reload for later compatible executable replacements. Older windows remain available alongside them during this one-time transition. Verification scope The 2026-11-20 performance and reload report records successful software and GPU-path handovers between two different ELF builds, plus safe refusal by the legacy broker. It identifies the tested source commits, executable hashes and renderer environments, and records the retained process, PTY, terminal and workspace checks. The final checks also sample complete old/new frames during tab switches and verify synchronized-output hold and explicit commit on private Xvfb displays. These finite pixel samples establish the recorded test results; they do not guarantee uninterrupted frames on every physical desktop or compositor. The runtime iteration report adds stateless-query and ED2 checks, refused stateful-resource controls, and native detach/exec/reattach coverage. The tests verify child and PTY identities, restored pixels and continued input/output; they do not serialize arbitrary Kitty, Sixel or UI resources. To compare two reload-capable local builds: python3 tests/reload_runtime.py --binary /absolute/path/to/before-ztty \ --target /absolute/path/to/after-ztty \ --output artifacts/reload-runtime/report.json Opening a separate broker for another build On Linux, a new standalone window launched without an explicit ZTTY_SOCKET compares the running executable with the current build. If the default broker belongs to an older build, the new window uses a separate broker for the current build. Later independent windows from the same build reuse that broker, including when identical binaries are installed at different paths or the old default broker exits. Existing windows and their children continue running. Tab/split operations with a target, explicit ZTTY_SOCKET addresses, and attach/control/MCP operations keep their existing routing. Installing a binary alone does not move sessions between brokers. An explicit reload keeps the sessions inside their existing broker. The selected address is inherited by the new window's child environment, so ztty attach, ztty list, and related commands started inside that window address its own broker. To address that pool from another shell, read printf '%s\n' "$ZTTY_SOCKET" inside the new window and set that value explicitly for the external command. Without an explicit address, non-GUI control commands continue to address the default broker. Finish work in older windows normally; closing them is not required to open a new independent window on the new build.

title: SSH sessions
body: 原生终端应用，在 Linux 上支持窗口、命令行与 MCP 共用会话。 SSH sessions ztty 0.6.1 can open a Linux terminal session over SSH and keep its PTY running after the connection closes. The remote ztty broker owns the shell, parsed screen and history. An SSH client is a view of that state. Reattaching a named session keeps its process and shell variables; its creation command runs once. This implements persistent SSH sessions in ztty. Both ends use ztty's own session protocol; it does not connect to a Rex Server or use Rex's wire format. Connect and reconnect Install ztty 0.6.1 or later on the local and remote Linux machines. The remote executable is found on the SSH user's PATH or at ~/.local/bin/ztty. ztty ssh dev main ztty ssh ssh://alice@build.example:2222 build ztty ssh -i ~/.ssh/build_key dev build ztty ssh -F ~/.ssh/work_config dev build ztty ssh --remote-bin /opt/ztty/bin/ztty dev build The first command creates main if it is absent and otherwise reattaches it. The default session name is main. Names contain 1–64 ASCII letters, digits, dots, underscores or hyphens. Names cannot start with - or be . or ... SSH aliases, IPv6 addresses, ports, identity files, agents and host-key checks use the system OpenSSH client. Press Ctrl+] to detach, including when an application enables Kitty's enhanced keyboard protocol. Closing the local window also disconnects its view. Run the same command to reconnect. A session that has finished keeps its final screen and exit status until explicitly closed. ztty ssh --list dev ztty ssh --close dev build The headless broker survives the SSH connection. A reboot, killing the broker, or a host policy that kills every process in a logged-out user's account ends its processes. It does not save running processes across machine restarts. Tabs, splits and ownership In an SSH window, Ctrl+Shift+T creates another remote shell on the same host. Ctrl+Shift+E/O splits right/down. The new pane gets an independent generated name beginning with pane-; ztty ssh --list HOST lists it for later reattachment. These actions inherit connection settings, and use the remote default shell. A previous pane's explicit creation command is not rerun in a new pane. The CLI can target an existing local ztty view using --tab LOCAL_SESSION, --split-right LOCAL_SESSION or --split-down LOCAL_SESSION. Both commands must address the same local broker (ZTTY_SOCKET selects it). Native tabs and splits currently use X11/XWayland. Independent windows also work on native Wayland. ztty ssh --observe dev build ztty ssh --takeover dev build An observer receives frames, discards input and leaves the writer's PTY size unchanged. A smaller observer sees the top-left portion; a larger one adds blank space. Attaching a second writer requires --takeover. Normal detach releases control; reconnect can reclaim a dead mux process using its PID and process start identity. Session identity checks protect every read and mutation from a closed-and-recreated name. OpenSSH shares the authenticated connection with ControlMaster=auto and a 60-second idle ControlPersist. Its control socket lives in an owner-only runtime directory. Each remote pane still has its own PTY and process. Commands and headless use Arguments after -- create the session's initial program. They are passed as literal arguments; use an explicit shell when shell syntax is wanted. ztty ssh dev build -- bash -lc 'cargo build; exec bash' ztty ssh --terminal dev build --terminal displays the remote session in the invoking terminal. The same multiplexer can also be used locally without a desktop: ztty mux attach work -- /bin/bash ztty mux list ztty mux attach --observe work ztty mux close work The default headless mux has a separate per-user broker namespace. An explicit ZTTY_SOCKET can isolate a test or choose an existing compatible broker. No additional network listener or tmux process is started. Display and performance The remote broker parses terminal output and answers device queries. Its view transfers text cells, colors and attributes, Unicode graphemes, hyperlinks, cursor state, alternate-screen state and input modes. Reconnect includes up to 2,000 recent history rows, within a 480 KiB frame budget. It projects terminal text; Kitty/Sixel image data, shell command marks and soft-wrap metadata are not included in this SSH view. An unchanged session parks a revision watcher without copying output or walking the screen. Changed frames are limited to one per 16 milliseconds. Stable-view updates redraw only changed rows and send necessary terminal state; initial attachment, resizing and screen switches redraw the full view. The terminal input queue and one pending output frame provide bounded backpressure. A slow or disconnected viewer cannot accumulate an unbounded transcript in the broker. Input acknowledgements wait until the remote PTY has accepted the entire input chunk. This prevents a large paste followed by Ctrl+] from losing its queued suffix. A PTY that stops accepting input for five seconds produces an explicit error; the client restores its terminal and releases input control. Reproduce the checks cargo test --locked --features wayland --test ssh_command --test mux_input --test terminal_frame cargo build --locked --release --features wayland python3 tests/ssh_mux.py --binary target/release/ztty --output artifacts/ssh-mux.json python3 tests/ssh_mux_gui.py --binary target/release/ztty \ --output artifacts/ssh-mux-gui.json --screenshot artifacts/ssh-mux-gui.png cargo run --locked --release --example ssh_frame_benchmark The SSH fixture creates temporary keys, a pinned known-host entry and a localhost-only sshd. It checks separate PTYs over one authentication, connection loss, reconnect without command reexecution, resize, observer isolation, byte input and exact exit status. GUI checks use an owned X server. Both fixtures clean up their own processes and leave existing sessions untouched.

title: Protocol scope
body: 原生终端应用，在 Linux 上支持窗口、命令行与 MCP 共用会话。 Protocol scope ztty 0.5.2 implements the following subset of public terminal protocols. The shared core is used by Linux, macOS, and Windows; native window integration and its verification status are described separately below. The 0.5.2 release report binds the current release's six-platform acceptance to its source and artifacts. Text and input protocols Protocol / behavior Scope ANSI / VT controls Cursor motion, save/restore, tabs, scrolling regions, erase, insert/delete, main/alternate screen, DEC line drawing SGR 16/256/RGB colors, semicolon and colon parameters, core attributes; font shaping and style rendering depend on the frontend UTF-8 Streaming decode across arbitrary chunks; CJK widths; complete extended grapheme clusters within bounded storage Kitty keyboard Flags 1/2/4/8/16, event reports, shifted alternatives, associated text, independent screen stacks; the Linux frontend does not supply a base-layout alternative Mouse DEC 9 (X10)/1000/1002/1003 tracking; legacy and SGR 1006 encoding Focus DEC 1004 Cursor appearance DECSCUSR block, underline, and bar with steady or blinking variants; DEC private modes 12 and 25 Bracketed paste DEC 2004; bounded paste with control-character sanitization Synchronized output DEC 2026, DECRQM, retained last frame, 150 ms recovery timeout OSC 0/2 Window title OSC 7 Working-directory metadata retained in the model OSC 8 Cell identity, history retention, underline, explicit Ctrl+click opening OSC 4/10/11 Color queries; reply with the request's BEL or ST terminator DSR / DA / DECRQM Implemented state reports; unknown modes report unsupported Window and cell size CSI 14 t reports text-area pixels; CSI 16 t reports cell pixels; CSI 18 t reports character dimensions XTGETTCAP TN=xterm-256color, Co=256, Tc; unknown capabilities report failure X11 clipboard Clipboard and primary selection, advertised text formats, UTF-8 and Latin-1 fallback, bounded INCR receiving OSC 52 Bounded clipboard requests with frontend policy; Linux enforces visible-view and input-ownership checks Native Wayland input XKB/compose and text-input-v3 preedit/commit; see Wayland configuration and limits The shared core retains extended grapheme clusters, including emoji ZWJ sequences, with at most 256 UTF-8 bytes per cluster and a bounded pool; this is separate from font rendering. Width changes reflow retained primary-screen soft wraps while preserving hard line boundaries. Alternate screens retain fixed-grid resize semantics, and history limits can evict content. See the core storage and reflow contract. Linux GPU text uses HarfBuzz run shaping; the Xft fallback draws Unicode cells without that complete-run shaping path. Linux supports italic glyphs and SGR 5/6 text blink. Cursor blinking remains separate. These capabilities do not establish identical complex-script or emoji presentation across every renderer. Primary DA uses CSI ? 62 ; 4 c: a VT220-style identification with the Sixel feature field. No other optional DA features are asserted. This also satisfies the minimum response length used by Kitty's graphics probe. Kitty graphics support and transport choices are established by their own queries. Kitty graphics zgraphics implements the bounded image lifecycle: receive image data, store decoded pixels, place an image, and delete its placements or data. zterm frames APC sequences and attaches placements to terminal content. The native frontend composites the resulting RGBA images; no Kitty renderer is embedded. Feature Implemented scope Transport Direct PTY data, t=d; base64 encoded. The Linux host also supplies bounded file (t=f), temporary-file (t=t) and shared-memory (t=s) reads Pixel formats f=24 RGB, f=32 RGBA, f=100 PNG; canonical storage is straight-alpha RGBA8 Compression Optional zlib, o=z, with bounded output Static actions Capability query a=q, transmit a=t, transmit and display a=T, place a=p, delete a=d Extensions Linux X11 integrates Kitty animation, Unicode placeholders and relative placements; extension acceptance records GPU and Xft coverage Transfer chunks m=1 continuation and m=0 final chunk; arbitrary PTY read boundaries; larger single APCs and repeated-action continuation headers from current clients Base64 endings Padded or unpadded final payload; nonfinal protocol chunks must contain complete groups without padding Identity Explicit image IDs i, image numbers I, automatic IDs, placement IDs p, replacement under an existing ID Geometry Source crop x/y/w/h, cell-relative offset X/Y, requested columns/rows c/r, viewport clipping Scaling Aspect ratio preserved; when both c and r are set, the image is centered within that box Cursor Placement advances the cursor according to its occupied box; C=1 leaves it unchanged Layers z >= 0 above text; negative z behind text; z < -1073741824 also behind explicitly colored backgrounds Deletion Visible placements, ID/number/placement, cursor or cell, row, column, z-index, and ID range selectors; uppercase forms free selected data once unreferenced Replies Success/error responses for identified requests; q=1 suppresses success, q=2 suppresses all replies; queries do not place or retain images Content lifetime Full-screen scroll can retain images in history; partial-region scroll moves placements anchored in that region; primary and alternate screens have independent scenes An image appears only after its final transfer completes successfully. Replacing an image ID removes the old placements; changing a placement ID replaces that placement. Cell metrics supplied by the frontend determine pixel geometry and size replies. Both image IDs and their generation values are used when deciding whether a renderer's cached pixels are still current. Existing kitten icat clients can emit image payloads larger than 4096 encoded bytes in one APC and use unpadded base64. The streaming receiver accepts that shape while retaining at most a 512-byte header and a 4096-byte encoded staging buffer. It incrementally decodes into a separately bounded pending transfer. This avoids accumulating an entire encoded APC in a general control-string buffer. Client emission behavior can be inspected in Kitty's graphics command writer. Image limits and recovery These are default limits per graphics scene, as defined by zgraphics::Limits: Resource Default bound Width or height 8192 pixels One decoded image 32 MiB Retained decoded image storage 32 MiB, counting vector capacity Pending transfer 16 MiB Stored images 128 Placements 512 Both dimensional and byte limits apply. A nominally permitted width and height can still exceed the decoded-image byte limit. Primary and alternate scenes have separate quotas; these figures are not a process-wide memory ceiling. PNG decoding uses temporary buffers, and frontends retain display resources. The memory accounting section explains those additional costs. Empty scenes allocate no image storage. PNG headers, chunk lengths, CRCs, and dimensions are checked before decoding; nonessential metadata is removed. Malformed PNG, incorrect pixel lengths, bad base64, unsupported options, and quota overruns are rejected. A pending m=1 transfer does not consume ordinary text between APCs. CAN, SUB, or a new escape sequence can cancel an unfinished APC, so a missing terminator does not trap subsequent escape sequences. Tests exercise valid text, keyboard input, and a new valid image after rejection. The test sources are zgraphics tests, zterm tests, and the graphics acceptance suite. Remaining boundaries Area Current boundary External Kitty transport The file/temporary-file/shared-memory host reader is Linux-only; macOS and Windows use direct transmission Image decoding and protocols APNG and ReGIS remain unsupported; Kitty frame animation is a separate implemented protocol Native Wayland No tabs, splits, workspace containers or runtime reload; desktop scaling and real IME/GPU acceptance remain separate work Text layout Complex-script and emoji presentation depend on the font and renderer; Xft does not provide the GPU path's complete-run HarfBuzz shaping Applications should query the required transport and extension capabilities. Successful static-image display alone does not establish full Kitty compatibility. Sixel The shared no_std core accepts ESC P ... q Sixel images, commits only at ST, and reuses the existing RGBA scene and native renderers. RGB/HLS color registers, repeat compression, raster extents, aspect ratio, transparent/opaque backgrounds, color overprinting, and arbitrary PTY chunk boundaries are implemented. Modes 80, 1070 and 8452 control display origin/scrolling, palette scope and cursor placement. Default scrolling starts at the text cursor and ends at column zero on the following text row; display mode preserves the cursor. Details and resource limits are in zgraphics. Sixel images use the scene's behind-text layer and remain anchored to cell rows. Text writes and partial erases clear intersecting Sixel source pixels; Kitty placements are unaffected. At scaled boundaries, a whole intersecting source pixel is cleared, as documented in the Sixel erasure regression. Partial-region scrolling follows the anchor policy. Shared palettes seed later images; changing a register does not recolor an already completed RGBA image. These limits remain distinct from complete VT340 framebuffer compatibility. Decoder validation uses the DEC manual, the modern xterm control reference, and an independent libsixel pixel comparison. The measurement records source/binary hashes, chunk sizes, exact pixel results and reference-decoder discrepancies. These decoder results are distinct from the native GUI acceptance below. Acceptance coverage The 0.5.2 release report records successful Verify and native Linux, macOS and Windows jobs on x86_64 and AArch64 for source 6e2ce246b0b50e6b82da99756832feae6e966f21. Each Linux artifact has 22 reports with 312 recorded checks, including 65 Wayland checks, bound to that artifact's ELF. The Linux GPU-path tests use software Mesa; they do not measure physical GPU performance, display latency or general desktop IME compatibility. This documentation update adds no new test execution. Historical acceptance snapshots The reports below retain their original source, binary and test scope. For example, the earlier native record at 2dc6769 passed four Linux x86_64 GUI suites and 25 Windows x86_64 checks, while its ARM64 gates failed and macOS completed eight protocol checks. Those historical outcomes are not the current 0.5.2 release status. The GUI suite has passed 12 checks under an isolated Xvfb/X11 server, as recorded in the GUI result: legacy keyboard input; Kitty disambiguation; all five Kitty flags with modifier, repeat, and release events; resize and SIGWINCH; ASCII/CJK selection and clipboard; bracketed paste with control stripping; a 139,264-byte paste under backpressure; SGR mouse input; Shift gesture ownership; explicit OSC 8 opening; configured ARGB background and cursor rendering; and synchronized output across writes and Expose events. The large-paste assertion includes the 12 bytes of bracketed-paste delimiters, for 139,276 delivered bytes. Unit tests also cover screen state and query semantics. The optional --fcitx test runs Fcitx 5 with Pinyin on Xvfb and a private D-Bus session, checking ordinary key forwarding and Chinese text committed to the PTY. That run did not establish IBus or deliberately fragmented INCR coverage; current clipboard-transfer results are recorded in the 0.5.2 release report. The graphics suite has passed all seven groups on Linux/Xvfb through a real PTY and window-pixel readback, recorded in the graphics result: Graphics capability and cell/window-size replies, with no image placed by a query. RGB, RGBA, and PNG colors, including four alpha levels and split PNG transmission. Chunked transmission, placement, soft deletion, image replacement, and data deletion. Source crop, clipping to the text viewport, and images below explicit cell backgrounds. Scrolling, window resize, primary/alternate isolation, and deletion without residual pixels. Malformed images, excessive dimensions, invalid base64, interrupted transfers, and subsequent keyboard/image recovery. Unmodified kitten icat 0.50 detecting stream, displaying a photo with explicit inline transport, and displaying a transparent-edge PNG through automatic detection. The interrupted-transfer check observed 0 bytes of RSS growth between its before/after samples across 80 aborted uploads after earlier image tests warmed the process. This is an observation for that run, not a measurement of peak allocation or a general zero-growth guarantee. The test enforces a finite growth allowance and records the actual value in its JSON result. The live Hyprland/XWayland run also passed on Hyprland 0.57.2: kitten icat --detect-support selected stream, and the real tools displayed both the photo and transparent-edge PNG. Only the owned test window was captured. The session's normal X0 pathname was absent; the probe used and removed its own temporary socket alias to the existing same-user XWayland endpoint, without changing compositor or authorization settings. This was the real desktop server, separate from Xvfb. Native artifact verification also passed in workflow run 44165748395, on source 7535aa29f1a2728a78a446ffea6784dcbc2aae92: Native environment Observed coverage Evidence macOS Intel 8 session/protocol checks through a real AppKit application and Darwin PTY: geometry, cursor reply, image query, chunked RGBA, PNG, alternate screen, malformed-input recovery, deletion Native report macOS Apple Silicon The same 8 session/protocol checks through a native application Native report Windows x86_64 17 checks: native child/Unicode arguments, ConPTY query round trip, RGB/RGBA/PNG pixel readback, alpha, scrolling, clipping, resize, alternate screen, deletion, keyboard recovery Native report Both historical macOS reports explicitly record pixel_readback: not_performed and ime_keyboard: not_performed; they do not establish either capability. Later native window-pixel acceptance is recorded in the six-platform candidate report and the 0.5.2 release report; those results do not turn the earlier runs into pixel tests. The Windows result uses the actual packaged ConPTY runtime and native window pixels, with the binary hash recorded in its report. This final native run includes the DA1 serialization fix described above. Formal packaging and native checks are defined in the release workflow. References xterm control sequences Kitty keyboard protocol Kitty graphics protocol Kitty icat ECMA-48 numeric parameter format Synchronized output OSC 8 hyperlinks Unicode width rules zvte parser API

title: 文本扩展：用 zplugin 处理选区并复制
body: 原生终端应用，在 Linux 上支持窗口、命令行与 MCP 共用会话。 文本扩展：用 zplugin 处理选区并复制 ztty 现在可以注册并调用独立编译的原生文本扩展。按 Ctrl+Shift+P 打开命令面板，找到 Copy using 名称，确认后将选区交给扩展；没有选区时使用当前可见区域，包括向上滚动后看到的内容。成功结果写入剪贴板，随后显示短暂提示。结果不会自动输入到 shell。空结果、错误和取消会保留原剪贴板。 首个实际示例是 Dedent：复制缩进代码块时，删除各非空行共有的前导空格，保留相对缩进、中文、组合字符和原换行。它是一个普通动态库，使用与后续扩展相同的注册及调用接口；宿主没有识别示例名称的特殊分支。 使用 在仓库根目录编译终端和独立示例： cargo build --release -p ztty cargo build --release --manifest-path examples/dedent-plugin/Cargo.toml plugin_path=$(realpath examples/dedent-plugin/target/release/libztty_dedent_plugin.so) ./target/release/ztty plugin check "$plugin_path" env -u ZTTY_SOCKET ./target/release/ztty --text-plugin "dedent=$plugin_path" plugin check 实际加载库、创建接口实例、销毁实例并检查合作卸载。新窗口中选中文字，按 Ctrl+Shift+P，输入 dedent，选择 Copy using dedent。面板也支持搜索 plugin。运行期间按 Esc 取消；若当前打开了搜索或命令面板，Esc 先关闭最上面的面板。 env -u ZTTY_SOCKET 只让这次新窗口启动自行选择当前构建的 broker，适用于从旧版本窗口试用候选二进制，不改变原有会话。正常安装后的独立启动无需这一步。显式 ZTTY_SOCKET 仍表示使用指定 broker。 也可以在配置文件中保存注册： text-plugin = dedent=/absolute/path/libztty_dedent_plugin.so text-plugin = another=/absolute/path/libanother.so 名称以 ASCII 字母开头，随后允许字母、数字、-、_，总长 1–32 字符。名称统一转为小写；后出现的同名注册替换前一个。命令行可以重复指定 --text-plugin NAME=PATH，并覆盖配置中的同名项。最多注册 8 项；路径必须是绝对 UTF-8 路径，允许空格，最长 4096 字节。注册不会加载库；只有主动执行动作或 plugin check/run 时才加载。注册规则 配置热重载沿用终端现有机制，也可按 Ctrl+Shift+R。修改或移除正在使用的注册会取消该次调用。重新载入的是文件内容；仅通过命令行提供的注册需要同时写入配置才能在重载后保留。关闭所属视图，或切换到隐藏它的标签页，也会取消调用。 命令行可以单独转换标准输入，不启动窗口： printf ' first\n second\n' | ./target/release/ztty plugin run "$plugin_path" 成功输出不附加额外换行。等待标准输入结束属于普通管道读取；执行期限从工作进程启动时开始计算。 接口与工作方式 共享接口 crate、当前宿主和示例统一使用 zplugin = "=0.3.1"，接口保持 #![no_std]。ztty-plugin-api 0.1.0 尚待首次发布，示例通过本仓库的路径依赖构建。接口标识是 dev.project-z.ztty.text，版本为 1： fn transform( &mut self, input: &str, output: &mut [u8], ) -> Result<u64, zplugin::Error>; 输入和输出借用仅在调用内有效。扩展把 UTF-8 结果写入宿主提供的缓冲区，返回有效字节数。宿主检查返回长度和 UTF-8，再决定是否写剪贴板。修改这个签名需要新的应用接口版本；不能在相同版本下改变 ABI。 每个库提供一个文本动作，可以注册不同名称和不同库。扩展通过 zplugin::interface 定义代理，使用 zplugin::export! 导出，并明确实现合作卸载的 UnloadSafe 契约。实例不能在调用结束后留下使用库内代码或借用内存的线程、任务、回调或注册。可直接从 Dedent 源码 开始实现。 示例拥有独立 Cargo workspace，让扩展使用 std，同时避免 Cargo 特征合并把 std 带进终端宿主。zplugin 核心和共享接口保持 no_std；宏工具的编译依赖不会成为终端运行时依赖。 一次界面调用按以下顺序执行： 用户确认动作，终端快照选区或当前可见文本。 broker 启动当前终端映像的独立 worker。库在 worker 内加载，broker 不调用库代码。 worker 创建实例、转换文本、销毁实例，然后调用合作卸载。 broker 验证完整结果和正常退出，在保留退出 worker 身份时清理其进程组，再回收 worker、写剪贴板。 工作进程使用独立进程组；GUI 对通信描述符做非阻塞读写，每轮限制工作量。关闭视图后仍保留作业对象，直到对应子进程被回收，避免遗留结果写入后来打开的视图。无扩展作业时不启动 worker、不建立扩展描述符或定时器；PTY 读入、VT 解析和逐字符绘制路径不调用扩展。宿主实现 · 界面接入 限额与适用范围 项目 限额或行为 单次输入、输出 各 1 MiB，UTF-8 母进程执行期限 2 秒，超时取消作业 worker 自身备用期限 3 秒的 alarm；母进程退出时终止直接 worker CPU 时间 1 秒 虚拟地址空间 256 MiB；不是常驻内存统计 文件描述符 最多 64；执行前关闭非标准描述符 core dump 禁用 并发 每视图一次调用，每 broker 最多 8 个未回收作业 失败处理 丢弃整次结果，保留剪贴板，显示短暂错误 原生扩展拥有当前用户权限，必须信任其代码和依赖。进程分离、执行期限与资源限额约束出错的扩展，不构成安全沙箱；不能用它执行不可信的原生代码。插件应遵守合作卸载约定，不能把测试夹具中故意泄漏子进程的方式作为实现示例。 本次宿主与 GUI 入口仅接入 Linux，在 x86-64 Linux 的原生动态库和私有 Xvfb 上验证。执行前通过 close_range 关闭继承描述符，因此要求 Linux 5.9 或更新版本；旧内核会拒绝启动该 worker。没有把共享 no_std 接口的可移植性当成 Windows/macOS GUI 已支持，也没有测量物理显示器延迟。 复现检查 以下命令分别构建真正独立链接的库、验证 CLI 生命周期，再验证真实 XTEST/剪贴板/PTY： python3 tests/build_text_plugins.py --output artifacts/zplugin python3 tests/plugin_cli.py --binary target/release/ztty --example artifacts/zplugin/example.so --fixtures artifacts/zplugin --output artifacts/zplugin/cli.json python3 tests/plugin_gui.py --binary target/release/ztty --example artifacts/zplugin/example.so --fixture artifacts/zplugin/fixture-valid.so --artifacts artifacts/zplugin/gui GUI 检查使用新建的私有 Xvfb、独立 broker socket 和合成文本，不操作用户桌面、剪贴板或现有会话。故障库覆盖接口版本不匹配、拒绝合作卸载、错误长度、非法 UTF-8、panic、原生崩溃、超时、CPU 限额、异常 stdout、遗留子进程通道以及母进程退出。它只用于测试，不应安装成日常扩展。 历史验证记录（zplugin 0.3.0） 验证源码为 68030066cb18e97fa5677a77881d54188fdc93f3，Linux ELF SHA-256 为 ec064a5220f3308f7c6722484f2e81a29314782241233f8668b450d07e517c51。同一 ELF 上的 CLI 22 项、私有 Xvfb GUI 10 项、日常工作流 19 项与重绘 11 项全部通过。Clippy 以 -D warnings 通过；Windows GNU 前端通过 cargo check，这不代表 Windows 已接入插件宿主。注册规则 2 项、SessionCore 真实 PTY 9 项与 Dedent 2 项测试通过，对应源码未被后续 worker 收尾修复修改。macOS 未测试。 独立审查发现并直接复现了一个退出边界：插件子进程关闭标准描述符后，原 worker 可以正常返回，而子进程仍留在进程组。修复使用 waitid(WNOWAIT) 保留已退出 leader 的身份，先终止属于本次调用的进程组，再 waitpid 回收；新增故障用例验证该子进程也被终止并由测试进程回收。测试没有按进程名称清理，也没有触碰用户会话。 验证汇总 · CLI 与生命周期 · GUI 检查 · 基线复现 · 依赖特征图 命令面板中的注册动作（历史附件） 选区处理后的轻量复制反馈（历史附件）

title: Input protocol compatibility
body: 原生终端应用，在 Linux 上支持窗口、命令行与 MCP 共用会话。 Input protocol compatibility The independent zinput codec remains no_std, uses alloc, forbids unsafe code and adds no dependencies. Unit tests verify generated bytes. The separate Linux X11 GUI gate below verifies delivery from X11 events through the frontend to an actual raw PTY, including terminal mode negotiation. Changes and protocol evidence Case Previous behavior Implemented behavior Primary reference Ctrl+Shift character shortcuts in legacy mode Shift collapsed into the Control mapping CSI-u preserves the Shift bit; Space retains its NUL exception Kitty legacy text keys, Ghostty keyboard encoder Printable keypad keys in normal keypad mode with Kitty flags 1–7 Digits and operators became private-use key events when disambiguation was enabled Digits, decimal and operators remain UTF-8 text; report-all retains keypad identity and associated text; Num Lock overrides application-keypad mode; with Num Lock off, application-keypad mode keeps functional events Kitty disambiguation, report-all Ctrl+tilde Literal tilde Control byte 30 Kitty legacy Control mapping X10 tracking mode 9 No report Left, middle and right presses, with no modifier bits; no releases, motion or wheel events XTerm mouse tracking, Ghostty mouse encoder Wheel buttons 4–7 and extra buttons 8–11 Only vertical Scroll events could be encoded Distinct button codes, horizontal wheel presses, extra-button releases and dragging XTerm other buttons and extended coordinates Button numbers in MouseEvent are zero-based. Callers therefore pass 5 for X11 button 6 and 7 for X11 button 8. Buttons beyond X11 number 11 are rejected because their encoding overlaps modifier bits. Wheel releases and motion are suppressed. Tracking mode and coordinate encoding remain separate decisions: setting sgr_mouse does not turn tracking on. The audit also checked existing Kitty alternate-key fields, base-layout fields, modifier transition state, event subfields, F3 disambiguation and associated-text release suppression. Those mechanisms already existed. New regression vectors exercise them without asserting that all native input paths are verified. Kitty protocol Reproducible checks Run from the repository root: cargo test --locked -p zinput -j 1 cargo clippy --locked -p zinput --all-targets -j 1 -- -D warnings cargo check --locked -p zinput --lib --target x86_64-unknown-none -j 1 The regression suite checks exact protocol vectors, all 32 Kitty flag combinations for Enter/Tab/Backspace release rules, all eleven xterm button numbers, invalid-button and coordinate overflow rejection, and append-only buffer reuse. Unknown or filtered mouse events must append no partial sequence. The bare-metal target check verifies that the library does not acquire a standard-library dependency. Verified Linux X11 integration The API keeps its existing public struct and enum shapes. Frontends can pass extra button numbers through the existing MouseEvent::Press, Release and Motion variants. MouseEvent::Scroll remains a vertical-wheel convenience. The Linux frontend now routes all four wheel directions and buttons 8–11, retains held extra-button state for dragging, and propagates terminal tracking mode 9. Its release routing follows the owner of the original press when Shift changes; local selection and configured actions cannot leak unmatched releases to the PTY. The real GUI regression in tests/input_gui.py passed all 27 vectors against the immutable candidate with SHA-256 b3d8fdb31d71ef9d1ed602b35673bf4648362fa354078e191e35a2cd75ac4631. The JSON evidence records exact expected and received bytes, binary/test/source hashes, the source commit and changes, pointer mapping, verified Xvfb socket ownership, and completed process cleanup. The actual window capture（历史附件） was visually checked: text is readable on the black background, overlays are closed, and no stray protocol bytes or drawing artifacts appear. Group Vectors Verified behavior Keyboard 3 Ctrl+I remains Tab; Ctrl+Shift+I produces distinct CSI-u; unshifted tilde plus Control produces byte 30 Wheels 4 Buttons 4–7 produce distinct vertical/horizontal SGR press codes without release reports Extra buttons 8 Buttons 8–11 retain identity on SGR press/release and mode-1002 drag motion Shift and press ownership 4 Primary/extra releases retain their remote destination after Shift changes; a local Shift press produces no remote release Focus 1 Mode-1004 focus-out/in replies acknowledge both real transitions; subsequent motion/release cannot reuse old held-button state X10 and mode changes 4 Left-button presses ignore modifiers; wheel/extra/motion probes are filtered; SGR selection is independent; resetting mode 9 preserves subsequently selected mode 1000 Configured actions 3 The custom search key and primary/extra mouse palette bindings consume their input and overlay text The private Xvfb pointer exposes buttons 1–10. Tested buttons 1, 3 and 4–10 use XTEST, as do keyboard input and pointer movement. Button 11 uses explicitly labelled XSendEvent press/release events with XTEST pointer motion because this virtual device cannot generate button 11. This establishes X11 event routing for button 11; physical-device delivery remains a separate gate. The Control+tilde case uses an unshifted tilde mapping on an unused keycode in the private server, leaving the user's keyboard configuration untouched. To reproduce, install Xvfb, Python Xlib and Pillow, build the Linux binary, then run from the repository root: python3 tests/input_gui.py \ --binary target/release/ztty \ --source-root "$PWD" \ --output artifacts/input-gui.json \ --screenshot artifacts/input-gui.png The script uses an isolated runtime directory, broker socket and owned Xvfb. It compares real PTY bytes, waits for focus reports rather than a fixed delay, and fails if its owned processes remain after cleanup. The --source-root tree must contain tools/isolated_xvfb.py and match the supplied binary. Remaining integration boundaries This gate covers the listed Linux X11 paths. Native Wayland, macOS and Windows event delivery, hardware buttons, IME/layout combinations, platform media keys, UTF-8 mouse coordinates, URXVT encoding and SGR pixel coordinates require their own acceptance tests. Complete Kitty/Ghostty equivalence is not established by these vectors. Ghostty separates mode-aware encoding from the frontend event source in its input guide. Numeric keypad routing acceptance (2026-11-19) The keypad report records 177 X11/PTY input vectors, 14 font scenarios and 4 keypad overlay scenarios. The GUI gate requires setxkbmap in addition to Xvfb, Python Xlib and Pillow. It configures numpad:pc and kpdl:dot only on its private server to exercise the actual Num Lock/Shift layer and physical decimal/Delete key. The codec retains explicit Kitty identity and event negotiation when Num Lock overrides DECKPAM. Clipboard images and application paste With the default bindings, Ctrl+Shift+V invokes ztty's text paste; Ctrl+V is delivered to the foreground application. In a locally running Codex CLI 0.170.0 composer, Ctrl+V requests an image attachment through Codex's own clipboard reader. Codex also recognizes a pasted path to an existing image file. These routes require the Codex process to have access to the corresponding clipboard or file; custom key bindings can change which application receives the shortcut. Codex image shortcut, clipboard reader, image-path handling. The ztty 0.5.1 X11/XWayland frontend requests TARGETS before reading selection data. It accepts an advertised UTF8_STRING, text/plain;charset=utf-8, text/plain, or STRING target and requires the returned property type to match. UTF-8 text is validated after a complete transfer, including all INCR chunks; STRING retains its Latin-1 conversion. An image-only selection produces a visible no-text message without requesting image bytes or putting them into the PTY. OSC 52 reads use the same type checks. The native Wayland frontend already selects advertised text MIME types and now also validates the completed UTF-8 response. The reported desktop advertised only image/png through a types-only Wayland query. Its X11 selection could not be inspected because the desktop denied X11 authorization; no real image contents were read. This establishes the available Wayland format, not the exact behavior of that desktop's XWayland conversion. The isolated Xvfb regression uses synthetic owners, including an image-only owner that incorrectly returns PNG bytes for text requests. Its scope is terminal text-paste negotiation and PTY delivery; it does not establish successful image attachment for every desktop or application. See the performance and reload report for the recorded results and their environment.

title: Daily workflow on Linux
body: 原生终端应用，在 Linux 上支持窗口、命令行与 MCP 共用会话。 Daily workflow on Linux The Linux shared runtime keeps the PTY and terminal model independent of its window. Search, command actions and configuration changes operate on that live session; they do not restart its child. The native macOS and Windows frontends do not implement the Linux search, session switcher, command palette or shared runtime. Windows implements font zoom and tab/split shortcuts in its native workspace; macOS does not yet implement font zoom or workspace UI. Keyboard and command palette Shortcut Action Ctrl+Shift+F Open history search; seed it with a single-line selection Enter / Shift+Enter in search (including keypad Enter) Next / previous match, wrapping at the ends F3 / Shift+F3 in search Next / previous match Alt+C in search Toggle case-sensitive / Unicode lowercase matching Ctrl+U or Ctrl+A in search/palette Clear the query Esc Close the temporary search/palette Ctrl+Shift+P Open the command palette; type to filter, arrows (including keypad Up/Down) to select, Enter (including keypad Enter) to run Ctrl+Shift+S Find a session by name, title or URI; focus its view or explicitly attach Ctrl+Shift+K / J Previous / next retained shell command Ctrl+Shift+Y Copy the selected command's output; otherwise copy the latest output Ctrl+Plus or Ctrl+Equal / Ctrl+Minus Increase / decrease font size Ctrl+Shift+Minus Decrease font size while Shift is held Ctrl+0 or Ctrl+Shift+0 Reset to the configured font size Ctrl+keypad Add / Subtract / 0 Increase / decrease / reset; keypad 0 needs Num Lock on Ctrl+Tab / Ctrl+Shift+Tab Next / previous workspace tab Ctrl+Shift+R Reload the session's configuration file Ctrl+Shift+C / V Copy selection / paste clipboard Shift+PageUp / PageDown Scroll history Plus follows the active keyboard layout, including Ctrl+Shift+Equal on common keyboards and a different shifted key on other layouts. Zoom changes the font and PTY grid within the existing pixel-sized window. Ctrl+0 restores the latest successfully loaded configuration font. With Num Lock off, keypad 0 keeps its Insert behavior. Split resizing uses Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Equal / Minus. The native Windows reset shortcut is Ctrl+0. Windows can reserve Ctrl+Shift+0 when multiple keyboard layouts are active; that alias works only if delivered. Microsoft's shortcut guidance describes the system setting. The Linux shortcuts in the table remain available. Custom bindings are checked before these defaults. For example, keybind = ctrl+shift+plus = none disables that shifted zoom chord, while keybind = ctrl+kp-add = font-decrease changes only Ctrl+keypad Add. The palette appears only when requested. It uses the existing window and does not send its query or action keystrokes to the child. It exposes the same named actions as custom bindings and ztty action NAME ACTION. Filters accept several case-insensitive words in any order, and action rows show a currently effective shortcut, including custom overrides. Workspace shortcuts are listed in workspaces. The session switcher labels existing views and detached sessions separately. Selecting an existing view focuses its actual window, tab and pane without changing its PTY or input owner. A detached session requires an explicit Attach entry. Observing views and sessions controlled by another actor remain read-only; switching does not take input ownership. The selected URI distinguishes sessions with the same display name. If a Focus target detaches while the list is open, the action reports that change rather than silently creating a new view. Search uses literal UTF-8 matching across rows joined by terminal autowrap. Each search starts case-sensitive. Alt+C switches to Unicode lowercase comparison and back; the search bar displays the mode. Copying retains the original spelling. This comparison does not normalize accents or perform full Unicode case folding. Explicit line breaks remain boundaries. It highlights complete wide and combining cells, including the visible portion of a match extending outside the viewport. Queries are limited to 1,024 bytes; the streaming matcher retains one normalized query's positions, not a copy of the history. The highlight map uses one bit per visible cell, at most 16 KiB for a 512×256 grid. Repeated Next/Previous navigation reuses the match count and up to 128 match coordinates while the query, case mode and terminal text revision are unchanged. The first search still scans retained text; moving beyond the cached window can scan again. Closing search releases its cache. See the bounded navigation measurements. Copying a selection joins automatic line wraps while retaining explicit newlines. Wide-glyph wrap padding is omitted, meaningful spaces are retained, and UTF-8 cells remain whole within the 4 MiB selection limit. An active search can copy its complete match even when it spans more than a viewport. Output or a resize invalidates saved match coordinates; copying refreshes the search first. Search does not provide regular expressions. Retained primary-screen text reflows across width changes using recorded soft wraps; hard line boundaries remain intact. Narrowing the screen can still evict history under the existing row and byte limits. Match counts refresh when editing, navigating or copying the query. Native macOS and Windows share the selection-copy rules, while their search and command palette interfaces remain unimplemented. See the core reflow contract and 0.5.2 release evidence. Returning to live output Scrolling into history shows a small Back to live ↓ control near the lower right corner. Clicking it returns to the newest output and hides the control. The terminal keeps its full row count; there is no permanent toolbar at the live screen. Shift+PageUp/PageDown and the existing scroll actions remain available. When the child produces more output while you are reading history, the visible rows stay anchored, including after the retained-history buffer reaches its limit, and the control changes to New output · Back to live ↓ with a blue border. If the inspected content is evicted, the view stops at the oldest row still retained. The indicator remains until the view returns to the bottom. Scrolling up again starts with the ordinary label, so an earlier output arrival does not appear as a new notification. The control sits above an open search row or command palette. Clicking it keeps that interface open and preserves its input mode. It also works in an observing view without acquiring control or resizing the child. Its mouse press, drag and release stay within the view controls, including when the application requests mouse reports. In narrow views the label becomes Live ↓ or ↓; the control is hidden if a complete target cannot fit above the active interface. Shell command regions Enable the appropriate script using shell/README.md. ztty shell-integration bash|zsh|fish|nu prints the packaged script, so it can be loaded explicitly without changing unrelated shell configuration. The scripts send OSC 133 prompt/input/output/end marks and OSC 7 working-directory metadata. ztty commands work ztty command-output work 1 The CLI returns JSON. Command-output responses contain text, complete, truncated and command_id. MCP additionally accepts part: "input" and a max_bytes bound through session_command_read. At most 128 metadata records are retained; extracted text is limited to 65,536 UTF-8 bytes. Copying through the GUI refuses truncated output, so an incomplete region is not silently presented as a complete command result. Command regions point into the existing terminal history. They are rendered text, not immutable stdout, and physical lines become newline separators. Overwriting/erasing text, changing the width of a live region or exhausting history can invalidate a region. Navigation skips unavailable records. Already retained, intact historical commands remain usable after a font change. Bash hook acceptance The Bash integration preserves existing PROMPT_COMMAND strings or array entries, their exit-status behavior, and an inherited PS0 suffix. Repeated sourcing and nested shells must not duplicate execution marks. The dedicated PTY gate is part of the local Linux check; the four-shell gate also checks Bash syntax and the first source result independently of the second. Bash regression, old-script failure and exact versions record the current evidence. Bash before 5.1 has not been executed in this acceptance run. Custom keys and mouse buttons Bindings are lines in the same configuration file as fonts and colors: keybind = ctrl+shift+x = search keybind = ctrl+shift+p = palette keybind = ctrl+shift+t = none mousebind = ctrl+button3 = palette Modifiers are ctrl, shift, alt, super. Keys include ASCII characters, f1–f35, enter, escape, tab, backspace, space, arrows, home, end, pageup, pagedown, equal/plus, minus, kp-add, kp-subtract, and kp-0. Mouse buttons are button1–button11. Binding comparisons ignore the Caps Lock and Num Lock modifier bits, but the active layout still resolves the key itself: keypad 0 is kp-0 with Num Lock on and Insert with it off. Custom bindings replace defaults for the exact chord. none consumes a chord without running an action. Each matched press and its release are withheld from application input, including buttons while an application has enabled mouse reports. There are at most 128 custom chords; unknown actions and malformed chords reject the config. The palette lists action descriptions and effective shortcuts; exact binding names are in src/actions.rs. Selection, copy and navigation remain available while observing; paste requires local input ownership. In ordinary shell mode, Caps Lock, Num Lock and Scroll Lock change keyboard state without sending private-use escape sequences. Programs that explicitly enable the enhanced keyboard protocol still receive negotiated lock-key events. With Num Lock enabled, keypad digits type numbers. With it disabled, keypad zero is the standard Insert key (ESC [ 2 ~), whose handling belongs to the application. Live configuration The session remembers its explicit --config path, otherwise the default config path. Linux inotify watches the containing directory, including atomic saves. It follows replacement/recreation of that directory through the nearest existing ancestor and releases watches after their last session closes. There is no periodic idle polling. Manual reload is Ctrl+Shift+R. Valid changes update fonts, padding, theme, cursor and selection colors, custom bindings and supported opacity/blur settings in the existing window. Invalid configuration retains the last valid state and shows a temporary error line. Font validation and PTY resizing precede the live appearance commit. A window created with an opaque visual needs detach/attach before enabling a supported transparent visual; an X server without an alpha visual retains its opaque fallback. Theme changes preserve explicit RGB colors and update default/ANSI colors using source flags in the existing cell. Font reset returns to the latest successfully loaded config font. A font change preserves the PTY PID and window. Observing views cannot resize the child; their window appearance can still change independently. Reproducible checks cargo test --locked --workspace cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings cargo build --release --locked python3 tests/daily_workflow.py --binary ./target/release/ztty python3 tests/session_switcher.py --binary ./target/release/ztty python3 tests/input_gui.py --binary ./target/release/ztty --source-root . python3 tests/install_test.py python3 tests/mcp_transport.py --binary ./target/release/ztty python3 tests/mcp_sessions.py --binary ./target/release/ztty python3 tests/mcp_security.py --binary ./target/release/ztty cargo build --locked -p zterm --example shell_probe python3 tests/shell_integration.py python3 tests/bash_integration.py The daily workflow test uses private Xvfb, XTEST key/button events, a real raw PTY, actual clipboard transfers and pixel captures. It records binary/source hashes and cleans only its own processes. Its coverage is Linux X11; hardware GPU, native Wayland, macOS/Windows feature parity and IME accessibility are independent acceptance gates. The current harness also exercises the scrollback return control with real mouse input and additional PTY output. It checks history anchoring, clearing the new-output indication, search/palette coexistence and read-only ownership. Its screenshots include scrollback-return, scrollback-new-output, scrollback-live, scrollback-search, scrollback-palette and scrollback-observer. The archived run below predates these additional checks. The 2026-11-18 run passed all 12 daily GUI scenarios and the existing workspace GUI regression. GUI evidence, final build/Clippy/no_std log and stdio/HTTP ownership/security evidence record the exact binary and source hashes. Earlier failed checks led to the invalid-region navigation fix and the visible config-error diagnostic; the linked final records are the passing reruns. Actual history search（历史附件） Actual temporary command palette（历史附件） Configuration-directory race regression A real GUI run exposed a missed reload when the config directory was renamed and rebuilt. A replacement directory could appear after the direct watch failed but before its ancestor watch was installed. If its file was then written after reconnect, the ancestor did not receive that child-directory write. Reconnect now installs the nearest existing ancestor watch before probing each child directory again. It either reaches the new parent or keeps the watch that will report its future creation. This adds no polling timer or permanent extra watch. Shared descriptors remain alive until their last configured path is removed. Three real inotify tests schedule this filesystem race precisely and use the real libc watch calls. The old implementation fails both race cases; the fixed implementation passes all three cases. The third case checks shared-descriptor retention and final release. See the source/test hashes and comparison record, old failure log, and fixed trace. The normal local gate now runs all Rust integration tests and MCP security tests.

title: ssmcp observation on Linux
body: 原生终端应用，在 Linux 上支持窗口、命令行与 MCP 共用会话。 ssmcp observation on Linux tools/ztty-observer opens ssmcp command output in a read-only ztty window without requesting keyboard focus. Sequential commands reuse the live ssmcp viewer and window. Closing a window created for that viewer retires the viewer child; the next ssmcp command can open another observation window. This integration currently uses Linux X11 or XWayland. The recorded acceptance run used a separately owned Xvfb server, not the user's desktop. It does not establish native Wayland, macOS, Windows, physical input-device or compositor latency acceptance. Start an observing connection Use an already authorized ssmcp account and an executable ztty build: ZTTY_BIN="$PWD/target/release/ztty" \ ssmcp --tty "$PWD/tools/ztty-observer" --name ztty-observed The adapter is a small executable shell script. It selects ${ZTTY_BIN:-ztty} and passes --observe before the terminal arguments supplied by ssmcp. The Rust implementation contains no ssmcp-specific process names or command parsing. See the adapter, CLI parsing and Linux session implementation. ssmcp starts the terminal with -e ssmcp __tty-view DIRECTORY SLOT. That helper reads the output retained by ssmcp for the real command. There are two PTYs with different jobs: the command's PTY produces stdout/stderr; the viewer's PTY carries the resulting bytes into ztty. Opening the observation window does not execute the command a second time. Input and lifetime rules Operation Input and focus Closing the observing window ztty --observe -e COMMAND ... Starts a fresh read-only window; does not request focus. Typing, paste and mouse reporting do not write to its child. Resizing does not resize the observed PTY. Retires the child created for this window while its input still belongs to the local actor. ztty attach --observe NAME Observes the existing session; attaching to an existing view also cancels queued local input and asynchronous paste. Detaches the view and preserves the existing PTY, including sessions whose input still belongs to the local actor. Input has been acquired by another actor The local view cannot operate that actor's PTY. Preserves the other actor's PTY even if this view originally created it. ztty close NAME Checks the current input owner. Explicitly retires the named session when the caller owns it. --observe is a standalone-window option; combining it with --tab, --split-right or --split-down is rejected. A PTY still has one GUI view. This adapter does not add concurrent independent GUI observers for the same PTY. The difference between creation and attachment is necessary for reusable command viewers. If closing a freshly created observation window only detaches it, the ssmcp viewer keeps sending its heartbeat while its window is hidden. ssmcp can then reuse that invisible viewer for a later command. The first real integration run reproduced this failure; the session code now remembers whether a view created its child, and clears that ownership when the view becomes an attachment. Recorded acceptance The pre-fix report preserves the failure. The first two real native exec commands executed once each and reused the same viewer/window. After WM_DELETE_WINDOW, the third command completed with exit 0, but the session remained detached and no window became visible during the 12-second observation interval. The run cleaned up all its processes. The final corrected run, run-03, executes three actual native exec commands and records ten passing checks. It uses the candidate containing both the observation-window lifetime fix and the configuration-watch fix. Its hashes are: Artifact SHA-256 ztty candidate a339a7d258ad313379b5cfea40d8b125aa8c810ecaebd40005b489413a1b6d4d Installed ssmcp executable e7e3d84b6afc869c5e340fbf9cf0c8c4092e60f6ce68c85379b4b64e8cc0c048 Executed tests/ssmcp_observer.py 370abf802ea5edddaf93106f2b45f6b7291787b775d0e3d42587a1722a764d0d The executed test hash matches the source-controlled script, including the new-session incarnation assertions and the second screenshot capture. The passing checks are: Reused existing account authorization without provisioning an account or reading credentials. Displayed the actual command's PTY output in a fresh read-only window without taking X11 focus. Verified that ztty ran the installed ssmcp __tty-view process for the exact native exec slot. Injected keyboard, paste-shortcut and mouse events with XTEST; the viewer PTY input queue stayed empty and ztty did not request clipboard contents. Resized the observation window and checked that the viewer PTY dimensions stayed unchanged. Ran a second command in the same ssmcp slot, viewer process and ztty window without taking focus. Recorded exactly one execution per command and confirmed that both stdout and stderr were actual PTYs. Verified both commands' exit codes and their exact combined PTY output. Closed the window and verified that a third real command obtained a visible read-only observer without taking focus or rerunning the command. Closed the private observation session explicitly and verified that no test-owned processes remained. X11 resource numbers may be reused after a display connection closes. Compare the broker PID, session creation time and viewer PID when distinguishing the reopened window from the previous one; the numeric window_id alone is insufficient. The first screenshot（历史附件） captures actual pixels from the first two commands. The reopened-window screenshot（历史附件） captures the third command after closing and recreating its observer. Both were inspected for readable text, natural wrapping and the intended black background with padding. The JSON separately records new_session_incarnation=true, the three actual executions and an empty remaining-process list. The independent tests/daily_workflow.py suite also exercises both lifetime branches without requiring an ssmcp account: closing an observer attached to an already visible, locally owned session preserves the same functioning PTY; closing a fresh --observe window removes its own session and reaps its child. Existing checks continue to cover an agent-owned PTY and explicit local takeover. The final daily-workflow report records fourteen passing checks against the same ztty candidate hash, including actual configuration-directory rename and recreation. An earlier daily-workflow failure is retained separately: the lifecycle-fixed candidate timed out while waiting for the new background after configuration-directory recreation. It had completed seven checks and had not reached the new observer lifecycle assertions. The final report uses the subsequent configuration-watch fix; no timeout or pre-existing assertion was relaxed to obtain its result. The reports retain binary hashes and source-file hashes. An acceptance report made from uncommitted source records that state explicitly; it is not a substitute for the clean-source native release gate or cross-platform acceptance. Reproduce the real connection test Requirements are Linux, an installed and already authorized ssmcp client with --tty, Xvfb, Python with python-xlib and Pillow, and the candidate ztty binary. The test refuses to provision authorization. It creates an ephemeral connection with --no-browser --no-setup --no-watchdog, uses an owned random display through tools/isolated_xvfb.py, and creates a private broker socket. It never invokes an ssmcp model or agent tool. Start the coordinator from the source tree. Use a new control directory for every run: python3 tests/ssmcp_observer.py \ --binary target/release/ztty \ --source-root . \ --ssmcp /absolute/path/to/ssmcp \ --control-dir artifacts/ssmcp-observer-run \ --output artifacts/ssmcp-observer.json \ --screenshot artifacts/ssmcp-observer.png Use ssmcp's authorized client listing to find the unique client_name written to ready.json. Call only that new client's native ssmcp.exec.start, ssmcp.exec.wait and ssmcp.exec.read tools. Run each command array exactly as supplied; the command appends a single execution record, prints harmless markers and waits for the coordinator's completion signal. Coordinator file Controller action Receipt written into the control directory ready.json Start first_command on the matching ephemeral client. first-start.json: job_id, output_mode, tty_slot from the start result. await-second.json Wait/read the first job, then start second_command. first-done.json: job_id, exit_code, running, stdout, stderr; then second-start.json with the three start fields. await-finish.json Wait/read the second job. second-done.json with the five completion fields. await-third.json Start third_command after the coordinator has closed the original window. third-start.json with the three start fields. await-third-finish.json Wait/read the third job. third-done.json with the five completion fields. finished.json Read the completed report and inspect its screenshot. No further calls on the ephemeral client; the coordinator disconnects it. Write receipts through the original authorized development connection or directly on the test machine. Do not run extra receipt-writing commands on the observed client: those commands would themselves create observations and invalidate the exact command count. Receipts contain only the fields listed above; no account configuration, authorization URL or credential is copied into evidence. The coordinator has a bounded overall deadline. On success, failure or interruption it stops only its own processes, checks process birth tokens before sending signals, releases its owned Xvfb and deletes private account connection logs. A failure remains a failing report; a screenshot of an earlier passing stage does not override it. The account-independent GUI regressions run with: python3 tests/daily_workflow.py \ --binary target/release/ztty \ --output artifacts/daily-workflow.json \ --screenshots artifacts/daily-workflow These acceptance tools are source-controlled. Real account integration stays separate from the unattended release gate because it requires an existing external account session; the corresponding local observer lifecycle checks run in the native Linux GUI gate.

title: 概览
body: 文本行布局、终端几何与 ANSI 帧差分原语。 ztuio ztuio 提供文本终端界面的几何、定宽行和 ANSI 帧差分。调用方提供已排版的当前帧与上一帧，库通过 core::fmt::Write 输出需要更新的行、终端模式与光标位置。 库使用 #![no_std] 和 #![forbid(unsafe_code)]，仅引用 core，没有第三方依赖。字符串、帧和输出缓冲由调用方持有，库内部不申请堆内存。测试、示例和基准使用 std。源码 · 依赖声明 使用 需要 Rust 1.100 或更新版本。Cargo 包名和 Rust 导入名均为 ztuio： [dependencies] ztuio = { git = "https://github.com/LIghtJUNction/ztuio" } 固定源码时指定 rev，并提交应用的 Cargo.lock。相邻源码检出可使用 path = "../ztuio"。 use ztuio::Row; let mut output = String::new(); // 调用方已测得两个汉字占 4 个显示列。 Row::with_columns("界面", 4) .write_padded(&mut output, 12) .unwrap(); 固定数组示例 展示无堆缓冲的输出方式。缓冲不足会返回错误，调用方可以选择固定数组、复用的字符串或自己的写出适配器。 接口与职责 接口 用途 调用方负责 Size、Point、Rect 单元坐标、裁剪和分栏 像素尺寸与实际窗口布局 Row::measured / Row::with_columns 接受已测得的显示列数 Unicode、grapheme 与终端宽度规则 Row::write_padded 写入文本并补空格到目标宽度 可信单行内容、样式和背景 Frame 借用当前帧和上一帧 行的生命周期、拼接与布局 write_diff 输出变化行、模式和最终光标 设备 I/O、部分写入恢复与退出时的模式恢复 帧坐标从零开始，ANSI CUP 坐标从一开始。差分包含 SGR reset、整行擦除、应用光标、鼠标和 bracketed paste 模式；空画布与完全不变的帧写出零字节。输出约定 帧写出使用固定栈数组生成 ANSI 坐标，减少格式化与写出调用。相同行先比较借用切片的地址与长度，再在需要时比较内容。这些实现保留相同的 ANSI 字节顺序；契约测试覆盖数字位数边界、完整 u16 行范围和不同分配中的相同行。 输入与失败处理 传入的行内容与显示列数由调用方校验。库信任已经过滤并排版好的文本和 SGR 样式；图片解码、键盘输入、Unicode 测宽和终端设备访问由应用负责。 完整写出的帧才能作为下一次差分基线。行宽超限会在写出前返回 TooWide；输出接口失败时可能已有部分字节写入。调用方应写完剩余内容，或丢弃差分基线，以 previous = None 全量重画。 验证 cargo +1.100.0 test --locked cargo +1.100.0 run --locked --example fixed_buffer cargo +1.100.0 clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings cargo +1.100.0 check --locked --lib --target x86_64-unknown-none CI 为 Linux、Windows、macOS 配置相同的契约测试、示例检查与格式检查，并单独检查无操作系统目标。终端字体、背景、输入与图片的交互需要由消费这些接口的应用验证。 性能记录 cargo bench --bench diff -- 200000 测量首帧、不变画面、单行变化、全行变化、尺寸变化、光标变化和模式变化。它复用调用方输出缓冲，并在计时前比较 ANSI 输出。 2026-11-18 的历史测量记录了原始导出版本的环境、样本与场景差异。首次测量也保留用于追溯。当前源码合入了后续帧写出优化；评估当前性能时应重新运行基准并记录提交、工具链、目标架构和系统负载。基准范围是帧差分与字符串写入，设备 I/O 和端到端交互由应用单独测量。 来源与许可证 本库从 SSMCP 的文本终端核心独立维护，并汇入其后续帧写出优化。固定来源提交与保留的历史记录见 provenance。 MIT License · Copyright © 2026 LIghtJUNction

title: 输出与布局约定
body: 文本行布局、终端几何与 ANSI 帧差分原语。 输出与布局约定 帧基线必须已完整写出 write_diff 读取当前帧和最后一个完整写出的帧，不修改它们。调用方将结果写到终端；若写入被中断，保留尚未写出的字节继续写，或丢弃差分基线并用 previous=None 全量重画。不要把只写了一部分的当前帧作为新基线。 帧的行高来自 Frame::size().rows。Frame::row(index) 必须为范围内每一行返回有效字符串；当布局含分栏时，行必须已完成拼接和宽度限制。终端模式属于调用方声明的 Modes，库不会探测或恢复终端先前状态。 same_layout 默认比较尺寸。分栏改变而终端尺寸不变时，调用方可额外比较布局结构；SSMCP 比较自己的完整 Geometry，保持原有重画规则。 文字宽度由调用方决定 字节数、Unicode 字符数和显示列数不是同一个量。Row 接受可见列数，检查目标宽度，然后补 ASCII 空格。超宽返回 TooWide，不写任何内容；输出设备拒绝写入则返回 Output，此时设备可能已收到部分字节。 库不裁剪 grapheme，不维护宽字符表，不解析 OSC，也不接收任意终端控制流。Frame 行可以包含可信 SGR 样式；调用方必须过滤移动光标、换行、清屏及其它会逃出行边界的控制序列。需要全宽背景时，应在渲染每个单元或补齐空格前设定背景色。 SSMCP 的 Activity 行先经有界 cell normalization，再用安全的单元序列化器生成字形和 SGR；这个应用层步骤保留图片半块的显式背景，并将空白补到分栏边界。它不是 ztuio 内置的 Unicode/终端模拟器。 复杂度与资源 库没有 heap allocator、全局可变状态、OS I/O、线程或锁。帧差分在行数与被比较的文本字节数上是线性的，除调用方输出之外使用常量辅助空间。相等行比较仍然需要读字符串；零分配不意味着零计算。 write_spaces 按固定长度的静态空格片段写入，不构造重复字符串。调用方仍应对需要写出的宽度和总帧大小设限。几何坐标使用 u16；矩形的排他边界必须可表示，构造时检查溢出。 测试覆盖与剩余边界 契约测试检查 ANSI 次序、不变帧、单行更新、尺寸和布局改变、模式/光标更新、输出缓冲错误、Unicode 宽度显式提供、行超宽拒绝、矩形溢出与分栏不重叠。应用层还需用真实终端或独立 VT 解码器检查背景、字体宽度和原生图片行为。 本库不承诺所有终端实现遵守同一套 Unicode、SGR 或 DEC 模式。ANSI 文本差分和 Kitty 等图像通道的写出次序，由上层协调。

title: 导出来源与验证边界
body: 文本行布局、终端几何与 ANSI 帧差分原语。 导出来源与验证边界 固定来源 独立仓库通过 git subtree split --prefix=crates/ztui 从以下固定版本导出，随后只调整仓库元数据和文档： 项目 值 来源仓库 https://github.com/LIghtJUNction/ssmcp 来源提交 3570af1507031e83eede4abeb0853e609f039f46 来源目录 crates/ztui 来源目录 Git tree 56c69a513ec8920ac3667f832cdfd50199d705dd subtree split 提交 15e7b5d5174273ab34438af1727db20991500b52 导出提交 Git tree 56c69a513ec8920ac3667f832cdfd50199d705dd src/ Git tree fb49cbbcefdb5b89bfddf28775ef9a1daee1680e 两个目录 tree 完全相同，说明导出时 12 个文件的路径、模式和内容一致。独立仓库的后续准备提交只修改 Cargo.toml 的 repository 地址与 README，新增本记录、重复测量 JSON 和忽略构建目录的规则；不修改 src/、tests/、benches/、examples/ 或 MIT 许可证。 subtree 保留了三条涉及该目录的历史提交，按新到旧排列： 15e7b5d5174273ab34438af1727db20991500b52 — merge: reconcile reviewed PRs 25, 26 and 30 352084bd97ec18e19d083720a331542c38321244 — feat(client): integrate ztui, native images and terminal dialogue reminders [skip ci] 40909ec584977cf565beb2e7d275d1ab876d51b3 — feat: add no_std display primitives and gateway guide 这些是重写目录根路径后的 subtree 提交，不应与原 SSMCP 提交 SHA 混用。 既有验证 SSMCP R14 在固定提交 aa8b95d66655adfd4d97ac8191e2b935bcd57c44 上完成 workspace 测试、严格 Clippy、workspace 打包与优化构建。公开报告的默认 Rust 汇总为 1,142 passed、26 ignored、0 failed，范围包含整个 SSMCP workspace，不是 ztui 自身的测试数量。 固定 R14 验证报告 本次导出检查目录 tree、源码字节、元数据、文档链接及 Git 差异，不把既有 workspace 结果当作独立仓库提交的新一次构建。独立检出后的测试和正式发布是后续分别记录的步骤；没有随仓库创建执行 Cargo、发布 crate、创建 tag 或启动远端 CI。 性能证据 重复测量来源提交为 343163e0b5e8d6d43e6f854d49adbaa913c24c67。该版本与导出来源的 crates/ztui/src tree 都是 fb49cbbcefdb5b89bfddf28775ef9a1daee1680e。性能表引用这份既有实验，不把独立仓库的新提交标作测量来源。 本地证据副本 原样来自公开的固定证据 JSON。原始报告 SHA-256 为 dea76fc32d373653d5bc8f77fb1213b3b9a581d48fb5b61cc2570e45bc01cf54；公开副本已经去掉本机绝对路径，保留原数值。 3 次基准进程分别执行七个场景。每个场景、每种实现执行两轮各 200,000 次，第二轮交换顺序；计时前各做一次字节等价比较。因此，21 是固定场景等价检查次数，每种实现、每个场景累计计时调用 120 万次。统计口径是每次运行的 ztui/原实现配对比值的中位数。 完整记录保留较慢场景、首次尺寸变化 3.3873 比值及环境负载。不包含终端、GPU 和端到端交互，不以库内部零分配推导进程 RSS，也不将不同 run 的绝对耗时中位数相除冒充配对比值。 可复查的声明 声明 直接证据 边界 库使用 no_std，禁止 unsafe，零第三方依赖 src/lib.rs、src/*.rs、Cargo.toml 应用输出和测宽函数不在此承诺内 导出未修改运行时、测试、示例与基准 固定 source/split tree 与文件哈希核对 文档和仓库地址有明确调整 性能有快有慢 七场景三次运行的完整 JSON 固定 fixture，非所有终端或完整应用 既有 R14 验证通过 固定 SSMCP workspace 报告 不冒充导出后独立验证 Consolidated frame writer The frame writer and contract tests include the fixed ANSI control-sequence formatting and equal-row fast path from SSMCP commit 4e3132d60600dca5053af81cdefa6962c3058ac4. The public geometry, row and frame APIs remain unchanged; the package and Rust import name are ztuio. The contract suite compares emitted bytes at all decimal coordinate boundaries, including the full u16 row range.

title: 概览
body: Linux 原生输入法，在应用中组合拼音、显示候选并提交文字。 ztype English · 安装与服务 · 本轮验收 · 历史记录 基于 zinput 的 Linux 原生输入法。 Ztype 0.4.2 提供 X11/XWayland XIM 和 Wayland input-method-v2 两条输入路径。按键在当前应用中组合，独立候选窗显示拼音、当前页和候选，确认后通过输入法协议提交文字。日常输入不需要打开独立演示面板。 0.4.2 为原生候选窗调整文字层级、20 px 左右留白与 Material 3 浅色配色。ztty 的 XIM 与原生 Wayland 两条路径均完成真实终端输入验收；Wayland 路径使用 ztty PR #23 的光标更新兼容修复，具体源码和二进制身份见本轮记录。 词库、候选页大小、初始中英文模式、标点和 Enter 行为均可配置。拼音支持外部加权词库、多词库合并、词语组合、隔音符号和可选的用户选词学习。语言数据与程序分开安装，Ztype 运行时不依赖 Rime 或 Fcitx5 服务。 完整词库在真实 Wayland 输入框中的候选窗 构建并安装 git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/LIghtJUNction/ztype.git cd ztype cargo build --release --locked # 下载固定版本的公开词库，校验来源并保留许可证 python3 scripts/install_dictionary.py --source rime-ice # 安装程序、配置示例及编译进去的原生服务；此命令不切换输入法 python3 scripts/install.py --binary target/release/ztype ~/.local/bin/ztype config ~/.local/bin/ztype convert --text shurufa # 输入法 Linux 原生构建使用系统 C 编译器、pkg-config、X11/XCB、XKB、Wayland、FreeType、fontconfig 及图形开发库。Rust 最低版本以 Cargo.toml 的 rust-version 为准。命令行核心可以用 --no-default-features 独立构建。 词库安装器固定读取 Rime Ice 的两个公开词表，合并后生成 573,194 条记录，其中 21,014 条是隔音符号别名，例如 xi'an。这不是 57 万个不同汉语词语：同一词语可以有多个拼音编码。词表、来源记录和 GPL-3.0 许可证保留在用户数据目录；仓库内的程序许可证与下载词库的许可证分别保留。内置小词表只用于无外部数据时的基础转换与测试，不代表日常词库。 启动与应用连接 在原输入法释放对应的 Wayland seat 或 XIM 名称后，再启动 Ztype： ztype wayland-doctor ztype start ztype status # 修改配置或升级后 ztype restart # 停止 ztype stop 安装器的 --activate 会启用当前会话支持的服务并重启它们，确保旧进程实际被新程序替换。常规安装不启动服务。服务通过 readiness 通知确认词库和原生输入连接已初始化；status 会报告失败和仍运行旧二进制的情况。完整说明见安装与服务。 X11/XWayland 应用通过启动时的 XMODIFIERS=@im=ztype 选择默认端点。ZTYPE_XIM_NAME 可以指定其他端点名称。已有应用不会自动改变自己的环境变量；如果它们已经选择 @im=fcitx，可在 Fcitx5 完全退出后，以 ZTYPE_XIM_NAME=fcitx ztype start 提供相同名称。服务会拒绝占用已有输入法的名称。名称可配置不等于依赖 Fcitx5。 原生 Wayland 应用还需要自身的 text-input 支持。浏览器的 Wayland 显示后端和输入法协议开关是两件事，具体启动选项和实测结果见本轮验收记录。 日常操作 按键 默认行为 字母 在当前组合位置输入拼音 Space 提交当前候选 数字 1–9 选择当前页对应候选；码表引擎保留数字编码 PageUp / PageDown、拼音模式下的 - / = 翻页 Tab / Shift+Tab、↑ / ↓ 切换候选 ← / →、Home / End 移动组合中的光标 Backspace / Delete 删除光标前 / 后的字符 Enter 提交原始拼音；可配置为提交候选 Escape 取消组合 Ctrl+Space 切换中英文输入 默认每页 5 个候选，可设置为 1–9 个；候选集合最多保留 128 个，页内数字与显示序号一致。中文模式可输出中文标点，英文模式传递原键。焦点切换和敏感字段会清理组合；Wayland 密码/PIN 等敏感字段透传按键，不参与学习。 候选窗通过原生输入协议显示，不抢走应用焦点。Wayland 使用应用报告的文字位置；XIM 客户端提供 spot location 时按该位置显示。未提供位置的客户端使用窗口边缘回退位置，目前 Ztty 的 XIM 路径属于这种情况，不能把该路径描述为跟随终端内的字符光标。 配置与词库 配置默认位于 $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/ztype/config，未设置时为 ~/.config/ztype/config。ztype config 显示实际路径、词库来源及解析后的选项；错误会标明配置文件和行号。 engine=pinyin page_size=5 initial_mode=chinese chinese_punctuation=true enter_behavior=raw learning=false # 显式词库可以写多次；相对路径相对于本配置文件 # dictionary=/absolute/path/common.tsv # dictionary=/absolute/path/domain.tsv # 仅在主动开启学习时写入已选词及次数 # user_dictionary=~/.local/share/ztype/user.tsv 没有显式 dictionary 时，自动发现 XDG 系统与用户数据目录中 ztype/dictionaries/*.tsv。--dict PATH 只使用指定词库；--config PATH 使用指定配置；--no-config 关闭用户配置和自动词库发现，适用于可重复的测试。 词表格式为 code<TAB>text<TAB>frequency，第三列可省略。同一编码按频率排序，重复编码和文字合并，普通拼音可从词语组合成未预存的句子。这是词频与词语切分方法，没有神经语言模型，也不保证所有句子都能自动消歧。单文件最多 64 MiB、2,000,000 条记录，一次最多加载 32 个词库。 ztype candidates --text ni ztype convert --text wozaitushuguanxuexi # 我在图书馆学习 ztype convert --text "xi'an" # 西安 ztype convert --engine table --dict phrases.tsv --text hello --candidate 10 学习默认关闭。主动启用时只记录用户提交的编码、候选和次数，使用独立文件、进程锁和原子保存；不会自动读取其他输入法的个人数据。已有用户词库也可以只读加载。普通输入进程不下载词库；联网下载只由显式运行的安装脚本完成。 框架与平台范围 部分 职责与当前范围 zinput 核心 组合缓冲区、焦点上下文、候选和提交生命周期，以及引擎接口 zinput-x11 XIM 连接、按键与长按、XKB 布局更新、候选窗口适配 zinput-wayland input-method-v2、virtual-keyboard-v1、焦点状态、预编辑/提交及候选 surface ztype 词库与排序、配置、编辑与选词规则、候选内容、服务和安装流程 zgpui 原生图形与候选文字绘制 输入框架以操作系统协议为边界，不把 Arch、某个用户名或固定词条写成运行条件。但“可跨发行版编译”和“所有桌面环境都已支持”是不同的验收范围。 环境 支持边界 Linux X11 / XWayland 已实现 XIM；真实 Ztty 多版本已验收，其他客户端仍取决于其 XIM 支持 Hyprland 等 input-method-v2 合成器 已实现所需协议；本轮的实际应用结果见验收记录 KDE Plasma 原生 Wayland 当前未实现其 input-method-v1 适配，不能声称全面支持 GNOME 原生 Wayland 当前未实现 GNOME/IBus 集成，不能声称全面支持 Windows / macOS 部分便携核心和历史构建记录存在；TSF / InputMethodKit 输入法前端尚未实现 桌面协议依据：KDE Plasma Keyboard、IBus Wayland 桌面说明。应用和桌面验收只覆盖记录中的版本与配置。 其他引擎和开发检查 kana 提供罗马字到假名转换，不做日文汉字转换；unicode 解析 Unicode 标量；literal 保留原始 UTF-8；table 使用用户码表。原生服务支持 pinyin、kana、table；其余引擎和显式可信原生插件通过 CLI 或独立 panel 使用。面板是辅助工具，操作方式与原生候选窗不同。 ztype convert --engine kana --text konnichiha ztype convert --engine unicode --text 'U+1F30D U+4F60 U+597D' cargo test --all-targets --locked cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings python3 scripts/test_install.py python3 scripts/test_daily_input.py --binary target/release/ztype 真实输入验收同时检查应用收到的 UTF-8、候选窗实际像素、焦点与进程清理，不能只以服务处于 running 状态判断可用。本轮证据、命令、依赖版本和剩余限制记录在日常输入验收，早期结果保留在历史验证。 0.4.0 日常输入记录保留此前的依赖和应用基线。 0.2.1 交互试用记录作为历史验收保留。

title: ztype
body: Linux 原生输入法，在应用中组合拼音、显示候选并提交文字。 ztype 简体中文 · Installation and services · Current acceptance record · Historical verification A Linux native input method built on zinput. Version 0.4.2 provides X11/XWayland XIM and Wayland input-method-v2 frontends, a separate candidate window, editable composition, paging, external weighted dictionaries and persistent configuration. It composes and commits text in the focused application; opening the standalone panel is optional. Version 0.4.2 gives the native candidate window clearer typography, 20 px horizontal spacing and light Material 3 color roles. Real ztty input is verified through both XIM and native Wayland; the latter uses the cursor-update compatibility fix in ztty PR #23. The acceptance record identifies the exact sources, executable hashes and tested scope. Native Wayland candidate window with the installed vocabulary Build and install git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/LIghtJUNction/ztype.git cd ztype cargo build --release --locked python3 scripts/install_dictionary.py --source rime-ice python3 scripts/install.py --binary target/release/ztype ~/.local/bin/ztype config ~/.local/bin/ztype convert --text shurufa # 输入法 Use the Rust version specified by Cargo.toml. Native Linux builds require a C compiler, pkg-config and the relevant X11/XCB, XKB, Wayland, FreeType, fontconfig and graphics development libraries. The portable CLI can be built with --no-default-features. The vocabulary installer verifies pinned public Rime Ice sources, retains their GPL-3.0 license and provenance, and writes 573,194 code/text records to the user data directory. This includes 21,014 apostrophe aliases; it is not a count of distinct words. The small bundled table supports basic conversion and tests. Install an external vocabulary for ordinary pinyin use. Downloaded language data and this program retain their separate licenses. The input service does not depend on Rime or Fcitx5 libraries or daemons. Installation writes the binary, configuration example and services supported by the binary. It does not switch the active input method unless --activate is explicitly supplied. After the previous input method releases the native endpoint: ztype wayland-doctor ztype start ztype status ztype restart ztype stop Service readiness is reported after dictionary and native connection initialization. Upgrades with --activate restart the services so the old executable cannot remain silently active. See service installation for XDG locations and lifecycle details. X11/XWayland applications select XMODIFIERS=@im=ztype at launch. ZTYPE_XIM_NAME configures the service endpoint. Existing applications retain their original environment; a compatible endpoint name can be used after its previous owner exits. Native Wayland applications need text-input support in addition to the compositor protocols. Starting a browser with a Wayland rendering backend alone does not establish input-method support. Native input controls Key Default action Space Commit the selected candidate 1–9 Select an item on the current page; table engines retain numeric codes PageUp / PageDown, pinyin - / = Change candidate page Tab / Shift+Tab, Up / Down Change candidate Left / Right, Home / End Move within the composition Backspace / Delete Delete before / after the composition cursor Enter Commit raw pinyin; configurable to commit the candidate Escape Cancel composition Ctrl+Space Toggle Chinese and direct input The default page size is five, configurable from one to nine. The candidate set holds up to 128 items. Page labels match number-key selection. Chinese punctuation is configurable. Sensitive Wayland fields pass through original keys, and focus changes invalidate composition. The candidate surface does not take input focus. Wayland positions it using the text-input rectangle. XIM uses the client's spot location when supplied and a window-edge fallback otherwise. Current Ztty XIM clients use the fallback; terminal character-caret following is not claimed for that path. Configuration and dictionaries ztype config prints resolved settings and dictionary paths. The default file is $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/ztype/config, or ~/.config/ztype/config. Invalid settings report the file and line. engine=pinyin page_size=5 initial_mode=chinese chinese_punctuation=true enter_behavior=raw learning=false # dictionary=/absolute/path/common.tsv # dictionary=/absolute/path/domain.tsv # user_dictionary=~/.local/share/ztype/user.tsv Without explicit dictionaries, Ztype discovers ztype/dictionaries/*.tsv in system and user XDG data directories. Repeat dictionary to merge sources. Relative paths are relative to the configuration file. --dict PATH overrides automatic/configured dictionaries; --config PATH selects a configuration; --no-config disables user settings and automatic discovery for reproducible tests. TSV records contain code<TAB>text<TAB>frequency, with an optional frequency. Larger frequencies rank first. Pinyin lookup merges duplicate entries, handles apostrophe boundaries and can combine known words into an unstored sentence. It uses word-frequency segmentation, not a neural language model, so sentence disambiguation is limited. Limits are 64 MiB and 2,000,000 records per file, with at most 32 source files. ztype candidates --text ni ztype convert --text wozaitushuguanxuexi # 我在图书馆学习 ztype convert --text "xi'an" # 西安 ztype convert --engine table --dict phrases.tsv --text hello --candidate 10 Learning is disabled by default. When enabled with an explicit user dictionary, it stores selected code/text/count records using a private file, process locking and atomic replacement. It does not import personal data from another input method. Existing user dictionaries can also be loaded without enabling writes. Only the separately invoked vocabulary installer downloads public data.
