Both native checks passed on the developer machine for 0.5.0; see the validation record. Those checks do not exercise a live ChatGPT desktop installation. Native acceptance needs an actual application exposing the required accessibility nodes, a uniquely identified dedicated conversation, an empty editor, and explicitly authorized draft text. Sending needs separate explicit authority. Record the observed draft and application result only for actions actually performed; no private conversation content belongs in the repository.

title: Development and release
body: 用有界脚本观察和操作桌面、浏览器与设备，并支持持久会话。 Development and release Use Rust 1.100 or newer. The version and release scripts require Python 3.11 or newer for the standard-library TOML parser. The default host build has only Project Z Rust dependencies. Build-time packages for graphical tests are optional and are not linked into zuse. Local gates python3 scripts/check.py cargo check --locked --no-default-features --lib cargo check --locked --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu cargo check --locked --target aarch64-apple-darwin cargo bench --locked --bench core The check script checks formatting, runs Clippy and tests, and checks the no_std library, including WebAssembly when that target is installed. Package validation is also performed before publication. Inspect the script for the precise current sequence. Native integration checks use independent fixtures. The X11 and AT-SPI fixtures require Linux with the system dependencies listed in Platforms; the browser fixture requires an installed Chromium executable: python3 tests/native_x11.py cargo test --locked --test browser_native -- --ignored python3 tests/run_accessibility_native.py python3 tests/transports.py The tests do not need the operator's browser profile. Android wire tests use a fake ADB service. Read-only device checks are kept separate from input tests. Bump python3 scripts/bump.py patch --dry-run python3 scripts/bump.py patch --commit --tag --push The bump script requires a clean working tree, updates the package version and lockfile, creates the release commit/tag, and atomically pushes main and the tag. Minor, major, and explicit stable versions are also accepted. GitHub's Bump and release workflow exposes the same version input. It calls the reusable release workflow after pushing; this avoids relying on a GITHUB_TOKEN-generated tag to trigger another workflow. Published targets OS Targets Linux x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu macOS x86_64-apple-darwin, aarch64-apple-darwin Windows x86_64-pc-windows-msvc Release identity is checked against Cargo.toml and the exact tagged commit. Each native build is packaged with its license, README, documentation, and runnable examples. GitHub releases publish all required archives. Publishing to crates.io requires a separately validated registry stage; the native release workflow does not publish the Cargo package. The CI workflow runs for pull requests or manual dispatch. Local verification is the development gate; tagged native builds and publication remain the release gate. Reproducibility and resource use The core benchmark reports work counts and elapsed time as JSON. Run it with a release profile when making performance comparisons. Measure the executable's RSS separately from a browser or application it controls; those external processes have their own memory use. Release archives normalize metadata and timestamps. Package validation must include benches, examples, tests, and both README languages so a registry download can reproduce the build. Dependency propagation Library updates include all direct and transitive consumers. Follow the required maintenance procedure, coordinate existing owners, and retain consumer test/commit receipts or a concrete blocker and takeover owner.

title: Native serial and USB I/O
body: 用有界脚本观察和操作桌面、浏览器与设备，并支持持久会话。 Native serial and USB I/O zuse exposes serial streams and USB interfaces through its Rust library and the shared CLI/MCP executor. Device selection is explicit. Serial uses platform APIs directly; USB loads the installed libusb 1.0 library through Project Z's zsys loader. Neither adapter launches a serial or USB command-line helper. Implementation and verification scope The transfer acceptance below exercised Linux PTYs and a synthetic C implementation of the libusb ABI. It did not open a physical serial port or perform a physical USB claim or transfer. A separate real-system check enumerated serial candidate names and USB descriptors without opening handles. The evidence record distinguishes these scopes. Adapter Implemented path Evidence from this acceptance Linux serial termios, nonblocking file I/O and poll Real kernel PTY: binary transfers, raw/8N1 settings, baud, timeout, backpressure and restoration macOS serial Darwin termios and poll Source implementation; no macOS execution in this acceptance Windows serial Win32 COM handle, DCB and COMMTIMEOUTS Source and ABI review; no Windows execution in this acceptance Linux USB System libusb 1.0 loaded through zsys Real Rust-to-C calls into a synthetic shared library, plus separate real-system descriptor enumeration macOS / Windows USB System libusb 1.0 through the corresponding zsys loader Source implementation; no live platform or device verification in this acceptance The USB fixture checks argument layout, buffer contents, result handling and native resource lifetime. It does not establish transfer compatibility with firmware, a kernel driver, cable, hub or operating-system USB backend. Serial candidate paths are operating-system names, not a count of attached physical serial devices. Serial API Opening configures the selected port as 8N1 with software and hardware flow control disabled. The adapter captures the previous configuration first. Linux and macOS save termios; Windows saves the DCB and communication timeouts. See the implementation, Microsoft's DCB definition and COMMTIMEOUTS definition. Operation Parameters and behavior serial.ports() Lists candidate names without opening or configuring them serial.open(path, baud=115200) Selects one device path and configures 8N1 serial.status() Reports the current connection's path, baud and format serial.read(length=4096, timeout=1000) Returns an available chunk up to the requested length; timeout is in milliseconds serial.write(text=..., timeout=1000) Writes the text's UTF-8 bytes serial.write(base64=..., timeout=1000) Writes decoded binary bytes; exactly one payload field is required serial.close() Attempts configuration restoration, then closes the handle Unix paths must explicitly name a device below /dev. Windows accepts COM1 through COM4096, with the optional Win32 device prefix. Supported baud values are 50, 75, 110, 134, 150, 200, 300, 600, 1200, 1800, 2400, 4800, 9600, 19200, 38400, 57600, 115200 and 230400. A driver can still reject a rate accepted by argument validation. The following example uses a placeholder device path. Replace it with the port selected for the task: serial.ports() serial.open(path="/dev/serial/by-id/your-device", baud=115200) serial.status() serial.write(text="ping\n", timeout=1000) serial.read(length=256, timeout=1000) serial.close() A serial read returns when data becomes available; it does not promise to fill the requested buffer. The agent supplies application framing, such as a length prefix or line terminator. An empty timeout result carries timed_out=true. Serial writes advance through the remaining buffer after a short system write. Already written bytes are not sent again. A deadline or I/O failure reports the cumulative bytes_written count and stops subsequent program steps. Normal close and Rust drop attempt to restore the captured configuration. Explicit close reports restoration failure; drop cannot return that error to its caller. Forced process termination cannot run Rust cleanup. The PTY acceptance verifies restoration after explicit close, normal session completion and a runtime write failure. USB API USB selection requires bus number, device address, vendor ID and product ID together. The adapter rechecks the descriptor at the selected bus/address before opening the handle. Changed identity or ambiguous selection produces an error. Opening claims one interface without requesting automatic kernel-driver detachment or changing the active configuration. A driver or application already owning the interface produces an explicit busy error. Libusb documents the relevant device and interface operations. Operation Parameters and defaults usb.devices() Enumerates numeric descriptors without opening handles usb.open(...) Required: bus, address, vendor_id, product_id; optional: interface=0 usb.status() Reports selected identity/interface and kernel_driver_detached=false usb.bulk_read(...) / usb.interrupt_read(...) Required: endpoint; defaults: length=4096, timeout=1000 usb.bulk_write(...) / usb.interrupt_write(...) Required: endpoint, base64; default: timeout=1000 usb.control_read(...) Required: request_type, request; defaults: value=0, index=0, length=64, timeout=1000 usb.control_write(...) Required: request_type, request, base64; defaults: value=0, index=0, timeout=1000 usb.close() Releases the interface and closes the handle and context Bulk and interrupt endpoint numbers are 1 through 15, with the direction bit set for reads. Decimal 1 is OUT endpoint 1; decimal 129 is IN endpoint 1. Control reads require the IN bit in request_type; control writes require OUT. The executor validates direction and integer widths before executing any step. This program uses the synthetic identifiers from the acceptance fixture. Its identifiers and transfer requests are examples for that fixture: usb.devices() usb.open(bus=7, address=9, vendor_id=4660, product_id=43981, interface=2) usb.status() usb.bulk_write(endpoint=1, base64="AAECAw==", timeout=1000) usb.bulk_read(endpoint=129, length=256, timeout=1000) usb.interrupt_write(endpoint=2, base64="BAUGBw==", timeout=1000) usb.interrupt_read(endpoint=130, length=256, timeout=1000) usb.control_write(request_type=64, request=90, value=4660, index=513, base64="AQID", timeout=1000) usb.control_read(request_type=192, request=91, value=4661, index=514, length=32, timeout=1000) usb.close() Each bulk, interrupt or control write makes one transfer call. A short write or transfer error fails the operation; zuse does not replay the request or continue to later steps. Errors include a transferred-byte count when the API supplies one. Control-transfer failures report that completion is unknown because that API has no separate partial byte count. Bulk and interrupt reads can return data together with timed_out=true, preserving bytes received before timeout. A failed control read reports unknown completion instead of inventing a partial count. See usb.rs and libusb's synchronous transfer API. USB cleanup releases the interface before closing the handle, exiting the context and unloading the library. Handle/context cleanup continues even when release fails. Libusb documents that release resets the interface to its first alternate setting, normally alternate setting 0. This does not restore every original device setting. The adapter does not explicitly call set-configuration, set-alternate-setting or reset-device during open/close. Bytes, limits and time budgets Read values share this JSON shape. bytes is the actual count, base64 always contains the data, and text contains UTF-8 or null when decoding fails. This is an operation's value; CLI execution also wraps values in its program result: { "bytes": 5, "base64": "aGVsbG8=", "text": "hello", "timed_out": false } Native serial, bulk and interrupt buffers are limited to 65,536 bytes. Their read lengths must be at least one byte. Control data is limited to 65,535 bytes by the 16-bit length field; zero-length control data is permitted. Successful writes return bytes_written and complete=true. The DSL separately limits each string to 65,536 bytes. Base64 expansion makes the practical binary payload in one DSL string about 48 KiB, while the native library accepts 64 KiB buffers. Prefer chunks of at most 32 KiB before encoding when the device's protocol permits chunking. USB transfer boundaries can be meaningful, so zuse does not split a transfer automatically. These limits are defined in language.rs and device_io.rs. Each read/write timeout must be 1 through 30,000 milliseconds. The executor adds configured device timeouts to the program's existing wait budget, whose default limit is 60,000 milliseconds. This is a conservative sum of requested budgets, not measured elapsed time. Embedded callers can configure runtime::Options.max_wait_ms. runtime.rs validates the entire program before execution. Transfer timeouts do not impose a hard wall-clock deadline on every USB operation. Enumeration, open, claim, release and close have no independently enforced timeout in this adapter. Interface release is a blocking libusb call with no timeout argument; setting a transfer timeout does not bound later cleanup. Whole-program validation rejects invalid types, directions, sizes, baud rates, payload combinations and base64 before earlier steps execute. Runtime failures, including busy interfaces and disconnection, stop subsequent steps but retain earlier effects. Bytes already delivered to a device cannot be undone by the executor. Acceptance evidence The sanitized evidence identifies the PTY/C ABI executable by SHA-256: ef1394bc6947eb6085dc057a1a084ee9509c6af5ba0ed8e67d6bced8c88eaa44 The final transfer reports were written on 2026-11-19 at approximately 22:33 UTC. The evidence filename follows the release reporting date, 2026-11-20. Initial and corrected transfer harness runs used the same executable. The separate real-system enumeration used a later executable and has its own SHA-256 in the record. Check Observed result Linux serial PTY 5/5 groups: all 256 byte values in both directions; raw 8N1 at 115200; 80 ms empty-read timeout; saved termios restoration Serial backpressure 15,360 of 32,768 bytes written before timeout; error count matched peer data; later write stopped; configuration restored Serial preflight 7 invalid programs rejected by both check and eval; no earlier write reached the PTY Synthetic libusb C ABI 11/11 groups: exact identity selection, busy interface, 256-byte bulk/interrupt transfers, 32-byte control transfers, argument widths and buffers USB partial/error cases Four partial-write scenarios made one transfer each; 17 bytes survived read timeout; invalid counts and unknown control completion rejected USB cleanup/preflight Release/close/exit/unload ordering, cleanup after release failure, and 11 invalid programs rejected before loading the fake library Real-system enumeration 32 serial candidate paths and 9 USB descriptors observed in read-only mode; no port open, USB claim or transfer The first transfer run exposed two harness assumptions. It expected all JSON on stdout, while CLI validation failures use a nonzero exit with structured JSON on stderr. It also put 65,536 raw bytes into one base64 string, exceeding the DSL string limit before the intended backpressure case could begin. The scripts now accept structured stderr only on failure and use a 32 KiB backpressure payload. Initial failure messages remain in the evidence. The USB harness proves fake-library selection through enumeration before attempting any open or transfer test. Only its CLI child processes receive a private LD_LIBRARY_PATH. The C image uses system libusb declarations but contains no physical USB backend. The serial harness accepts no device-path argument and creates its own PTYs. To reproduce the transfer checks, point the scripts at the executable being evaluated. Serial uses Python's standard library; USB additionally requires a C compiler and the libusb development header: python3 tests/native_serial.py --binary target/debug/zuse --output target/native-serial python3 tests/native_usb.py --binary target/debug/zuse --output target/native-usb Each script writes a JSON report, and USB also records synthetic native-call traces. Physical hardware transfers and live Windows/macOS behavior remain separate verification work.

title: 绘图原语与窗口锚点
body: 用有界脚本观察和操作桌面、浏览器与设备，并支持持久会话。 绘图原语与窗口锚点 用一段 Zuse 程序完成一组点按和笔画，可以减少工具往返与重复坐标换算。 mouse.stroke 负责整条折线的按下、移动和抬笔；窗口锚点保存已经观察过的局部区域。 直接执行 -c 与 eval 使用同一个执行器，接受完整脚本，无需 Python 包装或临时文件。 先检查可用后端，再观察目标窗口： zuse doctor zuse -c 'window.list()' 从结果中复制画板所在窗口的明确 id，确认它已获得焦点，并观察画布相对窗口的区域。 下面的 WINDOW_ID、区域位置和尺寸都是待填写的示例参数；替换为实际观察结果后执行。 先在画板中选好画笔和颜色，脚本将点击一个点并画两条折线。 zuse -c ' mouse.use(kind="user", appearance="system") anchor.set(name="board", window="WINDOW_ID", x=160, y=180, width=640, height=480) mouse.click_at(anchor="board", x=40, y=40) mouse.stroke(anchor="board", points="40,120;160,40;280,120", duration=240) mouse.stroke(anchor="board", points="40,160;160,80;280,160", duration=240) anchor.clear(name="board") mouse.release() ' 在命令末尾加 --dry-run 可检查语法、参数和静态预算；该模式不读取真实窗口或执行输入。 单次 -c 退出后会结束本次会话；后续命令需要重新选择鼠标和设置锚点。 常用原语 调用 作用与默认值 anchor.set(name,window,x,y,width,height) 保存明确窗口及其局部区域；x、y 默认 0，其他参数必填。 anchor.clear(name) 移除当前会话中指定名称的锚点。 mouse.click_at(x,y,anchor,button,settle,duration,curve,jitter,seed) 默认用 duration=350、curve="smooth"、jitter=0.6、seed=1 移动后点按；button="left"，settle=30，anchor 可省略。 mouse.stroke(points,duration,anchor,button,settle) 按顺序发送折线顶点并抬笔；duration=300，button="left"，settle=30。 draw.line(x1,y1,x2,y2) 描出起点至终点的线段。 draw.triangle(x1,y1,x2,y2,x3,y3) 用三个数值顶点描出闭合三角形，适合递归生成图案。 draw.rect(x,y,width,height) 从左上角出发描出闭合矩形；宽高必须为正数。 draw.circle(x,y,radius,steps) 以 x,y 为圆心描圆；半径必须为正数，steps=64。 draw.polygon(points) 描出至少三个顶点组成的多边形，自动补齐闭合点。 mouse.move(x,y,duration=0) 立即移动，只发送目标点一次，回执为 samples=1。 普通 mouse.move(x,y) 默认也为 350 ms、smooth 加减速和 0.6 轻微抖动；终点精确到达。 mouse.click_at 支持显式 duration=0，以及 jitter=0；先完整检查移动路径，再移动和点按。 五个 draw.* 原语共用 mouse.stroke 的输入、取消和抬笔路径，均支持可选的 anchor、duration=300、settle=30、button="left"，只描边，使用应用当前画笔和颜色。 坐标与尺寸允许有限小数；圆的 steps 为 3–4095 条线段，实际点数为 steps+1。 闭合点计入 4096 点上限；圆精确复制起点闭合，多边形已有闭合点时不会再追加。 例如 draw.circle(anchor="board",x=160,y=100,radius=40,duration=160)。 原有 mouse.circle 仍只移动指针；需要按住画笔描圆时使用 draw.circle。 表中的参数使用 name=value 形式。时间单位为毫秒，settle 允许 0–1000。 点按默认移动 350 ms 后等待一次 settle，合计预留 380 ms；折线在移动到起点后、按下后各等待一次。 这些等待和 duration 一起计入程序的 --max-wait-ms 预算。 points 使用分号分隔坐标对，例如 "10,20;80,40;120,10"，允许小数。 每条折线接受 2–4096 个点，每个程序最多 65536 个绘图点；执行前检查整条路径。 非零 duration 必须至少为线段数对应的毫秒数；duration=0 显式选择立即提交全部顶点。 顶点按顺序发送，程序不会用一条起终点连线替换中间顶点。 折线完成后释放按钮；按下或移动失败、执行被取消时也会尝试释放，并报告清理失败。 如果当前鼠标已经持有该按钮，点按和折线会拒绝接管。 delivery="submitted" 记录输入已提交；画作是否完成仍需读取应用状态或查看画面。 锚点与坐标 锚点的 x,y,width,height 使用窗口内部的原生坐标单位。 带 anchor 的点按、折线和图形使用该区域左上角为原点；省略时使用桌面坐标。 截图像素与原生坐标可能受缩放影响，填写参数时应依据当前窗口几何和截图映射换算。 局部点必须满足 0 <= x < width、0 <= y < height。 每次带锚点的操作开始前，Zuse 检查同一个窗口的 ID、PID、焦点、位置、尺寸和缩放。 窗口移动、缩放或失焦会返回 stale_anchor；重新观察后再设置锚点，程序不会自动换窗。 进入运行阶段后，同名锚点的替换若失败，旧值也会被移除。 锚点保存窗口及区域的位置，不追踪网页画布内部的平移、缩放、滚动或遮挡。 发生这些变化后应重新观察区域；窗口检查也不构成整个笔画期间的连续跟踪。 这适合位置稳定的绘图批次，语义控件定位仍使用 target.locate 等已有接口。 持久 shell 与函数复用 zuse shell 保留鼠标、函数和锚点，适合同一画板的连续操作。 每一行必须是一段完整程序；上一行结束后，下一行可以复用已经注册的函数。 zuse shell --idle-timeout-ms 900000 在该 shell 中先输入一行完成观察后的初始化和函数注册，再输入第二行复用。 同样先将 WINDOW_ID 和区域参数替换为实际观察值： mouse.use(kind="user",appearance="system"); anchor.set(name="board",window="WINDOW_ID",x=160,y=180,width=640,height=480); fn line(points){mouse.stroke(anchor="board",points=points,duration=240)} line(points="40,120;160,40;280,120"); line(points="40,160;160,80;280,160") 默认空闲超时为 900000 ms，即 15 分钟；此处 --idle-timeout-ms 控制 shell，必须为正整数。 计时发生在等待下一行输入期间，命令执行时间不计入空闲时间。 超时或输入 :quit 后会话结束，保留的函数、锚点和鼠标资源随之释放。 操作前检查与结果确认 先释放来自键盘或其他控制程序的 Super、Alt、Ctrl、Shift 等修饰键，再开始绘画。 外部残留的 Super 状态可能使窗口管理器接管拖动，导致画板没有收到预期笔画。 支持键盘状态检查的后端可用 zuse -c 'keyboard.state()' 辅助观察。 按颜色或图层组织一次内联调用，在批次之间确认画面，避免每个顶点都请求截图。 用 timer.start() 和 timer.stop() 查看执行耗时；异常时读取失败步骤及已完成动作， 确认画板现状后再继续，避免重复提交已经画出的笔画。 接口以 zuse schema 为准。相关实现位于 drawing.rs 和 runtime.rs，路径、锚点和取消行为见 绘图测试。

title: iOS through WebDriverAgent
body: 用有界脚本观察和操作桌面、浏览器与设备，并支持持久会话。 iOS through WebDriverAgent zuse controls the native iOS interface through an explicitly selected local WebDriverAgent (WDA) endpoint. WDA runs the device-side XCTest automation; zuse sends bounded HTTP requests from its Rust client. A running Appium server is not required by the zuse adapter. The current iOS acceptance consists of 20 passing isolated protocol tests, including the actual MCP Engine screenshot path. No physical Apple device was available for this acceptance. Device provisioning, USB forwarding and on-device application behavior still need physical iOS validation. See Verification for the exact scope. Prepare the device-side service The operator must prepare a working WDA service before running the zuse examples. Keep the following information together: the selected device's UDID, the WDA runner build, its device-side HTTP port, and the local forwarding port. Use a zuse build whose zuse schema output includes ios.connect. The adapter belongs to the default std build. Prepare an Apple development environment that can build, sign, install and run WebDriverAgentRunner on the selected device. For a physical device, the runner needs a valid signing identity and provisioning profile. Follow the WDA project instructions and upstream provisioning guide for that build. Pair the device with the development host and complete its trust prompts. Apple documents device pairing and running a signed app on a device. Enable Developer Mode where required and enable the device's UI Automation setting. See Apple's Developer Mode instructions and upstream device preparation. Keep the device available for the intended UI task. Have the operator run the WDA test runner using the prepared development workflow. Record the port on which this particular runner serves HTTP; the examples below use device port 8100. Arrange a local endpoint that forwards to that exact device and runner. Check its /status response before creating an automation session. Signing credentials, provisioning, trust dialogs, WDA installation and WDA startup remain part of the operator's device setup. The zuse connection command checks an existing endpoint. Upstream build preparation can have additional toolchain requirements; the Rust client does not perform those preparation steps. Forward an already running WDA over USB When the selected device and WDA build are reachable through usbmux, an operator-managed iproxy process can expose the service locally. Set IOS_UDID to the selected device's actual UDID, then use the current libusbmuxd iproxy syntax: iproxy --udid "${IOS_UDID:?Set IOS_UDID to the selected device UDID}" \ --local --source 127.0.0.1 8100:8100 The left port is the local listening port; the right port is WDA's device-side port. Leave the forwarding process running while zuse uses it. This command assumes WDA is already running; it does not build, sign or start the runner. Use a forwarding and runner-launch workflow compatible with the actual iOS version and host environment. For multiple devices, assign each selected UDID its own local port and use that port in ios.connect. zuse does not discover an iPhone or select the first attached device. Select and check the local endpoint The WDA endpoint must be an explicit http:// URL with a nonzero port and a loopback host. Supported examples include http://127.0.0.1:8100, http://localhost:8100 and http://[::1]:8100. localhost is mapped to IPv4 loopback; use [::1] explicitly for an IPv6 listener. A plain base-path prefix is supported when the local forwarding service requires one. Remote hostnames, non-loopback addresses, embedded credentials, query strings and fragments are rejected for the WDA endpoint. Choose the device in the external forwarding setup and give zuse the resulting loopback URL. Check the prepared service: curl --fail --silent --show-error http://127.0.0.1:8100/status A usable WDA status has value.ready set to true. The response may also identify an already active session. Treat that session as belonging to its existing owner until an explicit arrangement is made. Run an observation-only batch: zuse --read-only eval 'ios.connect(endpoint="http://127.0.0.1:8100"); ios.status(); ios.screen(); ios.snapshot()' ios.connect checks the endpoint and stores it in the current Runtime. It does not create a session or silently adopt the session reported by WDA. Status, screen geometry, native source and screenshots can be requested without creating a session. Keep related operations in one Runtime Use zuse shell for a persistent interactive workflow: zuse shell Enter each complete call on its own line: ios.connect(endpoint="http://127.0.0.1:8100") ios.session_start() ios.status() ios.open_url(url="https://example.com") ios.snapshot() ios.capture(path="ios-screen.png") ios.session_end() :quit This example creates an owned session only when the endpoint is available under the ownership rules below. It opens the URL through the device's default URL handler, observes the resulting native UI, captures a PNG and explicitly ends the owned session. The shell retains the connection and ownership between lines. Each separate zuse eval or zuse run process starts a fresh Runtime. To run a saved batch, save the ios.* calls as ios-task.zuse and use: zuse check ios-task.zuse zuse run ios-task.zuse check validates the complete source without contacting WDA. It checks argument types and bounds, endpoint syntax, source/raw options, supported keys and HTTP/HTTPS URL authority syntax. Reachability, the current active session and device behavior are checked during execution. Native input and Safari After creating or explicitly attaching to a session, the input operations are: Operation Call shape Tap ios.tap(x=120, y=240) Swipe ios.swipe(x1=120, y1=500, x2=120, y2=250, duration=350) Type text ios.type(text="Hello 世界") Key or device button ios.key(key="Enter") Launch an app ios.launch(bundle="com.apple.mobilesafari") Open a web URL ios.open_url(url="https://example.com") Choose coordinates from a current observation of the intended control. The values in the table illustrate syntax. Text is passed as Unicode to WDA's native typing route; the application's focus and keyboard state determine where it is received. Supported key names are Home, VolumeUp, VolumeDown, Enter/Return and Backspace. Swipe duration is movement time in milliseconds, defaults to 300, and accepts 1..10000. Safari can be launched and inspected as a native application. ios.open_url currently sends only the URL to WDA, whose URL route invokes the device's default URL handler when no application bundle is supplied. It therefore follows the phone's configured default browser. For a Safari-specific workflow, launch Safari and operate its native address field, or prepare Safari as the device's default browser. This adapter provides native Safari UI control. It exposes no Safari DOM selectors, JavaScript evaluation, Web Inspector connection or browser-context API. The browser.* CDP commands apply to their separately connected browser backend. Session ownership and replacement WDA maintains a global active session for an endpoint. Its session-creation handler clears the previous session before validating and creating the new one. zuse checks the current status before sending that request and tracks attached and owned identities separately. Request or state Behavior ios.connect(endpoint="…") Connects for observation without adopting the current WDA session. ios.connect(endpoint="…", session="…") Verifies and attaches to the exact supplied session ID. Input is permitted through that ID; ownership stays external. ios.session_start() Creates a session when no active session exists, or replaces a session already owned by this same instance. Existing external session or unknown active-session identity session_start refuses unless the caller explicitly supplies replace=true. ios.session_start(replace=true) Explicitly permits replacement of the endpoint's current global session. ios.session_end() Deletes only a session created by this instance, after checking that its exact ID is still active. Reconnect or process exit Drops local connection/ownership state. It does not delete the remote session. A successful session-start result contains the WDA identity at session.sessionId inside the operation's value. ios.status() reports attachedSessionId, owned, activeSessionKnown and activeSessionId. The active identity can change when another client uses the same WDA endpoint. To attach to an existing session, obtain its exact ID from its owner or a status response and provide it explicitly. Attaching does not grant deletion rights: ios.session_end() rejects cleanup of an externally owned session. End an owned session before reconnecting or exiting when remote cleanup is intended. replace=true authorizes the global replacement behavior. A failed creation may already have ended the previous WDA session; zuse clears the old attached input target before sending the creation request. A failed actual reconnect also leaves no old device target for subsequent input. WDA provides no atomic compare-and-create session operation. Another client can change the active session between the status check and creation. Assign one coordinator to each WDA endpoint or otherwise serialize session changes with its owner. The local ownership checks do not supply a cross-client lock. Observe coordinates and sensitive fields UIKit points and PNG pixels Input coordinates use UIKit points. ios.screen() returns WDA's screen geometry with coordinateSpace="points". ios.snapshot() includes that geometry alongside the native accessibility tree. Screenshot dimensions use PNG pixels. ios.capture reports width, height, coordinateSpace="pixels" and inputCoordinateSpace="points". WDA's screen route and screenshot route are separate observations. For example, if a same-orientation full-screen image is 1170 × 2532 pixels and the corresponding screen is 390 × 844 points, an image position of (300, 600) maps to (100, 200) points. This is an illustrative conversion, not a measured device result. Match the current image, geometry and orientation before converting coordinates; do not pass an image's pixel coordinates directly to ios.tap. Capture a file in an observation-only batch: zuse --read-only eval 'ios.connect(endpoint="http://127.0.0.1:8100"); ios.capture(path="ios-screen.png")' Successful capture replaces the requested output file. A failed capture preserves an existing destination. On Unix, the adapter creates its temporary image with mode 0600, then replaces the destination after receiving and checking the PNG structure. Default secure-field redaction Use these defaults for structured observation: ios.snapshot() ios.source() ios.source(format="json") WDA's JSON tree generator directly includes native values, labels and identifiers. zuse therefore filters structured results before returning them. For a recognized secure/password node and all its descendants, the result keeps only the element type, numeric rectangle, supported boolean state, child structure and redacted=true. Values, labels, names, identifiers, placeholders and unknown content attributes are omitted. The filter relies on the application's native secure role or secure flags. A custom widget that presents a secret as ordinary text needs its application to expose the correct accessibility semantics. Screenshot pixels retain the visible screen content. XML and description source require an explicit raw option because their sensitive content is not filtered: ios.source(format="xml", raw=true) ios.source(format="description", raw=true) ios.source(format="json", raw=true) also returns the unfiltered WDA tree. Raw output can include sensitive application text and becomes part of the normal CLI/MCP result. The default remains format="json", raw=false. Use the persistent MCP server Start a zuse MCP process and keep related calls on that running server: zuse mcp --stdio The server retains the selected iOS connection and owned session across tool calls. Through the MCP client's normal tool-call interface, call zuse.execute with these arguments: { "code": "ios.connect(endpoint=\"http://127.0.0.1:8100\"); ios.session_start(); ios.open_url(url=\"https://example.com\"); ios.snapshot()" } Then call zuse.screenshot: { "source": "ios" } The screenshot tool returns both structured capture metadata and a real image/png MCP image block. With no path, it uses and removes its temporary file. Supply path when a retained output file is wanted. The screenshot source enum also includes desktop, browser and android. End the owned session through the same running server: { "code": "ios.session_end()" } These are tool argument objects; the MCP client supplies the protocol envelopes. A separately started zuse server has fresh local ownership state. For an observation-only server, use: zuse mcp --stdio --read-only This permits connection, status, source and screenshots, including the requested screenshot output file. It rejects device input, app/URL opening and session creation/deletion. A tool request cannot disable the server's read-only setting. HTTP and Unix-socket transports retain the same runtime behavior: zuse mcp --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8377 zuse mcp --socket /tmp/zuse-ios-mcp.sock Run the transport appropriate for the client. Port 8377 in this example serves zuse's MCP protocol; port 8100 is the separately prepared WDA endpoint. Verification and troubleshooting The iOS protocol tests exercise the native client against isolated loopback WDA fixtures. All 20 tests passed in the integrated local test run. They cover session ownership, explicit replacement, invalidation after failed creation, Unicode/request payloads, HTTP framing and bounds, slow partial responses, secure-field filtering, URL preflight, PNG output preservation, and MCP image delivery/cleanup through the public Engine. Claim Evidence and current scope Native WDA request routes and payloads Fixed upstream source review plus isolated protocol tests. Owned-session cleanup and replacement rules Mocked external sessions, replacement, failed creation and changed active identity. Whole-program URL rejection before connection Runtime regression checks that the earlier connect sends no request. MCP iOS image content and temporary cleanup Real Engine path with a WDA fixture, exact PNG base64 and file-removal assertions. Physical iPhone/iPad operation, signing and USB forwarding Physical Apple-device acceptance is pending. Each public iOS operation uses one absolute 15-second network deadline, including all requests and partial reads within that operation. This is a per-operation limit; a script with several operations has several such budgets. Inputs and response sizes are also bounded. The client never automatically replays a failed action. Result Next step Endpoint connection fails or WDA is not ready Check the selected device, running runner, forwarding process, local port and /status response. Another active session exists Coordinate with its owner, explicitly attach to its ID, or intentionally authorize replacement. Input requires an attached or owned session Create a session or attach to the exact agreed session ID in the same Runtime. XML/description requires raw=true Use default JSON for filtered observation, or explicitly choose raw output. Action outcome is unknown or could not be confirmed Observe the device state before deciding whether another action is appropriate. Native input succeeds but the desired UI state is absent Re-observe focus, geometry and application state before issuing the next step. Fixed protocol references The implemented WDA contract was reviewed against appium/appium-ios commit 9a9092aa35e913a893f6dafddc2bfc13893d1daf, under packages/webdriveragent. The relevant upstream entry points are: Project and XCTest runner overview. Session lifecycle, app launch and URL opening. Session-ID route resolution. JSON/XML/description source routes and native JSON tree generation. Screen geometry and device buttons. PNG screenshot route. Tap/text routes, W3C touch actions and native text synthesis. Device URL dispatch and default application selection. The zuse implementation is src/ios.rs; MCP image integration is in src/mcp.rs. Use zuse schema for the command arguments supported by the actual installed build.

title: Bounded key holds
body: 用有界脚本观察和操作桌面、浏览器与设备，并支持持久会话。 Bounded key holds keyboard.hold and browser.hold keep one supported key down for a requested interval, then release it. Use them for applications that track a pressed key over time, such as a game. A successful receipt reports the submitted hold and release; confirm the resulting action through application state or an observation. keyboard.hold(key="Up", duration=400, window="0x123456") browser.hold(key="ArrowRight", duration=300) Both commands require duration in milliseconds, from 1 through 10000. Both accept Left, Up, Right, Down and their ArrowLeft, ArrowUp, ArrowRight, ArrowDown aliases. Native keyboard.hold also accepts slash or /, period or ., m and n; letter names are case-insensitive. browser.hold remains direction-only. Modifiers, lock keys and chords are rejected before input. Hold durations count toward the program's aggregate max_wait_ms budget. Read-only execution rejects these commands, including in dry-run mode. Sharing a keyboard during local multiplayer Native holds default to allow_other_keys=false: a held foreign key prevents input, and pressing another key during the hold ends it. For an authorized game with separate player controls, explicitly opt in on each call: keyboard.hold(key="Up", duration=180, window="0x123456", allow_other_keys=true) keyboard.hold(key="slash", duration=80, window="0x123456", allow_other_keys=true) Use the observed focused window ID. These calls run in sequence; they do not hold movement and fire simultaneously. With the opt-in, the other player's ordinary keys, such as WASD, Space, Q and E, may already be down or change during the hold. Zuse checks the current keymap and continues to reject modifiers, lock/layout changes and unsupported key actions. It refuses a requested key that is already held before its own press. Cleanup releases only the key pressed by this call; it never sends keyup for the other player's keys. Choose disjoint controls: a shared native keyboard cannot distinguish two players pressing the same key. The option applies only to keyboard.hold. It does not change keyboard.key, typing or browser holds. Use the short slash hold for a game's / binding; confirm whether a > icon means the physical period key before choosing period. Shift/Ctrl game actions remain outside this API. On Hyprland, creating a virtual keyboard is rejected when removing it could select a different main keyboard. With allow_other_keys=true, that case can instead use the existing native keyboard through one retained evdev file descriptor. This fallback requires an exact, globally unique mapping from the compositor name to the kernel's device name, the requested key capability, and existing read/write permission. It rejects virtual/reserved names, ambiguous numeric suffixes, duplicate normalized names, incomplete inventories and unsupported names. It checks the captured current XKB map, kernel pressed-key state and compositor state before input; it never grabs a device, selects another keyboard or changes permissions. A successful fallback receipt includes transport: "native_evdev". Default exclusive holds retain their existing behavior. The supported name normalization and collision rules follow Hyprland v0.57.2: deviceNameToInternalString and getNameForNewDevice. Zuse accepts only the unambiguous ASCII subset and checks names across the complete device inventory. Target and cancellation keyboard.hold supports Linux X11 and Hyprland. It observes the current foreground window once, retaining its native ID, process ID, bounds and scale. An explicit window must already have focus. With no window, the observed foreground window is retained for the whole call. The command does not focus a window. Identity, focus, geometry or scale changes end the hold even with allow_other_keys=true. The existing Num Lock state is preserved. Browser tabs within one native window share its ID; stop input and observe again when the user changes pages. Other native platforms return an explicit unsupported-state error before input. browser.hold operates on the already selected desktop page. It retains the document, URL, active element and viewport. The page must be visible and focused. Navigation, a different active element, a changed viewport or a disconnected target ends the hold. The command never activates a tab and does not enable a remote debugging endpoint. It uses the existing browser connection. The input permission is acquired for keydown and rechecked during the hold. Waiting and protocol acknowledgements do not keep the dispatch lock. Cancellation, permission revocation and errors run keyup cleanup for the key owned by the call. Cleanup has a separate bounded protocol timeout so cancellation does not skip release. A disconnected transport can return a cleanup failure; the receipt does not claim a confirmed release in that case. The native evdev fallback releases only its own key on ordinary completion, cancellation and handled failure. A hard process termination, such as SIGKILL, cannot confirm cleanup on an existing physical device; closing that descriptor does not synthesize keyup. Do not treat process death as a release acknowledgement. The native event loop and transport scheduling determine the exact observed interval. The result includes held_ms, while receiver-side measurements record the interval the application actually saw. Browser input sends one keydown and one keyup; it does not synthesize periodic repeat events. Focused validation cargo test --locked --lib --test key_hold key_hold cargo test --locked --test key_hold_browser -- --ignored --nocapture The first command covers key/option validation, aggregate wait accounting, read-only rejection, concurrent key ownership, cancellation, revoked permission, target changes and release after a failed press. XKB unit fixtures classify ordinary keys and reject remapped modifier actions without native input. The second starts a separate sandboxed Chromium profile and checks trusted keydown/keyup events, receiver timing, cancellation and focus changes. For an explicitly authorized host preflight that sends no input, run cargo test --locked --lib native_evdev_preflight_current_keyboard_without_input -- --ignored --nocapture. It only inspects the currently selected keyboard, opens its verified existing device and checks identity/capability/pressed-state access. A virtual current keyboard is reported as skipped; the test does not switch keyboards. The evdev ownership and name-collision unit tests use in-memory writers and inventories. Private Wayland tests below exercise the virtual transport, so they do not establish successful evdev input or live-game behavior. The private Wayland runner has a hold-only mode. Supply the actual binary path from the Cargo build output: python3 tests/native_wayland_private.py --headless --hold-tests \ --binary "$ZUSE_BINARY" --report /tmp/zuse-key-holds.json This runner uses its owned headless compositor and GTK windows. It records actual GTK keydown/keyup timestamps and compositor held-key state, tests cancellation and focus changes, and checks Num Lock both off and on with the original keyboard's keypad input after each hold. For X11, the separate fixture starts its own authenticated Xvfb server and checks receiver events, cancellation, focus changes and both Num Lock states: python3 tests/native_key_hold_x11.py --binary "$ZUSE_BINARY" \ --report /tmp/zuse-key-holds-x11.json

title: 概览
body: 提供可导入的桌面观察函数与浏览器验收模块，供 Zuse 脚本复用。 zuse-skills 把 GUI 能力封装成可原生导入、带简短说明的 .zuse 函数。Zuse 负责解析、导入、参数替换和执行；本仓库提供 ChatGPT 桌面版的观察、条件草稿准备和独立动作声明，微信、QQ 的只读模块，以及自有 Chromium 的操作验收模块。 桌面模块不请求焦点，不调用系统键鼠。它们要求调用者先确认应用窗口范围；应用不提供后台访问能力时返回错误。ChatGPT 的空草稿与进程守卫机制已接入，真实 ChatGPT Desktop 的读写和发送仍处于 blocked，尚未验收。 最近记录的目标没有可用 AT-SPI 应用入口；模块声明和预检不能证明目标应用开放了后台控制接口。 原生入口 完整目录预检和条件草稿准备需要 Zuse 0.5 或具备相同守卫接口的运行时。原有 chatgpt_controls(scope)、chatgpt_find(scope, window, label) 的定义与签名保持不变。可从上游正式发行安装；开发时使用最新公开源码： cargo install --locked --git https://github.com/LIghtJUNction/zuse.git zuse-computer zuse --version git clone https://github.com/LIghtJUNction/zuse-skills.git cd zuse-skills 先查看一个模块的函数与说明。导入只注册声明；不会执行函数体，也不会启动浏览器： zuse eval 'import(path="skills/chatgpt-desktop/module.zuse",as="chatgpt"); functions(namespace="chatgpt")' --read-only functions() 原生返回名称、参数顺序、/// 说明及源码位置。查看全部 14 个函数，其中 ChatGPT 模块导出 8 个： zuse run examples/catalog.zuse --read-only 执行自有浏览器验收，填字段、点击 Preview，再读回本地页面结果： zuse run examples/chromium-preview.zuse 它新建私有无头 Chromium 会话，只访问模块内的 data: 页面，不连接现有浏览器或账号；完成后关闭会话。需要已安装的 Chromium/Chrome。可用 ZUSE_BROWSER 指定其可执行文件，保留浏览器沙箱。 检查具体调用，不启动浏览器 原生 Zuse 可以直接预检含引号的参数： zuse eval 'import(path="skills/chromium/module.zuse",as="fixture"); fixture.chromium_fixture(text="他说 \"hello\"；本地预览")' --dry-run 可选 Python 适配器也提供具体调用的预检入口： python3 zskills.py plan chromium_fixture '"他说 \"hello\"；路径 C:\\tmp\\demo"' python3 zskills.py run chromium_fixture '"仅检查"' --dry-run 原生 --dry-run 返回步骤计划；适配器另附实际参数和 function_executed:false。两种方式都不会启动浏览器或执行应用操作。预检通过只说明该程序满足语法和策略，不证明应用存在或目标正确。正常 run 会重新检查当前模块，不使用旧预检结果跳过检查。 一次导入，多次查询 zuse shell --read-only 会保留模块定义，直到退出。以下两行输入到同一 shell： import(path="skills/chatgpt-desktop/module.zuse", as="chatgpt") functions(namespace="chatgpt") 脚本中的相对导入从脚本所在目录解析；eval 和交互 shell 的相对路径从启动目录解析。独立的 CLI 进程不共享定义或浏览器会话。 桌面模块 模块 原生函数 已实现的行为 ChatGPT 桌面版 chatgpt_controls(scope)、chatgpt_find(scope, window, label) 保留原有只读接口：读取指定 AT-SPI 子树；查找唯一精确标签 ChatGPT 原生观察 windows()、inspect_window(scope)、read_conversation(scope)、read_draft(editor) 列出窗口供识别，或观察已经确认的窗口、会话、编辑器子树 ChatGPT 草稿机制 prepare_draft(editor, pid, message) 要求进程匹配、编辑器精确为空，再对同一对象写入并读回；不发送 ChatGPT 独立动作 send_prepared(send_button, action_index) 显式授权后调用一个新观察到的原生动作；发送结果仍需观察确认 微信 wechat_controls(scope)、wechat_find(scope, window, label) 同上，范围由调用者确认属于微信 QQ qq_controls(scope)、qq_find(scope, window, label) 同上，范围由调用者确认属于 QQ Chromium chromium_fixture(text) 在自有无头浏览器中填写、点击并读取本地验收页面 编写工具 zuse_capabilities() 读取当前运行时和后端能力 先使用宿主已授权的只读电脑工具，确认进程、窗口 ID 和 AT-SPI 窗口路径。scope 必须属于目标应用的明确窗口或更小子树，window 必须是同一个窗口的原生 ID，label 使用刚观察到的完整标签。不要用全桌面范围，也不要把 active 当作窗口身份。缺少这组证据时停止调用该桌面函数。 例如，仅在已验证 0/12/0 和 0x123456 确为目标窗口后： import(path="skills/chatgpt-desktop/module.zuse", as="chatgpt") chatgpt.chatgpt_controls(scope="0/12/0") chatgpt.chatgpt_find(scope="0/12/0", window="0x123456", label="New chat") 这些路径与 ID 只是语法示例，不能直接用于真实会话。应用重启、窗口或无障碍树变化后需要重新确认。原生 *_controls 通过有界 watch 取得所选窗口子树的观察结果，然后立即 watch.close；快照位于返回的 watch 结果中的 receipt.observation，不会留下持续订阅。该快照可能含该子树内的文本；*_find 返回目标描述，不点击它。查不到、匹配不唯一、后端不可用或范围不满足条件时不进行输入。 最近一次真实应用记录确认 ChatGPT 窗口和进程稳定存在。正常 AT-SPI 短时监听前和监听期间的完整根枚举分别记录 10、15 个应用，均无错误或截断，但没有 ChatGPT 目标进程。监听结束后服务状态恢复，观察进程退出；全程没有桌面输入、读取应用文本字段或主动修改设置。该记录仍未提供可信 scope；本次模块同步没有重新探测目标。微信、QQ 尚未完成真实应用验收。Windows/macOS 的原生无障碍支持不能由 Linux AT-SPI 测试推断。 条件草稿与单独发送 六个新增函数与上游原生模块同名、同参数、同函数体。先确认原生进程、窗口、唯一的目标会话和编辑器，再读草稿；缺少 Text 接口、空值之外的现有文字、空白草稿或不完整观察都不能作为可覆盖依据。 prepare_draft 将 expected_text="" 和调用者观察到的正整数 pid 交给 Zuse。Linux AT-SPI 在同一个原生对象上检查条件、写入并读回；这些应用调用不是原子事务，调用者仍需确认会话身份并响应用户接管。适配器保留 edit 的完整守卫回执和 observation，并返回 send_performed:false。写入后观察不完整时，错误明确提示已经提交写入，需要先检查当前编辑器再决定下一步。 条件编辑当前仅支持 Linux AT-SPI；Windows/macOS 在输入前拒绝带条件的编辑。运行时预检只验证调用契约，不能证明当地无障碍后端可用。 以下仅预检语法和策略；示例路径与 PID 不代表真实目标： python3 zskills.py plan prepare_draft '"0/1/0/0"' 42 '"待核验的草稿"' python3 zskills.py plan send_prepared '"0/1/0/1"' 0 pid、action_index 使用 JSON 整数，其余参数仍为最多 4096 UTF-8 字节的 JSON 字符串。预检写入或发送不访问应用；两者在 --read-only 下均被原生运行时拒绝。 发送需要对具体目标和消息的明确授权。适配器的实际 run send_prepared 还要求 --authorize-send，Python 调用要求 authorize_send=True；计划和导入不授予发送权限。该参数记录调用者已经取得授权，不替代宿主输入权限，也不会自动核验会话或草稿。调用前重新检查目标、草稿、发送节点和其提供的动作索引，调用后观察同一会话确认结果。单次原生动作回执始终标注 delivery_confirmed:false，不会据此宣称消息送达或自动重试。 机器可读的能力与阻断原因 python3 zskills.py capabilities chatgpt-desktop python3 zskills.py capabilities wechat python3 zskills.py capabilities qq 这个入口只执行原生导入和条件草稿的全程序预检，不枚举真实应用、不访问聊天内容。runtime.native_import 表示导入能力；runtime.guarded_prepare 单独报告守卫调用能否通过预检，导入成功不会被当作新接口可用。缺少兼容运行时时返回具体阻断原因。 ChatGPT 的 prepare、send 返回 implemented:true 表示已有函数机制，同时保持 state:blocked、application_accepted:false 和 target_checked:false。last_target_assessment 引用最近 AT-SPI 入口缺失的历史证据；它不是本次实时探测。只读操作仍要求 requires_verified_target。微信、QQ 的写入与发送继续返回 implemented:false、background_adapter_not_implemented。 完整应用验收条件与当前差距 分别记录模块可导入、后端可访问、草稿写入、显式发送及结果确认。真实 ChatGPT 的后台写入与发送尚未验收；微信、QQ 尚未实现写入和发送适配。 紧凑输出与并行调用 zskills.py 是可选的 Python 3.10+ 适配器。它把导入和执行交给 Zuse，不再自行解释 .zuse。无需第三方 Python 依赖。 python3 zskills.py list python3 zskills.py list --json python3 zskills.py run zuse_capabilities python3 zskills.py run chromium_fixture '"本地预览"' python3 zskills.py parallel '[["zuse_capabilities"],["zuse_capabilities"]]' 原有桌面 *_controls 继续要求 scope，*_find 继续要求 scope, window, label。新增的 pid 和 action_index 按 JSON 整数传入，其他参数使用 JSON 字符串。选择特定运行时：python3 zskills.py --zuse /path/to/zuse check。 适配器负责： 从原生 functions() 读取名称与说明，核对 catalog.json 的参数和后端声明，省去反复读取完整模块。 对 *_controls 只保留最多 40 个控件的角色与标签，每个标签最多 100 字符，不输出 text/值字段或坐标。可访问名称由目标应用提供，仍可能含用户内容；此投影不承诺任意文本脱敏。后端返回不完整子树时明确报错。 新的观察函数返回有界完整子树，可能包含会话或草稿文字；请求前确认范围。条件草稿保留编辑回执和观察结果，单独发送保留动作回执并明确尚未确认送达。 一批最多 8 个独立调用、最多 4 个工作进程。先为每一项执行真实 Zuse 全程序预检，全部通过后才执行第一项；结果保持输入顺序，每项失败单独返回。每个执行进程有 30 秒期限，取消后最多等待 18 秒退出。 并行使用独立运行时，适合只读查询或分别拥有的浏览器实例。适配器在执行第一项前拒绝任何包含原生桌面写入或发送的并行批次；这些动作需要独立执行。预检检查语法、参数、只读权限和允许的操作类别；被导入的模块仍是需要审阅的程序源码。 验证 python3 zskills.py check ZUSE_BIN=/path/to/zuse python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v 2026-11-22 01:51（Asia/Taipei），使用实际从 crates.io 安装的 zuse-computer 0.5.0 对模块源码 fce48d78dcbedbecaaa56a09fdf11b12b9a6b09a 完成发布后复验：14 个函数检查通过，34 项测试全部通过，0 跳过，耗时 2.122 秒。两项私有 Chromium 测试均实际执行。二进制、公开归档及测试日志摘要见发布版验收收据。真实 ChatGPT 的草稿和发送仍未验收，微信、QQ 的写入适配仍未实现。 本次六函数同步在 Zuse 0.5 候选源码的 dev 构建上完成。沙箱的 14 个函数原生 check 通过，32 项测试通过，2 项自有浏览器测试默认跳过；随后开发机启用私有 Chromium 验收，34 项全部通过，耗时 2.650 秒。验证时该候选构建的版本字符串仍为 0.4.2，守卫接口通过实际预检确认，没有把它记为已发布的 0.5 二进制。测试没有访问真实账号、操作用户桌面或发送消息，也未重跑旧 Zuse 0.4.0 发行二进制。新增覆盖包括整数参数、输入只读拒绝、独立发送授权、写入批次拒绝、完整编辑回执和诚实能力元数据。 以下是原版本的历史验证，不能用来证明新增草稿或发送能力已通过真实应用验收。2026-11-21 对源码 dbe3533684e39f90e7a7a05d55638629c242bb91 完成： 环境 运行时来源 结果 沙箱 Zuse 0.4.0 Git 0016f96067d1e4672c62be9d8008d210edcdae2d，dev 构建 22 项测试通过，2 项浏览器测试默认跳过；该沙箱 Chromium 启动曾收到 SIGABRT 原生 Linux 开发机 已发表 zuse-computer 0.4.0 包的原生发布验证阶段已有 dev 构建 原生 check 通过；24/24 项测试通过，耗时 2.245 秒，包含两个自有浏览器测试 原生浏览器验收实际完成单会话的字段填写、Preview 点击和结果读回，以及两个私有会话并行时的结果隔离。运行时所用包源码与已发表归档的全部 200 个文件逐字节匹配；本轮没有重新编译、从沙箱传入二进制或全局安装。测试没有连接真实账号，也没有操作用户桌面。 历史测试覆盖原生导入与说明、相对路径、持久 shell、导入无顶层副作用、参数注入、只读预检、子树边界、输出预算、并行预检顺序、具体调用计划及能力目录。当时的 8 个导出函数通过原生预检；真实 ChatGPT、微信、QQ 的读写支持按上文边界单独记录。 在具备正常 Chromium 运行条件的隔离环境复验： ZUSE_BIN=/path/to/zuse ZUSE_SKILLS_BROWSER_TESTS=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v 运行时与归档 SHA256、测试日志 SHA256、AT-SPI 观察结果见 验收收据。本地网页验收不替代真实应用的草稿或发送验收。 编写技能 · zgpui 原生后端提案 · 上游原生模块实现

title: zgpui → zuse: native automation contract (proposal)
body: 提供可导入的桌面观察函数与浏览器验收模块，供 Zuse 脚本复用。 zgpui → zuse: native automation contract (proposal) Generate one semantic descriptor per actionable built-in control from the same metadata that draws it: role, stable view key, localized label, enabled/visible flags, and supported actions with typed parameters. Neither pixels nor synthesized mouse movement is needed. Applications using stock controls get the default implementation; raw canvases/custom controls without semantics are reported unsupported unless they expose their own semantics. Discovery and dispatch Function key is deterministic from stable application/view/action keys (e.g. preferences.appearance.set_theme), not translated labels or transient widget order. Duplicate IDs are errors; IDs on virtualized/recycled rows include the model key. Generate the short description from role/action/label, with optional app-authored override. Expose just names/descriptions first; fetch the argument schema only for a selected function. Never expose passwords, form values, or hidden controls by default. Each session binds to an explicitly approved local application instance. Dispatch by instance, view generation, stable control ID and action ID. Verify the same generation, enabled state, and scope at dispatch on that app's UI thread; if the app replaced the control, return a stale-target error. Do not focus a window, move the system pointer, or fall back to generic input. Reuse the existing semantic/widget arena, use compact numeric IDs and static descriptors where possible, and stream bounded changes. Allocate no second scene tree; no observer work when unsubscribed. Local transport must authenticate callers and scope operations. Use separate app instances/sessions for parallel requests; serialize conflicting writes within one instance. Observe does not imply write permission. Measure cold catalog generation, incremental updates, steady-state dispatch and P95 application acknowledgement. Compare allocations and peak RSS against the same zgpui app with integration off; report the actual numbers, not a speed target as a result. First fixture: built-in button, edit field, and panel switch; with another window foreground, generate a manifest, invoke each permitted control, reject disabled/stale and duplicate keys, and demonstrate no focus or cursor change. This document is a proposed contract, not a shipped zgpui implementation.

title: zuse-skill-creator
body: 提供可导入的桌面观察函数与浏览器验收模块，供 Zuse 脚本复用。 Read only the applicable module and current runtime schema. Add skills/<id>/SKILL.md and module.zuse; add its public names, ordered parameters, backend and read-only policy to catalog.json. Place a concise /// description immediately before every exported fn. Native functions() reads these comments. Zuse function parameters are names, not typed declarations; builtin calls validate values after native AST substitution. Keep untrusted strings as parameters, never concatenate them into executable source. Import modules through the native import command. Modules contain declarations only; importing must not launch a browser, observe the desktop or perform input. Do not implement a second language parser in a wrapper. Require explicitly verified application/window scope. Prefer exact semantic targets to coordinates. Reject ambiguous, stale or unsupported targets. Never replace missing background access with a focus change, system pointer, another application or another account. Native writes require stable object identity, dispatch-time scope checks and a no-focus contract; numeric accessibility paths alone do not provide that. For an empty draft, use accessibility.set_text with expected_text="" and the observed expected_pid, retain its same-object readback receipt, and observe the editor afterward. Keep preparation and sending in separate functions. State that text checks and writes are separate application calls and that PID identifies a process, not a conversation. Require explicit send authorization and fresh target/draft verification; a native action receipt does not prove delivery. Keep discovery concise. functions(namespace="…") selects one module. An adapter can project bounded fields, but must not claim that all accessible names are free of user content. A truncated observation is incomplete evidence, not proof of absence. For parallel work, use separate owned sessions and preflight all branches before starting any. Keep native desktop writes and sends outside the adapter's parallel batches. Do not share mutable browser/runtime state without an explicit serialization model. Use the host's authorized computer tools for real desktop interaction; execution tools are only appropriate for owned, isolated fixtures. Test native import/metadata, malformed or effectful imports, argument injection, ambiguity, unavailable backends, output bounds and branch isolation. Run python3 zskills.py check and ZUSE_BIN=/path/to/zuse python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v. Run the opt-in browser tests where Chromium can start normally. Record the exact runtime and environment. Separate parser/preflight tests, mock receipt projections, owned fixture results and real application acceptance. Report shipped mechanisms with implemented, and keep application_accepted:false / blocked when target access is missing. Probe guarded-call support separately from module import. Preserve historical validation receipts. Commit source to Git; do not publish account data, profiles, compiled binaries or an unsupported success claim. zuse_capabilities() is a read-only native probe; it does not itself grant input permission or establish application identity.

title: 概览
body: 为 Zuse 提供绘图、分形、桌面操作、文字输入和计时函数。 Zuse standard library Reusable Zuse functions for drawing, fractals, desktop setup, explicit text input, and timing. The std package is source code: installation stores a pinned Git commit locally, and import registers its functions. Desktop actions begin when a script calls them. Version 0.1.0 requires Zuse 0.6.0 or later, with pkg, window anchors, mouse.stroke, draw.triangle, and bounded scalar programs. Use zuse --version and zuse schema to check the installed build. Install and inspect Create a project directory, then add the tagged package: mkdir my-drawing cd my-drawing zuse pkg init my-drawing zuse pkg add https://github.com/LIghtJUNction/zuse-std.git --rev v0.1.0 zuse -c 'import(path="pkg:std",as="std"); functions(namespace="std")' Commit the project's zuse.json and zuse.lock.json. The manifest records the requested source revision; the lockfile records its full Git commit. Another checkout restores the locked sources with: zuse pkg install --locked The package has no third-party package dependencies. Import uses installed files and does not fetch code or run installation hooks. Git transport and the package manager remain part of the installation process. Import a module Import the whole library for std.desktop, std.drawing, std.fractal, std.input, and std.timing: 22 functions across five exports. Import one export when a script needs a smaller namespace: import(path="pkg:std/drawing", as="art") functions(namespace="art") Function descriptions and parameter names are included in the catalog returned by functions. Arguments are named and required; the table below lists every public function. Source files are the authoritative implementation. Export Function Behavior desktop inspect() List windows and inspect held keyboard modifiers. desktop focus(window_id) Focus the specified window and wait 200 ms. desktop bind_canvas(name,window_id,x,y,width,height) Focus, borrow the system pointer, and create a window-local anchor. desktop click(canvas,x,y) Click a local point with 30 ms input settling and 70 ms application settling. desktop capture(window_id,path) Save a window screenshot at the requested path. desktop release_canvas(name) Clear the named anchor and release the session's mouse handle. drawing stroke(canvas,points,duration) Draw an open polyline with explicit timing. drawing line(canvas,x1,y1,x2,y2) Draw a line in 180 ms. drawing triangle(canvas,x1,y1,x2,y2,x3,y3) Outline three numeric vertices in one 240 ms stroke. drawing rectangle(canvas,x,y,width,height) Outline a rectangle in 240 ms. drawing circle(canvas,x,y,radius) Outline a circle with 64 segments in 360 ms. drawing polygon(canvas,points,duration) Close and outline a polygon with explicit timing. drawing arrow(canvas,x1,y1,x2,y2,head) Draw a line and an explicitly supplied arrowhead polyline. fractal sierpinski(canvas,x,y,width,height,depth) Compute and draw a Sierpinski triangle using bounded Zuse recursion. input type_in(window_id,text) Focus the specified window, wait 200 ms, then type into its current text target. input key_in(window_id,key) Focus the specified window, wait 200 ms, then submit a key or chord. input set_text(node_path,text) Focus an observed accessibility node and replace its text. timing start(), stop(), status(), reset() Forward to the session timer operations. timing pause(ms) Wait within the script's configured wait budget. Draw on an observed canvas Observe the intended window and its canvas first. Replace WINDOW_ID and the region below with those observations; the numbers are examples. Select the application's brush, width, and color before executing drawing functions. import(path="pkg:std", as="std") std.desktop.bind_canvas(name="board", window_id="WINDOW_ID", x=160, y=180, width=640, height=480) std.timing.start() std.drawing.rectangle(canvas="board", x=40, y=40, width=240, height=140) std.drawing.circle(canvas="board", x=160, y=110, radius=45) std.drawing.arrow(canvas="board", x1=310, y1=110, x2=430, y2=110, head="410,90;430,110;410,130") std.timing.stop() std.desktop.capture(window_id="WINDOW_ID", path="canvas.png") std.desktop.release_canvas(name="board") The drawing functions use the application's current brush and left mouse button. They outline shapes; they do not set colors or fill areas. points and head use x,y;x,y strings. The arrow helper accepts explicit head vertices so callers can choose its shape. Numeric geometry, including recursive subdivision, can be calculated directly in Zuse expressions. Coordinates are local to the named canvas anchor. The runtime rejects an anchor when its window identity, focus, position, dimensions, or scale changes. It does not track scrolling or zooming inside the page. Re-observe changed geometry before binding again. A completed input receipt means input was submitted; inspect the screenshot to confirm the application drew the intended result. The fixed waits make these small compositions easier to reuse; they are not application-readiness detection. For long workflows, use the runtime's bounded observation and waiting primitives. Multiple scripts can retain functions and anchors in zuse shell; its idle timeout controls cleanup of the session. Draw a fractal with Zuse expressions The fractal module computes every vertex with let, arithmetic, if/else, and recursive function calls. Each leaf uses one draw.triangle stroke. It contains no precomputed coordinate arrays and needs no external program to generate the geometry. Observe the window and canvas first, select the application's brush and color, then replace the window ID and anchor region below. This example assumes an observed 755 × 646 canvas and passes the complete program to Zuse through stdin: zuse script - --max-steps 4096 --max-wait-ms 90000 <<'ZUSE' import(path="pkg:std", as="std") std.desktop.bind_canvas(name="board", window_id="OBSERVED_WINDOW_ID", x=160, y=180, width=755, height=646) std.fractal.sierpinski(canvas="board", x=50, y=590, width=650, height=560, depth=5) std.desktop.capture(window_id="OBSERVED_WINDOW_ID", path="fractal.png") std.desktop.release_canvas(name="board") ZUSE x,y identify the left end of the base; height extends upward on the screen. Depth 0 draws one triangle, depth 2 draws 9, and depth 5 draws 243. Each leaf uses 60 ms of motion and two 10 ms settling waits, so depth 5 has a fixed drawing wait budget of 19,440 ms. Window checks and input dispatch add elapsed time. For a smaller namespace, import pkg:std/fractal with an explicit alias. Validate the package These commands load declarations, inspect the catalog, and validate every public function without sending desktop input: zuse run examples/catalog.zuse zuse check examples/validate-api.zuse The validation fixture intentionally contains a placeholder window ID and an example node path. Use check for that file. To verify an installed package, run the safe catalog example from the consuming project, or execute the inline catalog command in the installation section. Publish a package A package consists of a zuse.json manifest and ordinary .zuse source files. This repository is a small example: the manifest names the package, its version, its entry module, and its public exports. A package author can use their own Git repository and publish a version tag; no central registry account is required. After committing reviewed source and configuring that repository's origin, inspect and publish the current manifest version: zuse pkg publish --dry-run zuse pkg publish gh repo edit OWNER/REPO --add-topic zuse --add-topic zuse-package Add the zuse and zuse-package GitHub topics so other users can discover the repository with gh search repos --topic zuse. The topics are discovery labels; consumers should inspect the manifest and source before choosing a package. Use a new version for changed source. Consumers select a source revision with pkg add or pkg update and commit the resulting lockfile. See the Zuse package-management documentation for command behavior, dependency resolution, and the lockfile format. License MIT. See LICENSE.

title: 概览
body: 将 ANSI / VT 字节流增量解析为终端事件。 zvte CI An incremental ANSI/VT parser for terminal output. The published crate always uses #![no_std], only core, zero dependencies and zero heap allocations. All mutable state and bounded buffers live in Parser. Stable Rust 1.74.0 or newer. [dependencies] zvte = "0.1" Use use zvte::{Params, Parser, Perform}; #[derive(Default)] struct Output { characters: usize, controls: usize, sgr: usize } impl Perform for Output { fn print(&mut self, _: char) { self.characters += 1; } fn execute(&mut self, _: u8) { self.controls += 1; } fn csi_dispatch(&mut self, _: &Params, intermediates: &[u8], ignore: bool, action: char) { if !ignore && intermediates.is_empty() && action == 'm' { self.sgr += 1; } } } let mut parser = Parser::new(); let mut output = Output::default(); parser.advance(b"\x1b[31", &mut output); parser.advance(b"mred\x1b[0m\n", &mut output); assert_eq!((output.characters, output.controls, output.sgr), (3, 1, 2)); assert!(parser.is_ground()); Chunks may split any control sequence or UTF-8 codepoint. Empty chunks do nothing. Call finish(&mut handler) only at the end of the byte stream: it emits one replacement character for unfinished UTF-8, unhooks active DCS data, discards incomplete control commands and resets. reset() abandons a stream without callbacks. To inspect a real stream: printf '\033[31mred\033[0m\n' | cargo run --example inspect Callbacks Method Event print(char) One printable Unicode scalar text(&[u8]) A contiguous printable ASCII run; defaults to calling print for each byte execute(u8) A C0 or C1 control esc_dispatch ESC final byte and intermediates csi_dispatch CSI parameters, subparameters, intermediates and final byte hook, put, unhook DCS header, payload bytes and end osc_dispatch OSC fields and whether BEL terminated the command osc_overflow First OSC capacity overflow in the current command Override text when your consumer can process a slice efficiently. It contains printable ASCII, including DEL for vte compatibility; Unicode scalars use print. Text callback boundaries follow input chunk boundaries. Preserve event order when buffering output. The parser recognizes syntax; rendering, SGR interpretation, PTYs, screen storage and terminal applications belong to the caller. Bounds and compatibility The reference is alacritty/vte 0.15.0, with its std feature disabled and the same OSC capacity. The comparison project pins the registry version and lockfile. Semantics include: CSI/DCS have up to 32 numeric entries, including colon subparameters. Empty entries become zero. Decimal values saturate at 65535; extra entries set ignore. At most two intermediate/private marker bytes are retained. OSC stores 1024 payload bytes and 16 fields by default. Separators do not consume payload space. Parser::<4096>::new_with_size() changes storage at compile time; Parser::<0> is supported. Excess payload/fields are bounded and observable through osc_overflow(). Subsequent sequences continue normally. BEL, ESC, CAN and SUB terminate OSC. ESC completes OSC immediately; a following backslash dispatches a separate ESC event. Raw 0x9c remains OSC data, matching vte's UTF-8 semantics. DCS does recognize raw 0x9c as its terminator. The seven-bit ESC forms introduce sequences. Raw C1 bytes in ground are reported through execute; they do not start eight-bit CSI/OSC commands. SOS/PM/APC are consumed until cancellation/ESC. Invalid parameter ordering is discarded and parsing resynchronizes. Invalid UTF-8 uses replacement characters without losing following controls. Truncation waits for the next chunk. Two chunk-boundary corrections: vte 0.15.0 reports UTF-8-encoded C1 as print when its two bytes span input calls, but as execute in a single call. It can also drop an ASCII byte following a completed partial UTF-8 scalar. zvte consistently uses execute for C1 and preserves every text character. Dedicated regressions record both reference defects. Random differential tests compare whole-input vte events with whole and randomly chunked zvte events, with no normalization. Timed fixtures require exact callback/event equality with identical chunks. text, osc_overflow, finish, and reset are additional APIs. The core forbids unsafe code. Validated word-at-a-time ASCII scanning uses ordinary unaligned-safe byte copies and works without target CPU feature flags. The constant VT transition table avoids a large nested branch tree. The parser owns no external resource, performs no I/O, and can be moved between threads. Handler panics remain the caller's responsibility. Verify and measure Native measurements of the optimized 0.1.1 parser against bounded vte 0.15.0, using Rust 1.99.1 and strict scalar callbacks. The machines were Intel Xeon 6973P-C (x86_64) and Arm Neoverse-N2 (aarch64): Strict scalar callbacks x86_64 speedup aarch64 speedup ASCII text 1.976× 2.752× Original Unicode workload 1.561× 1.250× Unicode in single-byte chunks 2.256× 1.560× Original eleven-workload geometric mean 1.572× 1.622× Valid Unicode now uses one combined validation/decoding pass. Split scalars validate only newly received continuation bytes. Default parser size remains 1,248 bytes versus 1,432 bytes for the bounded reference; both allocate zero bytes. Full Unicode optimization report and raw measurements include all seventeen workloads, ns/byte, MiB/s, platform details, limitations and the original unchanged Unicode fixture. The ARM two-byte-script result is effectively parity. These results do not establish a universal speedup or an aggregate 2× result. The original 0.1.0 report remains available with its original CPU/run provenance. cargo test --locked cargo +1.74.0 test --locked cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings cargo doc --no-deps cargo +nightly miri test cargo test --manifest-path comparison/Cargo.toml --locked cargo run --release --manifest-path comparison/Cargo.toml --bin bench comparison/ is a separate Cargo workspace and is excluded from the published package and dependency tree. Its fixtures, differential tests, benchmark protocol and result files make performance claims reproducible. Strict per-character comparisons and batched-text measurements are reported separately. An allocator test verifies construction, parsing, finishing and resetting allocate nothing. CI additionally tests Linux x86_64/aarch64, macOS and Windows, runs Miri, and compiles WASM, Cortex-M and RISC-V targets at the MSRV. Release In Actions → Release, run the workflow on main and select patch, minor, major, or none. none publishes the current version or resumes a partially completed publication. Store the crates.io token in the repository secret CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN. The workflow runs the complete CI gate, validates the selected version and package, runs cargo publish --dry-run, pushes a version commit when needed, publishes to crates.io, creates the matching version tag and creates a GitHub Release with the .crate archive. A Cargo.toml change pushed to main also runs this workflow to publish the current version. All steps run in the same trusted workflow. PRs cannot publish, and releases do not depend on a bot-created tag triggering another workflow. If publication stops after the version commit is pushed, run a new workflow from the current main with none. Already-published versions are accepted only when their archive checksum matches; a conflicting version or tag fails closed. MIT licensed. The implementation is independent; vte is used as a test oracle.
